他把柴薪堆满炉膛，
火焰便仿佛烧着了圣诞的巨柴，
轰隆隆直冲烟囱上去。

于是她开口了，她的嗓音
于耳、于心都那样可爱，虽说被痛苦打断；
它听着遥远，虽说甜美清亮，
仿佛来自雨的外面；
仿佛来自凄凉夜风的外面，
像一个生怕讨不到欢迎的人，
怯怯送来的声音。

「我离得太远，觉不出冷，
又太冷，觉不出火；
它穿不透那一堆湿霉的泥土，
正浸着尖塔滴下的水：
蜡制的殓衣在锦缎之下，
在皮裘与羊毛层层之下，
冻在这样酷烈的霜里。」

她的嗓音、她的眼睛、她苍白的脸颊，
穿过他的心与脑，一阵战栗；
惊奇、怜悯与爱汇成
一股无形的痛楚的激情；
她的美以一种奇异的欢悦攫住了他：
他同她一起到了外面，活生生惨白的夜里，
同她一起在吹刮的雨中！

她骤然起身，跪倒，把她的娉婷
整个掷在他脚前：
「我倦了，倦了在雨里雪里雹子里
被吹来荡去！
可宁可无处安息，也强似同
那些名字会脏了我舌头的东西为伍！
我多恨那发霉的尸布！

「啊，虽说是鬼，我到底还是位贵女！」
青年骇然倒退。
她的眼睛睁大、发白、变冷，
浮起一种超乎一切的恐怖。
他抓住她的手：一股冰冷
直螫到他的腕，但他凭着坚定的意志，
把它握得又暖又牢。

「我能做什么救您呢，亲爱的？」
一听这话她霍然立起；
她踮起脚尖，他俯下耳朵，
她低语了，轻轻地低语。
她退开；她带着探问的恐惧凝望：
像人望着心上人的灵床，
他立着，一张鬼一样白的脸。

「六次——都徒然，哦不幸的我！——
我卑屈了自己来哀求！
这是最后一回：趁落日衰尽，
我随暮色一同长出，
在城四下里飘游、彷徨，
一道流落、孤单、被弃的影：
除了您，无人看见我。」

===Original===

He shivered, he shook, he had turned to clay,
Vile fear had gone into his blood;
His face was a dismal ashy gray,
Through his heart crept slime and mud;
The lady stood in a still dismay,
She drooped, she shrank, she withered away
Like a half-blown frozen bud.

“Speak once more. Am I frightful then?
I live, though they call it death;
I am only cold! Say ‘dear’ again.”
But scarce could he heave a breath;
Over a dank and steaming fen
He floated astray from the world of men,
A lost, half-conscious wraith.

“Ah, ’tis the last time! Save me!” Her cry
Entered his heart, and lay.
But he loved the sunshine, the golden sky,
And the ghosts’ moonlight is gray!﻿—
As feverous visions flit and fly
And without a motion elude the eye,
She stood three steps away.

But oh, her eyes!﻿—refusal base
Those live-soul-stars had slain!
Frozen eyes in an icy face
They had grown. Like a ghost of the brain,
Beside the lattice, thought-moved in space,
She stood with a doleful despairing grace:
The fire burned! clanged the rain!

Faded or fled, she had vanished quite!
The loud wind sank to a sigh;
Pale faces without paled the face of night,
Sweeping the window by;
Some to the glass pressed a cheek of fright,
Some shot a gleam of decaying light
From a flickering, uncertain eye.

Whence did it come, from the sky or the deep,
That faint, long-cadenced wail?
From the closing door of the down-way steep,
His own bosom, or out of the gale?
From the land where dead dreams, or dead maidens sleep?
Out of every night to come will creep
That cry his heart to quail!

The clouds had broken, the wind was at rest,
The sea would be still ere morn,
The moon had gone down behind its breast
Save the tip of one blunt horn:
Was that the ghost-angel without a nest﻿—
Across the moonset far in the west
That thin white vapour borne?

He turned from the lattice: the fire-lit room
With its ghost-forsaken chair
Was cold and drear as a rifled tomb,
Shameful and dreamless and bare!
Filled it was with his own soul’s gloom,
With the sense of a traitor’s merited doom,
With a lovely ghost’s despair!

He had driven a lady, and lightly clad,
Out in the stormy cold!
Was she a ghost?﻿—Divinely sad
Are the people of Hades old!
A wandering ghost? Oh, self-care bad,
Caitiff and craven and cowering, which had
Refused her an earthly fold!

===Chinese===

他颤抖，他摇撼，他已化成泥土，
卑污的恐惧钻进了他的血；
他的脸一片惨灰，
污泥浊水爬过他的心；
贵女立在一阵静静的惶乱里，
她低萎，她收缩，她枯残下去，
像一朵半开就冻僵的花蕾。

「再说一句。那么我可怕吗？
我活着，虽说他们管那叫死；
我只是冷！再说一声『亲爱的』。」
可他几乎提不起一口呼吸；
他仿佛漂在一片蒸腾的臭泽上，
远离了人的世界，
一道迷失的、半有知觉的游魂。

「啊，这是最后一次了！救救我！」
她的呼喊进入他的心，躺在那里。
可他爱阳光、爱金色的天，
而鬼的月光是灰的！——
像热病的幻象飞掠而过，
不动一寸便躲开人的眼睛，
她已站在三步之外。

可是，她的眼睛！——那卑怯的拒绝，
已杀害了那两颗活的魂灵之星！
它们已长成冰脸上一双
冻结的眼。像脑中的一个幻影，
在窗畔，被念头推动于空间，
她立着，一副哀哀欲绝的风致：
炉火还烧着！雨铿然敲着！

是淡去还是逃走，她已全然不见！
狂风降成一声叹息；
外面一张张苍白的脸，把夜的脸挤得更白，
一一掠过窗前；
有的把一张惊惶的脸颊贴上玻璃，
有的从一只摇曳不定的眼睛里，
射出一缕衰朽的光。

那声悠长顿挫的低泣，从哪里来，
从天上，还是从深渊？
从陡落之路那扇正阖上的门，
从他自己的胸中，还是从风里？
从死梦安睡、或死去的少女安睡的国土？
往后每一个夜里，那声
叫他心悸的哭喊，都会爬出来！

云破开了，风已安息，
海不到天亮就会静了，
月亮已沉下它自己的胸后，
只露出一只钝角：
那可是无巢的天使之鬼——
远远在西方、没月的去处，
被载着走的那一缕薄薄的白汽？

他从窗前转过身：炉火照亮的小房，
连同那把被鬼抛下的椅子，
冷冷清清，像一座被劫的墓，
无耻，无梦，空空荡荡！
它盛满了他自己灵魂的阴郁，
盛满了叛徒应得天谴的知觉，
盛满了一位可爱之鬼的绝望！

他把一位贵女，衣衫单薄地，
赶进了风暴的严寒！
她是鬼吗？——冥府古老的子民，
哀愁自有其神圣！
一个流落的鬼？哦，可鄙的自惜，
那怯懦、畏葸、蜷缩的心肠，竟
拒绝给她一个尘世的栖所！

===Original===

Ill had she fared, his lovely guest!﻿—
A passion of wild self-blame
Tore the heart that failed in the test
With a thousand hooks of shame,
Bent his proud head on his heaving breast,
Shore the plume from his ancient crest,
Puffed at his ancient name.

He sickened with scorn of a fallen will,
With love and remorse he wept;
He sank and kissed her footprints chill
And the track by her garment swept;
He kneeled by her chair, all ice-cold still,
Dropped his head in it, moaned until
For weariness he slept.

He slept until the flaming sun
Laughed at the by-gone dark:
“A frightful dream!﻿—but the night is done,”
He said, “and I hear the lark!”
All day he held out; with the evening gun
A booming terror his brain did stun,
And Doubt, the jackal, gan bark.

Followed the lion, Conviction, fast,
And the truth no dream he knew!
Night after night raved the conscience-blast,
But stilled as the morning grew.
When seven slow moons had come and passed
His self-reproach aside he cast,
And the truth appeared untrue.

A lady fair﻿—old story vile!﻿—
Would make his heart her boast:
In the growing glamour of her smile
He forgot the lovely ghost:
Forgot her for bitterness wrapt in wile,
For the lady was false as a crocodile,
And her heart was a cave of frost.

Then the cold white face, with its woe divine,
Came back in the hour of sighs:
Not always with comfort to those that pine
The dear true faces arise!
He yearned for her, dreamed of her, prayed for a sign;
He wept for her pleading voice, and the shine
Of her solitary eyes.

“With thy face so still, which I made so sad﻿—
Ah me! which I might have wooed﻿—
Thou holdest my heart in a love not glad,
Sorrowful, shame-subdued!
Come to me, lady, in pardon clad;
Come to my dreams, white Aidead,
For on thee all day I brood!”

She came not. He sought her in churchyards old,
In churchyards by the sea;
And in many a church, when the midnight tolled
And the moon shone eerily,
Down to the crypt he crept, grown bold,
Sat all night in the dead men’s cold,
And called to her: never came she.

Praying forgiveness more and more,
And her love at any cost,
Pining and sighing and longing sore
He grew like a creature lost;
Thin and spectral his body wore,
He faded out at the ghostly door,
And was himself a ghost.

===Chinese===

她受了大委屈了，他那可爱的客人！——
一阵狂烈的自我责备，
用一千只羞愧的钩子，
撕扯那临阵退缩的心，
把他高傲的头压上起伏的胸口，
从他古老的冠翎上拔下羽毛，
对他古老的家名嗤之以鼻。

他为意志的沉沦而作呕，
怀着爱与悔恨哭泣；
他伏下去，吻她冰凉的足印，
吻她裙裾扫过的痕迹；
他跪在那把椅子旁，椅子还冰冷，
把头埋进去，呜咽着，
直到倦极睡去。

他一觉睡到烈焰般的太阳
嘲笑昨夜的黑暗：
「一场可怕的梦！——可夜完了，」
他说，「我听见云雀了！」
他撑过了一天；傍晚的炮声一响，
一阵轰鸣的恐怖震懵他的头脑，
于是「疑心」，那头豺，吠了起来。

紧跟着，「确信」，那头狮子，追了上来，
他明白了那不是梦！
一夜又一夜，良心的狂风怒号，
却随晨光渐亮而平息。
七轮慢月来了又去，
他把自责抛开，
那真相便显得不像真的了。

一位美貌的贵女——老套的丑故事！——
要把他的心当她的战利品：
在她日渐加浓的笑靥的魔光里，
他忘了那可爱的鬼：
为了裹着狡诈的苦涩忘了她，
因为那贵女虚伪得像一条鳄鱼，
她的心是一座霜窟。

于是那张苍白、含着神圣悲愁的脸，
在叹息的时辰回来了：
对那些渴慕的人，亲爱的真脸
并不总是带着安慰升起！
他渴念她，梦见她，祈求一个征兆；
他为她的恳求的声音哭，为那
孤寂的眼睛的光辉哭。

「用你这样静的脸，我把它弄得那样悲——
唉，我本可以求爱的脸——
你握着我的心，用一种不欢欣的爱，
悲愁的、被羞愧压服的爱！
到我这里来吧，贵女，披着宽恕；
到我的梦里来，白皙的艾迪德（Aidead），
我整天整天冥想着你！」

她没有来。他去老教堂墓地寻她，
去海边的墓地寻她；
在许多座教堂里，当子夜敲响，
当月光惨惨地照着，
他大着胆子爬下地窖，
在死人的寒冷里坐整夜，
唤她：她从不曾来。

他一遍遍祈求宽恕，
求她的爱，不惜代价，
憔悴、叹息、苦苦想望，
他长得像一头迷失的生灵；
他的身子日渐消瘦成影，
他在那扇鬼门边淡去，
自己也成了鬼。

===Original===

But if he found the lady then,
So sorrowfully lost
For lack of the love ’mong earthly men
That was ready to brave love’s cost,
I know not till I drop my pen,
Wander away from earthly ken,
And am myself a ghost.

===Chinese===

可他后来可曾找到那位贵女——
那样悲苦地流落，
只因尘世的男人中间缺少
那情愿担起爱之代价的爱——
这我不知道，要等我搁下笔，
走出尘世的视野，
自己也成了鬼，才知晓。

## Abu Midjan / 阿布·米德詹
===Original===

“If I sit in the dust
For lauding good wine,
Ha, ha! it is just:
So sits the vine!”

Abu Midjan sang as he sat in chains,
For the blood of the grape ran the juice of his veins.
The Prophet had said, “O Faithful, drink not!”
Abu Midjan drank till his heart was hot;
Yea, he sang a song in praise of wine,
He called it good names﻿—a joy divine,
The giver of might, the opener of eyes,
Love’s handmaid, the water of Paradise!
Therefore Saad his chief spake words of blame,
And set him in irons﻿—a fettered flame;
But he sings of the wine as he sits in his chains,
For the blood of the grape runs the juice of his veins:

“I will not think
That the Prophet said
‘Ye shall not drink
Of the flowing red!’ ”

“ ’Tis a drenched brain
Whose after-sting
Cries out, ‘Refrain:
’Tis an evil thing!’

“But I will dare,
With a goodly drought,
To drink, nor spare
Till my thirst be out.

“I do not laugh
Like a Christian fool
But in silence quaff
The liquor cool

“At door of tent
’Neath evening star,
With daylight spent,
And Uriel afar!

“Then, through the sky,
Lo, the emerald hills!
My faith swells high,
My bosom thrills:

“I see them hearken,
The Houris that wait!
Their dark eyes darken
The diamond gate!

“I hear the float
Of their chant divine,
And my heart like a boat
Sails thither on wine!

“Can an evil thing
Make beauty more?
Or a sinner bring
To the heavenly door?

“The sun-rain fine
Would sink and escape,
But is drunk by the vine,
Is stored in the grape:

“And the prisoned light
I free again:
It flows in might
Through my shining brain

“I love and I know;
The truth is mine;
I walk in the glow
Of the sun-bred wine.

“I will not think
That the Prophet said
‘Ye shall not drink
Of the flowing red!’

“For his promises, lo,
Sevenfold they shine
When the channels o’erflow
With the singing wine!

“But I care not, I!﻿—’tis a small annoy
To sit in chains for a heavenly joy!”

Away went the song on the light wind borne;
His head sank down, and a ripple of scorn
Shook the hair that flowed from his curling lip
As he eyed his brown limbs in the iron’s grip.

===Chinese===

「我若坐在尘土里
赞美美酒，
哈，哈！这正当如仪：
葡萄藤也这样坐着！」

阿布·米德詹戴着镣铐坐着歌唱，
因为葡萄的血，在他的血管里流淌。
先知曾说过：「信士们，不要饮酒！」
阿布·米德詹却喝到心头火热；
是啊，他还唱了一支酒之歌，
给它起了好名字——神圣的欢悦，
力量的赋予者，眼睛的开启者，
爱的侍女，乐园的清水！
因此他的首领萨阿德出言责备，
给他上了铁镣——一束戴着枷的火焰；
可他戴着镣铐坐着，仍旧唱酒，
因为葡萄的血，在他的血管里流淌：

「我不肯相信
先知说过
『你们不可喝
那流动的红色！』」

「那是泡烂的脑子
事后的刺痛
在喊：『住手：
那是邪恶的东西！』

「可我偏要放胆，
畅快地灌，
喝个够，
不解渴不停。

「我不像
基督徒的傻子那样笑，
只默默痛饮
那清凉的酒液

「在帐门口
在晚星下，
白日已尽，
乌列尔远在天涯！

「于是，透过天宇，
看哪，绿玉的山峦！
我的信仰高涨，
我的胸中震颤：

「我看见她们侧耳，
那些守候的天女！
她们深暗的眼睛
把钻石之门映暗！

「我听见飘来
她们神圣的歌，
我的心像一只小船
乘着酒驶向那国！

「邪恶的东西
能添美几分？
罪人能把人
带到天门前？

「细密的太阳雨
本会沉落遁逃，
却被葡萄藤饮下，
被储进葡萄：

「那囚禁的光
由我再度释放：
它携着伟力
流过我发亮的头脑

「我又爱又知；
真理归我；
我走在
太阳所酿之酒的光焰里。

「我不肯相信
先知说过
『你们不可喝
那流动的红色！』

「因为看哪，他的应许，
七倍地生辉，
当酒的歌涌
漫过每一道渠！

「可我不在乎，我！——这点小烦扰，
换天国的欢悦，坐坐镣铐算什么！」

歌声乘着轻风远去；
他的头垂下来，一丝轻蔑的涟漪
摇动他从卷曲唇边飘下的须发，
他望着自己棕色的肢体在铁镣的掌握中。

===Original===

Sudden his forehead he lifted high:
A faint sound strayed like a moth-wing by!
Like beacons his eyes burst blazing forth:
A dust-cloud he spied in the distant north!
A noise and a smoke on the plain afar?
’Tis the cloud and the clang of the Muslim war!
He leapt aloft like a tiger snared;
The wine in his veins through his visage flared;
He tore at his fetters in bootless ire,
He called the Prophet, he named his sire;
From his lips, with wild shout, the Tecbir burst;
He danced in his irons; the Giaours he cursed;
And his eyes they flamed like a beacon dun,
Or like wine in the crystal twixt eye and sun.

The lady of Saad heard him shout,
Heard his fetters ring on the stones about
The heart of a warrior she understood,
And the rage of the thwarted battle-mood:
Her name, with the cry of an angry prayer,
He called but once, and the lady was there.

“The Giaour!” he panted, “the Godless brute!
And me like a camel tied foot to foot!
Let me go, and I swear by Allah’s fear
At sunset I don again this gear,
Or lie in a heaven of starry eyes,
Kissed by moon-maidens of Paradise!
O lady, grant me the death of the just!
Hark to the hurtle! see the dust!”

With ready fingers the noble dame
Unlocked her husband’s iron blame;
Brought his second horse, his Abdon, out,
And his second hauberk, light and stout;
Harnessed the warrior, and hight him go
An angel of vengeance upon the foe.

With clank of steel and thud of hoof
Away he galloped; she climbed the roof.

She sees the cloud and the flashes that leap
From the scythe-shaped swords inside it that sweep
Down with back-stroke the disordered swath:
Thither he speeds, a bolt of wrath!
Straight as an arrow she sees him go,
Abu Midjan, the singer, upon the foe!
Like an eagle he vanishes in the cloud,
And the thunder of battle bursts more loud,
Mingled of crashes and blows and falls,
Of the whish that severs the throat that calls,
Of neighing and shouting and groaning grim:
Abu Midjan, she sees no more of him!
Northward the battle drifts afar
On the flowing tide of the holy war.

Lonely across the desert sand,
From his wrist by its thong hung his clotted brand,
Red in the sunset’s level flame
Back to his bonds Abu Midjan came.

===Chinese===

忽然他高高扬起额头：
一声细响像蛾翅掠过！
他的双眼像烽火一样迸出光来：
他望见北天远处一团尘霾！
平原上远处一声轰响一片烟？
那是穆斯林战云与铿锵的兵戈！
他像落网的老虎一跃而起；
血管里的酒烧红了他的脸；
他徒然狂怒地撕扯镣铐，
他呼唤先知，他念出父亲的名字；
一声「特克比尔」（Tecbir，真主至大）的狂呼冲出唇间；
他戴着铁镣起舞；他咒诅那些异教徒；
他的双眼燃烧，像暗色的烽燧，
又像隔着眼睛与太阳的水晶里的酒。

萨阿德的夫人听见了他的呐喊，
听见他的铁镣在石上铿然作响——
她懂得一颗武士的心，
懂得被拦阻的战心的狂怒：
她的名字，他只带着一声怒祷唤了一遍，
夫人便已来到。

「异教徒！」他喘着说，「无法无天的畜生！
而我却像骆驼，四脚拴着四脚！
放我走，我以对安拉的敬畏起誓：
日落时我再戴上这身刑具，
不然就躺在满天星眼的天堂，
受乐园月女的亲吻！
哦夫人，赐我一个义人之死！
听那喊杀！看那尘烟！」

高贵夫人的手指敏捷利落，
开了她丈夫那铁的责罚；
牵出他的第二匹战马，他的阿布东（Abdon），
又取出他的第二副锁子甲，轻而坚固；
替武士披挂齐整，命他去吧，
做一位复仇的天使，扑向敌仇。

钢铿马蹄沉，他飞驰而去；她登上屋顶。

她望见那云、那闪闪烁烁的光，
是镰形的弯刀在里面挥荡，
反手扫倒紊乱的稻茬：
他向那边疾驰，一道愤怒的霹雳！
笔直如箭，她望见他冲去，
阿布·米德詹，那歌者，扑向敌阵！
像一头鹰，他没入战云，
战事的雷霆轰得更响，
夹着砍击、扑落与倒下，
夹着切断呼喊的咽喉的嗖嗖，
夹着嘶鸣、呐喊与沉沉的呻吟：
阿布·米德詹，她再没有看见他！
战斗朝北漂远，
顺着圣战的洪流。

孤单单越过荒漠的沙，
凝住的剑由皮带悬在腕下，
浴着落日平射的火焰，
阿布·米德詹回到他的锁镣之下。

===Original===

“Lady, I swear your Saad’s horse﻿—
The Prophet himself might have rode a worse!
Like the knots of a serpent the play of his flesh
As he tore to the quarry in Allah’s mesh!
I forgot him, and mowed at the traitor weeds,
Which fell before me like rushes and reeds,
Or like the tall poppies that sudden drop low
Their heads to an urchin’s unstrung bow!
Fled the Giaour; the faithful flew after to kill;
I turned to surrender: beneath me still
Was Abdon unjaded, fresh in force,
Faithful and fearless﻿—a heavenly horse!
Give him water, lady, and barley to eat;
Then haste thee and fetter the wine-bibber’s feet.”

To the terrace he went, and she to the stall;
She tended the horse like guest in hall,
Then to the warrior unhasting returned.
The fire of the fight in his eyes yet burned,
But he sat in a silence that might betoken
One ashamed that his heart had spoken﻿—
Though where was the word to breed remorse?
He had lauded only his chief’s brave horse!
Not a word she spoke, but his fetters locked;
He watched with a smile that himself bemocked;
She left him seated in caitiff-plight,
Like one that had feared and fled the fight.

But what singer ever sat lonely long
Ere the hidden fountain burst in song!
The battle wine foamed in the warrior’s veins,
And he sang sword-tempest who sat in chains.

“Oh, the wine
Of the vine
Is a feeble thing!
In the rattle
Of battle
The true grapes spring!

“When on whir
Of Tecbir
Allah’s wrath flies,
And the power
Of the Giaour
A blasted leaf lies!

“When on force
Of the horse
The arm flung abroad
Is sweeping,
And reaping
The harvest of God!

“Ha! they drop
From the top
To the sear heap below!
Ha! deeper,
Down steeper,
The infidels go!

“Azrael
Sheer to hell
Shoots the foul shoals!
There Monker
And Nakir
Torture their souls!

“But when drop
On their crop
The scimitars red,
And under
War’s thunder
The faithful lie dead,

“Oh, bright
Is the light
On hero slow breaking!
Rapturous faces
Bent for embraces
Watch for his waking!

“And he hears
In his ears
The voice of Life’s river,
Like a song
Of the strong,
Jubilant ever!

“Oh, the wine
Of the vine
May lead to the gates,
But the rattle
Of battle
Wakes the angel who waits!

“To the lord
Of the sword
Open it must!
The drinker,
The thinker
Sits in the dust!

“He dreams
Of the gleams
Of their garments of white;
He misses
Their kisses,
The maidens of light!

===Chinese===

「夫人，我向您起誓，您萨阿德的马——
先知本人骑过更差的也不算差！
它肌肉的收放像蛇结一样，
冲向安拉网里的猎物那样！
我忘了它，只顾收割叛乱的莠草，
它们在我面前倒下，像灯心草和芦苇，
又像高高的罂粟，忽然垂首
向顽童松弛的弓！异教徒逃了；
信士们追杀过去；我拨马归来：
胯下的阿布东仍未倦怠，气力犹酣，
忠心而无畏——一匹天国的马！
给它水喝，夫人，给它大麦吃；
然后请您快些，把酒徒的双脚锁上。」

他上露台去了，她进马厩；
她把那马当厅上宾客一样照看，
然后从容不迫回到武士跟前。
战斗的火仍在他的眼里烧，
可他坐在一片静默里，那静默
也许意味着：人为敞开了心而羞惭——
虽说哪一句话值得悔恨？
他夸的不过是主帅的骏马！
她一言不发，只把他的镣铐扣紧；
他含着自嘲的笑望着；
她留下他坐在囚徒的窘态里，
像一个临阵脱逃、畏惧战斗的人。

可哪个歌者会久久独坐，
不叫藏着的泉迸出歌来！
战斗的酒在武士的血管里翻涌，
他戴着镣铐坐着，唱起刀剑的风暴。

「哦，葡萄
酿的酒
是软弱的东西！
在鏖战的
铿锵里
真正的葡萄才涌起！

「当『真主至大』
的呼啸里
安拉的怒火飞起，
异教徒的
威势
便像一片焦叶委地！

「当借着
战马的
冲力，挥出的臂膀
横扫，
收割
上帝的庄稼！

「哈！他们从
顶上
跌进底下的枯堆！
哈！更深，
更陡，
异教徒们下坠！

「亚兹拉尔
径直把
污浊的一群射进地狱！
孟凯尔
和奈基尔
在那里折磨他们的魂！

「可当血红
的弯刀
落到他们的头顶，
信士们
在战的
雷霆下献身，

「哦，明亮
是那光，
照着缓缓倒下的英雄！
狂喜的脸
俯身待拥，
守着他的苏醒！

「他听见
耳中
生命之河的声息，
像一支
强者
永远欢腾的歌！

「哦，葡萄
酿的酒
或能引到门前，
可鏖战的
铿锵
才唤醒守候的天仙！

「唯有剑
之主
才必得进去！
饮酒的，
空想的
只坐在尘土里！

「他梦见
那闪动
的白衣的微光；
他错过
她们的吻——
那些光中的姑娘！

===Original===

“They long
For the strong
Who has burst through alarms﻿—
Up, by the labour
Of stirrup and sabre,
Up to their arms!

“Oh, the wine of the grape is a feeble ghost!
The wine of the fight is the joy of a host!”

When Saad came home from the far pursuit,
An hour he sat, and an hour was mute.
Then he opened his mouth: “Ah, wife, the fight
Had been lost full sure, but an arm of might
Sudden rose up on the crest of the battle,
Flashed blue lightnings, thundered steel rattle,
Took up the fighting, and drove it on﻿—
Enoch sure, or the good Saint John!
Wherever he leaped, like a lion he,
The battle was thickest, or soon to be!
Wherever he sprang with his lion roar,
In a minute the battle was there no more!
With a headlong fear, the sinners fled,
And we swept them down the steep of the dead:
Before us, not from us, did they flee,
They ceased in the depths of a new Red Sea!
But him who saved us we saw no more;
He went as he came, by a secret door!
And strangest of all﻿—nor think I err
If a miracle I for truth aver﻿—
I was close to him thrice﻿—the holy Force
Wore my silver-ringed hauberk, rode Abdon my horse!”

The lady rose up, withholding her word,
And led to the terrace her wondering lord,
Where, song-soothed, and weary with battle strain,
Abu Midjan sat counting the links of his chain:
“The battle was raging, he raging worse;
I freed him, harnessed him, gave him thy horse.”

“Abu Midjan! the singer of love and of wine!
The arm of the battle, it also was thine?
Rise up, shake the irons from off thy feet:
For the lord of the fight are fetters meet?
If thou wilt, then drink till thou be hoar:
Allah shall judge thee; I judge no more!”

Abu Midjan arose; he flung aside
The clanking fetters, and thus he cried:
“If thou give me to God and his decrees,
Nor purge my sin with the shame of these,
Wrath against me I dare not store:
In the name of Allah, I drink no more!”

===Chinese===

「她们渴盼
那冲破了
重重警讯的强者——
起来吧，凭马镫
与弯刀的辛劳，
起来，投进她们的怀抱！

「哦，葡萄的酒是一个虚弱的鬼！
战斗的酒才是全军的欢喜！」

萨阿德从远追中归家，
坐了一个时辰，哑了一个时辰。
随后他开口：「啊，夫人，那一仗
本是必输，可一条神勇的手臂
蓦地在战阵的浪尖上升起，
闪着蓝电，轰着铁雷，
接过战事，一路推击——
准是以诺，要不就是善的圣约翰！
他跳到哪里，像狮子一样，
哪里的战斗就最烈，或将要最烈！
他带着狮吼纵身跃到哪里，
哪里的战斗一分钟内就平息！
罪人们抱头鼠窜，
被我们扫下死亡的高坡：
他们逃在我们前，不是离我们远，
结果沉进一片新的红海！
可救了我们的那人，我们再没看见；
他来去都走的一扇秘门！
最奇的还有——我想我没说错，
我可以指天为誓说这是奇迹——
我三次贴近他——那股神力
穿的正是我银环的锁子甲，骑的是我的阿布东！」

夫人站起身，按住了话头，
领着满心诧异的主上走向露台；
那里，被歌声抚平、倦于战事的，
阿布·米德詹坐着，数着链环：
「战斗正酣，他比战斗更酣；
我放了他，给他披挂，把你的马借他一乘。」

「阿布·米德詹！爱与酒的歌者！
原来战场上的那条手臂，也是你的？
起来吧，甩掉你脚上的铁镣：
战斗之主，岂配得上镣铐相加？
你若愿意，就喝到白头：
安拉会审判你；我不再审判！」

阿布·米德詹站起身；他把
铿锵的镣铐甩在一旁，这样呼喊：
「你既把我交给安拉和他的裁断，
不再用这羞辱来涤我的罪愆，
我不敢再对你怀藏怨怒：
奉安拉的名，我从此滴酒不沾！」

## An Old Story / 一则古老的故事
===Original===

I

In the ancient house of ages,
See, they cannot rest!
With a hope, which awe assuages,
Tremble all the blest.
For the son and heir eternal,
To be son yet more,
Leaves his stately chair supernal
For the earth’s low floor;

Leaves the room so high and old,
Leaves the all-world hearth,
Seeks the out-air, frosty-cold,
Of the twilight earth﻿—
To be throned in newer glory
In a mother’s lap,
Gather up our broken story,
And right every hap.

II

There Earth’s foster-baby lies,
Sleep-dimmed all his graces,
’Neath four stars of parents’ eyes,
And two heavens of faces!
See! the cow and ass, dumb-staring,
Feel the skirts of good
Fold them in dull-blessed sharing
Of infinitude.

Make a little room betwixt you,
Pray you, Ass and Cow!
Sure we shall, if I kneel next you,
Know each other now!
To the pit-fallen comes salvation﻿—
Love is never loath!
Here we are, thy whole creation,
Waiting, Lord, thy growth!

III

On the slopes of Bethlehem,
Round their resting sheep,
Shepherds sat, and went and came,
Guarding holy sleep;
But the silent, high dome-spaces,
Airy galleries,
Thronged they were with watching faces,
Thronged with open eyes.

Far across the desert floor,
Come, slow-drawing nigher,
Sages deep in starry lore,
Priests of burning Fire.
In the sky they read his story,
And, through starlight cool,
They come riding to the Glory,
To the Wonderful.

IV

Babe and mother, coming Mage,
Shepherd, ass, and cow!
Angels watching the new age,
Time’s intensest Now!
Heaven down-brooding, Earth upstraining,
Far ends closing in!
Sure the eternal tide is gaining
On the strand of sin!

See! but see! Heaven’s chapel-master
Signs with lifted hand;
Winds divine blow fast and faster,
Swelling bosoms grand.
Hark the torrent-joy let slip!
Hark the great throats ring!
Glory! Peace! Good-fellowship!
And a Child for king!

===Chinese===

I

在那历代的古老宅子里，
看哪，他们安不下心！
怀着被敬畏抚慰的希望，
众有福者都在战栗。
因为那永恒的儿子与嗣子，
为了更是儿子，
离了祂崇高的天上宝座，
路下尘世的低地；

离了那高而古老的殿堂，
离了那全世界的炉床，
去寻暮色大地那
霜寒的户外——
为要在新的荣光里登基，
登在一位母亲的膝上，
把我们破碎的故事收拾完整，
把每一桩遗际归正。

II

那里，大地的养婴躺着，
睡意朦胧了他一切的荣美，
头顶四颗星的父母之眼，
和两片天堂似的脸！
看哪！牛和驴，默然凝望，
觉出善的衣裙
把它们也裹进迟钝有福的
共享无穷里。

请你们中间腾出一点地方，
求求你，驴和牛！
倘若我就跪在你们身边，
咱们准能从此相识！
救恩临到陷在坑里的——
爱从不迟疑！
主啊，你整个的造物都在这里，
等候着你的长大！

III

在伯利恒的山坡上，
羊群安睡的四周，
牧人们坐着，走来走去，
守护圣洁的睡眠；
而那寂静高朗的穹苍，
那空灵的长廊里，
却挤满了守望的脸，
挤满了睁开的眼睛。

远远越过荒漠，
来啦，缓缓地临近，
深通星象的贤士，
拜火的祭司。
他们在天空中读出祂的故事，
于是穿过清凉的星光，
策马来朝那荣光，
来朝那奇妙者。

IV

婴儿与母亲，来袭的博士，
牧人、驴与牛！
天使守望着新纪元，
时间最炽烈的「此刻」！
天堂低伏，大地高仰，
两极正在合拢！
永恒的潮水定然正涨，
漫上罪的沙洲！

看哪！只管看！天堂的领乐师
扬手起了拍；
神圣的风越吹越急，
鼓起庄严的胸襟。
听那放闸的洪流般的欢喜！
听那洪大的喉咙齐鸣！
荣光！平安！亲睦！
一个婴孩，为王！

## A Book of Dreams / 梦之书
===Original===

Part
I

I

I lay and dreamed. The Master came,
In seamless garment drest;
I stood in bonds ’twixt love and shame,
Not ready to be blest.

He stretched his arms, and gently sought
To clasp me to his heart;
I shrank, for I, unthinking, thought
He knew me but in part.

I did not love him as I would!
Embraces were not meet!
I dared not ev’n stand where he stood﻿—
I fell and kissed his feet.

Years, years have passed away since then;
Oft hast thou come to me;
The question scarce will rise again
Whether I care for thee.

In thee lies hid my unknown heart,
In thee my perfect mind;
In all my joys, my Lord, thou art
The deeper joy behind.

But when fresh light and visions bold
My heart and hope expand,
Up comes the vanity of old
That now I understand:

Away, away from thee I drift,
Forgetting, not forgot;
Till sudden yawns a downward rift﻿—
I start﻿—and see thee not.

Ah, then come sad, unhopeful hours!
All in the dark I stray,
Until my spirit fainting cowers
On the threshold of the day.

Hence not even yet I child-like dare
Nestle unto thy breast,
Though well I know that only there
Lies hid the secret rest.

But now I shrink not from thy will,
Nor, guilty, judge my guilt;
Thy good shall meet and slay my ill﻿—
Do with me as thou wilt.

If I should dream that dream once more,
Me in my dreaming meet;
Embrace me, Master, I implore,
And let me kiss thy feet.

II

I stood before my childhood’s home,
Outside its belt of trees;
All round my glances flit and roam
O’er well-known hills and leas;

When sudden rushed across the plain
A host of hurrying waves,
Loosed by some witchery of the brain
From far, dream-hidden caves.

And up the hill they clomb and came,
A wild, fast-flowing sea:
Careless I looked as on a game;
No terror woke in me.

For, just the belting trees within,
I saw my father wait;
And should the waves the summit win,
There was the open gate!

With him beside, all doubt was dumb;
There let the waters foam!
No mightiest flood would dare to come
And drown his holy home!

Two days passed by. With restless toss,
The red flood brake its doors;
Prostrate I lay, and looked across
To the eternal shores.

The world was fair, and hope was high;
My friends had all been true;
Life burned in me, and Death and I
Would have a hard ado.

Sudden came back the dream so good,
My trouble to abate:
At his own door my Father stood﻿—
I just without the gate!

===Chinese===

第一部
I

我躺着，做了个梦。主来了，
穿着无缝的衣袍；
我立在爱与羞的捆绑之间，
还没预备好受福。

祂张开双臂，温柔地想要
把我搂进祂的胸怀；
我退缩了，因为我不假思索地以为
祂认识我只是部分。

我爱祂爱得不够！
拥抱于我并不相宜！
我甚至不敢站在祂站的地方——
我俯伏下去，吻了祂的脚。

自那以后，年复一年过去；
你屡屡来到我这里；
「我是否在乎你」这个问题
几乎不会再起了。

我未识的心藏在你里面，
我完全的心智在你里面；
主啊，在我一切的欢喜里，你都是
那背后更深的欢喜。

可每当新的光与大胆的异象
扩张我的心与盼望，
从前那点虚荣便浮上来——
如今我算认清了它：

我便离了你，漂开去，
忘了你，却不曾被你忘；
直到脚下忽然裂开一道下坡——
我一惊——看不见了你。

啊，那时便来了悲哀的、无望的时辰！
我在黑暗里四处彷徨，
直到我衰疲的魂蜷缩下去，
蜷在白昼的门槛上。

因此，即便如今，我也不敢孩子气地
偎进你的胸怀，
虽则我深知，唯有那里
藏着那隐秘的安息。

但现在我不再从你的旨意退缩，
也不负疚地审判我的罪；
你的善必迎上来杀死我的恶——
你要怎样待我，就怎样待我。

倘若我再做那个梦，
请到我梦里来会见我；
拥抱我吧，主，我恳求，
容我吻你的脚。

II

我立在我童年的家门前，
在它那圈树墙之外；
我的目光四处飞掠、游走，
掠过熟识的丘陵与草场；

忽然，平原上奔涌而过
一大群匆匆的波涛，
被头脑里某种魔法
从远方藏梦的洞窟里放出。

它们爬上山坡，涌了上来，
一片狂野奔流的海：
我无所畏惧地看着，像看一场游戏；
我心里没有醒来恐怖。

因为，就在那圈树墙之内，
我看见我的父亲候着；
纵使波涛攻上山巅，
那里也有一扇敞开的门！

有他在旁，一切疑虑喑哑了；
任凭水流去翻沫！
最强的洪峰也绝不敢来
淹没他圣洁的家！

两天过去。红潮辗转翻腾，
撞破了它的门；
我俯伏在地，望向
那永恒的彼岸。

世界美好，盼望高扬；
我的朋友个个真诚；
生命在我里面燃烧，死亡同我
必有一场恶战。

那个好梦忽然回来了，
平息我的愁烦：
我父站在自家的门口——
我只在门外一栏之隔！

===Original===

“Thou know’st what is, and what appears,”
I said; “mine eyes to thine
Are windows; thou hear’st with thine ears,
But also hear’st with mine:”

“Thou knowest my weak soul’s dismay,
How trembles my life’s node;
Thou art the potter, I am the clay﻿—
’Tis thine to bear the load.”

III

A piece of gold had left my purse,
Which I had guarded ill;
I feared a lack, but feared yet worse
Regret returning still.

I lifted up my feeble prayer
To him who maketh strong,
That thence no haunting thoughts of care
Might do my spirit wrong.

And even before my body slept,
Such visions fair I had,
That seldom soul with chamber swept
Was more serenely glad.

No white-robed angel floated by
On slow, reposing wings;
I only saw, with inward eye,
Some very common things.

First rose the scarlet pimpernel
With burning purple heart;
I saw within it, and could spell
The lesson of its art.

Then came the primrose, child-like flower,
And looked me in the face;
It bore a message full of power,
And confidence, and grace.

And breezes rose on pastures trim
And bathed me all about;
Wool-muffled sheep-bells babbled dim,
Or only half spoke out.

Sudden it closed, some door of heaven,
But what came out remained:
The poorest man my loss had given
For that which I had gained!

Thou gav’st me, Lord, a brimming cup
Where I bemoaned a sip;
How easily thou didst make up
For that my fault let slip!

What said the flowers? what message new
Embalmed my soul with rest?
I scarce can tell﻿—only they grew
Right out of God’s own breast.

They said, to every flower he made
God’s thought was root and stem﻿—
Perhaps said what the lilies said
When Jesus looked at them.

IV

Sometimes, in daylight hours, awake,
Our souls with visions teem
Which to the slumbering brain would take
The form of wondrous dream.

Once, with my thought-sight, I descried
A plain with hills around;
A lordly company on each side
Leaves bare the middle ground.

Great terrace-steps at one end rise
To something like a throne,
And thither all the radiant eyes,
As to a centre, shone.

A snow-white glory, dim-defined,
Those seeking eyes beseech﻿—
Him who was not in fire or wind,
But in the gentle speech.

They see his eyes far-fixed wait:
Adown the widening vale
They, turning, look; their breath they bate,
With dread-filled wonder pale.

===Chinese===

「你知道什么是实情、什么是表象，」
我说；「我的眼睛之于你的眼睛
不过是窗；你用你的耳朵听，
却也用我的耳朵听见：

「你知道我软弱之魂的惶乱，
知道我生命的结点怎样颤抖；
你是陶匠，我是泥土——
该由你来担这重负。」

III

一块金币离开了我的钱袋，
都怪我保管不慎；
我怕短缺，可更怕
那悔恨一次次回头。

我向那使软弱者刚强的祂，
举起我微弱的祷告，
求从此别让缠人的忧虑之念
亏待我的灵魂。

还没等我的身体睡去，
我就见了那样美的异象，
很少有一颗打扫过的魂灵
比它更加安然地欢喜。

没有白衣的天使
驾着徐缓的翅缓缓飘过；
我只用内里的眼睛看见
几件顶平常的东西。

先是那猩红的殷勤花升起来，
带着燃烧的紫心；
我望进它里面，读得出
它那门手艺的功课。

随后来了报春花，孩子气的花，
正眼望着我；
它带着一个满有权能的消息，
还有笃定，还有恩慈。

牧场上又起了微风，
把我四面沐浴；
毛裹的羊铃含混地絮语，
或者只说出一半。

天上一扇门忽然关了，
可出来的留了下来：
我那点损失，已把最穷的人
换得了我所获的一切！

主啊，你给了我满满一杯，
我只哀叹了一小口；
我那一时疏失漏掉的，
你多么轻易就补足！

花说了什么？什么新的消息
用安息膏了我的魂？
我几乎说不上——只知道它们
径直从上帝自己的胸中长出。

它们说，祂造的每一朵花，
上帝的念头便是根与茎——
兴许说的，正是百合花当年
在耶稣注视下所说的。

IV

有时，在白昼醒着的时辰，
我们的魂里也挤满异象，
落到沉睡的头脑里便会
化成奇妙的梦。

有一回，我用思想的眼望见
一片四围是山的平原；
两侧各立着一列尊贵的会众，
让中央空出一片空场。

一端升起几级大露台，
通向一座宝座似的所在，
所有光辉的眼睛都朝那里，
如朝着圆心，发光。

一片雪白的荣光，轮廓朦胧，
那些寻索的眼睛在恳求——
那位不在火中、也不在风中的，
而在温柔的言语之中。

他们看见祂的眼睛远远凝候；
顺着那渐渐展宽的山谷，
他们转过身去望；他们屏住呼吸，
吓得发白，又满心惊奇。

===Original===

In raiment worn and blood-bedewed,
With faltering step and numb,
Toward the shining multitude
A weary man did come.

His face was white, and still-composed,
As of a man nigh dead;
The eyes, through eyelids half unclosed,
A faint, wan splendour shed.

Drops on his hair disordered hung
Like rubies dull of hue;
His hands were pitifully wrung,
And stricken through and through.

Silent they stood with tender awe:
Between their ranks he came;
Their tearful eyes looked down, and saw
What made his feet so lame.

He reached the steps below the throne,
There sank upon his knees;
Clasped his torn hands with stifled groan,
And spake in words like these:﻿—

“Father, I am come back. Thy will
Is sometimes hard to do.”
From all that multitude so still
A sound of weeping grew.

Then mournful-glad came down the One;
He kneeled and clasped his child;
Lay on his breast the outworn man,
And wept until he smiled.

The people, who, in bitter woe
And love, had sobbed and cried,
Raised aweful eyes at length﻿—and, Lo,
The two sat side by side!

V

Dreaming I slept. Three crosses stood
High in the gloomy air;
One bore a thief, and one the Good;
The other waited bare.

A soldier came up to the place,
And took me for the third;
My eyes they sought the Master’s face,
My will the Master’s word.

He bent his head; I took the sign,
And gave the error way;
Gesture nor look nor word of mine
The secret should betray.

The soldier from the cross’s foot
Turned. I stood waiting there:
That grim, expectant tree, for fruit
My dying form must bear.

Up rose the steaming mists of doubt
And chilled both heart and brain;
They shut the world of vision out,
And fear saw only pain.

“Ah me, my hands! the hammer’s blow!
The nails that rend and pierce!
The shock may stun, but, slow and slow,
The torture will grow fierce.”

“Alas, the awful fight with death!
The hours to hang and die!
The thirsting gasp for common breath!
The weakness that would cry!”

My soul returned: “A faintness soon
Will shroud thee in its fold;
The hours will bring the fearful noon;
’Twill pass﻿—and thou art cold.”

“ ’Tis his to care that thou endure,
To curb or loose the pain;
With bleeding hands hang on thy cure﻿—
It shall not be in vain.”

But, ah, the will, which thus could quail,
Might yield﻿—oh, horror drear!
Then, more than love, the fear to fail
Kept down the other fear.

===Chinese===

一个衣衫褴褛、血浸汗濡的人，
迈着踉跄麻木的步子，
朝着那光辉的会众
一路疲惫地走来。

他的脸苍白、静定，
像濒死之人的脸；
那双半阖的眼睑后的眼睛，
散着一脉微弱的清光。

发间凌乱地悬着水珠，
像色泽暗沉的红宝石；
他的双手可怜地绞扭着，
处处是扎穿的伤。

他们默然立着，怀着温柔的敬畏：
他从他们的行列间走来；
他们含泪的眼睛朝下望，看见了
是什么把他的脚磨成这样跛。

他走到宝座下的台阶前，
跪了下去；
绞着撕裂的双手，憋住一声呻吟，
说了这样几句：——

「父啊，我回来了。你的旨意
有时很难遵行。」
那全然寂静的会众里，
渐渐响起一片哭泣。

随后，那一位哀而含喜地下来；
祂跪下，抱住祂的孩子；
那耗竭的人躺在他胸膛上，
哭到后来笑了。

众人方才在苦痛
与爱里呜咽哭喊，此刻终于
仰起敬畏的眼睛——看哪，
那两个并肩坐着！

V

我睡中做梦。三座十字架
高高立在阴郁的空中；
一座钉着一个贼，一座钉着那善者；
另一座空着等候。

一个士兵走到那地方，
把我抓去充作第三人；
我的眼睛寻求主的脸，
我的意志寻求主的言语。

祂垂下了头；我便受了这记号，
顺从了这差遣；
我的手势、眼神、言语，
都不曾泄露那个秘密。

士兵从十字架脚下
转身。我立在那里等候：
那株狰狞的、有所期待的树，
必须以我垂死的身形结果。

疑虑蒸腾的雾气升起来，
冻僵了心，也冻僵了头脑；
它们把异象的世界关在外面，
恐惧只看得见苦痛。

「唉，我的手！那锤子的击打！
那撕开、扎穿的长钉！
那震荡或可打懵，可是慢慢地、慢慢地，
酷刑会越熬越凶。」

「可怕啊，同死亡的这场搏斗！
悬着的这几个时辰！
对一口寻常呼吸的渴喘！
那忍不住要哭喊的软弱！」

我的魂答话：「一阵昏沉
很快会把你裹进它的褶里；
时辰会带来那可怕的正午；
它会过去——那时你就冷了。」

「撑住你受苦的，是祂的事；
收紧或松开那疼痛，也在祂；
用你流血的手抓紧你的救治——
这不会是枉然。」

可是啊，这样还会发颤的意志，
也可能屈服——哦，凄厉的恐怖！
于是，比对失败的恐惧——比爱更强——
压住了那另一种恐惧。

===Original===

I stood, nor moved. But inward strife
The bonds of slumber broke:
Oh! had I fled, and lost the life
Of which the Master spoke?

VI

Methinks I hear, as o’er this life’s dim dial
The last shades darken, friends say, “He was good;”
I struggling fail to speak my faint denial﻿—
They whisper, “His humility withstood.”

I, knowing better, part with love unspoken;
And find the unknown world not all unknown:
The bonds that held me from my centre broken,
I seek my home, the Saviour’s homely throne.

How he will greet me, walking on, I wonder;
I think I know what I will say to him;
I fear no sapphire floor of cloudless thunder,
I fear no passing vision great and dim.

But he knows all my weary sinful story:
How will he judge me, pure, and strong, and fair?
I come to him in all his conquered glory,
Won from the life that I went dreaming there!

I come; I fall before him, faintly saying:
“Ah, Lord, shall I thy loving pardon win?
Earth tempted me; my walk was but a straying;
I have no honour﻿—but may I come in?”

I hear him say: “Strong prayer did keep me stable;
To me the earth was very lovely too:
Thou shouldst have prayed; I would have made thee able
To love it greatly!﻿—but thou hast got through.”

Part
II

I

A gloomy and a windy day!
No sunny spot is bare;
Dull vapours, in uncomely play,
Go weltering through the air:
If through the windows of my mind
I let them come and go,
My thoughts will also in the wind
Sweep restless to and fro.

I drop my curtains for a dream.﻿—
What comes? A mighty swan,
With plumage like a sunny gleam,
And folded airy van!
She comes, from sea-plains dreaming, sent
By sea-maids to my shore,
With stately head proud-humbly bent,
And slackening swarthy oar.

Lone in a vaulted rock I lie,
A water-hollowed cell,
Where echoes of old storms go by,
Like murmurs in a shell.
The waters half the gloomy way
Beneath its arches come;
Throbbing to outside billowy play,
The green gulfs waver dumb.

Undawning twilights through the cave
In moony glimmers go,
Half from the swan above the wave,
Half from the swan below,
As to my feet she gently drifts
Through dim, wet-shiny things,
And, with neck low-curved backward, lifts
The shoulders of her wings.

===Chinese===

我立着，一动不动。可内里的争斗
挣破了睡眠的束缚：
哦！我若逃走了，岂不就失掉了
主所说到的那种生命？

VI

我想我听见，当此生的昏表上
最后几道影暗下去，朋友们说：「他是好的；」
我挣扎着，说不出微弱的否认——
他们低语：「是他的谦逊不肯认。」

我知道底细，便无言地怀着爱别过；
却发现那未知的世界并非全然未知：
那把我从中心拴开的绳索断了，
我寻我的家，救主那家常的宝座。

祂将怎样迎我，我一路猜想；
我想我知道自己要对祂说什么；
我不怕那蓝宝石的、无云之雷的地板，
我不怕那伟大而朦胧的过眼异象。

可祂知道我全部疲惫的罪史：
祂那么纯、那么强、那么美，将怎样审我？
我朝着祂、带着祂全然得胜的荣光而来，
那荣光，正是从我在那边梦过的生命里赢得！

我来了；我伏倒在祂面前，轻声说：
「啊，主，我能赢得你慈爱的赦免吗？
尘世引诱了我；我的行走不过是一次迷途；
我没有荣耀——可我能进来吗？」

我听见祂说：「刚强的祷告曾使我站稳；
在我看，尘世也实在可爱：
你本该祷告；我本会使你能够
大大地爱它！——可你也总算走过来了。」

第二部
I

一个阴沉刮风的日子！
没有一块向阳的空地；
沉闷的水汽，不成体统地嬉闹，
在空气里滚滚翻腾：
我若让它们从我心的窗户里
进出往来，
我的念头也会随着风
不安地扫来扫去。

我放下帐幔，做个梦。——
来了什么？一只巨大的天鹅，
羽衣像一线阳光，
叠着轻盈的翅！

她来了，从做着梦的海原被遣来，
由海女送到我的岸，
雍容的头颅傲而谦地低垂，
乌黑的桨渐渐放缓。

我独自躺在一座穹隆的岩洞里，
一间被水凿空的斗室，
旧日风暴的回声从那里过，
像贝壳里的低语。

水从幽暗的拱下
漫进来，占了一半路；
应和着外面波涛的戏耍，
绿色的深湾无声地摇漾。

不亮的微明穿过洞窟，
带月色似的微芒，
一半来自浪上的天鹅，
一半来自水下的天鹅，
她朝我的脚边轻轻漂来，
穿过湿而发亮的朦胧之物，
脖颈低低地向后弯起，
托起她双翼的肩。

===Original===

Old earth is rich with many a nest
Of softness ever new,
Deep, delicate, and full of rest﻿—
But loveliest there are two:
I may not tell them save to minds
That are as white as they;
But none will hear, of other kinds﻿—
They all are turned away.

On foamy mounds between the wings
Of a white sailing swan,
A flaky bed of shelterings,
There you will find the one.
The other﻿—well, it will not out,
Nor need I tell it you;
I’ve told you one, and can you doubt,
When there are only two?

Fill full my dream, O splendid bird!
Me o’er the waters bear:
Never was tranquil ocean stirred
By ship so shapely fair!
Nor ever whiteness found a dress
In which on earth to go,
So true, profound, and rich, unless
It was the falling snow!

Her wings, with flutter half-aloft,
Impatient fan her crown;
I cannot choose but nestle soft
Into the depth of down.
With oary-pulsing webs unseen,
Out the white frigate sweeps;
In middle space we hang, between
The air- and ocean-deeps.

Up the wave’s mounting, flowing side,
With stroke on stroke we rack;
As down the sinking slope we slide,
She cleaves a talking track﻿—
Like heather-bells on lonely steep,
Like soft rain on the glass,
Like children murmuring in their sleep,
Like winds in reedy grass.

Her white breast heaving like a wave,
She beats the solemn time;
With slow strong sweep, intent and grave,
Hearkens the ripples rime.
All round, from flat gloom upward drawn,
I catch the gleam, vague, wide,
With which the waves, from dark to dawn,
Heave up the polished side.

The night is blue; the stars aglow
Crowd the still, vaulted steep,
Sad o’er the hopeless, restless flow
Of the self-murmurous deep﻿—
A thicker night, with gathered moan!
A dull dethroned sky!
The shadows of its stars alone
Left in to know it by!

What faints across yon lifted loop
Where the west gleams its last?
With sea-veiled limbs, a sleeping group
Of Nereids dreaming past.
Row on, fair swan;﻿—who knows but I,
Ere night hath sought her cave,
May see in splendour pale float by
The Venus of the wave!

II

A rainbow-wave o’erflowed her,
A glory that deepened and grew,
A song of colour and odour
That thrilled her through and through:
’Twas a dream of too much gladness
Ever to see the light;
They are only dreams of sadness
That weary out the night.

===Chinese===

古老的地上藏着许多巢，
柔软常新，
深沉、精致、满是安息——
可最可爱的只有两处：
我只说给心地
同它们一样洁白的人听；
别样的人听不见——
他们全被引开了。

在一只白色行船的天鹅
双翼之间，泡沫堆起的丘上，
一层薄羽叠成的遮蔽，
你会在那里找到一处。
另一处——呃，它说不出口，
我也不必告诉你；
我已告诉你一处了，既然总共只有两处，
你还能怀疑吗？

装满我的梦吧，啊华美的鸟！
载我渡过这片水：
这样安详的海洋，从没有被
一艘这样秀美的船搅动过！

也从来没有哪一种白，在人间
找到过一件可以上身的衣裳，
这样真、这样深、这样丰——
除非是落下来的雪！

她的双翼半张，轻轻扑动，
急切地扇着她的冠；
我由不得自己，软软偎进
那绒羽的深处。

看不见的蹼如桨一记记划动，
白色的快船荡了出去；
我们悬在中途，悬在
气之渊与海之渊之间。

沿着浪头涌起、流淌的坡，
一桨接一桨，我们攀爬；
顺着下沉的斜面滑落时，
她犁开一道会说话的水路——
像孤坡上的帚石楠铃，
像细雨打在玻璃上，
像孩子睡梦里咕哝，
像风穿过芦草。

她雪白的胸像浪一样起伏，
敲着庄严的拍子；
缓而有力的每一划，专注而凝重，
应和着涟漪的韵脚。

四下里，从平铺的幽暗里泛上来，
我捕捉到那片光，茫远而宽，
那是波浪从黑暗到破晓，
一轮轮涌起的磨光的侧腹。

夜是蓝的；星星烧亮着
挤满寂静的穹坡，
哀哀地照着那无望的、
自语不休的深流——
一团更浓的夜，带着郁积的呜咽！
一片黯然失位的空天！
只留下它群里星的影子，
叫人凭此认得它！

横越那边抬起的环洞、
西方最后一点微光的，是什么？
是海蒙着四肢的一群，
睡梦中漂过的涅瑞伊得斯。
划吧，美的天鹅；——谁知今夜
趁夜还没归洞之前，
我会不会看见波浪的维纳斯
披着淡金的光华漂过！

II

一道虹彩的浪漫过了她，
一份愈来愈深的荣光，
一首颜色与芳香的歌，
把她彻里彻外颤动：
那是一个太欢乐的梦，
见不得天光；
唯有悲哀的梦
才熬得过长夜。

===Original===

Slow darkness began to rifle
The nest of the sunset fair;
Dank vapour began to stifle
The scents that enriched the air;
The flowers paled fast and faster,
They crumbled, leaf and crown,
Till they looked like the stained plaster
Of a cornice fallen down.

And the change crept nigh and nigher,
Inward and closer stole,
Till the flameless, blasting fire
Entered and withered her soul.﻿—
But the fiends had only flouted
Her vision of the night;
Up came the morn and routed
The darksome things with light.

Wide awake I have often been in it﻿—
The dream that all is none;
It will come in the gladdest minute
And wither the very sun.
Two moments of sad commotion,
One more of doubt’s palsied rule﻿—
And the great wave-pulsing ocean
Is only a gathered pool;

A flower is a spot of painting,
A lifeless, loveless hue;
Though your heart be sick to fainting
It says not a word to you;
A bird knows nothing of gladness,
Is only a song-machine;
A man is a reasoning madness,
A woman a pictured queen!

Then fiercely we dig the fountain:
Oh! whence do the waters rise?
Then panting we climb the mountain:
Oh! are there indeed blue skies?
We dig till the soul is weary,
Nor find the water-nest out;
We climb to the stone-crest dreary,
And still the sky is a doubt!

Let alone the roots of the fountain;
Drink of the water bright;
Leave the sky at rest on the mountain,
Walk in its torrent of light;
Although thou seest no beauty,
Though widowed thy heart yet cries,
With thy hands go and do thy duty,
And thy work will clear thine eyes.

III

A great church in an empty square,
A haunt of echoing tones!
Feet pass not oft enough to wear
The grass between the stones.

The jarring hinges of its gates
A stifled thunder boom;
The boding heart slow-listening waits,
As for a coming doom.

The door stands wide. With hideous grin,
Like dumb laugh, evil, frore,
A gulf of death, all dark within,
Hath swallowed half the floor.

Its uncouth sides of earth and clay
O’erhang the void below;
Ah, some one force my feet away,
Or down I needs must go!

See, see the horrid, crumbling slope!
It breathes up damp and fust!
What man would for his lost loves grope
Amid the charnel dust!

Down, down! The coffined mould glooms high!
Methinks, with anguish dull,
I enter by the empty eye
Into a monstrous skull!

===Chinese===

迟缓的黑暗开始劫掠
落日那美丽的巢；
湿沉的水汽开始闷熄
充盈空气的芬芳；
花褪色得越来越快，
叶与冠都碎了，
直到它们看去像剥落下来
的一段染色的檐饰。

那变故悄悄近了、近了，
向内里、贴身地潜近，
直到那无焰的、摧折的火
进入，烤枯了她的魂。——
可群魔不过嘲弄了
她夜里的幻象；
早晨起来，用光
把那些黑暗的东西驱散。

我常常醒着就在其中——
那个「一切皆无」的梦；
它会在最欢乐的一刻袭来，
把太阳本身烤萎。
两分钟悲哀的动乱，
再一分钟疑虑的瘫症——
于是那伟大的、波涛搏动的海洋
成了一汪积潦；

一朵花是一块颜料，
一种无生命、无爱的色；
哪怕你的心憔悴欲绝，
它也不同你说一句话；
一只鸟不知欢喜为何物，
不过是一架歌的机器；
男人是一场讲道理的疯癫，
女人是一幅画出来的王后！

于是我们狂怒地掘泉：
哦！水究竟从哪里升起？
于是我们喘息着登山：
哦！果真有蓝天吗？
我们掘到魂都倦了，
也寻不出那水的巢；
我们爬到荒寒的石顶，
天仍旧是一个疑团！

且放开泉的根；
只管喝那明亮的水；
且让天安安稳稳在山上，
只管走在它的光之洪流里；
虽然你看不见美，
虽然你寡居的心还在哭，
也请用你的双手去做你的工，
你的工会擦亮你的眼。

III

空荡广场上的一座大教堂，
一处回声盘踞的地方！
脚步稀疏，磨不损
石缝间的草。

它大门的铰链呕哑一响，
像一声闷住的雷；
预感的心慢慢地听着、等着，
像等一场将临的灾祸。

门敞着。咧着狰狞的笑，
像哑笑，邪恶、冰冻，
一道死亡的深渊，里面全黑，
吞下了半边地面。

它那土与黏土的丑壁
悬在下面的虚空之上；
啊，谁把我的脚强行拉走吧，
不然我必要下去！

看，看那可怕的、崩落的陡坡！
它呼出潮湿与霉味！
谁肯为他逝去的爱
在尸骸的尘里摸索！

下，下！装棺的泥土高耸幽幽！
我想，带着钝钝的苦痛，
我正从那空掉的眼窝
走进一颗巨大的头骨！

===Original===

Stumbling on what I dare not guess,
Blind-wading through the gloom,
Still down, still on, I sink, I press,
To meet some awful doom.

My searching hands have caught a door
With iron clenched and barred:
Here, the gaunt spider’s castle-core,
Grim Death keeps watch and ward!

Its two leaves shake, its bars are bowed,
As if a ghastly wind,
That never bore a leaf or cloud,
Were pressing hard behind.

They shake, they groan, they outward strain:
What thing of dire dismay
Will freeze its form upon my brain,
And fright my soul away?

They groan, they shake, they bend, they crack;
The bars, the doors divide;
A flood of glory at their back
Hath burst the portals wide!

In flows a summer afternoon;
I know the very breeze!
It used to blow the silvery moon
About the summer trees.

The gulf is filled with flashing tides;
Blue sky through boughs looks in;
Mosses and ferns o’er floor and sides
A mazy arras spin.

The empty church, the yawning cleft,
The earthy, dead despair
Are gone, and I alive am left
In sunshine and in air!

IV

Some dreams, in slumber’s twilight, sly
Through the ivory wicket creep;
Then suddenly the inward eye
Sees them outside the sleep.

Once, wandering in the border gray,
I spied one past me swim;
I caught it on its truant way
To nowhere in the dim.

All o’er a steep of grassy ground,
Lay ruined statues old,
Such forms as never more are found
Save deep in ancient mould,

A host of marble Anakim
Shattered in deadly fight!
Oh, what a wealth one broken limb
Had been to waking sight!

But sudden, the weak mind to mock
That could not keep its own,
Without a shiver or a shock,
Behold, the dream was gone!

For each dim form of marble rare
Stood broken rush or reed;
So bends on autumn field, long bare,
Some tall rain-battered weed.

The shapeless night hung empty, drear,
O’er my scarce slumbering head;
There is no good in staying here,
My spirit moaned, and fled.

V

The simplest joys that daily pass
Grow ecstasies in sleep;
A wind on heights of waving grass
In a dream has made me weep.

No wonder then my heart one night
Was joy-full to the brim:
I was with one whose love and might
Had drawn me close to him!

But from a church into the street
Came pouring, crowding on,
A troubled throng with hurrying feet,
And Lo, my friend was gone!

Alone upon a miry road
I walked a wretched plain;
Onward without a goal I strode
Through mist and drizzling rain.

===Chinese===

在我不敢猜的东西上绊跌，
盲涉着穿过幽暗，
一路向下、一路向前，我沉，我挤，
去赴某个可怖的命途。

我摸索的手抓住了一扇门，
铁箍铁闩，紧锁紧闭：
在这里，瘦蜘蛛的城堡核心，
狰狞的死亡守望驻防！

它的两扇门颤动，门闩弯了，
仿佛一阵阴惨的风——
从没载过一片叶一朵云的风——
在背后狠狠顶撞。

它们颤，它们呻吟，向外挣：
怎样一种恐怖的东西
会把它的形骸冻上我的脑，
把我的魂吓走？

它们呻吟，它们颤动，它们弯，它们裂；
门闩、门扇分开了；
它们背后一股荣光的洪流
把门扇轰然撞开！

涌进来的是一个夏日的午后；
我认得那阵微风！
它从前常把银色的月亮
在夏夜的树间吹得游走。

深渊盛满了闪动的水潮；
蓝天从枝叶间看进来；
苔藓和蕨在四壁与地上
织一挂迷离的绣幔。

空荡的教堂、张口的裂罅、
那土腥的、死一样的绝望
都不见了，而我活着，留在
阳光里，空气里！

IV

有些梦，趁着睡眠的微明，悄悄
溜过那扇象牙的小门；
忽然间，内里的眼睛
看见它们跑到了睡的外面。

有一回，我在灰蒙的边界游荡，
瞥见一个从我身边游过；
我逮住它那逃学的一路——
它正往朦胧里的「无处」去。

在一片青草的陡坡上，
横陈着毁损的古像，
那样的形骸如今再寻不见，
除非深深掘进古老的封土——

一大群大理石的亚衲族巨人，
在死斗中碎裂！
啊，哪怕只是一条断臂，
对醒着的眼睛也是何等的财富！

可是忽然，仿佛嘲弄这
守不住自家珍藏的弱心，
不颤一下、不惊一下——
看哪，梦没了！

因为每一尊朦胧的珍奇石像，
立着的不过是折断的灯心草、芦苇；
像秋日久荒的田里，
一茎被雨打得偃倒的高草。

无形无状的夜空，空落、凄凉，
罩在我这半睡的头顶；
待在这里没什么好处，
我的魂哀叹一声，逃走了。

V

日常流逝的最简单的欢喜，
在睡眠里长成狂喜；
一阵吹过草浪高岗的风，
曾在梦里使我落泪。

怪不得有一夜，我的心
满满盛着欢喜：
我与一位爱和大能兼备的在一起，
祂把我拉近了身旁！

可从一座教堂里涌到街上，
挤挤挨挨冲过来的，
是一群脚步仓皇的乱众，
看哪，我的朋友不见了！

我独自走在一条泥泞的路上，
走过一片凄凉的平原；
没有目的地，我只顾前行，
穿过雾，穿过细雨。

===Original===

Low mounds of ruin, ugly pits,
And brick-fields scarred the globe;
Those wastes where desolation sits
Without her ancient robe.

The dreariness, the nothingness
Grew worse almost than fear;
If ever hope was needful bliss,
Hope sure was needful here!

Did potent wish work joyous change
Like wizard’s glamour-spell?
Wishes not always fruitless range,
And sometimes it is well!

I know not. Sudden sank the way,
Burst in the ocean-waves;
Behold a bright, blue-billowed bay,
Red rocks and sounding caves!

Dreaming, I wept. Awake, I ask﻿—
Shall earthly dreams, forsooth,
Set the old Heavens too hard a task
To match them with the truth?

VI

Once more I build a dream, awake,
Which sleeping I would dream;
Once more an unborn fancy take
And try to make it seem!
Some strange delight shall fill my breast,
Enticed from sleep’s abyss,
With sense of motion, yet of rest,
Of sleep, yet waking bliss!

It comes!﻿—I lie on something warm
That lifts me from below;
It rounds me like a mighty arm
Though soft as drifted snow.
A dream, indeed!﻿—Oh, happy me
Whom Titan woman bears
Afloat upon a gentle sea
Of wandering midnight airs!

A breeze, just cool enough to lave
With sense each conscious limb,
Glides round and under, like a wave
Of twilight growing dim!
She bears me over sleeping towns,
O’er murmuring ears of corn;
O’er tops of trees, o’er billowy downs,
O’er moorland wastes forlorn.

The harebells in the mountain-pass
Flutter their blue about;
The myriad blades of meadow grass
Float scarce-heard music out.
Over the lake!﻿—ah! nearer float,
Nearer the water’s breast;
Let me look deeper﻿—let me dote
Upon that lily-nest.

Old homes we brush﻿—in wood, on road;
Their windows do not shine;
Their dwellers must be all abroad
In lovely dreams like mine!
Hark﻿—drifting syllables that break
Like foam-bells on fleet ships!
The little airs are all awake
With softly kissing lips.

Light laughter ripples down the wind,
Sweet sighs float everywhere;
But when I look I nothing find,
For every star is there.
O lady lovely, lady strong,
Ungiven thy best gift lies!
Thou bear’st me in thine arms along,
Dost not reveal thine eyes!

Pale doubt lifts up a snaky crest,
In darts a pang of loss:
My outstretched hand, for hills of rest,
Finds only mounds of moss!
Faint and far off the stars appear;
The wind begins to weep;
’Tis night indeed, chilly and drear,
And all but me asleep!

===Chinese===

低矮的瓦砾堆、丑陋的坑，
砖窑场把大地划伤；
那些荒地，荒凉坐在那里，
连她古老的衣袍也没有。

这凄凉、这空无，
长得几乎比恐惧更糟；
倘若盼望曾是必需的福，
这里就真真必需盼望！

是强力的愿望施行了欢乐的改变，
像术士的魔咒吗？
愿望并不总是白白奔走，
有时候，这样正好！

我不知道。道路忽然下陷，
海潮轰然灌入；
看哪，一湾明亮的、蓝色波澜的海，
红岩与訇响的洞窟！

梦中我哭了。醒来我问——
难道尘世的梦，当真
给古老的天堂出了难题，
叫它难以用实情与之相配？

VI

我又一次醒着造一个梦，
好睡时去做；
又一次接过一个未生的幻想，
设法使它显为真！
某种奇异的欢喜要充满我的胸，
从睡眠的深渊里引来，
带着一种动、又一种静的感觉，
一种睡着、又醒着的至福！

它来了！——我躺在一样温软的东西上，
它自下面把我托起；
它把我环拢，像一条巨臂，
却柔软得像积起的雪。

真是个梦！——哦，我真有福，
被一位泰坦似的女子驮着，
漂在一片温柔的海上——
那海是游荡的午夜气流！

一阵风，凉得恰够让知觉
洗过每一条有意识的肢体，
滑来滑去，像一匹
渐渐昏暗的暮色的浪！

她驮我越过沉睡的城镇，
越过絮语的麦穗；
越过树顶，越过波状的丘，
越过荒凉的石南野。

山径上的圆叶风铃草，
摇曳着它们的蓝；
草场上千万片草叶，
飘出几乎听不见的乐音。
过湖了！——啊，再漂低些，
再贴近水的心口；
让我看深些——让我痴痴凝望
那一巢百合。

我们拂过旧日的家——林中的、路上的；
它们的窗不亮；
住在里面的人想必全出门了，
都在同我一样可爱的梦里！
听——飘散的音节，碎裂如
疾船上飞沫的铃！
小小的气流全醒了，
长满轻吻的唇。

轻笑顺着风漾下来，
甜叹四处漂浮；
可我举目四望什么也找不见，
因为每一颗星都在那里。
哦，可爱又强大的女子，
你最好的礼物还未给出！
你把我抱在臂弯里带走，
却不肯露出你的眼睛！

惨白的疑虑竖起蛇一般的冠，
刺进来一阵失去的痛：
我伸出的手，本想攀住安息的丘，
却只摸到一座座的苔！

星星黯了，远远地淡去；
风开始呜咽；
真是夜了，寒凉而凄清，
万物都睡了——只除了我！

## To Aurelio Saffi / 致奥雷利奥·萨菲
===Original===

To God and man be simply true;
Do as thou hast been wont to do;
Bring out thy treasures, old and new﻿—
Mean all the same when said to you.

I love thee: thou art calm and strong;
Firm in the right, mild to the wrong;
Thy heart, in every raging throng,
A chamber shut for prayer and song.

Defeat thou know’st not, canst not know,
Although thy aims so lofty go
They need as long to root and grow
As infant hills to reach the snow.

Press on and prosper, holy friend!
I, weak and ignorant, would lend
A voice, thee, strong and wise, to send
Prospering onward without end.

===Chinese===

对上帝、对世人，都简简单单地真诚；
照你一向的习惯去做；
把你的珍宝，新旧都提出来——
说与你听时，心意始终如一。

我爱你：你平静而坚强；
在正道上坚定，对错谬温和；
你的心，在每一群暴怒的人中，
都是一间关起门祷告与歌唱的密室。

你不知道败，也不可能知道，
虽说你的目标那样高远，
需要同样长久扎根生长——
如婴孩般的山丘要长到雪线。

向前推进并昌盛吧，圣洁的朋友！
我，软弱而无知，愿献一声嗓，
送你，坚强而有智慧的人，
昌盛向前，永无止境。

## A. M. D. / A. M. D.
===Original===

Methinks I see thee, lying straight and low,
Silent and darkling, in thy earthy bed,
The mighty strength in which I trusted, fled,
The long arms lying careless of kiss or blow;
On thy tall form I see the night-robe flow
Down from the pale, composed face﻿—thy head
Crowned with its own dark curls: though thou wast dead,
They dressed thee as for sleep, and left thee so!
My heart, with cares and questionings oppressed,
Not oft since thou didst leave us turns to thee;
But wait, my brother, till I too am dead,
And thou shalt find that heart more true, more free,
More ready in thy love to take its rest,
Than when we lay together in one bed.

===Chinese===

我仿佛看见你，直挺挺地低低躺着，
寂默而暗，在你泥土的床上，
我所信赖的那副大力，已遁走，
长长的手臂摊着，吻与击都再不在乎；
在你高大的身上，我看见睡袍
从那苍白、安详的脸上垂流下来——你的头
还戴着自己深色的发卷：虽说你已死，
他们仍把你装扮得如同安睡，就这样留下了你！
我这颗心，被操劳与疑问压着，
自你离去，不常转向你；
可等着吧，我的兄弟，等我也就死，
你便会发现这颗心更真、更自由，
更愿在你的爱里安歇，
胜过当年我们同榻共眠的时光。

## A Memorial of Africa / 非洲的纪念
===Original===

I

Upon a rock I sat﻿—a mountain-side,
Far, far forsaken of the old sea’s lip;
A rock where ancient waters’ rise and dip,
Recoil and plunge, eddy, and oscillant tide,
Had worn and worn, while races lived and died,
Involved channels. Where the sea-weed’s drip
Followed the ebb, now crumbling lichens sip
Sparse dews of heaven that down with sunset slide.
I sat long-gazing southward. A dry flow
Of withering wind sucked up my drooping strength,
Itself weak from the desert’s burning length.
Behind me piled, away and up did go
Great sweeps of savage mountains﻿—up, away,
Where snow gleams ever, panthers roam, they say.

II

This infant world has taken long to make,
Nor hast Thou done with it, but mak’st it yet,
And wilt be working on when death has set
A new mound in some churchyard for my sake.
On flow the centuries without a break;
Uprise the mountains, ages without let;
The lichens suck; the hard rock’s breast they fret;
Years more than past, the young earth yet will take.
But in the dumbness of the rolling time,
No veil of silence shall encompass me﻿—
Thou wilt not once forget and let me be;
Rather wouldst thou some old chaotic prime
Invade, and, moved by tenderness sublime,
Unfold a world, that I, thy child, might see.

===Chinese===

一

我坐在一块岩石上——那是山坡，
早已、早已被古海的唇舍弃；
一块岩石，古时潮水的起落、
回卷与跌冲、漩涡与摇荡的潮汐，
在一代代生生死死里磨了又磨，
磨出交错的沟槽。昔日海藻滴水
随退潮滑落的地方，如今碎裂的地衣啜饮
随夕阳滑下的、天赐的稀薄露珠。
我久久坐着，朝南凝望。一阵干枯的
枯萎之风，吸干我垂萎的力气，
它自己也疲弱，来自沙漠灼烧的绵长。
在我身后，蛮荒的群山层层叠起，绵延直上——
上去，远去，
那里终年雪光闪耀，有豹子游荡，人们这样说。

二

这婴孩的世界用了很久才造好，
而你还没有造完，仍在造着，
还要继续工作下去，当死亡为我的缘故
在某座教堂墓园里堆起新的坟丘。
诸世纪川流不息，从不中断；
群山升起，历经世代不曾停歇；
地衣啜饮；它们侵蚀硬岩的胸膛；
这年轻的大地，还要接纳比过去更多的年月。
但在滚动的时光的喑哑之中，
没有一层沉默的慕会将我罩住——
你不会有一刻忘掉我、任我去；
你宁可闯入某个太初的混沌，
怀着崇高的温柔，动身展开一个世界，
好叫我，你的孩子，能够看见。

## A Gift / 一件礼物
===Original===

My gift would find thee fast asleep,
And arise a dream in thee;
A violet sky o’er the roll and sweep
Of a purple and pallid sea;
And a crescent moon from my sky should creep
In the golden dream to thee.

Thou shouldst lay thee down, and sadly list
To the wail of our cold birth-time;
And build thee a temple, glory-kissed,
In the heart of the sunny clime;
Its columns should rise in a music-mist,
And its roofs in a spirit-rhyme.

Its pillars the solemn hills should bind
’Neath arches of starry deeps;
Its floor the earth all veined and lined;
Its organ the ocean-sweeps;
And, swung in the hands of the grey-robed wind,
Its censers the blossom-heaps.

And ’tis almost done; for in this my rhyme,
Thanks to thy mirror-soul,
Thou wilt see the mountains, and hear the chime
Of the waters after the roll;
And the stars of my sky thy sky will climb,
And with heaven roof in the whole.

===Chinese===

我的礼物会寻到沉睡的你，
在你里面升起一场梦：
一片紫罗兰色的天，笼着那吞吐翻涌的
紫红与苍白的海；
一弯新月，从我的天空
悄悄爬进你金色的梦。

你将躺下，忧伤地听
我们寒凉降生时的啼哭；
你将在阳光地带的心里，
筑起一座蒙受荣光的殿堂；
它的柱廊升起在乐音的雾中，
它的屋顶升起在灵性的韵里。

庄严的群山作它的巨柱，
撑起星辰深渊的拱顶；
大地脉络交织，作它的地面；
海洋的浩荡作它的琴；
而那灰袍的风挥动香炉，
炉里是成堆的繁花。

而这几乎已经成了；因为在我这首诗里，
多亏你那镜般的灵魂，
你将看见群山，听见涛声滚过之后
流水的清鸣；
而我天空的星，将攀上你的天空，
把这一切同覆在天国底下。

## The Man of Songs / 歌之人
===Original===

“Thou wanderest in the land of dreams,
O man of many songs!
To thee what is, but looks and seems;
No realm to thee belongs!”

“Seest thou those mountains, faint and far,
O spirit caged and tame?”
“Blue clouds like distant hills they are,
And like is not the same.”

“Nay, nay; I know each mountain well,
Each cliff, and peak, and dome!
In that cloudland, in one high dell,
Nesteth my little home.”

===Chinese===

「你在梦的国度里游荡，
哦，写了许多歌的人！
实在于你，不过是望上去、看似乎；
没有一片疆土归于你！」

「你可看见那些山，淡而远，
哦，被囚而驯服的灵？」
「那不过是像远山的蓝云，
而相像，并不是相同。」

「不，不；每一座山我都熟识，
每一处崖、每一座峰、每一个穹丘！
在那云乡，在一个高高的山坳里，
安稳着我小小的家。」

## Better Things / 更好的事
===Original===

Better to smell the violet
Than sip the glowing wine;
Better to hearken to a brook
Than watch a diamond shine.

Better to have a loving friend
Than ten admiring foes;
Better a daisy’s earthy root
Than a gorgeous, dying rose.

Better to love in loneliness
Than bask in love all day;
Better the fountain in the heart
Than the fountain by the way.

Better be fed by mother’s hand
Than eat alone at will;
Better to trust in God, than say,
My goods my storehouse fill.

Better to be a little wise
Than in knowledge to abound;
Better to teach a child than toil
To fill perfection’s round.

Better to sit at some man’s feet
Than thrill a listening state;
Better suspect that thou art proud
Than be sure that thou art great.

Better to walk the realm unseen
Than watch the hour’s event;
Better the “Well done, faithful slave!”
Than the air with shoutings rent.

Better to have a quiet grief
Than many turbulent joys;
Better to miss thy manhood’s aim
Than sacrifice the boy’s.

Better a death when work is done
Than earth’s most favoured birth;
Better a child in God’s great house
Than the king of all the earth.

===Chinese===

与其啜饮灼灼的美酒，
不如嗅一嗅紫罗兰；
与其看钻石的光闪，
不如听一听小溪。

与其要十个艳羡的仇敌，
不如有一个相爱的朋友；
与其要一朵华艳将谢的玫瑰，
不如要雏菊带土的根。

与其终日沐浴在爱里，
不如在孤独中去爱；
与其要路边的喷泉，
不如要心里的泉。

与其随心独自进餐，
不如由母亲的手喂养；
与其说『我的库房装满我的财物』，
不如信靠上帝。

与其学识渊博，
不如略有一点智慧；
与其苦填那圆满的圆，
不如去教一个孩子。

与其令满堂听众战栗，
不如坐在某人脚下；
与其确信自己伟大，
不如怀疑自己骄傲。

与其紧盯一时的风云，
不如行走在看不见的国度；
与其让呐喊撕破天空，
不如得一声『好，忠心的仆人！』

与其要许多喧腾的欢乐，
不如有一场安静的悲伤；
与其牺牲少年的心，
不如错过壮年的志向。

与其得地上最得宠的诞生，
不如在工成之后死去；
与其做全地的君王，
不如做上帝大家宅里的孩子。

## The Journey / 旅程
===Original===

I

Hark, the rain is on my roof!
Every murmur, through the dark,
Stings me with a dull reproof
Like a half-extinguished spark.
Me! ah me! how came I here,
Wide awake and wide alone!
Caught within a net of fear,
All my dreams undreamed and gone!

I will rise; I will go forth.
Better dare the hideous night,
Better face the freezing north
Than be still, where is no light!
Black wind rushing round me now,
Sown with arrowy points of rain!
Gone are there and then and now﻿—
I am here, and so is pain!

Dead in dreams the gloomy street!
I will out on open roads.
Eager grow my aimless feet﻿—
Onward, onward something goads!
I will take the mountain path,
Beard the storm within its den;
Know the worst of this dim wrath
Harassing the souls of men.

Chasm ’neath chasm! rock piled on rock!
Roots, and crumbling earth, and stones!
Hark, the torrent’s thundering shock!
Hark, the swaying pine tree’s groans!
Ah! I faint, I fall, I die,
Sink to nothingness away!﻿—
Lo, a streak upon the sky!
Lo, the opening eye of day!

II

Mountain summits lift their snows
O’er a valley green and low;
And a winding pathway goes
Guided by the river’s flow;
And a music rises ever,
As of peace and low content,
From the pebble-paven river
Like an odour upward sent.

And the sound of ancient harms
Moans behind, the hills among,
Like the humming of the swarms
That unseen the forest throng.
Now I meet the shining rain
From a cloud with sunny weft;
Now against the wind I strain,
Sudden burst from mountain cleft.

Now a sky that hath a moon
Staining all the cloudy white
With a faded rainbow﻿—soon
Lost in deeps of heavenly night!
Now a morning clear and soft,
Amber on the purple hills;
Warm blue day of summer, oft
Cooled by wandering windy rills!

Joy to travel thus along
With the universe around!
Every creature of the throng,
Every sight and scent and sound
Homeward speeding, beauty-laden,
Beelike, to its hive, my soul!
Mine the eye the stars are made in!
Mine the heart of Nature’s whole!

III

Hills retreating on each hand
Slowly sink into the plain;
Solemn through the outspread land
Rolls the river to the main.
In the glooming of the night
Something through the dusky air
Doubtful glimmers, faintly white,
But I know not what or where.

===Chinese===

I

听，雨打在我的屋顶！
黑暗里每一声絮语，
都刺我一记钝钝的责备，
像一颗将熄的火星。
是我！啊是我！我怎么会在这里，
全然醒着，又全然孤单！
落进一张恐惧织的网，
所有的梦，未做便已散尽！

我要起来；我要出去。
宁可去招惹狰狞的黑夜，
宁可去直面冰冻的北风，
也不呆在这里，这里没有光！
黑风此刻在我四周奔突，
撒满了箭镞似的雨点！
那里、那时、此刻，全都清空——
我在这里，疼痛也在这里！

明沉的街道，在梦里死了！
我要出去，上开阔的路。
我漫无目的的脚变得急切——
向前，向前，有什么在驱策！
我要走山径，
直捣风暴的老巢；
要尝一尝这黯淡的忿怒
骚扰世人魂灵的最深处。

壑下叠壑！岩上堆岩！
树根、崩碎的土、乱石！
听，山洪雷一样的撞击！
听，摇曳的松树的呻吟！
啊！我晕，我倒，我死，
沉向虚无——！
看哪，天上一道微光！
看哪，白昼睁开的眼睛！

II

山顶驮着积雪，
俯瞰一座低低的绿谷；
一条蜿蜒的小路
循着河水的流向延伸；
有一种乐音不断升起，
像安宁与低低的知足，
从那铺满卵石的河里，
像香气一般向上送来。

古老的祸患之声
在身后群山之间呻吟，
像蜂群的嗡营，
无数无形者挤满森林。
这时我遇上闪亮的雨，
从一朵阳光织边的云里；
这时我顶着风挣扎，
它从山罅间猛然迸出。

这时一片有月的夜空，
把裉色的虹，染上
满天的云白——转眼
便没入天夜的深处！
这时一个清柔的早晨，
琥珀色敷上紫色的山；
温蓝的夏日白昼，不时
被游荡的风溪吹凉！

何等的欢喜，就这样前行，
宇宙四面围绕！
同行万物的每一个，
每一眼景、每一缕香、每一声响，
都满载着美，奔回家去，
像归巢的蜂，我的魂！
星星在其中制成的眼睛，是我的！
自然全体的心，是我的！

III

两侧的山缓缓退去，
渐渐沉入平原；
庄严地穿过铺展的大地，
大河滚滚奔向沧海。
在夜色四合的幽暗中，
有什么穿过暝暝的空气，
隐约闪烁，淡淡的白，
我却不知是什么、在哪里。

===Original===

Is it but a chalky ridge
Bared of sod, like tree of bark?
Or a river-spanning bridge
Miles away into the dark?
Or the foremost leaping waves
Of the everlasting sea,
Where the Undivided laves
Time with its eternity?

Is it but an eye-made sight,
In my brain a fancied gleam?
Or a faint aurora-light
From the sun’s tired smoking team?
In the darkness it is gone,
Yet with every step draws nigh;
Known shall be the thing unknown
When the morning climbs the sky!

Onward, onward through the night
Matters it I cannot see?
I am moving in a might
Dwelling in the dark and me!
End or way I cannot lose﻿—
Grudge to rest, or fear to roam;
All is well with wanderer whose
Heart is travelling hourly home.

IV

Joy! O joy! the dawning sea
Answers to the dawning sky,
Foretaste of the coming glee
When the sun will lord it high!
See the swelling radiance growing
To a dazzling glory-might!
See the shadows gently going
’Twixt the wave-tops wild with light!

Hear the smiting billows clang!
See the falling billows lean
Half a watery vault, and hang
Gleaming with translucent green,
Then in thousand fleeces fall,
Thundering light upon the strand!﻿—
This the whiteness which did call
Through the dusk, across the land!

See, a boat! Out, out we dance!
Fierce blasts swoop upon my sail!
What a terrible expanse﻿—
Tumbling hill and heaving dale!
Stayless, helpless, lost I float,
Captive to the lawless free!
But a prison is my boat!
Oh, for petrel-wings to flee!

Look below: each watery whirl
Cast in beauty’s living mould!
Look above: each feathery curl
Dropping crimson, dropping gold!﻿—
Oh, I tremble in the flush
Of the everlasting youth!
Love and awe together rush:
I am free in God, the Truth!

===Chinese===

它不过是一道裸露的白垩山脊，
剥了草皮，像剥了皮的树？
还是一座跨河的长桥，
远在数里之外、没入黑暗？
还是那永恒之海
最前方腾跃的浪头，
在那里，那不可分者
用它的永恒濯洗时间？

它不过是眼睛造出的景象，
是我脑中一缕幻想的微光？
还是一痕淡淡的极光，
来自太阳疲倦的、冒着烟的马队？
黑暗里它不见了，
可我每迈一步，它便近一分；
那未知之物终将被识得，
当早晨爬上天空！

向前，向前，穿过黑夜，
看不见又何妨？
我正运动在一股大能里，
它住在黑暗中，也住在我里！
终点或道路，我都不会失——
何必吝于歇息，何必怕于游荡；
一切都好，只要行路人的心
时时刻刻正走在回家的路上。

IV

欢喜！哦欢喜！破晓的海
应和着破晓的天，
这是将临的欢庆的前味，
当太阳高高称尊！
看那澎涨的光辉，
长成一片耀眼的光荣与大能！
看那些影子温柔地退去，
在狂野闪光的浪峰之间！

听浪头铿然相击！
看跌落的浪探身
撑起半座水造的穹隆，悬着，
闪着通透的绿，
随即碎作千片羊毛，
把雷一样的光砸上沙滩！——
正是这一片白，曾在暝色里
隔着大地呼唤我！

看，一条船！出去，出去，我们舞蹈！
狂风猛扑我的帆！
何等可怕的浩瀚——
翻滚的丘、耸涌的谷！
无凭、无助、迷失，我漂着，
做了那无法无天的自由的俘囚！
可我的船是一座牢笼！
哦，愿生出海燕的翅膀逃走！

看下面：每一泓水的旋涡，
都铸着活的美之模！
看上面：每一绺羽状的卷云，
滴着绯红，滴着黄金！——
哦，在那永恒青春的
光华中，我战栗！
爱与敬畏一齐奔涌：
我在上帝、即真理之中，自由了！

## Prayer / 祷告
===Original===

We doubt the word that tells us: Ask,
And ye shall have your prayer;
We turn our thoughts as to a task,
With will constrained and rare.

And yet we have; these scanty prayers
Yield gold without alloy:
O God, but he that trusts and dares
Must have a boundless joy!

===Chinese===

我们怀疑那句告诉我们的话：祈求，
你们就必得着所求的；
我们把祷告当作苦差，
心意勉强而稀军。

然而我们确实得着了；这些寥寥的祷告
炼出无搒的黄金：
哦上帝，那又信靠又敢于求的人，
必得一份无边的喜乐！

## Rest / 安息
===Original===

I

When round the earth the Father’s hands
Have gently drawn the dark;
Sent off the sun to fresher lands,
And curtained in the lark;
’Tis sweet, all tired with glowing day,
To fade with fading light,
And lie once more, the old weary way,
Upfolded in the night.

If mothers o’er our slumbers bend,
And unripe kisses reap,
In soothing dreams with sleep they blend,
Till even in dreams we sleep.
And if we wake while night is dumb,
’Tis sweet to turn and say,
It is an hour ere dawning come,
And I will sleep till day.

II

There is a dearer, warmer bed,
Where one all day may lie,
Earth’s bosom pillowing the head,
And let the world go by.
There come no watching mother’s eyes,
The stars instead look down;
Upon it breaks, and silent dies,
The murmur of the town.

The great world, shouting, forward fares:
This chamber, hid from none,
Hides safe from all, for no one cares
For him whose work is done.
Cheer thee, my friend; bethink thee how
A certain unknown place,
Or here or there, is waiting now,
To rest thee from thy race.

III

Nay, nay, not there the rest from harms,
The still composed breath!
Not there the folding of the arms,
The cool, the blessed death!
That needs no curtained bed to hide
The world with all its wars,
No grassy cover to divide
From sun and moon and stars.

It is a rest that deeper grows
In midst of pain and strife;
A mighty, conscious, willed repose,
The death of deepest life.
To have and hold the precious prize
No need of jealous bars;
But windows open to the skies,
And skill to read the stars!

IV

Who dwelleth in that secret place,
Where tumult enters not,
Is never cold with terror base,
Never with anger hot.
For if an evil host should dare
His very heart invest,
God is his deeper heart, and there
He enters in to rest.

When mighty sea-winds madly blow,
And tear the scattered waves,
Peaceful as summer woods, below
Lie darkling ocean caves:
The wind of words may toss my heart,
But what is that to me!
’Tis but a surface storm﻿—thou art
My deep, still, resting sea.

===Chinese===

一

当父的双手绕着大地
温柔地拉上黑暗；
遣太阳去更清新的一片天地，
把云雀也遮进帷幔；
在燃烧的白昼后倦极之时，
随渐暗的光一同消隐，
又一次躺下，循着旧日困乏的方式，
被夜色轻轻裹紧，何等甘美。

若母亲俯身向着我们的睡眠，
收割尚未成熟的亲吻，
她们便把安恬的梦与睡意调和，
直到我们在梦中又沉沉睡去。
而若我们在夜还沉默时醒来，
翻身说一句，多么可喜：
离破晓还有整整一个时辰呢，
我要一觉睡到天亮才起。

二

有一张更亲切、更温暖的床，
在那里可以终日躺卧，
大地的胸脯枕着那头颅，
任人世从身旁走过。
再没有母亲守望的眼睛，
俯视着这片安眠；
替代它们的是繁星，向下凝望，
城镇的喧嚣涌到这床边，
便悄然消散。

大千世界喧腾着向前奔赴：
这间卧房，虽不藏于隐秘，
却对一切安然藏身，因为无人再挂念
那做工已毕的人。振作吧，我的朋友；nay，想一想吧：
或在此处或在彼方，
某一个无名的处所此刻正等候，
让你从你的奔逐中安歇一场。

三

不，不，那里并非脱离伤害的安息，
并非沉静自持的呼吸！
那里没有交叠在胸前的双臂，
没有那清凉、蒙福的死！
那样的安息无须床帏遮蔽
这个满是战乱的人世，
无须一层青草分隔
死者与太阳、月亮和星辰。

那是一种在痛苦与争斗之中
愈加深沉的安息；
一种刚强的、清醒的、自主的静谧，
是至深生命的死寂。
持有并守住这无价的珍宝，
无须嫉妒的门闩；
只须窗户向诸天敞开，
并有解读星辰的本领！

四

那居住在隐秘之处的，
纷扰不得而入，
他永不因卑怯的恐怖而寒冷，
永不因怒火而滚烫。
因为纵有邪恶的大军胆敢
围困他内心最深处，
上帝是他更深的心，在那深处
他进入里面安息。

当强劲的海风狂野地吹刮，
撕碎四散的波涛，
幽暗的海底岩洞里却静谧
一如夏日的树林：
言语的风或会掀动我的心，
但那于我又有何妨！
那不过是表层的风暴——你才是
我深沉、静谧、安息的海洋。

## To A. J. Scott / 致 A. J. 司各特
===Original===

*With the Following Poem*

I walked all night: the darkness did not yield.
Around me fell a mist, a weary rain,
Enduring long. At length the dawn revealed

A temple’s front, high-lifted from the plain.
Closed were the lofty doors that led within;
But by a wicket one might entrance gain.

’Twas awe and silence when I entered in;
The night, the weariness, the rain were lost
In hopeful spaces. First I heard a thin

Sweet sound of voices low, together tossed,
As if they sought some harmony to find
Which they knew once, but none of all that host

Could wile the far-fled music back to mind.
Loud voices, distance-low, wandered along
The pillared paths, and up the arches twined

With sister arches, rising, throng on throng,
Up to the roof’s dim height. At broken times
The voices gathered to a burst of song,

But parted sudden, and were but single rimes
By single bells through Sabbath morning sent,
That have no thought of harmony or chimes.

Hopeful confusion! Who could be content
Looking and hearkening from the distant door?
I entered further. Solemnly it went﻿—

Thy voice, Truth’s herald, walking the untuned roar,
Calm and distinct, powerful and sweet and fine:
I loved and listened, listened and loved more.

May not the faint harp, tremulous, combine
Its ghostlike sounds with organ’s mighty tone?
Let my poor song be taken in to thine.

Will not thy heart, with tempests of its own,
Yet hear aeolian sighs from thin chords blown?

===Chinese===

*以下面这首诗同献*

我走了一整夜：黑暗不曾退让。
一场雾、一场令人困倦的雨
落在我四周，久久不停。终了，曙光显出

一座神庙的正面，自平原高高耸起。
通向庙内的高大门扉紧闭；
唯有一扇小门可以进去。

我进门时，唯有敬畏与寂静；
黑夜、困倦、雨水，都消失在
满舍希望的空阔里。我先听见一阵细而

甜美的低语，低低地交叠在一处，
仿佛它们想寻回某种和声——
它们曾熟悉的；可那一大群歌者中没有一个

能诱那远遁的音乐重新回到心上。
高亢的人声隔着距离显得低微，沿着
柱列的通道游走，又缠上

一道道彼此相缠的拱，一重又一重，
直上屋顶昏暗的高处。断断续续地，
人声聚成一阵爆发的歌唱，

却又蓦地散开，只剩一句句零落的单响，
如安息日清晨一只只单钟的鸣声，
全不想什么和声与钟乐。

满舍希望的纷乱！有谁站在远处门边，
望着听着，便能心满意足？
我再往里走。那声音庄严地行进——

是你的声音，真理的先锋，行在失调的喧声之中，
平静而清晰，有力而甜美而纯净：
我爱它而倾听，倾听而爱得更深。

那微弱的竖琴，颤颤地，何尝不可
把它幽灵似的声响与风琴的雄浑融成一体？
但愿我贫弱的歌被收进你的歌里。

你自己的心中不也正翻涌着风暴，
却仍听见薄薄的琴弦上吹来的风之叹息么？

## Light / 光
===Original===

First-born of the creating Voice!
Minister of God’s Spirit, who wast sent
Waiting upon him first, what time he went
Moving about mid the tumultuous noise
Of each unpiloted element
Upon the face of the void formless deep!
Thou who didst come unbodied and alone
Ere yet the sun was set his rule to keep,
Or ever the moon shone,
Or e’er the wandering star-flocks forth were driven!
Thou garment of the Invisible, whose skirt
Sweeps, glory-giving, over earth and heaven!
Thou comforter, be with me as thou wert
When first I longed for words, to be
A radiant garment for my thought, like thee!

We lay us down in sorrow,
Wrapt in the old mantle of our mother Night;
In vexing dreams we strive until the morrow;
Grief lifts our eyelids up﻿—and Lo, the light!
The sunlight on the wall! And visions rise
Of shining leaves that make sweet melodies;
Of wind-borne waves with thee upon their crests;
Of rippled sands on which thou rainest down;
Of quiet lakes that smooth for thee their breasts;
Of clouds that show thy glory as their own;
O joy! O joy! the visions are gone by!
Light, gladness, motion, are reality!

Thou art the god of earth. The skylark springs
Far up to catch thy glory on his wings;
And thou dost bless him first that highest soars.
The bee comes forth to see thee; and the flowers
Worship thee all day long, and through the skies
Follow thy journey with their earnest eyes.
River of life, thou pourest on the woods,
And on thy waves float out the wakening buds;
The trees lean toward thee, and, in loving pain,
Keep turning still to see thee yet again;
South sides of pines, haunted all day by thee,
Bear violins that tremble humanly.
And nothing in thine eyes is mean or low:
Where’er thou art, on every side,
All things are glorified;
And where thou canst not come, there thou dost throw
Beautiful shadows, made out of the dark,
That else were shapeless; now it bears thy mark.

===Chinese===

创造之音的头生之子！
上帝之灵的执事，你最先奉差
在他左右伺候——当他在翻腾的喧声里
行走于那无人掌舵的诸元素之间，
行在虚空无形之渊的面上！
你，无身无偶地降临
早在太阳奉命守其职分之前，
早在月亮放光之前，
早在流散的星群被驱出之前！
你，那不可见者的衣裳，衣裾
带着荣光，扫过大地与诸天！
你，安慰者，求你与我同在，如同当初
我渴慕言辞时那样——让我的思想
也披上一件发光的衣裳，像你一样！

我们在忧伤里躺下，
裹在夜之母亲那件旧斗篷中；
在烦扰的梦里挣扎到天明；
忧伤替我们掀起眼皮——看哪，光！
墙上的阳光！异象纷纷升起：
闪亮的叶子奏出甜美的乐音；
乘风之浪，浪尖上载着你；
你把光雨落上起涟漪的沙滩；
安静的湖泊为你把胸脯抹平；
云彩把你的荣耀当作自己的炫示；
哦欢喜！哦欢喜！幻象已过去！
光、欢畅、运动，才是真实！

你是大地之神。云雀腾起，
高高地飞，要用翅膀承接你的荣耀；
你先赐福给那飞得最高的。
蜜蜂出来看你；百花
终日敬拜你，并隔着天空
以恳切的眼睛追随你的行踪。
生命之河啊，你倾泻在树林上，
苏醒的蓓蕾随你的波浪漂出；
树向你倾身，怀着爱恋的痛楚，
还不住回转，想再看你一眼；
松树的南面，终日被你流连，
挂着会像人一样颤抖的提琴。
在你眼中没有卑贱低陋之物：
你在哪里，哪里的每一样东西，
四面八方都得着荣耀；
你不能到的地方，你就抛下
美丽的影子——用黑暗造出来的，
黑暗本无形；如今它带上了你的印记。

===Original===

And men have worshipped thee.
The Persian, on his mountain-top,
Waits kneeling till thy sun go up,
God-like in his serenity.
All-giving, and none-gifted, he draws near,
And the wide earth waits till his face appear﻿—
Longs patient. And the herald glory leaps
Along the ridges of the outlying clouds,
Climbing the heights of all their towering steeps.
Sudden, still multitudinous laughter crowds
The universal face: Lo, silently,
Up cometh he, the never-closing eye!
Symbol of Deity, men could not be
Farthest from truth when they were kneeling unto thee!

Thou plaything of the child,
When from the water’s surface thou dost spring,
Thyself upon his chamber ceiling fling,
And there, in mazy dance and motion wild,
Disport thyself﻿—etherial, undefiled.
Capricious, like the thinkings of the child!
I am a child again, to think of thee
In thy consummate glee.
How I would play with thee, athirst to climb
On sloping ladders of thy moted beams,
When through the gray dust darting in long streams!
How marvel at the dusky glimmering red,
With which my closed fingers thou hadst made
Like rainy clouds that curtain the sun’s bed!
And how I loved thee always in the moon!
But most about the harvest-time,
When corn and moonlight made a mellow tune,
And thou wast grave and tender as a cooing dove!
And then the stars that flashed cold, deathless love!
And the ghost-stars that shimmered in the tide!
And more mysterious earthly stars,
That shone from windows of the hill and glen﻿—
Thee prisoned in with lattice-bars,
Mingling with household love and rest of weary men!
And still I am a child, thank God!﻿—to spy
Thee starry stream from bit of broken glass
Upon the brown earth undescried,
Is a found thing to me, a gladness high,
A spark that lights joy’s altar-fire within,
A thought of hope to prophecy akin,
That from my spirit fruitless will not pass.

===Chinese===

人们曾敬拜你。
波斯人在他的山顶上，
跪着等候你的太阳升起，
它那样安详，如同神明。
它只施予、不受馈赠，它临近了，
辽阔的大地等着它露面——
耐心的久候。先驱的荣光
跳上外围云层的山脊，
攀着云峰陡峭的高处向上。
蓦地，无数无声的欢笑拥上
万有的脸：看哪，静默地，
它升起来了，那只永不闭合的眼睛！
神性的象征——人跪拜你的时候，
离真理并不算太远！

你是孩童的玩伴；
当你从水面跃起，
把自己抛上他卧房的天花板，
在迷乱的舞步和狂野的 motion 里
自娱自乐——缥缈，无瑕，
任性，像孩子的念头一样！
一想到你在你那极致的欢畅里，
我就又成了孩子。
我多想同你玩要，渴盼着爬上
你那尘雾的光柱搭成的斜梯，
当你穿过灰尘，射成长长的光流！
我多惊叹那暗红的微光——
你把我的合拢的手指，变成
像雨云一样遮住太阳卧榻的云！
在月光里，我也永远爱你！
但最爱是在收获的时节，
当谷物同月光酿出一片柔和的调子，
你也像一只咕鸣的鸽子，庄重而温存！
还有那些闪烁着冷冷的、不死之爱的星辰！
还有在潮水里微闪的鬼影星！
还有更神秘的人间星辰，
从山间幽谷的窗里亮起——
你被囚在窗棂后面，
同家的爱、同劳人的安歇交融在一起！
感谢上帝，我至今还是个孩子——
能在棕色泥土上一块没人留意的碎玻璃里
窥见你星也似地流出，
对我来说就是一件拾到的宝贝，一场高远的欢喜，
一粒点着喜乐祭坛之火的火星，
一个近乎预言的希望之念，
它决不会从我心里白白流过。

===Original===

Thou art the joy of age:
Thy sun is dear when long the shadow falls.
Forth to its friendliness the old man crawls,
And, like the bird hung out in his poor cage
To gather song from radiance, in his chair
Sits by the door; and sitteth there
His soul within him, like a child that lies
Half dreaming, with half-open eyes,
At close of a long afternoon in summer﻿—
High ruins round him, ancient ruins, where
The raven is almost the only comer﻿—
Half dreams, half broods, in wonderment
At thy celestial ascent
Through rifted loop to light upon the gold
That waves its bloom in some high airy rent:
So dreams the old man’s soul, that is not old,
But sleepy mid the ruins that infold.

What soul-like changes, evanescent moods,
Upon the face of the still passive earth,
Its hills, and fields, and woods,
Thou with thy seasons and thy hours art ever calling forth!
Even like a lord of music bent
Over his instrument,
Giving to carol, now to tempest birth!
When, clear as holiness, the morning ray
Casts the rock’s dewy darkness at its feet,
Mottling with shadows all the mountain gray;
When, at the hour of sovereign noon,
Infinite silent cataracts sheet
Shadowless through the air of thunder-breeding June;
When now a yellower glory slanting passes
’Twixt longer shadows o’er the meadow grasses;
And now the moon lifts up her shining shield,
High on the peak of a cloud-hill revealed;
Now crescent, low, wandering sun-dazed away,
Unconscious of her own star-mingled ray,
Her still face seeming more to think than see,
Makes the pale world lie dreaming dreams of thee!
No mood, eternal or ephemeral,
But wakes obedient at thy silent call!

Of operative single power,
And simple unity the one emblem,
Yet all the colours that our passionate eyes devour,
In rainbow, moonbow, or in opal gem,
Are the melodious descant of divided thee.
Lo thee in yellow sands! Lo thee
In the blue air and sea!
In the green corn, with scarlet poppies lit,
Thy half-souls parted, patient thou dost sit.
Lo thee in dying triumphs of the west!
Lo thee in dew-drop’s tiny breast!
Thee on the vast white cloud that floats away,
Bearing upon its skirt a brown moon-ray!
Gold-regent, thou dost spendthrift throw
Thy hoardless wealth of gleam and glow!
The thousand hues and shades upon the flowers
Are all the pastime of thy leisure hours;
The jewelled ores in mines that hidden be,
Are dead till touched by thee.

===Chinese===

你是老年的欢喜：
影子拉长之后，你的太阳何等可亲。
老人爬向它的友善，
像笼中挂出的鸟儿向光取歌，坐在
门边的椅上；坐在那儿的
还有他心里的灵魂，像一个孩子躺着，
半梦半醒，眼睛半开半阖，
在夏日长长的午后将尽时分——
四周是高高的废墟，古老的废墟，那里
几乎只有乌鸦来临——
半梦半醒，出神地望着
你那升向天庭的路径：
穿过裂开的箭窗，落在那金色上，
它在某个高而透风的裂缝里摇曳生花；
老人的灵魂就这样梦着——它并不老，
只是在囚裹它的废墟中间倦得欲睡。

你在静止不动的大地脸上——
它的山丘、田野和树林——
唤出多少灵魂似的变迁、易逝的情绪，
凭你的季节、你的时辰，永远唤个不停！
就像一位音乐的主宰俯身
在他的乐器上，
时而给出歌唱，时而生出风暴！
当清晨的光线圣洁般澄澈，
把岩石湿黑的影子投在脚边，
把灰色的山点点缀满阴影；
当威严的正午时分，
无穷无声的瀑布如帷幔倾泻，
无影地穿过孕育雷霆的六月之气；
当一片更黄的荣光斜斜掠过，
在更长的影子间拂过草地；
当月亮举起她闪亮的盾，
高高地显在一座云山的峰顶；
当新月低垂，被太阳照得迷离，
浑然不觉自己那掺着星光的光线，
她那安静的脸像在沉思多于在看，
叫惨白的世界躺着梦见了你！
没有一种情绪，永恒也罢、片刻也罢，
不听你无声的召唤便醒来的！

你，独一运作之力，
单纯合一的惟一表记，
然而我们炽热的眼睛所吞下的万色，
在彩虹、月虹或蛋白宝石里，
都是你分开自身时的美妙的花腔。
看，你在黄色的沙里！看，你
在蓝空的蓝海里！
在绿谷间、点着红罂粟的谷地里，
你把半个灵魂分出去，自己安然端坐。
看你在西天垂死的凯旋里！
看你在露珠小小的胸怀里！
在那一大片飘远的白云上，
裙边还载着一道棕黄的月光！
黄金的君王啊，你挥霍地抛洒
你无穷无尽的闪耀与光辉！
千种色泽落在百花上，
都是你闲时辰的消遣；
矿里藏着的宝石矿石，
没被你碰过，便是死的。

===Original===

Everywhere,
Thou art lancing through the air!
Every atom from another
Takes thee, gives thee to his brother;
Continually,
Thou art wetting the wet sea,
Bathing its sluggish woods below,
Making the salt flowers bud and blow;
Silently,
Workest thou, and ardently,
Waking from the night of nought
Into being and to thought;
Influences
Every beam of thine dispenses,
Potent, subtle, reaching far,
Shooting different from each star.
Not an iron rod can lie
In circle of thy beamy eye,
But its look doth change it so
That it cannot choose but show
Thou, the worker, hast been there;
Yea, sometimes, on substance rare,
Thou dost leave thy ghostly mark
Even in what men call the dark.
Ever doing, ever showing,
Thou dost set our hearts a glowing﻿—
Universal something sent
To shadow forth the Excellent!

When the firstborn affections﻿—
Those winged seekers of the world within,
That search about in all directions,
Some bright thing for themselves to win﻿—
Through pathless woods, through home-bred fogs,
Through stony plains, through treacherous bogs,
Long, long, have followed faces fair,
Fair soul-less faces, vanished into air,
And darkness is around them and above,
Desolate of aught to love,
And through the gloom on every side,
Strange dismal forms are dim descried,
And the air is as the breath
From the lips of void-eyed Death,
And the knees are bowed in prayer
To the Stronger than despair﻿—
Then the ever-lifted cry,
“Give us light, or we shall die,”
Cometh to the Father’s ears,
And he hearkens, and he hears:﻿—
As some slow sun would glimmer forth
From sunless winter of the north,
We, hardly trusting hopeful eyes,
Discern and doubt the opening skies.
From a misty gray that lies on
Our dim future’s far horizon,
It grows a fresh aurora, sent
Up the spirit’s firmament,
Telling, through the vapours dun,
Of the coming, coming sun!
’Tis Truth awaking in the soul!
His Righteousness to make us whole!
And what shall we, this Truth receiving,
Though with but a faint believing,
Call it but eternal Light?
’Tis the morning, ’twas the night!

===Chinese===

处处，
你都在刺穿空气！
每一个原子从另一个原子
接住你，又把你传给弟兄；
不间断地，
你把湿的海弄得更湿，
为海底迟钝的丛林洗浴，
叫咸水的花开又花落；
无声地，
你工作着，并且炽热地，
把万物从虚无之夜
唤入存在与思想；
你每一道光
都散出影响，
有力，精微，及于辽远，
又从每颗星射出不同的光芒。
没有一根铁棒
能躺进你光眼的圈里
而不被你的注视改变——
它不由自主地显出：
你这位工作者到过那里；
是的，有时在稀有的物质上，
你甚至留下你幽灵似的印记，
就在人们叫作黑暗的地方。
永远作为，永远显现，
你叫我们的心灼灼发光——
一种普遍的什么，被差来
影射那至善者！

当头生的情感——
那些在内心世界里生翼的搜寻者，
四处探望，
想为自己赢得一件明亮之物——
穿过无路的树林，穿过家中生的雾，
穿过多石的荒原，穿过骗人的沼泽，
久久地追随过一张张美丽的脸，
美丽而无魂的脸，都消失在空气里；
黑暗围在他们四周、在他们头上，
再没有一点可爱之物，
而昏暗里四面八方，
隐隐辨出怪异凄惨的形影，
空气像空洞眼珠的死神
唇间呼出的气息，
双膝于是跪下祷告，
向那位比绝望更强者——
于是那永远上达的呼求，
「给我们光，不然我们就死了，」
传到父的耳中，
他俯听，他听见了：——
像一个迟缓的太阳，从北方
无日的严冬里微微透出，
我们几乎不敢信自己的眼睛，
看出了又怀疑那开启的天空。
在我们暗淡未来那遥远的地平线上
笼罩的灰雾里，
升起一遭新鲜的极光，
涌上灵魂的苍穹，
穿过暗沉的水汽，预告着
那将要来、将要来的太阳！
这是真理在灵魂里苏醒！
是他的义，使我们完全！
既然我们领受了这真理，
哪怕只怀着微弱的信，
又怎能只称它作永恒的光？
这已是清晨，那已是黑夜！

===Original===

All things most excellent
Are likened unto thee, excellent thing!
Yea, he who from the Father forth was sent,
Came like a lamp, to bring,
Across the winds and wastes of night,
The everlasting light.
Hail, Word of God, the telling of his thought!
Hail, Light of God, the making-visible!
Hail, far-transcending glory brought
In human form with man to dwell﻿—
Thy dazzling gone; thy power not less
To show, irradiate, and bless;
The gathering of the primal rays divine
Informing chaos, to a pure sunshine!

Dull horrid pools no motion making!
No bubble on the surface breaking!
The dead air lies, without a sound,
Heavy and moveless on the marshy ground.

Rushing winds and snow-like drift,
Forceful, formless, fierce, and swift!
Hair-like vapours madly riven!
Waters smitten into dust!
Lightning through the turmoil driven,
Aimless, useless, yet it must!

Gentle winds through forests calling!
Bright birds through the thick leaves glancing!
Solemn waves on sea-shores falling!
White sails on blue waters dancing!
Mountain streams glad music giving!
Children in the clear pool laving!
Yellow corn and green grass waving!
Long-haired, bright-eyed maidens living!
Light, O radiant, it is thou!
Light!﻿—we know our Father now!

Forming ever without form;
Showing, but thyself unseen;
Pouring stillness on the storm;
Breathing life where death had been!
If thy light thou didst draw in,
Death and Chaos soon were out,
Weltering o’er the slimy sea,
Riding on the whirlwind’s rout,
In wild unmaking energy!
God, be round us and within,
Fighting darkness, slaying sin.

===Chinese===

万样至美的东西
都被比作你，至美的东西！
是的，那位从父那里奉差而来的，
来时也像一盏灯，要把
那永远的光，带过夜的风与荒野。
欢迎你，上帝之道，他心意的言说！
欢迎你，上帝之光，那使他可见的！
欢迎你，远超一切的荣耀，
披着人的形体与人同住——
你的炫目敛去了；你显明、照耀、赐福的
能力却未曾稍减；
你把太初的神圣光线聚拢，
注入混沌，成为纯粹的日光！

死寂的臭水潭不起一丝波纹！
水面没有一个水泡破裂！
死气沉沉的空气悄无声息，
沉重而凝滞地压在泥沼地上。

狂风和雪一般的飞雪，
猛烈，无形，凶暴而迅疾！
发丝似的水汽被疯狂地撕碎！
水被击打成尘埃！
闪电驱进这乱局，
无目标，无用处，却又不能不闪！

柔风在林间呼唤！
明鸟在密叶间闪现！
庄严的浪在岸边拍落！
白帆在蓝水上起舞！
山溪奏出欢快的音乐！
孩子们在清潭里洗浴！
金黄的谷、青绿的草起伏摇摆！
长发亮眼的少女们活着！
光啊，璀璨的，那就是你！
光！——如今我们认得我们的父了！

永远赋形而自己无形；
显现，而自己不被看见；
把静密倾在风暴上；
在死过的地方吹入生命！
你若收回你的光，
死与混沌立刻就脱出，
在黏滑的海上翻腾，
乘着旋风的溃军奔突，
带着狂野的毁灭之能！
上帝啊，环绕我们，住在我们里面，
与黑暗争战，把罪击杀。

===Original===

Father of Lights, high-lost, unspeakable,
On whom no changing shadow ever fell!
Thy light we know not, are content to see;
Thee we know not, and are content to be!﻿—
Nay, nay! until we know thee, not content are we!
But, when thy wisdom cannot be expressed,
Shall we imagine darkness in thy breast?
Our hearts awake and witness loud for thee!
The very shadows on our souls that lie,
Good witness to the light supernal bear;
The something ’twixt us and the sky
Could cast no shadow if light were not there!
If children tremble in the night,
It is because their God is light!
The shining of the common day
Is mystery still, howe’er it ebb and flow﻿—
Behind the seeing orb, the secret lies:
Thy living light’s eternal play,
Its motions, whence or whither, who shall know?﻿—
Behind the life itself, its fountains rise!
In thee, the Light, the darkness hath no place;
And we have seen thee in the Saviour’s face.

Enlighten me, O Light!﻿—why art thou such?
Why art thou awful to our eyes, and sweet?
Cherished as love, and slaying with a touch?
Why in thee do the known and unknown meet?
Why swift and tender, strong and delicate?
Simple as truth, yet manifold in might?
Why does one love thee, and another hate?
Why cleave my words to the portals of my speech
When I a goodly matter would indite?
Why mounts my thought of thee beyond my reach?
—In vain to follow thee, I thee beseech,
For God is light.

===Chinese===

众光之父，高不可及、不可言说，
在你身上永无变动的影子落下！
你的光我们不认识，见了便已满足；
你自己我们不认识，存在便已满足！——
不，不！不认识你，我们就永不能满足！
可你的智慧既无法表述，
难道我们就要想象你胸中是黑暗么？
我们的心醒着，高声为你作证！
连覆在我们灵魂上的那些影子，
