Outstretched in fear upon a bank,
Lest, gazing up on awful space,
I should fall down into the blank,
From off the round world’s face.

And let my brothers come with me
To play our old games yet again,
Children on earth, more full of glee
That we in heaven are men.

===Chinese===

昼与年的一切声色，
一切人群与形相，每片叶每颗宝石，
都是你的，上帝啊，我也不怕
拿它们同你交谈。

你的心太伟大，不会轻看——
你的一日环抱几个世纪；
从我们称作微小的事物里，你的眼睛
看见伟大之物向外张望。

所以我唱的这首祷告的歌，
可以字句井然地到你面前：
它虽出身卑微，却无须
战栗地攀着自己的琴弦。

我想，凡受造的没有一样失丧；
没有一轮照过的月亮，
没有一朵掠过我眼睛的云，
不曾进到我的灵魂。

那些逝去的年岁，都收存在
你这只匣子里——我昏暗的灵魂里；
终有一天，你要把钥匙一转，
给我看那闪亮的全部。

可它们即使在我里面死了，也活在
你里面；你的比喻就是——时间、
世界、形相——一切给我
思绪和这首韵语的东西。

而在我所谓的死之后，
当我渡过那未知的海，
某个 Heaven 的早晨，怀着盼望的呼吸，
这首祷告将向你升起。

哦，让我再作一回孩子，
在幽暗里梦见盛大的荣光，
梦见太阳月亮星星
给我低矮的屋子作顶。

哦，再唤回那些月亮，它们跨过
蓝色的深渊，躲在灰雾后面爬行；
给我看我错过的庄严天空——
因为我那时在你里面睡着。

再让聚拢的荣光涨起，
抬起世界昏暗的东方之眼；
再让拉长的影子宣告
它的时候到了，该死了。

可先给我看——哦，蒙福的景象！——
我幼年那座低矮的房子：
冬天在夜里派来狂野的风，
把雪堆抛上屋顶；

或无声地带来一场美丽的混沌，
满的、无形的、满是奇形，
闪光空气里幽灵似的白树——
一座沉睡风暴的殿堂。

那里，一个带露的清晨骤然破晓；
一个人正在翻土；
春天就这样在我们心里生了，
它一路爬过严寒来到那里。

在后来的青春岁月里，春天
成了一切形相的形相，
为了那些时而迸出真理、
时而在风暴里叹息的心。

让我顺着欢畅的年岁走下去，
脚边绕着一队队的雏菊；
放风筝，或者在穹拱
夏日暑气的光焰里，

伸展开四肢，伏在堤上害怕，
生怕仰望着可畏的太空，
我会从浑圆世界的脸上
跌进那一片空无。

也让我的兄弟们同我一起来，
把旧日的游戏再玩一遍，
作地上的孩子，却更欢——
因为我们在 Heaven 里是成人。

===Original===

If then should come the shadowy death,
Take one of us and go,
We left would say, under our breath,
“It is a dream, you know!”

“And in the dream our brother’s gone
Upstairs: he heard our father call;
For one by one we go alone,
Till he has gathered all.”

Father, in joy our knees we bow:
This earth is not a place of tombs:
We are but in the nursery now;
They in the upper rooms.

For are we not at home in thee,
And all this world a visioned show;
That, knowing what Abroad is, we
What Home is too may know?

And at thy feet I sit, O Lord,
As once of old, in moonlight pale,
I at my father’s sat, and heard
Him read a lofty tale.

On with my history let me go,
And reap again the gliding years,
Gather great noontide’s joyous glow,
Eve’s love-contented tears;

One afternoon sit pondering
In that old chair, in that old room,
Where passing pigeon’s sudden wing
Flashed lightning through the gloom;

There try once more, with effort vain,
To mould in one perplexed things;
There find the solace yet again
Hope in the Father brings;

Or mount and ride in sun and wind,
Through desert moors, hills bleak and high,
Where wandering vapours fall, and find
In me another sky!

For so thy Visible grew mine,
Though half its power I could not know;
And in me wrought a work divine,
Which thou hadst ordered so;

Giving me cups that would not spill,
But water carry and yield again;
New bottles with new wine to fill
For comfort of thy men.

But if thou thus restore the past
One hour, for me to wander in,
I now bethink me at the last﻿—
O Lord, leave out the sin.

And with the thought comes doubt, my God:
Shall I the whole desire to see,
And walk once more, of that hill-road
By which I went to thee?

Now far from my old northern land,
I live where gentle winters pass;
Where green seas lave a wealthy strand,
And unsown is the grass;

Where gorgeous sunsets claim the scope
Of gazing heaven to spread their show,
Hang scarlet clouds in the topmost cope,
With fringes flaming low;

With one beside me in whose eyes
Once more old Nature finds a home;
There treasures up her changeful skies,
Her phosphorescent foam.

O’er a new joy this day we bend,
Soft power from heaven our souls to lift;
A wondering wonder thou dost lend
With loan outpassing gift﻿—

A little child. She sees the sun﻿—
Once more incarnates thy old law:
One born of two, two born in one,
Shall into one three draw.

===Chinese===

倘若那时影影绰绰的死来了，
带走我们中的一个、走开，
留下的会压低了声音说：
「你知道，这是一场梦！」

「在梦里，我们的弟兄上楼去了：
他听见父亲在叫他；
因为我们是一个一个单独去的，
直到他把我们都聚齐。」

父啊，我们欢欢喜喜屈膝：
这大地不是一片坟场：
我们如今还在育儿室里；
他们在楼上的房间里。

因为我们岂不是在你里面在家，
这整个世界不过一场看得见的戏，
好叫我们知道了什么是「在外」，
也就知道了什么是「在家」？

主啊，我坐在你脚前，
如同多年前，在淡淡的月光里，
我坐在父亲脚前，听他
读一个崇高的故事。

让我顺着我的历史走下去，
把流逝的年岁再收一遍，
收大正午欢畅的光焰，
收黄昏心满意足的泪；

某个下午，再坐在那把旧椅子上，
在那间旧屋里沉思，
在那里，鸽子突然的翅膀
像闪电掠过幽暗；

在那里，再作一次徒劳的尝试，
把纷乱的事物捏成一个；
在那里，再得一次父所赐的
盼望带来的安慰；

或者在太阳和风里骑马出去，
穿过荒凉的沼原、荒凉的高山，
在那里，游荡的水汽落下，
而在我里面找到另一片天！

因为这样，你那可见的世界成了我的，
虽然它一半的伟力我并不能知；
它在我里面做成了神圣的工，
那是你这样安排的；

你给我不会泼洒的杯子，
只把水带来、再奉还；
给我新皮袋盛新酒，
好安慰你的人类。

可你若这样把过去归还给我，
一个钟头，任我在里面游荡，
那末了我想起一件事——
主啊，请把罪留下，别带来。

可这念头一起，疑惑也来了，我的上帝：
我究竟想不想看那全部，
再去走一遍那条山路——
我由它走到你那里去的山路？

如今我远离我北方的故土，
住在一座冬天温和的地方；
绿色的海洗着富庶的沙滩，
青草不用播种；

那里华美的落日占用
整个凝望的天堂来铺陈它们的演出，
把猩红的云挂上最高的穹顶，
底边燃着低低的火；

我身边有一个人，在她眼睛里
古老的 Nature 再一次找到了家；
在那里她收藏她变幻的天空，
收藏她磷光的浪沫。

今天我们俯向一个新的欢喜，
一种柔和的、从 Heaven 来的能力，举起我们的灵魂；
你借出一件惊奇中的惊奇，
一笔远超礼物的借贷——

一个小小孩儿。她看见了太阳——
再一次成全你古老的律法：
由二生一，由一生二，
必将把三拉成一体。

===Original===

But is there no day creeping on
Which I should tremble to renew?
I thank thee, Lord, for what is gone﻿—
Thine is the future too!

And are we not at home in Thee,
And all this world a visioned show,
That, knowing what Abroad is, we
What Home is too may know?

===Chinese===

可是，难道没有一个日子正在逼近，
叫我不敢重新经历？
主啊，我为已往的感谢你——
将来也是你的！

我们岂不是在你里面在家，
这整个世界不过一场看得见的戏，
好叫我们知道了什么是「在外」，
也就知道了什么是「在家」？

## Far and Near / 远与近
===Original===

The fact which suggested this poem is related by Clarke in his
*Travels*
.

I

Blue sky above, blue sea below,
Far off, the old Nile’s mouth,
’Twas a blue world, wherein did blow
A soft wind from the south.

In great and solemn heaves the mass
Of pulsing ocean beat,
Unwrinkled as the sea of glass
Beneath the holy feet.

With forward leaning of desire
The ship sped calmly on,
A pilgrim strong that would not tire
Or hasten to be gone.

II

List!﻿—on the wave!﻿—what can they be,
Those sounds that hither glide?
No lovers whisper tremulously
Under the ship’s round side!

No sail across the dark blue sphere
Holds white obedient way;
No far-fled, sharp-winged boat is near,
No following fish at play!

’Tis not the rippling of the wave,
Nor sighing of the cords;
No winds or waters ever gave
A murmur so like words;

Nor wings of birds that northward strain,
Nor talk of hidden crew:
The traveller questioned, but in vain﻿—
He found no answer true.

III

A hundred level miles away,
On Egypt’s troubled shore,
Two nations fought, that sunny day,
With bellowing cannons’ roar.

The fluttering whisper, low and near,
Was that far battle’s blare;
A lipping, rippling motion here,
The blasting thunder there.

IV

Can this dull sighing in my breast
So faint and undefined,
Be the worn edge of far unrest
Borne on the spirit’s wind?

The uproar of high battle fought
Betwixt the bond and free,
The thunderous roll of armed thought
Dwarfed to an ache in me?

===Chinese===

促成这首诗的那件实事，克拉克在他的《游记》里有所记述。

一

头上蓝天，脚下碧海，
远处，是尼罗河古老的河口，
这是一个蓝色的世界，一股柔和的风
从南方吹来。

磅礴而庄严地，那一大片
搏动的海洋起伏着，
平滑无皱，如同那玻璃之海
在圣脚之下。

怀着前倾的渴望，
船从容地前行，
一个不知疲倦的朝圣者，
也不急于赶完路程。

二

听！——在海波上！——那滑近来的
会是什么声音？
不是恋人在船圆圆的侧影下
颤声低语！

没有一片帆横过深蓝的穹苍
顺从地划着白色的航迹；
没有远逃的疾翼小船靠近，
没有尾随的鱼在嬉戏！

那不是海波的涟漪，
也不是缆索的叹息；
风和水从来不曾发出
这样近似言语的低鸣；

也不是向北振翅的鸟群，
也不是藏身船员的谈笑：
旅人追问，却是徒然——
他寻不到真实的答案。

三

一百里格平坦的海路之外，
在埃及骚动的海岸上，
那个晴朗的日子，两个民族
在轰隆的炮声中厮杀。

这低回切近的飘忽低语，
正是那远方战斗的喧嚣；
这里一番舔舐般的涟漪微动，
那边是摧折的雷霆。

四

我胸中这声沉闷的叹息，
这样微弱而无从辨认，
难道竟是远方动乱的残响，
乘着心灵的風传来？

那奴隶与自由人之间
鏖战正酣的呐喊，
那武装思想的隆隆滚动的雷
竟萎缩成我体内的一阵隐痛？

## My Room / 我的房间
===Original===

*To G. E. M.*

’Tis a little room, my friend﻿—
Baby walks from end to end;
All the things look sadly real
This hot noontide unideal;
Vaporous heat from cope to basement
All you see outside the casement,
Save one house all mud-becrusted,
And a street all drought-bedusted!
There behold its happiest vision,
Trickling water-cart’s derision!
Shut we out the staring space,
Draw the curtains in its face!

Close the eyelids of the room,
Fill it with a scarlet gloom:
Lo, the walls with warm flush dyed!
Lo, the ceiling glorified,
As when, lost in tenderest pinks,
White rose on the red rose thinks!
But beneath, a hue right rosy,
Red as a geranium-posy,
Stains the air with power estranging,
Known with unknown clouding, changing.
See in ruddy atmosphere
Commonplaceness disappear!
Look around on either hand﻿—
Are we not in fairyland?

On that couch, inwrapt in mist
Of vaporized amethyst,
Lie, as in a rose’s heart:
Secret things I would impart;
Any time you would believe them﻿—
Easier, though, you will receive them
Bathed in glowing mystery
Of the red light shadowy;
For this ruby-hearted hue,
Sanguine core of all the true,
Which for love the heart would plunder
Is the very hue of wonder;
This dissolving dreamy red
Is the self-same radiance shed
From the heart of poet young,
Glowing poppy sunlight-stung:
If in light you make a schism
’Tis the deepest in the prism.

This poor-seeming room, in fact
Is of marvels all compact,
So disguised by common daylight
By its disenchanting gray light,
Only eyes that see by shining,
Inside pierce to its live lining.
Loftiest observatory
Ne’er unveiled such hidden glory;
Never sage’s furnace-kitchen
Magic wonders was so rich in;
Never book of wizard old
Clasped such in its iron hold.

===Chinese===

致 G. E. M.

这是一间小小的房间，我的朋友——
婴儿从这头走到那头；
一切东西在炎热的正午里
都显得乏味而确凿，毫无诗意；
从顶到地下室，蒸腾的热气
笼罩着窗外你望见的万物，
除了一座糊满泥污的房屋，
和一条被干旱蒙上尘土的街道！
看哪，那儿它最快乐的幻象——
洒水车淌着水，一路嘲笑！
让我们关上那刺目的空旷，
拉起窗帘挡住它的脸！n
合上这房间的眼睑，
让它充满一片猩红的幽暗：
看，四壁染上温暖的红晕！
看，天花板也变得荣耀，
仿佛白色玫瑰沉入最温柔的粉红，
心里思念着红玫瑰！
而在下方，一色纯正的玫瑰红，
红得像一束天竺葵，
以一种令人出神的力量染着空气，
已知与未知交相明灭、变幻。
看在这红彤彤的氛围里，
平庸琐碎尽数消隐！
向左右两边环顾——
我们岂不是身在仙境？n
那张卧榻，裹在
汽化的紫水晶的雾里，
躺在其中如同躺在玫瑰的花心：
我愿意吐露一些秘密；
任何时候你都可能相信它们——
不过，若让它们浸在
红光幽影的灼灼神秘里，
你会更容易领受；
因为这颗红宝石心的颜色，
是一切真实的核心，
为了爱甘愿掏出心来的人，
正需要这惊奇之色；
这消融一切的梦幻的红，
正是年轻诗人心中
被罂粟般的阳光灼亮的
那同一道光芒：
若你把光一刀劈开，
它是棱镜里最深的一色。n
这看似寒碜的房间，其实
处处由奇迹拼合而成，
只是被平常的白昼、
被它令人幻灭的灰光伪装起来，
唯有以发光看物的眼睛，
才能穿透它活着的衬里。
最高的天文台
也不曾揭开这样的隐秘荣光；
圣贤的炉灶厨房里
也从没有这么多魔法奇珍；
老巫师的书中
也从没有扣住过这么多，在铁扣之下。

===Original===

See that case against the wall,
Darkly-dull-purpureal!﻿—
A piano to the prosy,
But to us in twilight rosy﻿—
What?﻿—A cave where Nereids lie,
Naiads, Dryads, Oreads sigh,
Dreaming of the time when they
Danced in forest and in bay.
In that chest before your eyes
Nature self-enchanted lies;﻿—
Lofty days of summer splendour;
Low dim eves of opal tender;
Airy hunts of cloud and wind;
Brooding storm﻿—below, behind;
Awful hills and midnight woods;
Sunny rains in solitudes;
Babbling streams in forests hoar;
Seven-hued icebergs; oceans frore.﻿—
Yes; did I not say “enchanted,”
That is, hid away till wanted?
Do you hear a low-voiced singing?
’Tis the sorceress’s, flinging
Spells around her baby’s riot,
Binding her in moveless quiet:﻿—
She at will can disenchant them,
And to prayer believing grant them.

You believe me: soon will night
Free her hands for fair delight;
Then invoke her﻿—she will come.
Fold your arms, be blind and dumb.
She will bring a book of spells
Writ like crabbed oracles;
Like Sabrina’s will her hands
Thaw the power of charmed bands.
First will ransomed music rush
Round thee in a glorious gush;
Next, upon its waves will sally,
Like a stream-god down a valley,
Nature’s self, the formless former,
Nature’s self, the peaceful stormer;
She will enter, captive take thee,
And both one and many make thee,
One by softest power to still thee,
Many by the thoughts that fill thee.﻿—
Let me guess three guesses where
She her prisoner will bear!

On a mountain-top you stand
Gazing o’er a sunny land;
Shining streams, like silver veins,
Rise in dells and meet in plains;
Up yon brook a hollow lies
Dumb as love that fears surprise;
Moorland tracts of broken ground
O’er it rise and close it round:
He who climbs from bosky dale
Hears the foggy breezes wail.
Yes, thou know’st the nest of love,
Know’st the waste around, above!
In thy soul or in thy past,
Straight it melts into the vast,
Quickly vanishes away
In a gloom of darkening gray.

===Chinese===

看那靠墙的匣子，
暗沉而发闷的紫色！——
在乏味的人眼里是一架钢琴，
可在我们玫瑰色的暮霭里——
是什么？——是一个洞穴，涅瑞伊得斯们躺在里面，
纳伊阿德斯、德律阿得斯、俄瑞阿得斯在其中叹息，
梦着当年她们在森林里、在海湾里
翩翩起舞的时光。
在你眼前的那口箱子里，
躺着自我施了魔的自然；——
夏日辉煌的崇高白昼；
蛋白石般温柔的低暗黄昏；
云与风的轻盈狩猎；
酝酿的风暴——在下方，在身后；
可畏的群山与午夜森林；
幽寂里的明媚阵雨；
古老森林中潺潺的溪流；
七彩的冰山；冻结的海洋。——
是的；我方才不是说「施了魔」么，
也就是说，藏起来等到需要时再取？
你听见一阵低声的歌唱吗？
那是女巫的歌声，正把魔咒
撒向她婴孩的喧闹，
把她捆入一动不动的安静：——
她随时可以解开魔咒，
应许给祈求而相信的人。n
你相信我：夜晚很快就会
腾出她的双手，好安排美好的欢愉；
那时便唤她——她自会前来。
合起双臂，装聋作哑。
她会带来一本咒语之书，
写得像难解的神谕；
她的双手会像萨布丽娜的手一样，
消解魔缚的力量。
先是获赎的音乐将
以壮丽的激流涌向你；
接着，踏着音乐的波浪，
像河神顺流下到山谷，
自然之灵亲自出场，那无形造物的造物者，
自然之灵，那平和的攻击者；
她将进来，把你俘虏，
使你既成一又成多，
以最柔软的力量使你安静为一，
又以充盈的思想使你为多。——
让我猜上三猜，她会
把她囚住的你带往何方！n
你站在一座山巅上
俯瞰一片阳光普照的大地；
闪亮的溪流像银色的脉络，
从洼地涌起，在平原汇聚；
沿那小溪上行有一处幽谷，
静默如害怕惊扰的爱情；
一片片破碎的高沼地
在它四周隆起、将它围拢：
从树木葱茏的谷底攀上来的人，
听得见雾蒙蒙的风在哀号。
是的，你认得那爱之巢，
认得四围和头顶的荒原！
它就在你的灵魂里或你的过往里，
倏然融进浩茫，
很快消失在
一片渐深的灰色幽暗中。

===Original===

Sinks the sadness into rest,
Ripple like on water’s breast:
Mother’s bosom rests the daughter﻿—
Grief the ripple, love the water;
And thy brain like wind-harp lies
Breathed upon from distant skies,
Till, soft-gathering, visions new
Grow like vapours in the blue:
White forms, flushing hyacinthine,
Move in motions labyrinthine;
With an airy wishful gait
On the counter-motion wait;
Sweet restraint and action free
Show the law of liberty;
Master of the revel still
The obedient, perfect will;
Hating smallest thing awry,
Breathing, breeding harmony;
While the god-like graceful feet,
For such mazy marvelling meet,
Press from air a shining sound,
Rippling after, lingering round:
Hair afloat and arms aloft
Fill the chord of movement soft.

Gone the measure polyhedral!
Towers aloft a fair cathedral!
Every arch﻿—like praying arms
Upward flung in love’s alarms,
Knit by clasped hands o’erhead﻿—
Heaves to heaven a weight of dread;
In thee, like an angel-crowd,
Grows the music, praying loud,
Swells thy spirit with devotion
As a strong wind swells the ocean,
Sweeps the visioned pile away,
Leaves thy heart alone to pray.

As the prayer grows dim and dies
Like a sunset from the skies,
Glides another change of mood
O’er thy inner solitude:
Girt with Music’s magic zone,
Lo, thyself magician grown!
Open-eyed thou walk’st through earth
Brooding on the aeonian birth
Of a thousand wonder-things
In divine dusk of their springs:
Half thou seest whence they flow,
Half thou seest whither go﻿—
Nature’s consciousness, whereby
On herself she turns her eye,
Hoping for all men and thee
Perfected, pure harmony.

But when, sinking slow, the sun
Leaves the glowing curtain dun,
I, of prophet-insight reft,
Shall be dull and dreamless left;
I must hasten proof on proof,
Weaving in the warp my woof!

What are those upon the wall,
Ranged in rows symmetrical?
Through the wall of things external
Posterns they to the supernal;
Through Earth’s battlemented height
Loopholes to the Infinite;
Through locked gates of place and time,
Wickets to the eternal prime
Lying round the noisy day
Full of silences alway.

That, my friend? Now, it is curious
You should hit upon the spurious!
’Tis a door to nowhere, that;
Never soul went in thereat;
Lies behind, a limy wall
Hung with cobwebs, that is all.

===Chinese===

忧伤沉入安息，
如水面的涟漪：
母亲的胸怀安放着女儿——
悲伤是那涟漪，爱是那水；
你的头脑像一具风神琴静卧，
被遥远的天际吹拂，
直到新的幻象轻轻聚拢，
像雾气在碧空里生长：
洁白的身影，泛着风信子的绯红，
在迷宫般的动作中移动；
带着轻盈而含盼的步态，
静候着逆势的节拍；
甜蜜的节制与自如的行动，
昭示着自由的法则；
始终是狂欢的主宰——
那顺从而完美的意志；
憎恶毫厘的差失，
吐纳着、孕育着和谐；
那一双双神般优美的脚，
正与这令人惊叹的回旋相配，
从空气中踏出清亮的声音，
荡漾随后，萦绕四周：
飘扬的头发，高举的手臂，
奏满了柔和动作的和弦。n
多面体的舞阵消散了！
耸立起一座美丽的大教堂！
每一道拱——像祈求的双臂
在爱的惊惶中向上高举，
被头顶合十的手紧紧相连——
向天空扛起一份沉重的敬畏；
在你里面，仿佛一群天使，
音乐生长，高声祈祷，
你的灵被虔诚充满而鼓胀，
如同强风吹鼓海洋，
随后扫走那幻象的殿宇，
只留下你的心独自祈祷。n
当祈祷像落日
从天边渐渐暗去、消逝，
另一种心绪又悄然
滑过你内在的孤独：
束着音乐的魔带，
看，你自己成了魔术师！
你睁着眼走过大地，
沉思着万千奇物
在它们源泉的神圣幽暗中的太初之生：
它们从何处涌来，你看见一半，
它们向何处而去，你看见一半——
那是自然的意识，借此
她把目光转向自身，
为众生、也为你祈望
那成全了的、纯净的和谐。n
但当太阳缓缓沉落，
留下灼灼却晦暗的幕帐，
而我，被夺去先知的视力，
将变得迟钝而无梦；
我必须赶紧拿出证明又证明，
在经线上织进我的纬线！n
墙上那一排排的东西，
排列得整整齐齐，是什么？
穿过事物的外墙，
它们是通往上界的小门；
穿过大地垛堞般的高墙，
它们是眺望无限的箭窗；
穿过被锁的空间与时间之门，
它们是通向永恒太初的小门，
那太初环卧在喧嚣的白昼四周，
永远充满寂静。n
那个吗，我的朋友？说来也怪，
你偏偏撞上一个假的！
那是一扇通向乌有的门；
从来没有灵魂进去过；
门后是一堵抹着灰泥的墙，
挂着蛛网，仅此而已。

===Original===

Do not open that one yet,
Wait until the sun is set.
If you careless lift its latch
Glimpse of nothing will you catch;
Mere negation, blank of hue,
Out of it will stare at you;
Wait, I say, the coming night,
Fittest time for second sight,
Then the wide eyes of the mind
See far down the Spirit’s wind.
You may have to strain and pull,
Force and lift with cunning tool,
Ere the rugged, ill-joined door
Yield the sight it stands before:
When at last, with grating sweep,
Wide it swings﻿—behold, the deep!

Thou art standing on the verge
Where material things emerge;
Hoary silence, lightning fleet,
Shooteth hellward at thy feet!
Fear not thou whose life is truth,
Gazing will renew thy youth;
But where sin of soul or flesh
Held a man in spider-mesh,
It would drag him through that door,
Give him up to loreless lore,
Ages to be blown and hurled
Up and down a deedless world.

Ah, your eyes ask how I brook
Doors that are not, doors to look!
That is whither I was tending,
And it brings me to good ending.

Baby is the cause of this;
Odd it seems, but so it is;﻿—
Baby, with her pretty prate
Molten, half articulate,
Full of hints, suggestions, catches,
Broken verse, and music snatches!
She, like seraph gone astray,
Must be shown the homeward way;
Plant of heaven, she, rooted lowly,
Must put forth a blossom holy,
Must, through culture high and steady,
Slow unfold a gracious lady;
She must therefore live in wonder,
See nought common up or under;
She the moon and stars and sea,
Worm and butterfly and bee,
Yea, the sparkle in a stone,
Must with marvel look upon;
She must love, in heaven’s own blueness,
Both the colour and the newness;
Must each day from darkness break,
Often often come awake,
Never with her childhood part,
Change the brain, but keep the heart.

So, from lips and hands and looks,
She must learn to honour books,
Turn the leaves with careful fingers,
Never lean where long she lingers;
But when she is old enough
She must learn the lesson rough
That to seem is not to be,
As to know is not to see;
That to man or book, appearing
Gives no title to revering;
That a pump is not a well,
Nor a priest an oracle:
This to leave safe in her mind,
I will take her and go find
Certain no-books, dreary apes,
Tell her they are mere mock-shapes
No more to be honoured by her
But be laid upon the fire;
Book-appearance must not hinder
Their consuming to a cinder.

===Chinese===

先别打开那一扇，
且等到太阳落山。
你若漫不经心拉起门闩，
什么也窥不见；
只有纯粹的虚无、无色的空白，
会从里面瞪视着你；
我说，等夜晚降临，
那才是 Second Sight 最相宜的时辰，
那时心灵睁大的眼睛
能望进圣灵之风的最深处。
你可能得又拉又拽，
用巧妙的工具又撬又抬，
那扇粗陋、拼接不齐的门
才肯让出它挡住的景观：
当它终于带着吱嘎的扫荡声
豁然洞开——看哪，那深渊！n
你正站在万物
涌现的物质的边缘；
苍古的沉寂，迅疾如闪电，
在你脚边射向地狱！
别怕，你这以真实为生的人，
凝望将使你重获青春；
但若有谁的灵魂或肉体之罪
曾把他缠进蛛网，
这景象便会拖着他穿过那扇门，
把他交给无学问的学问，
让他在千万年里被吹卷、被抛掷，
在一个无功业的世界里上下翻滚。n
啊，你的眼睛在问，我怎么受得了
那些不存在的门、用来看的门！
这正是我方才要说下去的话头，
它也正好把我引到圆满的收束。n
这一切的缘由是那婴孩；
说来奇怪，但事情就是这样；——
婴孩，用她可爱的咿呀，
半是熔化、半是含混的话语，
满是暗示、联想和接引，
夹着断续的诗句和音乐的片段！
她像一位迷途的天使，
必须有人指给她回家的路；
她这株天国的植物，扎根在低处，
必须开出一朵神圣的花，
必须经过高洁而不懈的栽培，
慢慢舒展成一位优雅的淑女；
因此她必须生活在惊奇之中，
看上下四方无一物是平常；
月亮、星星和大海，
毛虫、蝴蝶和蜜蜂，
甚至石头里的一星闪光，
她都必须带着惊叹凝望；
她必须爱，在那天堂的蓝色里，
既爱那颜色，也爱那崭新；
她必须每天从黑暗中醒来，
一次又一次地清醒过来，
永远不与童年分别，
头脑尽管变，初心却要长存。n
于是，从嘴唇、双手和眼神里，
她必须学会敬重书籍，
用细心的小手翻动书页，
在久留之处永不俯倚；
可等地长大一些，
她还须学会那门粗粝的功课：
看似如何并不等于真是如何，
正如知道并不等于看见；
无论对人对书，外表的样子
都不能授予被敬重的权利；
水泵并不就是水井，
祭司也并不就是神谕：
为了把这一点稳妥地留在她心里，
我要带她去寻几本
徒有其表的「非书」，那些阴沉的猴子，
告诉她它们只是徒具其形，
再也不配她的敬重，
只该搁到火上去；
书的外表不能阻挠
它们烧成一块焦炭。

===Original===

Would you see the small immortal
One short pace within Time’s portal?
I will fetch her.﻿—Is she white?
Solemn? true? a light in light?
See! is not her lily-skin
White as whitest ermelin
Washed in palest thinnest rose?
Very thought of God she goes,
Ne’er to wander, in her dance,
Out of his love-radiance!

But, my friend, I’ve rattled plenty
To suffice for mornings twenty!
I should never stop of course,
Therefore stop I will perforce.﻿—
If I led them up, choragic,
To reveal their nature magic,
Twenty things, past contradiction,
Yet would prove I spoke no fiction
Of the room’s belongings cryptic
Read by light apocalyptic:
There is that strange thing, glass-masked,
With continual questions tasked,
Ticking with untiring rock:
It is called an eight-day clock,
But to me the thing appears
Busy winding up the years,
Drawing on with coiling chain
The epiphany again.

===Chinese===

你想看看那小小的不朽者吗，
在时间之门内一步之遥的地方？
我去把她抱来。——她可是洁白？
庄重？真诚？光中之光？
看！她那百合般的肌肤
岂不白得像最白的貂皮，
在最淡最薄的玫瑰色里洗过？
她行走如同上帝的一个念头，
在她的舞蹈里，永远
不会流浪到他爱的光辉之外！n
可是，我的朋友，我已经絮叨得
够二十个早晨用的了！
我当然永远也停不下来，
所以只好强迫自己打住。——
我本可以一件一件地召唤它们，
让它们列队登台，显出各自的本性，
二十件东西，无可辩驳地
证明我方才说的一切并非虚构，
证明这房间里那些隐秘的什物，
须以启示录之光来研读：
比如那件蒙着玻璃面具的怪物，
被无休止的提问驱使着，
滴答作响，不知疲倦地摇摆：
人们叫它八天上弦的时钟，
可在我眼里，这东西分明
在忙着给岁月上紧发条，
用盘卷的链条，把又一次显现
一路牵引过来。

## Sympathy / 同情
===Original===

Grief held me silent in my seat;
I neither moved nor smiled:
Joy held her silent at my feet,
My shining lily-child.

She raised her face and looked in mine;
She deemed herself denied;
The door was shut, there was no shine;
Poor she was left outside!

Once, twice, three times, with infant grace
Her lips my name did mould;
Her face was pulling at my face﻿—
She was but ten months old.

I saw; the sight rebuked my sighs;
It made me think﻿—Does God
Need help from his poor children’s eyes
To ease him of his load?

Ah, if he did, how seldom then
The Father would be glad!
If comfort lay in the eyes of men,
He little comfort had!

We cry to him in evil case,
When comfort sore we lack;
And when we troubled seek his face,
Consoled he sends us back;

Nor waits for prayer to rise and climb﻿—
He wakes the sleeping prayer;
He is our father all the time,
And servant everywhere.

I looked not up; foreboding hid
Kept down my heart the while;
’Twas he looked up; my Father did
Smile in my infant’s smile.

===Chinese===

忧伤使我默默坐在座位上；
我既不动也不笑：
喜悦使她默默在我脚边，
我那闪亮的百合般的孩子。

她仰起脸来看我的脸；
她以为自己被拒绝了；
门关着，里面没有光；
可怜的她被留在了门外！

一次，两次，三次，带着婴孩的娇憨，
她的嘴唇把我的名字轻轻塑出；
她的脸正拉扯着我的脸——
她才不过十个月大。

我看见了；这情景责备了我的叹息；
它使我思索——难道上帝
也需要他可怜的孩子们眼中的慰藉，
好卸下他的重担？

啊，若他真的需要，那天父
将多么难得欢欣！
若安慰只在世人的眼里，
他所得的安慰何其稀少！

我们在厄运中向他呼求，
在我们渴亟安慰的时候；
而当我们带着烦忧寻求他的脸，
他已得了安慰送我们回来；

他也不等祷告升起、攀缘——
是他唤醒沉睡的祷告；
他自始至终是我们的父亲，
又在处处做我们的仆人。

我没有抬头；郁结的预感
一直压着我的心；
是他抬起了头；是我的天父
在我婴孩的微笑里微笑。

## Little Elfie / 小埃尔菲
===Original===

I have a puppet-jointed child,
She’s but three half-years old;
Through lawless hair her eyes gleam wild
With looks both shy and bold.

Like little imps, her tiny hands
Dart out and push and take;
Chide her﻿—a trembling thing she stands,
And like two leaves they shake.

But to her mind a minute gone
Is like a year ago;
And when you lift your eyes anon,
Anon you must say “No!”

Sometimes, though not oppressed with care,
She has her sleepless fits;
Then, blanket-swathed, in that round chair
The elfish mortal sits;﻿—

Where, if by chance in mood more grave,
A hermit she appears
Propped in the opening of his cave,
Mummied almost with years;

Or like an idol set upright
With folded legs for stem,
Ready to hear prayers all the night
And never answer them.

But where’s the idol-hermit thrust?
Her knees like flail-joints go!
Alternate kiss, her mother must,
Now that, now this big toe!

I turn away from her, and write
For minutes three or four:
A tiny spectre, tall and white,
She’s standing by the door!

Then something comes into my head
That makes me stop and think:
She’s on the table, the quadruped,
And dabbling in my ink!

O Elfie, make no haste to lose
Thy ignorance of offence!
Thou hast the best gift I could choose,
A heavenly confidence.

’Tis time, long-white-gowned Mrs. Ham,
To put you in the ark!
Sleep, Elfie, God-infolded lamb,
Sleep shining through the dark.

===Chinese===

我有一个关节像木偶的孩子，
她才三岁半；
蓬乱的发间一双眼睛闪着野气，
神情又羞怯又大胆。

像两个小淘气鬼，她的小手
忽地伸出去，又推又抓；
若责骂她——她便站着发抖，
两只小手像两片叶子直哆嗦。

可是在她心里，一分钟以前
就仿佛一年前那么久远；
你刚一抬眼，转眼之间
又得对她说一声「不行！」

有时虽然并没有什么烦心事，
她也会闹着不肯睡；
于是裹着毯子，在那把圆椅里，
这个小精灵般的凡人坐着；——

倘若碰巧心情沉静一些，
她就像一位隐士
支在他的洞穴口，
几乎老成了木乃伊；

又像一尊端坐的神像，
盘起的双腿就是像座，
准备整夜倾听祷告
却一概不予回应。

可这尊神像隐士哪里安分？
她的膝盖像连枷一样起落！
妈妈只好轮流亲她，
一会儿这个脚趾，一会儿那个大脚趾！

我背过身去写东西，
不过三四分钟：
一个又高又白的小幽灵，
已站在门边！

接着有什么事让我猛然回头
停下笔来细看：
那四脚小兽已经上了桌子，
正搅玩我的墨水！

哦埃尔菲，别急着失去
你对过错的懵懂无知！
你拥有我能选出的最好礼物——
一种天国的信赖。

到点了，穿长白袍的哈姆太太，
该把你放进方舟里了！
睡吧埃尔菲，上帝怀抱中的羔羊，
睡着，照亮这黑夜。

## The Thank-Offering / 感恩祭
===Original===

My Lily snatches not my gift;
Glad is she to be fed,
But to her mouth she will not lift
The piece of broken bread,
Till on my lips, unerring, swift,
The morsel she has laid.

This is her grace before her food,
This her libation poured;
Even thus his offering, Aaron good
Heaved up to thank the Lord,
When for the people all he stood,
And with a cake adored.

So, Father, every gift of thine
I offer at thy knee;
Else take I not the love divine
With which it comes to me;
Not else the offered grace is mine
Of sharing life with thee.

Yea, all my being I would bring,
Yielding it utterly,
Not yet a full-possessed thing
Till heaved again to thee:
Away, my self! away, and cling
To him that makes thee be!

===Chinese===

我的百合从不抢我给的食物；
得到喂养她自然欢喜，
但她不肯把那块掰开的面包
举到自己嘴边，
直到她精准而飞快地
把那一小口先放上我的嘴唇。

这是她饭前的谢恩，
这是她浇奠的祭；
当年善人亚伦献他的供物，
也正是这样向主举起感恩，
当他为全民站在那里，
以一块饼敬奉上主。

所以，父啊，你赐的每一件礼物，
我都要在你的膝前献上；
否则我便不曾领受那随礼物
一同临到我的神圣之爱；
否则那分享你生命的恩典
便不算真正归于我。

是的，我愿把我的全人带来，
毫无保留地交出，
在重新向你举起之前，
它还不算完全属于我：
走开吧，我的己！走开，去紧靠
那使你存在的主！

## The Burnt-Offering / 燔祭
===Original===

Thrice-happy he whose heart, each new-born night,
When old-worn day hath vanished o’er earth’s brim,
And he hath laid him down in chamber dim,
Straightway begins to tremble and grow bright,
And loose faint flashes toward the vaulted height
Of the great peace that overshadoweth him:
Keen lambent flames of hope awake and swim
Throughout his soul, touching each point with light!
The great earth under him an altar is,
Upon whose top a sacrifice he lies,
Burning in love’s response up to the skies
Whose fire descended first and kindled his:
When slow the flickering flames at length expire,
Sleep’s ashes only hide a glowing fire.

===Chinese===

三倍有福的人：每个新生的夜晚，
当疲惫的旧日从大地边缘消隐，
当他躺进幽暗的卧房，
他的心便立刻开始颤动、发亮，
向那笼罩着他的浩大平安
隐隐放出微光，直上穹苍：
希望的莹莹火烙醒转、游动，
漫过他整个灵魂，把每一点都映亮！
他身下的大地是一座祭坛，
他作为祭牲躺在坛顶，
在爱的回应中向诸天燃烧，
而那火原是从天而降、将他点燃：
当摇曳的火焰终于缓缓熄灭，
睡眠的灰烬下只藏着灼灼的火。

## To S. F. S. / 致 S. F. S.
===Original===

They say that lonely sorrows do not chance:
More gently, I think, sorrows together go;
A new one joins the funeral gliding slow
With less of jar than when it breaks the dance.
Grief swages grief, and joy doth joy enhance;
Nature is generous to her children so.
And were they quick to spy the flowers that blow,
As quick to feel the sharp-edged stones that lance
The foot that must walk naked in life’s way﻿—
Blest by the roadside lily, free from fear,
Oftener than hurt by dash of flinty spear,
They would walk upright, bold, and earnest-gay;
And when the soft night closed the weary day,
Would sleep like those that far-off music hear.

===Chinese===

人们说，孤独的忧伤不会凭空而至；
我想，忧伤们结伴而行反倒更温柔：
新来的一位加入缓缓滑行的送葬行列，
总比它突然闯进舞会少些震刺。
忧伤抚平忧伤，喜悦则使喜悦更深；
大自然对她的儿女就是这样慷慨。
倘若他们能敏锐地看见路旁绽放的花，
也如敏锐地感到那尖利的石子——它刺伤
必须赤足走在人生路上的脚——
那么，受了路边百合的祝福，无所惧怕，
他们受燧石长矛骤击的时候反而更少，
他们会走得端正、勇敢而诚挚地欢畅；
而当温柔的夜晚合上疲惫的一天，
他们会睡得像听见远处音乐的人。

## The Unseen Face / 未见的脸
===Original===

“I do beseech thee, God, show me thy face.”
“Come up to me in Sinai on the morn!
Thou shall behold as much as may be borne.”
And on a rock stood Moses, lone in space.
From Sinai’s top, the vaporous, thunderous place,
God passed in cloud, an earthy garment worn
To hide, and thus reveal. In love, not scorn,
He put him in a clift of the rock’s base,
Covered him with his hand, his eyes to screen﻿—
Passed﻿—lifted it: his back alone appears!
Ah, Moses, had he turned, and hadst thou seen
The pale face crowned with thorns, baptized with tears,
The eyes of the true man, by men belied,
Thou hadst beheld God’s face, and straightway died!

===Chinese===

「我恳求你，上帝，将你的面容显给我看。」
「早晨你上西乃山来见我！
你将看见你所能承受的那么多。」
于是摩西站在磐石上，孤身于苍茫之间。
从西乃山顶，那云雾雷轰之地，
上帝在云中经过，披一件尘世的衣裳，
用以遮掩，也因此显明。出于爱，而非轻蔑，
他把他安置在磐石根的缝隙里，
用手遮住他，挡住他的眼睛——
走过——然后抬起手：显现的只有他的背！
啊摩西，他若转过身来，你若看见
那苍白的、戴荆冠、被泪水浇洗的脸，
那被人谎告的真正人的眼睛，
你便是看见了上帝的面，随即死去！

## Concerning Jesus / 关于耶稣
===Original===

I

If thou hadst been a sculptor, what a race
Of forms divine had thenceforth filled the land!
Methinks I see thee, glorious workman, stand,
Striking a marble window through blind space﻿—
Thy face’s reflex on the coming face,
As dawns the stone to statue ’neath thy hand﻿—
Body obedient to its soul’s command,
Which is thy thought, informing it with grace!
So had it been. But God, who quickeneth clay,
Nor turneth it to marble﻿—maketh eyes,
Not shadowy hollows, where no sunbeams play﻿—
Would mould his loftiest thought in human guise:
Thou didst appear, walking unknown abroad,
God’s living sculpture, all-informed of God.

II

If one should say, “Lo, there thy statue! take
Possession, sculptor; now inherit it;
Go forth upon the earth in likeness fit;
As with a trumpet-cry at morning, wake
The sleeping nations; with light’s terror, shake
The slumber from their hearts, that, where they sit,
They leap straight up, aghast, as at a pit
Gaping beneath;” I hear him answer make:
“Alas for me, I cannot nor would dare
Inform what I revered as I did trace!
Who would be fool that he like fool might fare,
With feeble spirit mocking the enorm
Strength on his forehead!” Thou, God’s thought thy form,
Didst live the large significance of thy face.

III

Men have I seen, and seen with wonderment,
Noble in form, “lift upward and divine,”
In whom I yet must search, as in a mine,
After that soul of theirs, by which they went
Alive upon the earth. And I have bent
Regard on many a woman, who gave sign
God willed her beautiful, when he drew the line
That shaped each float and fold of beauty’s tent:
Her soul, alas, chambered in pygmy space,
Left the fair visage pitiful﻿—inane﻿—
Poor signal only of a coming face
When from the penetrale she filled the fane!﻿—
Possessed of thee was every form of thine,
Thy very hair replete with the divine.

IV

===Chinese===

一

你若曾是一个雕刻家，将有怎样一族
神圣的形体从此充满大地！
我仿佛看见你，光荣的匠人，伫立着，
在盲目的空间里凿开一扇大理石的窗——
你的面容映在将成的面容上，
石头在你手底渐渐苏醒为雕像——
身体顺服它灵魂的号令，
那灵魂便是你的思想，赋予它恩典！
本该如此。但那赋予泥土生命的上帝，
并不把泥土变成大理石——他造眼睛，
而不是没有阳光嬉戏的幽暗空穴——
他要以人的形像铸成他最高的思想：
于是你出现了，行走于世间无人识得，
上帝活的雕像，处处被上帝浸透。

二

若有人说：「看哪，你的雕像在那里！
领受吧，雕刻家；现在占有它；
以相称的形貌走上大地；
如清晨的号角长鸣，唤醒
沉睡的列国；以光的可畏，震落
他们心中的酣眠，使他们从所坐之处
猛然直跳起来，惊惶失措，如同脚下
裂开深渊；」我听见他如此回答：
「我这人可悲，既不能也不敢
给我一路临摹、一路敬畏的东西注入生命！
谁肯为活得像愚人而自甘为愚人，
用孱弱的心灵去嘲讽那盘踞在
他额头的巨大力量！」而你，以上帝的思想为形骸，
活出了你面容的全部深广意义。

三

我见过一些人，并且惊叹着见过，
形体高贵，「昂然而神性」，
但我仍须在他们里面，如在矿中，
发掘那使他们活在世上行走的灵魂。
我也曾凝望过许多女子，她们显出
上帝定意她美的记号，当他勾勒出
那塑造美之帐幕每一道飘拂褶皱的线条：
可她的灵魂，唉，蛰居在侏儒般的空间，
让那姣好的面容显得可怜——空洞——
只是一面寒酸的旗，预示一张将来
她自内殿充满圣殿时的脸！——
而你，你身上的每一处形貌都被灵魂占满，
连你的头发也充盈着神性。

四

===Original===

If thou hadst built a temple, how my eye
Had hungering fed thereon, from low-browed crypt
Up to the soaring pinnacles that, tipt
With stars, gave signal when the sun drew nigh!
Dark caverns in and under; vivid sky
Its home and aim! Say, from the glory slipt,
And down into the shadows dropt and dipt,
Or reared from darkness up so holy-high?﻿—
Thou build’st the temple of thy holy ghost
From hid foundation to high-hidden fate﻿—
Foot in the grave, head at the heavenly gate,
From grave and sky filled with a fighting host!
Man is thy temple; man thy work elect;
His glooms and glory thine, great architect!

V

If thou hadst been a painter, what fresh looks,
What outbursts of pent glories, what new grace
Had shone upon us from the great world’s face!
How had we read, as in eternal books,
The love of God in loneliest shiest nooks!
A lily, in merest lines thy hand did trace,
Had plainly been God’s child of lower race!
And oh how strong the hills, songful the brooks!
To thee all nature’s meanings lie light-bare,
Because thy heart is nature’s inner side;
Clear as, to us, earth on the dawn’s gold tide,
Her notion vast up in thy soul did rise;
Thine is the world, thine all its splendours rare,
Thou Man ideal, with the unsleeping eyes!

VI

But I have seen pictures the work of man,
In which at first appeared but chaos wild:
So high the art transcended, they beguiled
The eye as formless, and without a plan.
Not soon, the spirit, brooding o’er, began
To see a purpose rise, like mountain isled,
When God said, Let the Dry appear! and, piled
Above the waves, it rose in twilight wan.
So might thy pictures then have been too strange
For us to pierce beyond their outmost look;
A vapour and a darkness; a sealed book;
An atmosphere too high for wings to range;
And so we could but, gazing, pale and change,
And tremble as at a void thought cannot brook.

VII

===Chinese===

你若曾建造一座殿宇，我的眼
将何等饥渴地在那里饱餐，从低眉的地下圣窟
直到扶摇直上的尖塔，塔尖缀着星辰，
在太阳临近时发出信号！
幽暗的洞穴在其内其下；鲜亮的天空
是它的家与归指！请说，是从荣耀中滑落，
降下、沉入阴影之中，
还是从黑暗里向上筑起、圣洁如许高？——
你建造的，是你圣灵的殿宇，
从隐密的根基到高而隐密的定命——
脚在坟墓，头在天门，
从坟墓到高天，充满一支争战的军队！
人就是你的殿；人是你的选民之工；
他的幽暗与荣光都属你，伟大的建筑师！

五

你若曾是一个画家，何等清新的面目，
何等迸涌的郁积荣光，何等崭新的恩典
将从这大世界的脸上照临我们！
我们将怎样像读永恒的书卷一样，
在最偏僻最害羞的角落里读出上帝的爱！
一朵百合花，只消你手勾出的寥寥数笔，
便分明是上帝较低族类的儿女！
还有群山何等坚强，溪流何等歌唱！
对你，自然的一切意义都轻然袒露，
因为你的心就是自然的内里；
如同大地在我们眼中映着黎明的金潮，
她浩瀚的理念清晰地在你灵魂中升起；
这世界是你的，一切稀世的华彩都是你的，
你这理想之人，有着从不阖上的双眼！

六

但我见过人手绘成的图画，
初看只是狂乱的一片混沌：
艺术太高超了，竟欺骗了眼睛，
让它们显得无形，仿佛没有章法。
不久，沉思其上的心灵，才开始
看见一个目的升起，像孤悬的海山，
当上帝说：让旱地露出来！它便
堆涌在波涛之上，升起于苍白的微光。
你那时的图画，或许也因此太奇异，
使我们无法穿透它们最外的一望；
一场雾霭与黑暗；一部封缄的书；
一层翅膀飞不到的大气；
于是我们只能凝望着，脸色发白、变幻，
战栗着，仿佛面对虚空、思想无法承受。

七

===Original===

But earth is now thy living picture, where
Thou shadowest truth, the simple and profound
By the same form in vital union bound:
Where one can see but the first step of thy stair,
Another sees it vanish far in air.
When thy king David viewed the starry round,
From heart and fingers broke the psaltery-sound:
Lord, what is man, that thou shouldst mind his prayer!
But when the child beholds the heavens on high,
He babbles childish noises﻿—not less dear
Than what the king sang praying﻿—to the ear
Of him who made the child and king and sky.
Earth is thy picture, painter great, whose eye
Sees with the child, sees with the kingly seer.

VIII

If thou hadst built some mighty instrument,
And set thee down to utter ordered sound,
Whose faithful billows, from thy hands unbound,
Breaking in light, against our spirits went,
And caught, and bore above this earthly tent,
The far-strayed back to their prime natal ground,
Where all roots fast in harmony are found,
And God sits thinking out a pure consent;﻿—
Nay, that thou couldst not; that was not for thee!
Our broken music thou must first restore﻿—
A harder task than think thine own out free;
And till thou hast done it, no divinest score,
Though rendered by thine own angelic choir,
Can lift one human spirit from the mire.

IX

If thou hadst been a poet! On my heart
The thought flashed sudden, burning through the weft
Of life, and with too much I sank bereft.
Up to my eyes the tears, with sudden start,
Thronged blinding: then the veil would rend and part!
The husk of vision would in twain be cleft!
Thy hidden soul in naked beauty left,
I should behold thee, Nature, as thou art!
O poet Jesus! at thy holy feet
I should have lien, sainted with listening;
My pulses answering ever, in rhythmic beat,
The stroke of each triumphant melody’s wing,
Creating, as it moved, my being sweet;
My soul thy harp, thy word the quivering string.

X

===Chinese===

但大地如今是你活的图画，你在其中
投下真理的影像，简单的与深邃的
被同一个形貌在生命的天系里缚定：
有人只能看见你阶梯的第一级，
另一人却看见它远遁入高空。
当你的王大卫仰望星斗环列，
心和指尖迸出瑟琴之声：
主啊，人算什么，你竟垂听他的祷告！
但当孩童仰望高天，
他只是咿呀出稚气的声响——在造了
孩童、王与天空的那位耳中，
却不比王的祷歌少了亲爱。
大地是你的画，伟大的画家，你的眼
既与孩童同看，也与王者先知同看。

八

你若曾造一架洪大的乐器，
坐下奏出井然有序的声响，
那忠实的音浪从你手中解脱，
迸碎成光，扑向我们的心灵，
将迷途远远的灵，掳掠、托举，越过这尘世的帐幕，
送回他们太初诞生的故乡，
在那里一切根须都紧扎于和谐，
上帝坐着，思出一纯然的同心；——
不，那不是你的事；那不是为你预备的！
你必须先恢复我们破碎的音乐——
这比自由地想出你自己的乐章更难；
在你做成之前，纵有最神圣的总谱，
由你自己的天使诗班演奏，
也不能把一个人的灵从泥泞中举起。

九

你若曾是一个诗人！这念头
蓦地闪过我心，烧穿生命的织物，
我在过载之中失魂般沉没。
泪水骤然涌上我的眼睛，
蜂拥而来，遮蔽了视线：那时帷幕就要裂开！
异象的外壳将从中间劈开！
你隐藏的灵魂赤裸着美留在那里，
我将看见你，自然啊，看见你的本相！
哦诗人耶稣！在你圣洁的脚前
我早已躺卧，因聆听而成圣；
我的脉搏永远以韵律的搏动
应和每一支凯旋旋律的振翅，
它一面移动，一面造出我甘甜的生命；
我的灵魂是你的竖琴，你的话是颤动的弦。

十

===Original===

Thee had we followed through the twilight land
Where thought grows form, and matter is refined
Back into thought of the eternal mind,
Till, seeing them one, Lo, in the morn we stand!﻿—
Then started fresh and followed, hand in hand,
With sense divinely growing, till, combined,
We heard the music of the planets wind
In harmony with billows on the strand!﻿—
Till, one with earth and all God’s utterance,
We hardly knew whether the sun outspake,
Or a glad sunshine from our spirits brake﻿—
Whether we think, or winds and blossoms dance!
Alas, O poet leader, for such good
Thou wast God’s tragedy, writ in tears and blood!

XI

Hadst thou been one of these, in many eyes,
Too near to be a glory for thy sheen,
Thou hadst been scorned; and to the best hadst been
A setter forth of strange divinities;
But to the few construct of harmonies,
A sudden sun, uplighting the serene
High heaven of love; and, through the cloudy screen
That ’twixt our souls and truth all wretched lies,
Dawning at length, hadst been a love and fear,
Worshipped on high from Magian’s mountain-crest,
And all night long symbolled by lamp-flames clear,
Thy sign, a star upon thy people’s breast﻿—
Where that strange arbitrary token lies
Which once did scare the sun in noontide skies.

XII

But as thou camest forth to bring the poor,
Whose hearts are nearer faith and verity,
Spiritual childhood, thy philosophy﻿—
So taught’st the A.B.C. of heavenly lore;
Because thou sat’st not lonely evermore,
With mighty truths informing language high,
But, walking in thy poem continually,
Didst utter deeds, of all true forms the core﻿—
Poet and poem one indivisible fact;
Because thou didst thine own ideal act,
And so, for parchment, on the human soul
Didst write thine aspirations﻿—at thy goal
Thou didst arrive with curses for acclaim,
And cry to God up through a cloud of shame.

XIII

===Chinese===

我们本要追随你走过那微明之地，
那里思想凝成形体，物质被提纯
复归为永恒心智的思想，
直到看见二者为一——看哪，清晨我们已站定！——
然后重新起步，手牵着手，继续追随，
感官在神性地增长，直到合而为一，
我们听见诸行星的音乐
与岸边的波涛汇成交响！——
直到与大地、与上帝的一切言说合为一体，
我们几乎分不清，是太阳在外发声，
还是喜乐的阳光从我们灵中迸现——
是我们思想，还是风与花在起舞！
可惜啊，诗歌的引领者，为了这样的善，
你竟成了上帝的悲剧，以泪与血写成！

十一

你若曾是这其中之一，在许多人眼里，
太近了，近得你的光辉不成其为光辉，
你必被藐视；即使对最好的人，
你也不过是个宣讲怪异神祇的人；
可对那少数能构造和谐的人，
你是一轮骤起的太阳，照亮爱那
高峻澄澈的穹苍；并且，透过那层
横在我们灵魂与真理之间的悲惨云幕，
你终将破晓，成为爱与敬畏，
在术士的山巅受人崇奉，
整夜有澄净的灯焰为你作表记，
你的标记，是你子民胸前的一颗星——
在那奇异专断的徽记安放之处，
它曾一度吓退正午天空中的太阳。

十二

但你出来，本是为带給贫穷的人——
他们的心离信心与真实更近——
属灵的孩童身分，你的哲学——
于是你教导天学的字母表；
因为你从不曾孤独地端坐，
以宏大的言语承载宏大的真理，
而是行走在你自己的诗篇里，不断
以行动说话——一切真实形体的核心——
诗人与诗，一个不可分割的事实；
因为你亲自活出了你自己的理想，
于是以人的灵魂代替羊皮纸，
在上面写下你的向往——抵达终点时，
迎接你的是咒骂而非喝彩，
你透过羞辱的云向上帝呼喊。

十三

===Original===

For three and thirty years, a living seed,
A lonely germ, dropt on our waste world’s side,
Thy death and rising thou didst calmly bide;
Sore companied by many a clinging weed
Sprung from the fallow soil of evil and need;
Hither and thither tossed, by friends denied;
Pitied of goodness dull, and scorned of pride;
Until at length was done the awful deed,
And thou didst lie outworn in stony bower
Three days asleep﻿—oh, slumber godlike-brief
For man of sorrows and acquaint with grief!
Life-seed thou diedst, that Death might lose his power,
And thou, with rooted stem and shadowy leaf,
Rise, of humanity the crimson flower.

XIV

Where dim the ethereal eye, no art, though clear
As golden star in morning’s amber springs,
Can pierce the fogs of low imaginings:
Painting and sculpture are a mockery mere.
Where dull to deafness is the hearing ear,
Vain is the poet. Nought but earthly things
Have credence. When the soaring skylark sings
How shall the stony statue strain to hear?
Open the deaf ear, wake the sleeping eye,
And Lo, musicians, painters, poets﻿—all
Trooping instinctive, come without a call!
As winds that where they list blow evermore;
As waves from silent deserts roll to die
In mighty voices on the peopled shore.

XV

Our ears thou openedst; mad’st our eyes to see.
All they who work in stone or colour fair,
Or build up temples of the quarried air,
Which we call music, scholars are of thee.
Henceforth in might of such, the earth shall be
Truth’s temple-theatre, where she shall wear
All forms of revelation, all men bear
Tapers in acolyte humility.
O master-maker, thy exultant art
Goes forth in making makers! Pictures? No,
But painters, who in love and truth shall show
Glad secrets from thy God’s rejoicing heart.
Sudden, green grass and waving corn up start
When through dead sands thy living waters go.

XVI

===Chinese===

三十三年，你是一粒活的种子，
一粒孤独的胚芽，落在我们荒芜世界的坡上，
静静等待你的死与你的复活；
多少缠附的野草使你苦痛，
它们从邪恶与匮乏的休耕土里生出；
你被抛来掷去，被朋友否认；
被迟钝的善良怜悯，被骄傲讥诮；
直到那可怕的事终于做成，
你精疲力竭，躺卧在石凿的园子里，
沉睡三日——哦，那神一般短暂的睡眠，
属于这多受痛苦、常经忧患的人！
你这生命的种子死了，使死亡丧失权柄，
而你，带着扎下的茎干和成荫的叶，
复活，成为人道的猩红花朵。

十四

那属天的眼目昏暗处，任何艺术，纵然清明
如金色晨星映在黎明的琥珀泉中，
也穿不透低贱臆想的浓雾：
绘画与雕刻不过是一场嘲弄。
那听觉的耳朵聋聩处，
诗人也是徒然。唯有尘世之物
才能取信。当高飞的云雀歌唱，
石像又怎能侧耳去听？
睁开聋的耳，唤醒睡的眼，
看哪，乐师、画家、诗人——全都
本能地成群结队，不召自来！
如风，随意吹拂，永不止息；
如浪，从寂静的荒漠滚滚而来，
以雄浑的声音死在人烟的海岸。

十五

你开了我们的耳；你使我们的眼看见。
凡在石头或色彩中劳作的，
或以采掘的空气筑起殿宇
（我们称之为音乐）的，都是你的门徒。
从此，借着这些人的力量，大地要成为
真理的殿宇剧场，她将在其中穿戴
启示的一切形相，万人都要手持烛火，
以辅祭的谦卑侍立。
哦主匠人，你欢腾的艺术
向外成就的是制造匠人的人！图画？不，
是画家们，他们要以爱与真实显明
从你上帝喜乐的心中而来的欢欣奥秘。
当你活水的江河穿过死寂的沙地，
青草与摆动的庄稼骤然拔地而起。

十六

===Original===

From the beginning good and fair are one,
But men the beauty from the truth will part,
And, though the truth is ever beauty’s heart,
After the beauty will, short-breathed, run,
And the indwelling truth deny and shun.
Therefore, in cottage, synagogue, and mart,
Thy thoughts came forth in common speech, not art;
With voice and eye, in Jewish Babylon,
Thou taughtest﻿—not with pen or carved stone,
Nor in thy hand the trembling wires didst take:
Thou of the truth not less than all wouldst make;
For Truth’s sake even her forms thou didst disown:
Ere, through the love of beauty, truth shall fail,
The light behind shall burn the broidered veil!

XVII

Holy of holies, my bare feet draw nigh:
Jesus, thy body is the shining veil
By which I look on God, nor grow death-pale.
I know that in my verses poor may lie
Things low, for see, the thinker is not high!
But were my song as loud as saints’ all-hail,
As pure as prophet’s cry of warning wail,
As holy as thy mother’s ecstasy﻿—
He sings a better, who, for love or ruth,
Into his heart a little child doth take.
Nor thoughts nor feelings, art nor wisdom seal
The man who at thy table bread shall break.
Thy praise was not that thou didst know, or feel,
Or show, or love, but that thou didst the truth.

XVIII

Despised! Rejected by the priest-led roar
Of the multitude! The imperial purple flung
About the form the hissing scourge had stung,
Witnessing naked to the truth it bore!
True son of father true, I thee adore.
Even the mocking purple truthful hung
On thy true shoulders, bleeding its folds among,
For thou wast king, art king for evermore!
I know the Father: he knows me the truth.
Truth-witness, therefore the one essential king,
With thee I die, with thee live worshipping!
O human God, O brother, eldest born,
Never but thee was there a man in sooth,
Never a true crown but thy crown of thorn!

===Chinese===

从太初起，善与美本是一体，
但世人偏要把美从真里剥出，
虽然真理永远是美的心脏，
他们却气短地只追赶美，
又否认、躲避内住的真理。
因此，在村舍、会堂与集市，
你的思想以平常的话语出口，而非艺术；
在犹太的巴比伦，你以声音与眼目施教——
不用笔，不用凿刻的石头，
也不曾把颤动的琴弦握在手中：
你要使真理不少于全部地归人；
为了真理，你连她的形式也撇下：
一旦对美之爱将使真理衰微，
那背后的光必烧毁那绣花的幔子！

十七

至圣所啊，我赤裸的脚临近了：
耶稣，你的身体是那发光的幔子，
我借它仰望上帝，而不至于面如死灰。
我知道我寒酸的诗行里也许躺着
低微之物，因为看哪，这思想者并不高！
但纵然我的歌响亮如众圣的欢呼，
纯净如先知警示的哭号，
圣洁如你母亲的狂喜——
那为爱或怜把一个小孩子
接进心里的，唱得比这更好。
不是思想也不是情感，不是艺术也不是智慧，
能给那在你桌上掰饼的人封印。
对你的称许不在于你知、你感、
你显明、你爱，而在于你行了真理。

十八

受藐视！被祭司煽动的群众
呼啸着弃绝！帝国的紫袍披在
那被嘶鸣的鞭子抽打过的身体上，
赤裸裸地为它所承载的真理作证！
真父的真子，我敬拜你。
连那戏弄的紫袍也真实地披挂
在你真实的肩头，血渗进它的皱褶，
因为你是王，你是永远的王！
我认识天父：他也认识我是属真理的。
真理的见证者，因此是那唯一根本的王，
我与你同死，我与你同活、敬拜！
哦属人的上帝，哦兄长，长子啊，
从来只有你是真实的人，
从来只有你荆棘的冠冕是真实的冠冕！

## Death and Birth / 死与生
===Original===

’Tis the midnight hour; I heard
The Abbey-bell give out the word.
Seldom is the lamp-ray shed
On some dwarfed foot-farer’s head
In the deep and narrow street
Lying ditch-like at my feet
Where I stand at lattice high
Downward gazing listlessly
From my house upon the rock,
Peak of earth’s foundation-block.

There her windows, every story,
Shine with far-off nebulous glory!
Round her in that luminous cloud
Stars obedient press and crowd,
She the centre of all gazing,
She the sun her planets dazing!
In her eyes’ victorious lightning
Some are paling, some are brightening:
Those on which they gracious turn,
Stars combust, all tenfold burn;
Those from which they look away
Listless roam in twilight gray!
When on her my looks I bent
Wonder shook me like a tent,
And my eyes grew dim with sheen,
Wasting light upon its queen!
But though she my eyes might chain,
Rule my ebbing flowing brain,
Truth alone, without, within,
Can the soul’s high homage win!

He, I do not doubt, is there
Who unveiled my idol fair!
And I thank him, grateful much,
Though his end was none of such.
He from shapely lips of wit
Let the fire-flakes lightly flit,
Scorching as the snow that fell
On the damned in Dante’s hell;
With keen, gentle opposition,
Playful, merciless precision,
Mocked the sweet romance of youth
Balancing on spheric truth;
He on sense’s firm set plane
Rolled the unstable ball amain:
With a smile she looked at me,
Stung my soul, and set me free.

Welcome, friend! Bring in your bricks.
Mortar there? No need to mix?
That is well. And picks and hammers?
Verily these are no shammers!﻿—
There, my friend, build up that niche,
That one with the painting rich!

Yes, you’re right; it is a show
Picture seldom can bestow;
City palaces and towers,
Terraced gardens, twilight bowers,
Vistas deep through swaying masts,
Pennons flaunting in the blasts:
Build; my room it does not fit;
Brick-glaze is the thing for it!

Yes, a window you may call it;
Not the less up you must wall it:
In that niche the dead world lies;
Bury death, and free mine eyes.

There were youths who held by me,
Said I taught, yet left them free:
Will they do as I said then?
God forbid! As ye are men,
Find the secret﻿—follow and find!
All forget that lies behind;
Me, the schools, yourselves, forsake;
In your souls a silence make;
Hearken till a whisper come,
Listen, follow, and be dumb.

===Chinese===

正是午夜时分；我听见
修道院的钟报出时辰。
灯盏的光很少照在
某个矮小夜行者的头上，
在那条又深又窄的街道里，
它沟壑一般横在我脚下，
而我站在高处的窗前，
懒懒地向下凝望，
从我那坐落在磐石上的房子，
大地基石之巅。

那边她的窗户，一层又一层，
闪耀着遥远的星云般的光辉！
在那团光雾的围绕中，
恭顺的星辰拥挤簇拥着她，
她是万众凝望的中心，
她是使行星目眩的太阳！
在她眼中得胜的电光里，
有的星辰黯淡，有的更亮：
那些蒙她眷顾一顾的，
如焚的星，十倍地燃烧；
那些被她的目光撇下的，
在灰蒙的曙色里无精打采地游荡！
当我把目光投向她，
惊异像帐篷一样将我撼动，
我的眼因那光辉而昏花，
把光徒然耗在它们的女王身上！
但尽管她能锁住我的眼，
统治我涨落不息的头脑，
唯有真理，在外又在内，
才能赢得灵魂至高的敬意！

他，我毫不怀疑，就在那里，
是他揭去了我偶像的华美面纱！
我感激他，深深感念，
虽然他的本意并非如此。
他从俊俏机智的唇间
让火星轻轻飞落，
灼人如但丁地狱里
落在罪人身上的雪；
以锋利而温文的驳难，
以戏谑而毫不留情的精准，
嘲弄青春那甜蜜的浪漫
在球面真理上的摇摆；
他在感官这牢固的平面上
疾滚那不稳的圆球：
她含笑望了我一眼，
刺痛我的灵魂，又使我自由。

欢迎，朋友！把你的砖搬进来。
灰浆呢？不用和？
那就好。还有镐和锤？
说真的，这些可不是骗人的玩意儿！——
喏，朋友，把那个壁龛砌上，
那间彩绘华丽的壁龛！

是的，你说得对；这确是一幅
图画难得给予的景观：
城中的宫殿与高塔，
梯层的花园、暮色的凉亭，
穿过摇曳桅樯的深邃远景，
在疾风中招展的尖旗：
砌吧；它配不进我的房间；
砖釉正是它相宜的归宿！

是的，你可以称它为一扇窗；
但仍旧得把它砌死：
那壁龛里躺着死去的世界；
埋葬死亡，解放我的双眼。

曾有一些青年依附于我，
说我教导他们，却任他们自由：
他们还会照我当时说的做吗？
但愿不会！你们既是人，
就去寻那秘诀——追随而后寻见！
忘掉背后一切的往事；
撇下我、撇下学派、也撇下你们自己；
在你们灵魂里造出一片静默；
侧耳直到有低语传来，
聆听，追随，然后缄默。

===Original===

There! ’tis over; I am dead!
Of my life the broken thread
Here I cast out of my hand!﻿—
O my soul, the merry land!
On my heart the sinking vault
Of my ruining past makes halt;
Ages I could sit and moan
For the shining world that’s gone!

Haste and pierce the other wall;
Break an opening to the All!
Where? No matter; done is best.
Kind of window? Let that rest:
Who at morning ever lies
Pondering how to ope his eyes!

I bethink me: we must fall
On the thinnest of the wall!
There it must be, in that niche!﻿—
No, the deepest﻿—that in which
Stands the Crucifix. You start?﻿—
Ah, your half-believing heart
Shrinks from that as sacrilege,
Or, at least, upon its edge!
Worse than sacrilege, I say,
Is it to withhold the day
From the brother whom thou knowest
For the God thou never sawest!

Reverently, O marble cold,
Thee in living arms I fold!
Thou who art thyself the way
From the darkness to the day,
Window, thou, to every land,
Wouldst not one dread moment stand
Shutting out the air and sky
And the dayspring from on high!
Brother with the rugged crown,
Gently thus I lift thee down!

Give me pick and hammer; you
Stand aside; the deed I’ll do.
Yes, in truth, I have small skill,
But the best thing is the will.

Stroke on stroke! The frescoed plaster
Clashes downward, fast and faster.
Hark, I hear an outer stone
Down the rough rock rumbling thrown!
There’s a cranny! there’s a crack!
The great sun is at its back!
Lo, a mass is outward flung!
In the universe hath sprung!

See the gold upon the blue!
See the sun come blinding through!
See the far-off mountain shine
In the dazzling light divine!
Prisoned world, thy captive’s gone!
Welcome wind, and sky, and sun!

===Chinese===

好了！结束了；我死了！
我生命的断线
就从这里从我手中抛出！——
哦我的灵魂，这欢欣的国度！
在我心上，那倾覆的往日
下沉的拱顶停住了；
我能坐在这里哀悼千年，
为那逝去了的闪耀世界！

快，凿穿另一面墙；
为那万有开一个口！
哪里？无所谓；完成就是最好。
什么样的窗？且别管它：
谁在清晨还会躺着
苦思怎样睁开眼睛！

我想起来了：我们得凿
墙上最薄的地方！
一定是那儿，在那个壁龛！——
不，是最深的那一个——那里面
立着十字架。你吃了一惊？——
啊，你那半信的心
畏缩了，以为这是亵渎，
或至少踩在它的边上！
我说，比亵渎更糟的，
是把你所认识的弟兄
拒于白日之外，
为你从未见过的上帝！

怀着敬意，哦冰冷的大理石，
我用活着的双臂抱住你！
你自己就是那道路，
从黑暗通往白昼，
你是通向每一片土地的窗，
你绝不会肯有可怕的一刻
把空气和天空
和高处的晨光关在外面！
戴荆冠的兄长，
我这样轻轻把你请下来！

给我镐和锤；你
站开些；这活儿我来干。
是的，说实话，我手艺很差，
但心意便是最好的东西。

一击接一击！绘着壁画的灰泥
哗啦啦坠落，越来越急。
听，我听见外层一块石头
顺着粗糙的岩壁轰然滚落！
有一道缝了！有一条裂缝了！
大太阳正贴在它背后！
看，一大块向外飞出！
飞进了浩瀚宇宙！

看那蓝底上的金光！
看太阳耀眼地照进来！
看远方的群山
在神性的璀璨光芒中发亮！
囚禁的世界啊，你的囚徒走了！
欢迎你，风、天空和太阳！

## Longing / 渴望
===Original===

*Away from the City’s Herds!*

Away from the city’s herds!
Away from the noisy street!
Away from the storm of words,
Where hateful and hating meet!

Away from the vapour grey,
That like a boding of ill
Is blotting the morning gay,
And gathers and darkens still!

Away from the stupid book!
For, like the fog’s weary rest,
With anger dull it fills each nook
Of my aching and misty breast.

Over some shining shore,
There hangeth a space of blue;
A parting ’mid thin clouds hoar
Where the sunlight is falling through.

The glad waves are kissing the shore
Rejoice, and tell it for ever;
The boat glides on, while its oar
Is flashing out of the river.

Oh to be there with thee!
Thou and I only, my love!
The sparkling, sands and the sea!
And the sunshine of God above!

===Chinese===

远离城市的兽群！

远离城市的兽群！
远离喧闹的街道！
远离那词语的风暴，
那里仇恨者与被恨者相遇！

远离那灰色的雾霭，
它像不祥的预感，
正涂抹欢快的清晨，
还在聚拢、还在变暗！

远离那乏味的书本！
因为它，如浓雾令人疲乏的沉滞，
把阴暗的怒气填满
我酸痛而迷雾重重的胸膛的每个角落。

在某个闪亮的海岸上空，
悬着一片湛蓝；
灰白云翳间的一道分野，
阳光正从那里泻落。

欢欣的波涛亲吻着海岸，
欢喜着，把这诉说不停；
小舟滑行，桨儿
在河面上闪闪出水的光。

哦，多想与你同在那里！
只有你和我，我的爱人！
闪光的沙滩与大海！
还有头顶上帝的阳光！

## My Eyes Make Pictures / 我的眼睛造出图画
===Original===

> “My eyes make pictures, when they are shut.”
> —Coleridge

Fair morn, I bring my greeting
To lofty skies, and pale,
Save where cloud-shreds are fleeting
Before the driving gale,
The weary branches tossing,
Careless of autumn’s grief,
Shadow and sunlight crossing
On each earth-spotted leaf.

I will escape their grieving;
And so I close my eyes,
And see the light boat heaving
Where the billows fall and rise;
I see the sunlight glancing
Upon its silvery sail,
Where a youth’s wild heart is dancing,
And a maiden growing pale.

And I am quietly pacing
The smooth stones o’er and o’er,
Where the merry waves are chasing
Each other to the shore.
Words come to me while listening
Where the rocks and waters meet,
And the little shells are glistening
In sand-pools at my feet.

Away! the white sail gleaming!
Again I close my eyes,
And the autumn light is streaming
From pale blue cloudless skies;
Upon the lone hill falling
’Mid the sound of heather-bells,
Where the running stream is calling
Unto the silent wells.

Along the pathway lonely,
My horse and I move slow;
No living thing, save only
The home-returning crow.
And the moon, so large, is peering
Up through the white cloud foam;
And I am gladly nearing
My father’s house, my home.

As I were gently dreaming
The solemn trees look out;
The hills, the waters seeming
In still sleep round about;
And in my soul are ringing
Tones of a spirit-lyre,
As my beloved were singing
Amid a sister-choir.

If peace were in my spirit,
How oft I’d close my eyes,
And all the earth inherit,
And all the changeful skies!
Thus leave the sermon dreary,
Thus leave the lonely hearth;
No more a spirit weary﻿—
A free one of the earth!

===Chinese===

> 「我的眼睛闭上时，便会造出图画。」
> ——柯勒律治

晴美的早晨，我带来我的问候，
给高天，和它苍白的面容，
只有几缕碎云疾掠，
在疾驰的狂风前面，
疲倦的枝条摇曳，
全不顾秋天的忧伤，
光影交错，
落在每片斑驳的大地之叶上。

我要躲开它们的哀愁；
于是我合上双眼，
看见轻巧的小船起伏
在波涛的起落之间；
我看见阳光闪烁
在它银色的帆上，
一个青年狂野的心在那里舞蹈，
一位少女渐渐苍白。

而我正安静地踱步，
在光滑的卵石上走了一遍又一遍，
欢快的波浪在那里互相
追逐着奔向海岸。
词语在我聆听时到来，
在礁石与海水相遇的地方，
小小的贝壳闪闪发亮，
在我脚边的沙池里。

去吧！白帆闪着微光！
我再次合上双眼，
秋日的光线正倾泻
自苍白无云的蓝天；
落在孤寂的山丘上，
在石南花铃的声响中间，
奔流的溪水在那里
向沉默的泉井呼唤。

沿着那条寂寞的小路，
我的马和我缓缓前行；
没有一个活物，只有
归巢的乌鸦。
月亮那么大，正从
白色的云沫下探望；
而我正欣喜地走近
我父亲的家，我的家。

仿佛我在温柔的梦里，
庄严的树木向外凝望；
群山与湖水仿佛
在四周静静沉睡；
而我的灵魂里回响着
一架心灵之琴的音调，
仿佛我心爱的人
正在姊妹诗班中歌唱。

若我灵里享有平安，
我将多么常常合上双眼，
便承受了整个大地，
和全部变幻的天空！
就这样离开乏味的说教，
就这样离开冷清的炉台；
不再是一个疲惫的灵——
而是大地自由的一个！

## Death / 死亡
===Original===

When in the bosom of the eldest night
This body lies, cold as a sculptured rest;
When through its shaded windows comes no light,
And its pale hands are folded on its breast﻿—

How shall I fare, who had to wander out,
And of the unknown land the frontier cross,
Peering vague-eyed, uncertain, all about,
Unclothed, mayhap unwelcomed, bathed in loss?

Shall I depart slow-floating like a mist,
Over the city murmuring beneath;
Over the trees and fields, where’er I list,
Seeking the mountain and the lonely heath?

Or will a darkness, o’er material shows
Descending, hide them from the spirit’s sight;
As from the sun a blotting radiance flows
Athwart the stars all glorious through the night;

And the still spirit hang entranced, alone,
Like one in an exalted opium-dream﻿—
Soft-flowing time, insisting space, o’erblown,
With form and colour, tone and touch and gleam,

Thought only waking﻿—thought that may not own
The lapse of ages, or the change of spot;
Its doubt all cast on what it counted known,
Its faith all fixed on what appeareth not?

Or, worn with weariness, shall we sleep until,
Our life restored by long and dreamless rest,
Of God’s oblivion we have drunk our fill,
And wake his little ones, peaceful and blest?

I nothing know, and nothing need to know.
God is; I shall be ever in his sight!
Give thou me strength to labour well, and so
Do my day’s work ere fall my coming night.

===Chinese===

当这身体躺在最古老的夜的怀抱里，
冷得像一尊雕像的安息；
当它暗影重重的窗里再没有光透进，
它苍白的双手交叠在胸前——

我将如何，不得不只身漂泊出去，
跨越未知之地的疆界，
睁着迷茫的眼，四面窥望，
赤身无衣，也许无人迎接，浸没在丧失里？

我会像一缕薄雾缓缓飘离，
掠过下方低语的城市；
掠过树木与田野，随我所愿，
去寻那高山与寂寞的荒野？

还是有一重黑暗，降在
万物的形相之上，把它们从灵的眼里遮去；
如同太阳那抹煞一切的辉光
流过彻夜辉煌的群星；

而这安静的灵悬着，出神，独自，
像一个人在亢奋的鸦片梦里——
柔流的时间、坚执的空间都已被吹散，
连同形与色、音与触与微光，

唯有思想醒着——这思想不再认得
岁月的流逝，或地点的变换；
它对自以为已知的一切满怀疑惑，
对那看不见的一切笃信不疑？

还是，被疲惫磨倦了的我们，将沉睡，直到
长久而无梦的安息把生命复原，
我们畅饮够了上帝的遗忘之杯，
再作为他的小孩子醒来，平安而有福？

我一无所知，也一无所须知。
上帝存在；我将永远在他眼前！
只求你给我力量好好劳作，
趁我将至的夜幕落下之前，做完我一天的工。

## Lessons for a Child / 给孩子的功课
===Original===

I

There breathes not a breath of the summer air
But the spirit of love is moving there;
Not a trembling leaf on the shadowy tree,
Flutters with hundreds in harmony,
But that spirit can part its tone from the rest,
And read the life in its beetle’s breast.
When the sunshiny butterflies come and go,
Like flowers paying visits to and fro,
Not a single wave of their fanning wings
Is unfelt by the spirit that feeleth all things.
The long-mantled moths that sleep at noon
And rove in the light of the gentler moon;
And the myriad gnats that dance like a wall,
Or a moving column that will not fall;
And the dragon-flies that go burning by,
Shot like a glance from a seeking eye﻿—
There is one being that loves them all:
Not a fly in a spider’s web can fall
But he cares for the spider, and cares for the fly;
He cares for you, whether you laugh or cry,
Cares whether your mother smile or sigh.
How he cares for so many, I do not know,
But it would be too strange if he did not so﻿—
Dreadful and dreary for even a fly:
So I cannot wait for the how and why,
But believe that all things are gathered and nursed
In the love of him whose love went first
And made this world﻿—like a huge great nest
For a hen to sit on with feathery breast.

II

The bird on the leafy tree,
The bird in the cloudy sky,
The hart in the forest free,
The stag on the mountain high,
The fish inside the sea,
The albatross asleep
On the outside of the deep,
The bee through the summer sunny
Hunting for wells of honey﻿—
What is the thought in the breast
Of the little bird in its nest?
What is the thought in the songs
The lark in the sky prolongs?
What mean the dolphin’s rays,
Winding his watery ways?
What is the thought of the stag,
Stately on yonder crag?
What does the albatross think,
Dreaming upon the brink
Of the mountain billow, and then
Dreaming down in its glen?
What is the thought of the bee
Fleeting so silently,
Or flitting﻿—with busy hum,
But a careless go-and-come﻿—
From flower-chalice to chalice,
Like a prince from palace to palace?
What makes them alive, so very﻿—
Some of them, surely, merry.
And others so stately calm
They might be singing a psalm?

I cannot tell what they think﻿—
Only know they eat and drink,
And on all that lies about
With a quiet heart look out,
Each after its kind, stately or coy,
Solemn like man, gamesome like boy,
Glad with its own mysterious joy.

===Chinese===

一

夏日的空气里没有一丝呼吸，
不是爱的灵在其中运行；
暗影树上的叶子，没有一片颤动，
不与千百片叶和谐共舞，
而这灵能把它的音调从其余中分出，
读出它甲虫胸膛里的生命。
当阳光下的蝴蝶来来去去，
像花朵们互相拜访串门，
它们双翅扇起的每一道波动，
都逃不过那感知万物的灵。
披着长袍的飞蛾正午沉睡，
在更温柔的月光里游荡；
千万只蚊蚋像一面墙般起舞，
或像一列永不下坠的移动圆柱；
蜻蜓燃烧着掠过，
像寻视的眼中射出的一瞥——
有一位存在者爱着它们全部：
哪怕一只苍蝇落进蛛网，
他也顾念蜘蛛，也顾念苍蝇；
他顾念你，无论你笑还是哭，
顾念你的母亲是微笑还是叹息。
他怎能顾念这么多，我不知道，
但若他不这样，那才太奇怪——
连一只苍蝇也会觉得可怕而凄凉：
所以我不能等一个如何与为何，
只相信万物都被收聚、被养育
在那位爱先行者的爱里，
他造了这个世界——像一张巨大无比的巢，
让一位母亲用羽覆的胸怀伏在上面。

二

树上枝叶间的鸟，
云天里的鸟，
森林里自由的鹿，
高山上的雄鹿，
海里的鱼，
沉睡的信天翁
在深海的外缘，
蜜蜂穿过晴明的夏日
寻索蜜的泉井——
巢里的小鸟
胸中想着什么？
云雀在天空
续唱的歌里是什么？
海豚身上变幻的光纹，
绕着它水中的路径，是什么意思？
那雄鹿在想什么，
端立在远处的岩崖上？
信天翁在想什么，
梦在山一样的巨浪的边沿，
随后又梦进它的浪谷里？
蜜蜂在想什么，
这样悄无声息地飞掠，
或振翅而来——带着忙碌的嗡嗡，
一副漫不经心的来去——
从一朵花盏到另一朵花盏，
像一位王从一座宫殿到另一座宫殿？
是什么使它们这样活泼，这样十足——
它们中有些，想必是快乐的。
另一些又这样庄重安详，
仿佛正唱着一篇诗篇？

我说不出它们想什么——
只知道它们吃、它们喝，
并以安静的心
看待周遭的一切，
各从其类，或庄重或娇羞，
庄严如成人，嬉戏如孩童，
各怀着自己奥秘的欢喜。

===Original===

And God, who knows their thoughts and ways
Though his the creatures do not know,
From his full heart fills each of theirs:
Into them all his breath doth go;
Good and better with them he shares;
Content with their bliss while they have no prayers,
He takes their joy for praise.

If thou wouldst be like him, little one, go
And be kind with a kindness undefiled;
Who gives for the pleasure of thanks, my child,
God’s gladness cannot know.

III

Root met root in the spongy ground,
Searching each for food:
Each turned aside, and away it wound.
And each got something good.

Sound met sound in the wavy air﻿—
That made a little to-do!
They jostled not long, but were quick and fair;
Each found its path and flew.

Drop dashed on drop, as the rain-shower fell;
They joined and sank below:
In gathered thousands they rose a well,
With a singing overflow.

Wind met wind in a garden green,
They began to push and fret:
A tearing whirlwind arose between:
There love lies bleeding yet.

===Chinese===

而上帝，虽造物不认识他，
他却认识它们的心思与行径，
从他丰盈的心里充满它们每一个：
他的气息进入它们全体；
他分享给它们好的与更好的；
它们没有祷告，他却满足于它们的福乐，
把它们的欢喜当作赞美。

你若想学他，小家伙，去吧，
以一份纯净不杂的良善去行善；
谁若为着感谢的愉悦而施与，我的孩子，
他就尝不到上帝的欢欣。

三

根在松软的地里遇见根，
各自寻觅食物：
各自转开，蜿蜒而去，
各自得了些好东西。

声音在波动的空气里遇见声音——
那可惹了一点小乱子！
它们没有多久推搡，都爽快公道；
各自找到路径，飞走了。

雨点砸上雨点，当阵雨落下；
它们汇合，沉入地底：
聚成千万点，它们涌起一口井，
带着歌唱的溢流。

风在青翠的园中遇见风，
它们开始推挤愠怒：
一阵撕扯的旋风在中间升起：
爱至今还躺在那里流血。

## Hope Deferred / 迟延的希望
===Original===

*Summer Is Come Again. The Sun Is Bright,*

Summer is come again. The sun is bright,
And the soft wind is breathing. Airy joy
Is sparkling in thine eyes, and in their light
My soul is shining. Come; our day’s employ
Shall be to revel in unlikely things,
In gayest hopes, fondest imaginings,
And make-believes of bliss. Come, we will talk
Of waning moons, low winds, and a dim sea;
Till this fair summer, deepening as we walk,
Has grown a paradise for you and me.

But ah, those leaves!﻿—it was not summer’s mouth
Breathed such a gold upon them. And look there﻿—
That beech how red! See, through its boughs, half-bare,
How low the sun lies in the mid-day south!﻿—
The sweetness is but one pined memory flown
Back from our summer, wandering alone!
See, see the dead leaves falling! Hear thy heart,
Which, with the year’s pulse beating swift or slow,
Takes in the changing world its changing part,
Return a sigh, an echo sad and low,
To the faint, scarcely audible sound
With which the leaf goes whispering to the ground!
O love, sad winter lieth at the door﻿—
Behind sad winter, age﻿—we know no more.

Come round me, dear hearts. All of us will hold
Each of us compassed: we are growing old;
And if we be not as a ring enchanted,
Hearts around heart, with love to keep it gay,
The young, who claim the joy that haunted
Our visions once, will push us far away
Into the desolate regions, dim and gray,
Where the sea moans, and hath no other cry,
The clouds hang low, and have no tears,
Old dreams lie mouldering in a pit of years,
And hopes and songs all careless pass us by.
But if all each do keep,
The rising tide of youth will sweep
Around us with its laughter-joyous waves,
As ocean fair some palmy island laves,
To loneliness heaved slow from out the deep;
And our youth hover round us like the breath
Of one that sleeps, and sleepeth not to death.

Thus ringed eternally, to parted graves,
The sundered doors into one palace home,
Stumbling through age’s thickets, we will go,
Faltering but faithful﻿—willing to lie low,
Willing to part, not willing to deny
The lovely past, where all the futures lie.

===Chinese===

夏天又来了，阳光明亮

夏天又来了。阳光明亮，
柔和的风正在吹拂。轻盈的喜悦
在你眼中闪炸，在它们的光里
我的灵魂也在闪耀。来吧；我们今天的营生
就是沉洒在不太可能的事情里，
在最欢畅的希望、最痴迷的想象，
和假装的幸福里。来，我们要谈谈
亏缺的月亮、低语的风和一片朦胧的海；
直到这美好的夏天，随我们边走边深浓，
已长成你我的一座乐园。

可是啊，那些叶子！——那不是夏天的嘴
吐出的金黄。看那边——
那棵山毛榉多红！看，透过它半裸的枝干，
正午的太阳在南方沉得多低！——
那甜美不过是一段憔悴的记忆，
从我们的夏天里独自游荡而回！
看哪，看哪，枯叶正落下！听听你的心，
它随着年岁的脉搏或快或慢地跳，
在变迁的世界里演着变迁的角色，
还你一声叹息，一记低沉而悲伤的回响，
应和着叶子飘向地面时
那微弱的、几乎听不见的窸窣声！
哦爱人，哀愁的冬天正伏在门口——
在哀愁的冬天背后，是老年——再往后我们不得而知。

到我这儿来围坐，亲爱的心。我们每一个人
都要被众人环抱：我们正在老去；
倘若我们不是一个被施了魔法的环，
心围着心，用爱使它欢畅，
年轻人——他们要索取曾萦绕
我们梦想的那份欢乐——就会把我们远远推开，
推进那荒凉的地带，昏暗而灰沉，
那里海在呜咽，再没有别的呼声，
云压得很低，却没有眼泪，
旧梦在多年的坑穴里霉烂，
希望与歌声都漫不经心地从我们身边走过。
但若我们每个人都守定这环，
青春上涨的潮水就会
带着它欢笑的波浪环绕我们流涌，
如大洋轻抚一座棕榈的岛，
它从深处缓缓隆起，孤悬于寂寞；
而我们的青春将像一个人的呼吸
萦绕我们，那人睡着，却不是睡向死亡。

就这样永远环拥着，走向分开的坟墓——
那些拆散的门，通向同一座宫殿家园——
蹒跚穿过老年的荆丛，我们将前行，
颤抖却忠贞——甘愿低伏，
甘愿分离，却绝不愿否认
那可爱的往昔，一切未来都躺在其中。

===Original===

Oh! if thou be, who of the live art lord,
Not of the dead﻿—Lo, by that self-same word,
Thou art not lord of age, but lord of youth﻿—
Because there is no age, in sooth,
Beyond its passing shows!
A mist o’er life’s dimmed lantern grows;
Thou break’st the glass, out streams the light
That knows not youth nor age,
That fears no darkness nor the rage
Of windy tempests﻿—burning still more bright
Than when glad youth was all about,
And summer winds were out!

1845.

===Chinese===

哦！你若是那主宰活人、
不主宰死人的主——看哪，凭这同一句话，
你便不是老年的主，而是青春的主——
因为实在没有老年，
除了它表面的浮相！
一层雾在生命的灯笼上渐生；
你打碎玻璃，光便喷涌而出，
那光不识青春也不识老年，
不惧黑暗，也不惧狂风
怒号的暴风雨——反而烧得更亮，
比欢乐的青春环伺四周、
夏天的风四处吹拂时更亮！

一八四五年。

## The Death of the Old Year / 旧年之死
===Original===

The weary Old Year is dead at last;
His corpse ’mid the ruins of Time is cast,
Where the mouldering wrecks of lost Thought lie,
And the rich-hued blossoms of Passion die
To a withering grass that droops o’er his grave,
The shadowy Titan’s refuge cave.
Strange lights from pale moony Memory lie
On the weedy columns beneath its eye;
And strange is the sound of the ghostlike breeze,
In the lingering leaves on the skeleton trees;
And strange is the sound of the falling shower,
When the clouds of dead pain o’er the spirit lower;
Unheard in the home he inhabiteth,
The land where all lost things are gathered by Death.

Alone I reclined in the closing year;
Voice, nor breathing, nor step was near;
And I said in the weariness of my breast:
Weary Old Year, thou art going to rest;
O weary Old Year, I would I might be
One hour alone in thy dying with thee!
Would thou wert a spirit, whose low lament
Might mix with the sighs from my spirit sent;
For I am weary of man and life;
Weary of restless unchanging strife;
Weary of change that is ever changing;
Weary of thought that is ever ranging,
Ever falling in efforts vain,
Fluttering, upspringing from earth again,
Struggling once more through the darkness to wing
That hangs o’er the birthplace of everything,
And choked yet again in the vapour’s breast,
Sinking once more to a helpless rest.
I am weary of tears that scarce are dry,
Ere their founts are filled as the cloud goes by;
Weary of feelings where each in the throng
Mocks at the rest as they crowd along;
Where Pride over all, like a god on high,
Sits enshrined in his self-complacency;
Where Selfishness crawls, the snake-demon of ill,
The least suspected where busiest still;
Where all things evil and painful entwine,
And all in their hate and their sorrow are mine:
O weary Old Year, I would I might be
One hour by thy dying, to weep with thee!

===Chinese===

疲惫的旧年终于死了；
他的尸身被抛在时间的废墟中间，
那里躺着失落思想朽坏的残骸，
激情的艳色花朵
枯萎成垂在他墓上的衰草，
那影影绰绰的巨人的避难洞穴。
惨白如月的记忆投下奇异的光，
照在它眼下的荒草石柱上；
幽灵般的风声也奇异，
在骸骨般树木残存的叶里；
阵雨落下的声音也奇异，
当死去痛苦的云压上灵的上空；
而他栖居的家里无人听见，
那片死亡收聚一切失落之物的土地。

在将尽的年关我独自斜倚；
没有声音，没有呼吸，没有脚步走近；
我在胸中的疲惫里说：
疲惫的旧年，你就要安息了；
哦疲惫的旧年，但愿我能
在你临终时与你单独共度一个时辰！
但愿你是一个精灵，你低低的哀吟
能与我灵里发出的叹息相混；
因为我已厌倦了人与生活；
厌倦了永不安宁又永不更替的争斗；
厌倦了永远在变的变化；
厌倦了永远在游荡的思想，
总在徒劳的努力里跌落，
扑腾着，又从地上跃起，
再一次挣扎着要飞越那片黑暗，
它悬在万物诞生之地的上方，
却又在雾霭的怀里窒息，
再一度沉入无助的安歇。
我厌倦了那泪痕未干、
泉眼便又蓄满的泪水，当云掠过；
厌倦了那样的情感：其中每一个
都在拥挤前行时嘲弄其余；
那里骄傲凌驾一切，像高天的神，
端坐在自我满足的圣龛里；
那里自私爬行，那恶的蛇魔，
最忙渌处最不受人怀疑；
那里一切邪恶与痛楚交缠，
而它们的恨与它们的悲都归我承受：
哦疲惫的旧年，但愿我能
在你临终的身旁，与你同哭一场！

===Original===

Peace, the soul’s slumber, was round me shed;
The sleep where thought lives, but its pain is dead;
And my musings led me, a spirit-band,
Through the wide realms of their native land;
Till I stood by the couch of the mighty dying,
A lonely shore in the midnight lying.
He lay as if he had laid him to sleep,
And the stars above him their watch did keep;
And the mournful wind with the dreamy sigh,
The homeless wanderer of the sky,
Was the only attendant whose gentle breath
Soothed him yet on the couch of death;
And the dying waves of the heedless sea
Fell at his feet most listlessly.

But he lay in peace, with his solemn eye
Looking far through the mists of futurity.
A smile gleamed over the death-dew that lay
On his withered cheek as life ebbed away.
A darkness lay on his forehead vast;
But the light of expectancy o’er it was cast﻿—
A light that shone from the coming day,
Travelling unseen to the East away.
In his cloudy robes that lay shadowing wide,
I stretched myself motionless by his side;
And his eyes with their calm, unimpassioned power,
Soothing my heart like an evening shower,
Led in a spectral, far-billowing train,
The hours of the Past through my spirit again.

There were fears of evil whose stony eyes
Froze joy in its gushing melodies.
Some floated afar on thy tranquil wave,
And the heart looked up from its search for a grave;
While others as guests to the bosom came,
And left its wild children more sorrow, less shame;
For the death-look parts from their chilling brow,
And they bless the heads that before them bow;
And floating away in the far-off gloom.
Thankfulness follows them to their tomb.
There were Hopes that found not a place to rest
Their foot ’mid the rush of all-ocean’s breast;
And home to the sickening heart flew back,
But changed into sorrows upon their track;
And through the moan of the darkening sea
Bearing no leaf from the olive-tree.
There were joys that looked forth with their maiden eyes,
And smiled, and were gone, with a sad surprise;
And the Love of the Earthly, whose beauteous form
Beckoned me on through sunshine and storm;
But when the bounding heart sprang high,
Meeting her smile with a speechless sigh,
The arms sunk home with a painful start,
Clasping a vacancy to the heart.

===Chinese===

安宁，灵魂的睡眠，四围罩下；
那睡眠里思想还活着，它的痛却死了；
我的沉思领着我，像一队精灵，
穿过它们故乡的辽阔疆土；
直到我停在那垂死的巨人身旁，
午夜横陈的一片寂寞海岸。
他躺着，仿佛只是安寝，
头顶的星辰为他守夜；
哀愁的风带着梦似的叹息，
那天空中无家的流浪者，
是唯一的侍者，用轻柔的呼吸
还在死亡的卧榻上抚慰他；
而那不顾念的海垂死的波浪
毫无心事地碎在他脚边。

但他安详地躺着，庄严的眼
透过未来的迷雾远远凝望。
一道微笑掠过死亡的露珠，
那露珠在他枯槁的颊上，当生命退潮。
一片黑暗罩住他广阔的额头；
但期待的辉光覆在其上——
一道来自将临之日 的光，
无形地旅行，向东方而去。
在他云雾般的衣袍宽阔垂荫里，
我一动不动地伸展在他身侧；
而他双眼以那平静、无动于衷的威力，
像一场傍晚的阵雨抚慰我的心，
领着一列幽灵般、远荡的队伍，
把往昔的时辰再次引进我的灵。

其中有对恶事的恐惧，它们石头般的眼睛
把欢乐冻结在它涌流的旋律里。
有的远远漂在你平静的波上，
那寻觅坟墓的心便抬头仰望；
另一些像宾客一样进了胸怀，
给它们粗野的儿女留下更多悲伤、更少羞愧；
因为死的神色已从它们冰冷额头退去，
它们祝福那些向它们俯首的头颅；
当它们漂远，隐入遥处的幽暗，
感激跟随它们直到坟墓。
也有许多希望，找不到一处歇脚的地方，
在整片大洋胸膛的奔涌之中；
便飞回那患病的心里，
却在归途上化作了忧伤；
穿过那渐暗的海的呜咽，
不曾从橄榄树携来一片叶。
也有许多欢乐，用她们少女的眼睛张望，
微笑了，随后带着一阵伤心的惊奇消逝；
还有尘世之爱，她美丽的形影
在阳光与风暴中向我招手；
可当那跳跃的心高高跃起，
以无言的叹息迎接她的微笑，
双臂痛楚地一颤，垂回身侧，
抱住的只是一片空无，贴在心上。

===Original===

And the voice of the dying I seem to hear
But whether his breathing is in mine ear,
Or the sounds of the breaking billows roll
The lingering accents upon my soul,
I know not; but thus they seem to bear
Reproof to my soul for its faint despair:﻿—
Blame not life, it is scarce begun;
Blame not mankind, thyself art one.
And change is holy, oh! blame it never;
Thy soul shall live by its changing ever;
Not the bubbling change of a stagnant pool,
But the change of a river, flowing and full;
Where all that is noble and good will grow
Mightier still as the full tides flow;
Till it joins the hidden, the boundless sea,
Rolling through depths of Eternity.
Blame not thy thought that it cannot reach
That which the Infinite must teach;
Bless thy God that the Word came nigh
To guide thee home to thy native sky,
Where all things are homely and glorious too,
And the children are wondering, and glad, and true.

And he pointed away to an Eastern star,
That gleamed through his robes o’er the ocean afar;
And I knew that a star had looked o’er the rim
Of my world that lay all dreary and dim;
And was slowly dissolving the darkness deep
Which, like evil nurse, had soothed me to sleep;
And rising higher, and shining clearer,
Would draw the day-spring ever nearer,
Till the sunshine of God burst full on the morn,
And every hill and valley would start
With the joy of light and new gratitude born
To Him who had led me home to His heart;
And all things that lived in my world within
With the gladness of tears to His feet come in;
And the false Self be banished with fiends to dwell
In the gloomiest haunts of his native hell;
And Pride, that ruled like a god above,
Be trod ’neath the feet of triumphant Love.

And again he pointed across the sea,
And another vision arose in me:
And I knew I walked an ocean of fear,
Yet of safety too, for the Master was near;
And every wave of sorrow or dread,
O’er which strong faith should upraise my head,
Would show from the height of its troubled crest
Still nearer and nearer the Land of Rest.
And when the storm-spray on the wind should arise,
And with tears unbidden should blind mine eyes,
And hide from my vision the Home of Love,
I knew I must look to the star above,
And the mists of Passion would quickly flee,
And the storm would faint to serenity.

===Chinese===

而我仿佛听见那垂死者的话音，
但究竟是他的呼吸在我耳边，
还是碎裂的波涛翻滚的声音
把那萦回的字句送上我的灵魂，
我不知道；但它们似乎这样
为我的沮丧绝望带回责备：——
不要责怪生命，它才刚刚开始；
不要责怪人类，你自己便是其中之一。
而变化是神圣的，哦！永远不要责怪它；
你的灵魂将靠它永恒的变化而活；
不是死水塘里冒泡的变，
而是江河的变，奔涌而充盈；
在那里一切高贵与良善将生长，
随着满涨的潮水越发雄壮；
直到它汇入那隐秘的无垠之海，
滚过永恒的深处。
不要责怪你的思想够不着
那唯有无限者才能教授的功课；
要称颂你的上帝，那圣言已临近，
引你回家，回到你本乡的天上，
那里万物既亲切又荣耀，
儿女们满心惊奇、欢喜而真诚。

他抬手指向远处一颗东方的星，
它透过他的衣袍，在远海之上闪烁；
我便知道有一颗星已越过我那
凄凉昏暗的世界的边沿；
正慢慢消融那深沉的黑暗——
它曾像邪恶的乳母，哄我入睡；
它越升越高，越照越清，
要把那破晓越拉越近，
直到上帝的阳光在清晨迸涌，
每一座山丘、每一个山谷都将惊起，
带着光的喜悦和新生的感恩，
献给那领我回他心里的主；
而我内在世界里一切活着的，
都要带着泪的欢喜来到他脚前；
而虚假的自己要被放逐，与魔鬼同住
在它本乡地狱最阴森的巢穴；
而那像神一样高踞的骄傲，
要被踩在凯旋之爱的脚下。

他又一次指向海的彼岸，
另一个异象在我里面升起：
我便知道我正行走在一片恐惧的洋上，
却也是安全的洋上，因为主就在近旁；
而每一道忧伤或惊惶的波浪，
只要坚强的信心能抬起我的头越过它，
都会从它骚动的浪峰高处
显出那安息之地越来越近。
而当风暴的水沫乘风扬起，
当不由自主的泪水遮瞎我的眼，
把爱的家园从我的视野里藏起，
我知道我必须仰望上方那颗星，
激情的迷雾就会迅速逃散，
风暴也会弱成一片澄宁。

===Original===

And again it seemed as if words found scope,
The sorrowing words of a farewell Hope:
“I will meet thee again in that deathless land,
Whenever thy foot shall imprint the strand;
And the loveliest things that have here been mine,
Shall there in eternal beauty shine;
For there I shall live and never die,
Part of a glorious Eternity;
For the death of Time is To be forgot,
And I go where oblivion entereth not.”

He was dead. He had gone to the rest of his race,
With a sad smile frozen upon his face.
Deadness clouded his eyes. And his death-bell rung,
And my sorrowing thoughts his low requiem sung;
And with trembling steps his worn body cast
In the wide charnel-house of the dreary Past.
Thus met the noble Old Year his end:
Rest him in peace, for he was my friend.

As my thoughts returned from their wandering,
A voice in my spirit was lingering;
And its sounds were like Spring’s first breeze’s hum,
When the oak-leaves fall, and the young leaves come:

Time dieth ever, is ever born:
On the footsteps of night so treadeth the morn;
Shadow and brightness, death and birth,
Chasing each other o’er the round earth.
But the spirit of Time from his tomb is springing,
The dust of decay from his pinions flinging;
Ever renewing his glorious youth,
Scattering around him the dew of Truth.
Oh, let it raise in the desert heart
Fountains and flowers that shall never depart!
This spirit will fill us with thought sublime;
For the End of God is the spirit of Time.

===Chinese===

又一次，仿佛话语找到了出口，
那告别着的希望说出的忧伤话语：
「我会在那不死之地与你重逢，
无论何时你的脚踏上那片沙岸；
而在这里曾属于我的最美之物，
将在那里以永恒的美放光；
因为在那里我将活着，永不再死，
作那荣耀的永恒的一部分；
因为时间的死就是被遗忘，
而我去的所在，遗忘无法进入。」

他死了。他已归到他族人的安息，
脸上凝着一抹凄然的微笑。
死色蒙住了他的眼。他的丧钟响了，
我忧伤的思绪为他唱起低低的安魂曲；
我以颤抖的脚步把他磨损的身体
安放进凄凉往昔的广阔藏骸所。
高贵的旧年就这样到了终点：
愿他安息，因为他是我的朋友。

当我的思绪从漫游中归来，
一个声音还在我灵里萦回；
那声响像春风最初的低吟，
正当橡叶落尽、新叶初生：

时间永远在死，也永远在生：
清晨就这样踏着黑夜的脚印；
影子与光明，死亡与诞生，
在圆圆的大地上互相追赶。
但时间之灵正从坟墓里跃起，
把腐朽的尘土从翼上抖落；
永远更新他荣耀的青春，
把真理的露珠撒在四围。
哦，愿它在那荒漠的心里
涌起永不消逝的泉水和花朵！
这灵要以崇高的思想充满我们；
因为时间之灵，就是上帝的终局。

## A Thanksgiving / 感恩颂
===Original===

I Thank Thee, boundless Giver,
That the thoughts Thou givest flow
In sounds that like a river
All through the darkness go.
And though few should swell the pleasure,
By sharing this my wine,
My heart will clasp its treasure,
This secret gift of Thine.

My heart the joy inherits,
And will oft be sung to rest;
And some wandering hoping spirits
May listen and be blest.
For the sound may break the hours
In a dark and gloomy mood,
As the wind breaks up the bowers
Of the brooding sunless wood.

For every sound of gladness
Is a prophet-wind that tells
Of a summer without sadness,
And a love without farewells;
And a heart that hath no ailing,
And an eye that is not dim,
And a faith that without failing
Shall be complete in Him.

And when my heart is mourning,
The songs it lately gave,
Back to their fount returning,
Make sweet the bitter wave;
And forth a new stream floweth,
In sunshine winding fair;
And through the dark wood goeth
Glad laughter on the air.

For the heart of man that waketh,
Yet hath not ceased to dream,
Is the only fount that maketh
The sweet and bitter stream.
But the sweet will still be flowing
When the bitter stream is dry,
And glad music only going
On the breezes of the sky.

I thank Thee, boundless Giver,
That the thoughts Thou givest flow
In sounds that like a river
All through the darkness go.
And though few should swell the pleasure
By sharing this my wine,
My heart will clasp its treasure,
This secret gift of Thine.

===Chinese===

我感谢你，无限的赐予者，
因你所赐的思想
化作声响，像一条河
流过全部的黑暗。
尽管少有人分享这杯酒
来增添这份欢愉，
我的心仍将紧抱它的珍宝，
你这隐秘的馈赠。

我的心继承了这份喜悦，
将常常被歌声送入安眠；
而一些流浪的盼望之灵
或许听见而蒙福。
因为这声音能击破
那阴沉幽暗的时辰，
如风摇散那不见日光、
郁郁沉思的树林的浓荫。

因为每一声欢欣
都是一阵先知的风，
预告一个没有忧伤的夏天，
一场没有告别的爱；
预告一颗不再疼痛的心，
一双不再昏花的眼睛，
和一份永不动摇的信心，
将在他里面得以完全。

而当我的心哀恸时，
它近日所唱出的歌，
流回它们的泉源，
把苦涩的波酿成甘甜；
于是一道新的溪流涌出，
在阳光里婉蜒而明媚；
穿过幽暗的树林，
空气中荡漾着欢畅的笑声。

因为人那颗醒着、
却从未停止做梦的心，
是唯一能酿出
甘甜与苦涩溪流的泉。
但当苦涩的溪流干涸，
甘甜的将依旧流淌，
唯有欢欣的音乐
继续行走在天上的微风里。

我感谢你，无限的赐予者，
因你所赐的思想
化作声响，像一条河
流过全部的黑暗。
尽管少有人分享这杯酒
来增添这份欢愉，
我的心仍将紧抱它的珍宝，
你这隐秘的馈赠。

## The Gospel Women / 福音书中的妇女们
===Original===



===Chinese===

（组诗）

### I The Mother Mary / 一、母亲马利亚
===Original===

I

Mary, to thee the heart was given
For infant hand to hold,
And clasp thus, an eternal heaven,
The great earth in its fold.

He seized the world with tender might
By making thee his own;
Thee, lowly queen, whose heavenly height
Was to thyself unknown.

He came, all helpless, to thy power,
For warmth, and love, and birth;
In thy embraces, every hour,
He grew into the earth.

Thine was the grief, O mother high,
Which all thy sisters share
Who keep the gate betwixt the sky
And this our lower air;

But unshared sorrows, gathering slow,
Will rise within thy heart,
Strange thoughts which like a sword will go
Thorough thy inward part.

For, if a woman bore a son
That was of angel brood,
Who lifted wings ere day was done,
And soared from where she stood,

Wild grief would rave on love’s high throne;
She, sitting in the door,
All day would cry: “He was my own,
And now is mine no more!”

So thou, O Mary, years on years,
From child-birth to the cross,
Wast filled with yearnings, filled with fears,
Keen sense of love and loss.

His childish thoughts outsoared thy reach;
His godlike tenderness
Would sometimes seem, in human speech,
To thee than human less.

Strange pangs await thee, mother mild,
A sorer travail-pain;
Then will the spirit of thy child
Be born in thee again.

Till then thou wilt forebode and dread;
Loss will be still thy fear﻿—
Till he be gone, and, in his stead,
His very self appear.

For, when thy son hath reached his goal,
And vanished from the earth,
Soon wilt thou find him in thy soul,
A second, holier birth.

II

Ah, there he stands! With wondering face
Old men surround the boy;
The solemn looks, the awful place
Bestill the mother’s joy.

In sweet reproach her gladness hid,
Her trembling voice says﻿—low,
Less like the chiding than the chid﻿—
“How couldst thou leave us so?”

But will her dear heart understand
The answer that he gives﻿—
Childlike, eternal, simple, grand,
The law by which he lives?

“Why sought ye me?” Ah, mother dear,
The gulf already opes
That will in thee keep live the fear,
And part thee from thy hopes!

“My father’s business﻿—that ye know
I cannot choose but do.”
Mother, if he that work forego,
Not long he cares for you.

Creation’s harder, better part
Now occupies his hand:
I marvel not the mother’s heart
Not yet could understand.

III

===Chinese===

一

马利亚，那颗心是赐给你的，
让婴儿的手来握住，
于是把永恒的天，
连同偌大的大地，抱在怀里。

他以温柔的权能攫取了世界，
藉着使你归他自己；
你，卑微的王后，你属天的高度
连你自己也不知晓。

他全然无助地来到你的能力之下，
求温暖，求爱，求降生；
在你的怀抱里，每一个时辰，
他都更深地长入这个世界。

忧伤原是你的，哦崇高的母亲，
这忧伤你所有的姊妹共享，
她们守着天上
与我们这下层空气之间的门；

但无人分担的忧伤，缓缓积聚，
将在你心里升起，
陌生的意念将像一把利剑
刺透你的内心。

因为，若一个妇人生了一个
属于天使族类的儿子，
天还未尽他就展翅，
从她站立处腾空而去，

狂乱的悲恸会在爱的高座上咆哮；
她坐在门口，
会整日哭喊：「他原是我的，
如今不再是我的了！」

所以你，哦马利亚，年复一年，
从生产直到十字架，
被渴慕填满，被恐惧填满，
对爱与失去有敏锐的知觉。

他孩童的思想超出你所能及；
他那神一般的温柔
有时在人的言语里，
对你竟显得比人还要少人情。

陌生的剧痛在等你，温良的母亲，
一场更重的产痛；
到那时你孩子的灵
要在你里面再度诞生。

在那之前你将预感并惧怕；
失去会一直是你的恐惧——
直到他离去，而在他原来的地方，
他自己的本尊显现。

因为，当你的儿子抵达了他的目标，
从地上消失，
你不久便会在你灵魂里寻见他，
一次第二的、更圣洁的诞生。

二

啊，他站在那里！老人们带着惊异的神色
围住这孩子；
庄严的面容、可畏的场所
使母亲的欢喜静默。

她甜蜜的责备里藏着欢喜，
她颤抖的声音说——很低，
不像责备者，倒像被责备的——
「你怎么这样离开我们？」

但她亲爱的心能明白
他所给的回答吗——
孩子气的、永恒的、单纯的、庄严的，
他赖以存活的法则？

「为什么找我呢？」啊，亲爱的母亲，
那道鸿沟已经张开，
它将使那恐惧在你里面长活，
把你与你的盼望隔开！

「我父的事——你们知道的，
我不能不做。」
母亲啊，他若放下那工作，
他对你也就不会长久在意。

创造之工更难、更好的那一半
此刻正占用他的手：
我不奇怪母亲的心
那时还不能明白。

三

===Original===

The Lord of life among them rests;
They quaff the merry wine;
They do not know, those wedding guests,
The present power divine.

Believe, on such a group he smiled,
Though he might sigh the while;
Believe not, sweet-souled Mary’s child
Was born without a smile.

He saw the pitchers, high upturned,
Their last red drops outpour;
His mother’s cheek with triumph burned,
And expectation wore.

He knew the prayer her bosom housed,
He read it in her eyes;
Her hopes in him sad thoughts have roused
Ere yet her words arise.

“They have no wine!” she, halting, said,
Her prayer but half begun;
Her eyes went on, “Lift up thy head,
Show what thou art, my son!”

A vision rose before his eyes,
The cross, the waiting tomb,
The people’s rage, the darkened skies,
His unavoided doom:

Ah woman dear, thou must not fret
Thy heart’s desire to see!
His hour of honour is not yet﻿—
’Twill come too soon for thee!

His word was dark; his tone was kind;
His heart the mother knew;
His eyes in hers looked deep, and shined;
They gave her heart the cue.

Another, on the word intent,
Had read refusal there;
She heard in it a full consent,
A sweetly answered prayer.

“Whate’er he saith unto you, do.”
Out flowed his grapes divine;
Though then, as now, not many knew
Who makes the water wine.

IV

“He is beside himself!” Dismayed,
His mother, brothers talked:
He from the well-known path had strayed
In which their fathers walked!

With troubled hearts they sought him. Loud
Some one the message bore:﻿—
He stands within, amid a crowd,
They at the open door:﻿—

“Thy mother and thy brothers would
Speak with thee. Lo, they stand
Without and wait thee!” Like a flood
Of sunrise on the land,

A new-born light his face o’erspread;
Out from his eyes it poured;
He lifted up that gracious head,
Looked round him, took the word:

“My mother﻿—brothers﻿—who are they?”
Hearest thou, Mary mild?
This is a sword that well may slay﻿—
Disowned by thy child!

Ah, no! My brothers, sisters, hear﻿—
