They are our humble lord’s!
O mother, did they wound thy ear?﻿—
We thank him for the words.

“Who are my friends?” Oh, hear him say,
Stretching his hand abroad,
“My mother, sisters, brothers, are they
That do the will of God!”

My brother! Lord of life and me,
If life might grow to this!﻿—
Would it not, brother, sister, be
Enough for all amiss?

===Chinese===

生命之主在他们中间歇息；
他们畅饮喜庆的酒；
那些婚宴的宾客并不知道
在场的是神圣的能力。

要相信，他对这样一群人微笑过，
虽然他可能同时叹息；
不要以为，那心灵甜蜜的马利亚之子
生来不会微笑。

他看见石缸，高高倒尽，
倒出最后几滴红酒；
他母亲的面颊燃着胜利，
脸上带着期待的气色。

他知道她胸中收藏的祈求，
他从她眼里读出了它；
她寄望于他的念头，已勾起忧伤，
在她开口之前。

「他们没有酒了！」她迟疑地说，
祷告只起了一个头；
她的眼睛接下去说：「抬起你的头，
显明你是谁，我的儿子！」

一幅异象在他眼前升起：
十字架，等候的坟墓，
民众的狂怒，变暗的天空，
他无法逃避的定命：

啊亲爱的妇人，你切不可焦躁，
强求看见你心所愿！
他得荣耀的时刻还没有到——
对你，它来得已经太快！

他的话幽暗；他的语气却温存；
母亲懂得他的心；
他的眼深深望进她的眼，闪着光；
它们给了她的心暗示。

换一个人，专注在这句话上，
会读出拒绝的意思；
她却在其中听出完全的应允，
一个蒙应允的甘美祷告。

「他告诉你们什么，你们就做什么。」
他神圣的葡萄汁流涌而出；
虽然那时如同今日，并不多的人知道
是谁把水变成了酒。

四

「他癫狂了！」惊惶中，
他的母亲和兄弟们议论：
他离开了那人人熟识的路，
就是他们祖祖辈辈走的路！

他们心里烦乱地去找他。有人
大声传话进去：——
他站在里面，在人群中央，
他们站在敞开的门口：——

「你母亲和你兄弟想
跟你说话。看，他们
站在外面等你！」如同一片
旭日的光泛滥在地上，

一道新生的光布满他的脸；
光从他眼中涌流；
他抬起那恩慈的头，
环视四周，接住这话：

「我的母亲——兄弟——他们是谁？」
你听见了吗，温良的马利亚？
这是一柄足以致命的剑——
被你的孩子否认！

啊，不！我的兄弟、姊妹们，请听——
他们是我们谦卑之主的亲人！
哦母亲，这话可曾刺伤你的耳？——
我们却为这话感谢他。

「谁是我的朋友？」哦，听他说，
他的手向四围伸开，
「我的母亲、姊妹、兄弟，
就是那些遵行上帝旨意的人！」

我的兄长！生命与我的主，
但愿生命真能长到这般！——
兄长啊，姊妹啊，这岂不足够
抵偿一切的不完美？

===Original===

Yea, mother, hear him and rejoice:
Thou art his mother still,
But may’st be more﻿—of thy own choice
Doing his Father’s will.

Ambition for thy son restrain,
Thy will to God’s will bow:
Thy son he shall be yet again.
And twice his mother thou.

O humble man, O faithful son!
That woman most forlorn
Who yet thy father’s will hath done,
Thee, son of man, hath born!

V

Life’s best things gather round its close
To light it from the door;
When woman’s aid no further goes,
She weeps and loves the more.

She doubted oft, feared for his life,
Yea, feared his mission’s loss;
But now she shares the losing strife,
And weeps beside the cross.

The dreaded hour is come at last,
The sword hath reached her soul;
The hour of tortured hope is past,
And gained the awful goal.

There hangs the son her body bore,
The limbs her arms had prest!
The hands, the feet the driven nails tore
Had lain upon her breast!

He speaks; the words how faintly brief,
And how divinely dear!
The mother’s heart yearns through its grief
Her dying son to hear.

“Woman, behold thy son.﻿—Behold
Thy mother.” Blessed hest
That friend to her torn heart to fold
Who understood him best!

Another son﻿—ah, not instead!﻿—
He gave, lest grief should kill,
While he was down among the dead,
Doing his father’s will.

No, not instead! the coming joy
Will make him hers anew;
More hers than when, a little boy,
His life from hers he drew.

===Chinese===

是啊，母亲，听他并且欢喜：
你仍是他的母亲，
却可以成为更多——凭你自己的选择，
去行他父的旨意。

收敛你为儿子存的雄心，
把你的意志俯就上帝的意志：
他还将是你的儿子，
而你将两度是他的母亲。

哦谦卑的人，哦孝顺的儿子！
那个最孤苦、
却仍遵行了天父旨意的妇人，
生了你，人子！

五

人生最好的事物聚拢在终点，
从门口照亮它；
当妇人的帮助再无处可使，
她便越发哭泣，越发爱。

她屡屡疑惑，为他的性命惧怕，
是啊，怕他的使命受亏损；
如今她分担这场失败的争战，
在十字架旁哭泣。

那惧怕的时辰终于来了，
利剑刺透了她的灵魂；
受煎的盼望的时辰过去了，
可怕的目标已经抵达。

那里挂着她的儿子，她亲生的，
那她双臂曾环抱的肢体！
那被长钉撕裂的手、脚，
曾安睡在她的胸怀！

他说话；那话多么简短而微弱，
又多么神圣而亲爱！
母亲的心穿过忧伤渴望着，
要听她垂死的儿子。

「妇人，看你的儿子。——看
你的母亲。」蒙福的嘱托，
把那最懂他的朋友
交给她撕裂的心去怀抱！

另一个儿子——啊，不是代替的！——
他这样赐下，免得忧伤致她于死，
当他下到死人中，
行他父的旨意的时候。

不，不是代替！将临的喜乐
要使他重新归她；
比他还是个小男孩、
生命从她汲取的时候更属她。

### II The Woman That Lifted Up Her Voice / 二、那个扬声呼喊的妇人
===Original===

Filled with his words of truth and right,
Her heart will break or cry:
A woman’s cry bursts forth in might
Of loving agony.

“Blessed the womb, thee, Lord, that bare!
The bosom that thee fed!”
A moment’s silence filled the air,
All heard the words she said.

He turns his face: he knows the cry,
The fountain whence it springs﻿—
A woman’s heart that glad would die
For woman’s best of things.

Good thoughts, though laggard in the rear,
He never quenched or chode:
“Yea, rather, blessed they that hear
And keep the word of God!”

He would uplift her, not rebuke.
The crowd began to stir.
We miss how she the answer took;
We hear no more of her.

===Chinese===

满了他的真理与正直的话语，
她的心快要迸裂，快要呼喊：
一个妇人的呼喊迸发出来，
带着爱的剧痛的力量。

「那怀你、乳你的胎和怀是有福的！
主啊，那哺育你的胸怀！」
一刹那的静默充满空气，
众人都听见她所说的话。

他转过脸来：他认得这呼喊，
认得它涌出的泉源——
一颗妇人的心，甘愿为
妇人最珍视的东西而死。

善的念头，哪怕落在队伍后面，
他也从不熄灭、从不苛责：
「是，却还不如那听
上帝之道而遵守的人有福！」

他要高举她，不是责备她。
人群开始骚动。
她怎样领受了这句回答，我们错失了；
此后再没有她的音讯。

### III The Mother of Zebedee’s Children / 三、西庇太孩子的母亲
===Original===

She knelt, she bore a bold request,
Though shy to speak it out:
Ambition, even in mother’s breast,
Before him stood in doubt.

“What is it?” “Grant thy promise now,
My sons on thy right hand
And on thy left shall sit when thou
Art king, Lord, in the land.”

“Ye know not what ye ask.” There lay
A baptism and a cup
She understood not, in the way
By which he must go up.

Her mother-love would lift them high
Above their fellow-men;
Her woman-pride would, standing nigh,
Share in their grandeur then!

Would she have joyed o’er prosperous quest,
Counted her prayer well heard,
Had they, of three on Calvary’s crest,
Hung dying, first and third?

She knoweth neither way nor end:
In dark despair, full soon,
She will not mock the gracious friend
With prayer for any boon.

Higher than love could dream or dare
To ask, he them will set;
They shall his cup and baptism share,
And share his kingdom yet!

They, entering at his palace-door,
Will shun the lofty seat;
Will gird themselves, and water pour,
And wash each other’s feet;

Then down beside their lowly Lord
On the Father’s throne shall sit:
For them who godlike help afford
God hath prepared it.

===Chinese===

她跪下，她带来一个大胆的请求，
却又羞于启齿：
野心，即使在母亲的胸怀，
站在他面前也踌躇不定。

「要什么？」「求你现在应允：
当你在国里作王的时候，
我这两个儿子，一个坐在
你右边，一个坐在你左边。」

「你们不知道所求的是什么。」
在那条他必须上去的路里，
藏着一个洗、一个杯，
她并不能明白。

她母亲的爱想把他们抬高，
高过他们的同伴；
她妇人的骄傲想站在近旁，
分享他们那时的显赫！

倘若在加利利山顶三个人中，
他们两个先后受难、垂死，
她还会为顺遂的求告欢喜、
觉得蒙垂听吗？

她既不知道路，也不知道结局：
不久，在黑暗的绝望里，
她就不会再拿任何祈求
去烦扰那位恩慈的朋友。

比爱敢想敢求更高的，
他要安置他们；
他们要分他的杯和他的洗，
还要分他的国度！

他们进他宫殿的门时，
必避开那高座；
必束上腰带，倒出水来，
彼此洗脚；

然后在他们卑微的主身旁，
坐在父的宝座上：
因为那行神一样帮助的人，
上帝已为他们预备了这座位。

### IV The Syrophenician Woman / 四、叙利腓尼基族的妇人
===Original===

“Grant, Lord, her prayer, and let her go;
She crieth after us.”
Nay, to the dogs ye cast it so;
Serve not a woman thus.

Their pride, by condescension fed,
He shapes with teaching tongue:
“It is not meet the children’s bread
To little dogs be flung.”

The words, for tender heart so sore,
His voice did seem to rue;
The gentle wrath his countenance wore,
With her had not to do.

He makes her share the hurt of good,
Takes what she would have lent,
That those proud men their evil mood
May see, and so repent;

And that the hidden faith in her
May burst in soaring flame:
With childhood deeper, holier,
Is birthright not the same?

Ill names, of proud religion born﻿—
She’ll wear the worst that comes;
Will clothe her, patient, in their scorn,
To share the healing crumbs!

“Truth, Lord; and yet the puppies small
Under the table eat
The crumbs the little ones let fall﻿—
That is not thought unmeet.”

The prayer rebuff could not amate
Was not like water spilt:
“O woman, but thy faith is great!
Be it even as thou wilt.”

Thrice happy she who yet will dare,
Who, baffled, prayeth still!
He, if he may, will grant her prayer
In fullness of her will!

===Chinese===

「主啊，应允她的祷告，让她走吧；
她在我们后头喊叫。」
不，你们竟这样把她当狗打发；
不可这样对待一个妇人。

他们的骄傲，被降尊所喂养，
他用教导的舌头来重塑：
「拿儿女的饼
丢给小狗吃，是不合适的。」

这些话，对温柔的心是那样沉重，
他的声音似乎也在惋惜；
他面容上温和的怒意，
与她并没有相干。

他使她分担良善所受的伤害，
接受她愿意借出的，
好让那些骄傲的人看见
自己的恶意，从而悔悟；

也让她里面隐藏的信心
迸发为飞腾的火焰：
比起孩童，那更深、更圣的，
难道不正是同一份名分？

骄傲的宗教所生的恶名——
最坏的她也肯担当；
她要以忍耐为衣，穿上他们的藐视，
只为分享那医治的碎渣！

「主啊，不错；但是小狗
也吃主人桌子上
掉下来的碎渣——
这不算不合适吧。」

这被拒绝却不能冷却的祷告，
不是泼出去的水：
「妇人，你的信心是大的！
照你所要的，给你成全吧。」

三倍有福的她，仍敢于祈求，
被挡回，仍旧祷告！
他若能够，就必照她
心愿的丰满成全她！

### V The Widow of Nain / 五、拿因的寡妇
===Original===

Forth from the city, with the load
That makes the trampling low,
They walk along the dreary road
That dust and ashes go.

The other way, toward the gate
Their trampling strong and loud,
With hope of liberty elate,
Comes on another crowd.

Nearer and nearer draw the twain﻿—
One with a wailing cry!
How could the Life let such a train
Of death and tears go by!

“Weep not,” he said, and touched the bier:
They stand, the dead who bear;
The mother knows nor hope nor fear﻿—
He waits not for her prayer.

“Young man, I say to thee, arise.”
Who hears, he must obey:
Up starts the body; wide the eyes
Flash wonder and dismay.

The lips would speak, as if they caught
Some converse sudden broke
When the great word the dead man sought,
And Hades’ silence woke.

The lips would speak: the eyes’ wild stare
Gives place to ordered sight;
The murmur dies upon the air;
The soul is dumb with light.

He brings no news; he has forgot,
Or saw with vision weak:
Thou sees! all our unseen lot,
And yet thou dost not speak.

Hold’st thou the news, as parent might
A too good gift, away,
Lest we should neither sleep at night,
Nor do our work by day?

The mother leaves us not a spark
Of her triumph over grief;
Her tears alone have left their mark
Upon the holy leaf:

Oft gratitude will thanks benumb,
Joy will our laughter quell:
May not Eternity be dumb
With things too good to tell?

Her straining arms her lost one hold;
Question she asketh none;
She trusts for all he leaves untold;
Enough, to clasp her son!

The ebb is checked, the flow begun,
Sent rushing to the gate:
Death turns him backward to the sun,
And life is yet our fate!

===Chinese===

从城里出来，抬着那
使脚步低沉的重担，
他们沿着凄凉的路走去，
尘土与灰烬一路同行。

另一头，朝着城门，
脚步声沉重而响亮，
另一群人迎面而来，
因自由的盼望而高昂。

两支队伍越走越近——
一边是哀哭的呼号！
生命之主岂能任这样一支
死亡与眼泪的队伍走过！

「不要哭，」他说，触了棺杠：
抬的人站住了，那些抬死人的；
那母亲既无盼望也无惧怕——
他不等她开口祈求。

「少年人，我吩咐你，起来。」
谁听见，谁就必须顺从：
那身体一跃而起；眼睛睁大，
闪过惊奇与惶惑。

那嘴唇像要说话，仿佛它正接住
一段骤然中断的谈话，
当那句伟言落下，死者寻找的，
和阴间的寂静一齐醒来。

那嘴唇要说话：眼中狂乱的一瞥
让位给有序的视力；
低语在空气里消散；
灵魂被光照得静默。

他没有带回消息；他已忘记，
或是看得模糊：
你看我们一切未见的命运，
却仍旧不说。

你是否像父母那样，把消息、
把那太好的礼物扣住，
免得我们夜里睡不着，
白天也不肯做工？

那母亲没有给我们留下一点
她胜过忧伤的凯旋；
只有她的眼泪在圣洁的书页上
留下了它们的印记：

感激常使感谢语塞，
喜乐会止住我们的笑声：
永恒岂不也可能缄默，
因为有太多美好无法言说？

她伸出的双臂抱住她失而复得的孩子；
她什么也没有问；
他不说的，她一概信托；
抱住她的儿子，就已经足够！

退潮止住，涨潮开始，
涌着冲向城门：
死亡转身背向太阳，
而生命仍是我们的定命！

### VI The Woman Whom Satan Had Bound / 六、被撒但捆绑的女人
===Original===

For years eighteen she, patient soul,
Her eyes had graveward sent;
Her earthly life was lapt in dole,
She was so bowed and bent.

What words! To her? Who can be near?
What tenderness of hands!
Oh! is it strength, or fancy mere?
New hope, or breaking bands?

The pent life rushes swift along
Channels it used to know;
Up, up, amid the wondering throng,
She rises firm and slow﻿—

To bend again in grateful awe﻿—
For will is power at length﻿—
In homage to the living Law
Who gives her back her strength.

Uplifter of the down-bent head!
Unbinder of the bound!
Who seest all the burdened
Who only see the ground!

Although they see thee not, nor cry,
Thou watchest for the hour
To lift the forward-beaming eye,
To wake the slumbering power!

Thy hand will wipe the stains of time
From off the withered face;
Upraise thy bowed old men, in prime
Of youthful manhood’s grace!

Like summer days from winter’s tomb,
Shall rise thy women fair;
Gray Death, a shadow, not a doom,
Lo, is not anywhere!

All ills of life shall melt away
As melts a cureless woe,
When, by the dawning of the day
Surprised, the dream must go.

I think thou, Lord, wilt heal me too,
Whate’er the needful cure;
The great best only thou wilt do,
And hoping I endure.

===Chinese===

十八年来，她，这忍耐的灵魂，
把眼睛一直送向坟墓；
她地上的生命裹着悲苦，
她被压得这样弯、这样曲。

这话是对她说的！有谁在近旁？
那是怎样温柔的一双手！
哦！这是力量，还是纯粹的幻觉？
是新的盼望，还是挣断的捆索？

被郁积的生命沿着旧识的河道
迅猛地奔流；
起来，起来，在惊奇的众人中间，
她坚定而缓慢地站起——

再次弯下腰去，这一次是感激的敬畏——
因为意志终于成了力量——
向那活的话语顶礼，
是他把力量还给了她。

你，垂头者的抬升者！
你，被缚者的解索人！
你看见一切负重的，
他们却只看得见地面！

虽然他们看不见你，也不呼求，
你却在守候那个时辰，
要抬起那向前采光的眼，
要唤醒沉睡的力量！

你的手要从苍老的脸上
拭去岁月的污痕；
要扶起你年迈的老人，
使他们返老还童，风华重现！

如夏日从冬天的坟墓里升起，
你的妇女们也将那样站起；
苍老的死亡，只是一道影，不是定命，
看哪，它已无处可寻！

生命的一切疾患都将消融，
如一场无法医治的悲苦消融，
当白昼的破晓使它措手不及，
梦就必须离去。

我想，主啊，你也要医治我，
无论那必要的疗法是什么；
你只会行那至大至好的，
我便怀着盼望忍耐。

### VII The Woman Who Came Behind Him in the Crowd / 七、人群中从他背后摸他的女人
===Original===

Near him she stole, rank after rank;
She feared approach too loud;
She touched his garment’s hem, and shrank
Back in the sheltering crowd.

A shame-faced gladness thrills her frame:
Her twelve years’ fainting prayer
Is heard at last! she is the same
As other women there!

She hears his voice. He looks about.
Ah! is it kind or good
To drag her secret sorrow out
Before that multitude?

The eyes of men she dares not meet﻿—
On her they straight must fall!﻿—
Forward she sped, and at his feet
Fell down, and told him all.

To the one refuge she hath flown,
The Godhead’s burning flame!
Of all earth’s women she alone
Hears there the tenderest name:

“Daughter,” he said, “be of good cheer;
Thy faith hath made thee whole:”
With plenteous love, not healing mere,
He comforteth her soul.

===Chinese===

她悄悄挨近他，一排又一排；
她怕走近的动静太大；
她摸了一下他的衣裳繸子，便缩回
人群的遮蔽里。

一阵带着羞怯的狂喜流遍她全身：
她十二年微弱的祈求
终于蒙垂听！她和那里的
其他女人一样了！

她听见他的声音。他环顾四周。
啊！把这隐秘的伤痛
拖到众人面前，
这是仁慈，是好事吗？

众人的眼睛她不敢迎对——
它们势必直落在她身上！——
她抢先奔出，在他的脚前
俯伏在地，把一切告诉了他。

她投奔那唯一的避难所，
神性燃烧的火焰！
地上一切妇女中，唯独她
在那里听见了最温柔的称呼：

「女儿，」他说，「放心；
你的信救了你：」
他以丰盈的爱，不止于医治，
安慰了她的灵魂。

### VIII The Widow with the Two Mites / 八、投两个小钱的寡妇
===Original===

Here much and little shift and change,
With scale of need and time;
There more and less have meanings strange,
Which the world cannot rime.

Sickness may be more hale than health,
And service kingdom high;
Yea, poverty be bounty’s wealth,
To give like God thereby.

Bring forth your riches; let them go,
Nor mourn the lost control;
For if ye hoard them, surely so
Their rust will reach your soul.

Cast in your coins, for God delights
When from wide hands they fall;
But here is one who brings two mites,
And thus gives more than all.

I think she did not hear the praise﻿—
Went home content with need;
Walked in her old poor generous ways,
Nor knew her heavenly meed.

===Chinese===

这里，多与少换来换去，
随需要的秤和时间而变；
那里，多与少另有奇异的含义，
是这世界押不出韵的。

疾病可以比健康更康健，
服侍可以是高位的国度；
是啊，贫穷可以是丰施的财富，
借此像上帝那样给予。

拿出你们的财富来；任它去，
不要哀悼失去的掌控；
因为你们若囤积它，它的锈
必定要蛀到你们的灵魂。

投下你们的银钱，因为上帝喜悦
银钱从宽广的手中落下；
可这里有一个人，只带来两个小钱，
却这样献上了比众人更多的。

我想她并没有听见那称赞——
带着匮乏回家，心满意足；
照旧走她贫穷而慷慨的老路，
并不知道她天上的赏赐。

### IX The Women Who Ministered Unto Him / 九、服事他的妇女们
===Original===

Enough he labours for his hire;
Yea, nought can pay his pain;
But powers that wear and waste and tire,
Need help to toil again.

They give him freely all they can,
They give him clothes and food;
In this rejoicing, that the man
Is not ashamed they should.

High love takes form in lowly thing;
He knows the offering such;
To them ’tis little that they bring,
To him ’tis very much.

===Chinese===

他为他的工价劳苦，已尽够了；
是啊，什么都抵不了他的痛；
但那磨损、消耗、疲乏的力气，
需要扶持才能再度劳作。

她们把能给的都白白给了他，
给他衣裳，给他饮食；
并且以此为喜，因为这个人
并不以受她们接济为耻。

高贵的爱取了卑微的形相；
他知道这祭献的分量；
在她们，所献的微不足道，
在他，却是极重无比。

### X Pilate’s Wife / 十、彼拉多的妻子
===Original===

Why came in dreams the low-born man
Between thee and thy rest?
In vain thy whispered message ran,
Though justice was its quest!

Did some young ignorant angel dare﻿—
Not knowing what must be,
Or blind with agony of care﻿—
To fly for help to thee?

I know not. Rather I believe,
Thou, nobler than thy spouse,
His rumoured grandeur didst receive,
And sit with pondering brows,

Until thy maidens’ gathered tale
With possible marvel teems:
Thou sleepest, and the prisoner pale
Returneth in thy dreams.

Well mightst thou suffer things not few
For his sake all the night!
In pale eclipse he suffers, who
Is of the world the light.

Precious it were to know thy dream
Of such a one as he!
Perhaps of him we, waking, deem
As poor a verity.

===Chinese===

为何那出身卑微的人，在梦中
来到你与你安息之间？
你低声传的话白白流过，
虽然它寻求的是公义！

是哪个年幼无知的天使胆敢——
不知道事情必然如此，
或是被苦痛的煎迫弄瞎了眼——
飞来向你求援？

我不知道。我倒宁愿相信，
你，比你的丈夫更高贵，
听见了传闻中他的尊贵，
便坐着蹙眉深思，

直到你侍女们汇集的传闻
堆满了似真似幻的奇事：
你睡着了，那苍白的囚徒
又回到你的梦里。

你彻夜为他受了许多苦，
实在是应当的！
他苍白地受着遮蔽，而他
本是这世界的光。

你做的那个关于他的梦
若能知道，何等珍贵！
或许我们醒着时对他的臆想，
也同样是可怜的虚影。

### XI The Woman of Samaria / 十一、撒玛利亚的妇人
===Original===

In the hot sun, for water cool
She walked in listless mood:
When back she ran, her pitcher full
Forgot behind her stood.

Like one who followed straying sheep,
A weary man she saw,
Who sat upon the well so deep,
And nothing had to draw.

“Give me to drink,” he said. Her hand
Was ready with reply;
From out the old well of the land
She drew him plenteously.

He spake as never man before;
She stands with open ears;
He spake of holy days in store,
Laid bare the vanished years.

She cannot still her throbbing heart,
She hurries to the town,
And cries aloud in street and mart,
“The Lord is here: come down.”

Her life before was strange and sad,
A very dreary sound:
Ah, let it go﻿—or good or bad:
She has the Master found!

===Chinese===

在烈日下，为了凉水
她无精打采地走来：
而她跑回去时，水罐满满的
被忘在身后。

像一个追赶迷羊的人，
她看见一个疲乏的男子，
坐在那口深井旁，
却什么打水的器具都没有。

「请给我水喝，」他说。她的手
早已准备好回答；
她从这地古老的井里
为他满满地打上来。

他说话，从不曾有人这样说过；
她站着，双耳大开；
他说到将临的圣日，
把她逝去的年月一一数明。

她按捺不住悸动的心，
急忙跑进城去，
在街上和市集大声喊：
「主在这里：快来看。」

她从前的生活古怪而凄凉，
像一声沉闷的响动：
啊，随它去吧——是好是坏——
她已经寻见了主！

### XII Mary Magdalene / 十二、抹大拉的马利亚
===Original===

With wandering eyes and aimless zeal,
She hither, thither, goes;
Her speech, her motions, all reveal
A mind without repose.

She climbs the hills, she haunts the sea,
By madness tortured, driven;
One hour’s forgetfulness would be
A gift from very heaven!

She slumbers into new distress;
The night is worse than day:
Exulting in her helplessness,
Hell’s dogs yet louder bay.

The demons blast her to and fro;
She has no quiet place,
Enough a woman still, to know
A haunting dim disgrace.

A human touch! a pang of death!
And in a low delight
Thou liest, waiting for new breath.
For morning out of night.

Thou risest up: the earth is fair,
The wind is cool; thou art free!
Is it a dream of hell’s despair
Dissolves in ecstasy?

That man did touch thee! Eyes divine
Make sunrise in thy soul;
Thou seëst love in order shine:﻿—
His health hath made thee whole!

Thou, sharing in the awful doom,
Didst help thy Lord to die;
Then, weeping o’er his empty tomb,
Didst hear him Mary cry.

He stands in haste; he cannot stop;
Home to his God he fares:
“Go tell my brothers I go up
To my Father, mine and theirs.”

Run, Mary! lift thy heavenly voice;
Cry, cry, and heed not how;
Make all the new-risen world rejoice﻿—
Its first apostle thou!

What if old tales of thee have lied,
Or truth have told, thou art
All-safe with him, whate’er betide﻿—
Dwell’st with him in God’s heart!

===Chinese===

带着游移的眼和漫无目的的热切，
她一会儿跑到这里，一会儿跑到那里；
她的言语、她的举止，处处显出
一颗不得安息的心。

她攀登山丘，她徘徊海滨，
被癫狂折磨、驱赶；
哪怕一个时辰的忘却，
也必是来自天上的恩赐！

她刚刚睡去，又落入新的苦楚；
黑夜比白昼更糟：
地狱的狗越吠越响，
为她的无助欢欣。

群魔把她抛来掷去；
她没有一个安静的地方，
她又十足是个女人，只懂得
一种缠身不去的含垢耻辱。

一个属人的触摸！一阵死亡的剧痛！
于是在低低的欢喜里
你躺着，等候新的呼吸，
等候夜尽而来的清晨。

你起来了：大地晴美，
风凉爽；你自由了！
这是地狱绝境的一场梦
正熔化在狂喜里？

那人确实摸了你！神圣的眼睛
在你灵魂里造出日出；
你看见爱在秩序中发光：——
他的康健使你完全了！

后来，你有分于那可怕的定命，
曾助你的主受死；
再后，你在他空坟墓上哭着，
却听见他唤你：马利亚。

他仓促站着；他不能停留；
他要归回他的上帝那里去：
「去告诉我的弟兄，我上去
见我的父，也是他们的父。」

跑吧，马利亚！扬起你属天的声音；
喊吧，喊吧，别管怎样喊；
让整个新生的世界都欢喜——
你就是它的第一位使徒！

古来的传闻或说谎，
或说了真话，你反正
已在他里面万无一失，无论遭逢什么——
你与他同住在上帝的心里！

### XIII The Woman in the Temple / 十三、殿里的那个女人
===Original===

A still dark joy! A sudden face!
Cold daylight, footsteps, cries!
The temple’s naked, shining space,
Aglare with judging eyes!

All in abandoned guilty hair,
With terror-pallid lips,
To vulgar scorn her honour bare,
To lewd remarks and quips,

Her eyes she fixes on the ground
Her shrinking soul to hide,
Lest, at uncurtained windows found,
Its shame be clear descried.

All idle hang her listless hands,
They tingle with her shame;
She sees not who beside her stands,
She is so bowed with blame.

He stoops, he writes upon the ground,
Regards nor priests nor wife;
An awful silence spreads around,
And wakes an inward strife.

Then comes a voice that speaks for thee,
Pale woman, sore aghast:
“Let him who from this sin is free
At her the first stone cast!”

Ah then her heart grew slowly sad!
Her eyes bewildered rose;
She saw the one true friend she had,
Who loves her though he knows.

He stoops. In every charnel breast
Dead conscience rises slow:
They, dumb before that awful guest,
Turn, one by one, and go.

Up in her deathlike, ashy face
Rises the living red;
No greater wonder sure had place
When Lazarus left the dead!

She is alone with him whose fear
Made silence all around;
False pride, false shame, they come not near,
She has her saviour found!

Jesus hath spoken on her side,
Those cruel men withstood!
From him her shame she will not hide!
For him she will be good!

He rose; he saw the temple bare;
They two are left alone!
He said unto her, “Woman, where
Are thine accusers gone?”

“Hath none condemned thee?” “Master, no,”
She answers, trembling sore.
“Neither do I condemn thee. Go,
And sin not any more.”

She turned and went.﻿—To hope and grieve?
Be what she had not been?
We are not told; but I believe
His kindness made her clean.

Our sins to thee us captive hale﻿—
Ambitions, hatreds dire;
Cares, fears, and selfish loves that fail,
And sink us in the mire:

Our captive-cries with pardon meet;
Our passion cleanse with pain;
Lord, thou didst make these miry feet﻿—
Oh, wash them clean again!

===Chinese===

一场沉暗的欢乐！一张骤现的脸！
冰冷的日光、脚步、呼喊！
圣殿赤裸发亮的空场，
被审判的眼睛照得刺目！

她披散着负罪的乱发，
嘴唇吓得发白，
把她的名誉袒露给庸俗的讥嘲，
给淫猥的议论和讥诮，

她的眼睛定在地面，
要藏起她畏缩的灵魂，
免得它被人在无遮的窗前发现，
羞辱被看得一清二楚。

她无力的双手无力垂着，
羞耻使它们发麻；
她看不见身旁站的是谁，
她被罪责压得这样弯。

他弯下腰，在地上写字，
不理祭司，也不理那妇人；
一片可怕的寂静向四周漫开，
唤醒了一场内心的交战。

随后来了一个替你说话的声音，
苍白的妇人，惊惶万状：
「你们中间谁是没有罪的，
谁就可以先拿石头打她！」

啊，那时她的心才慢慢悲伤起来！
她迷乱的眼睛抬起；
她看见她唯一真心的朋友，
那位知道她、却仍爱她的。

他弯下腰。在每一具骸骨般的胸膛里，
死去的良心缓缓升起：
他们，在那可怕宾客面前哑口无言，
一个接一个转身走了。

在她死灰般的脸上，
泛起了活人的红润；
当拉撒路离开死人间时，
也未必有比这更大的奇事！

她单独与他同在，他的可畏
使四围都寂静；
虚假的骄傲、虚假的羞耻，都近不了身，
她寻见了她的救主！

耶稣已站在她一边说话，
那些残忍的人都被挡回！
她不愿向他隐瞒她的耻辱！
她要为他而学好！

他站起来；他看见圣殿空了；
只剩他们两个！
他对她说：「妇人，那些
控告你的人在哪里？」

「没有人定你的罪吗？」「主啊，没有，」
她浑身发抖地回答。
「我也不定你的罪。去吧，
从此不要再犯罪了。」

她转身走了。——是去盼望还是悲伤？
去做她从未做过的人？
经上没有告诉我们；但我相信
他的恩慈使她洁净了。

我们的罪把我们掳到你面前——
野心，和可怕的仇恨；
忧虑、恐惧和终必落空的自私之爱，
把我们陷在泥里：

愿你以赦免回应被掳之人的呼求；
以疼痛洁净我们的情欲；
主啊，这双泥泞的脚本是你造的——
哦，求你再把它洗净！

### XIV Martha / 十四、马大
===Original===

With joyful pride her heart is high:
Her humble house doth hold
The man her nation’s prophecy
Long ages hath foretold!

Poor, is he? Yes, and lowly born:
Her woman-soul is proud
To know and hail the coming morn
Before the eyeless crowd.

At her poor table will he eat?
He shall be served there
With honour and devotion meet
For any king that were!

’Tis all she can; she does her part,
Profuse in sacrifice;
Nor dreams that in her unknown heart
A better offering lies.

But many crosses she must bear;
Her plans are turned and bent;
Do what she can, things will not wear
The form of her intent.

With idle hands and drooping lid,
See Mary sit at rest!
Shameful it was her sister did
No service for their guest!

Dear Martha, one day Mary’s lot
Must rule thy hands and eyes;
Thou, all thy household cares forgot,
Must sit as idly wise!

But once more first she set her word
To bar her master’s ways,
Crying, “By this he stinketh, Lord,
He hath been dead four days!”

Her housewife-soul her brother dear
Would fetter where he lies!
Ah, did her buried best then hear,
And with the dead man rise?

===Chinese===

她的心因欣喜的骄傲而高昂：
她寒微的房屋里，
接待了她们民族的预言
多少世代前所预告的那人！

他穷吗？是的，出身也低微：
她的女人灵魂却骄傲，
因为早在盲目的众人之前
她就认得并迎接了将临的黎明。

他会坐上她寒酸的餐桌吗？
他要在那里受款待，
带着足以献给
任何一位君王的敬意与虔诚！

这是她仅有的一切；她尽了她的本分，
毫不吝惜地牺牲；
却不曾梦见她未知的心底
还躺着一分更好的祭。

但她必须背负许多十字架；
她的打算被扭转、被折曲；
她无论怎样竭力，事情总不肯
成就她心意的形状。

看哪，马利亚闲着双手、垂着眼皮，
安坐着！
妹妹竟不为客人
做一点服事，真是可耻！

亲爱的马大啊，终有一天，马利亚的份
要掌管你的手和眼；
你要忘掉一切家务，
同样安坐，同样静默地聪明！

可她又抢先一步，用她的话
去拦她主人的路，
喊道：「主啊，他现在必是臭了，
他已经死了四天了！」

她主妇的灵魂，想把亲爱的兄弟
捆锁在他躺卧的地方！
啊，她埋藏的至宝那时可曾听见，
与死人一同复活过来？

### XV Mary / 十五、马利亚
===Original===

I

She sitteth at the Master’s feet
In motionless employ;
Her ears, her heart, her soul complete
Drinks in the tide of joy.

Ah! who but she the glory knows
Of life, pure, high, intense,
In whose eternal silence blows
The wind beyond the sense!

In her still ear, God’s perfect grace
Incarnate is in voice;
Her thoughts, the people of the place,
Receive it, and rejoice.

Her eyes, with heavenly reason bright,
Are on the ground cast low;
His words of spirit, life, and light﻿—
They set them shining so.

But see! a face is at the door
Whose eyes are not at rest;
A voice breaks on divinest lore
With petulant request.

“Master,” it said, “dost thou not care
She lets me serve alone?
Tell her to come and take her share.”
But Mary’s eyes shine on.

She lifts them with a questioning glance,
Calmly to him who heard;
The merest sign, she’ll rise at once,
Nor wait the uttered word.

His “Martha, Martha!” with it bore
A sense of coming nay;
He told her that her trouble sore
Was needless any day.

And he would not have Mary chid
For want of needless care;
The needful thing was what she did,
At his feet sitting there.

Sure, joy awoke in her dear heart
Doing the thing it would,
When he, the holy, took her part,
And called her choice the good!

Oh needful thing, Oh Mary’s choice,
Go not from us away!
Oh Jesus, with the living voice,
Talk to us every day!

II

Not now the living words are poured
Into one listening ear;
For many guests are at the board,
And many speak and hear.

With sacred foot, refrained and slow,
With daring, trembling tread,
She comes, in worship bending low
Behind the godlike head.

The costly chrism, in snowy stone,
A gracious odour sends;
Her little hoard, by sparing grown,
In one full act she spends.

She breaks the box, the honoured thing!
See how its riches pour!
Her priestly hands anoint him king
Whom peasant Mary bore.

---

Not so does John the tale repeat:
He saw, for he was there,
Mary anoint the Master’s feet,
And wipe them with her hair.

Perhaps she did his head anoint,
And then his feet as well;
And John this one forgotten point
Loved best of all to tell.

’Twas Judas called the splendour waste,
’Twas Jesus said﻿—Not so;
Said that her love his burial graced:
“Ye have the poor; I go.”

Her hands unwares outsped his fate,
The truth-king’s felon-doom;
The other women were too late,
For he had left the tomb.

===Chinese===

一

她坐在主的脚前，
一动不动地忙碌；
她的耳、她的心、她整个的灵魂
啜饮着喜悦的潮水。

啊！除了她，谁知道那荣耀——
纯洁、高峻、炽烈的生命，
在它永恒的静默里，
吹着感官之外的风！

在她安静的耳中，上帝完全的恩典
化成了肉身的声音；
她的思绪，这地方的人民，
领受了它，就欢喜。

她的眼睛，因属天的明理而亮，
低低垂向地面；
他那些属灵、属生命、属光的话语——
正是它们使眼睛这样闪亮。

可是看哪！门口有一张脸，
那双眼睛不得安息；
一个声音带着急躁的请求，
打断了最神圣的教导。

「主啊，」那声音说，「你不在意吗？
她任我一个人伺候。
请叫她来搭把手。」
而马利亚的眼睛依旧闪亮。

她抬起眼，带着探问的一瞥，
安静地望向他，那听见一切的；
只消最轻的一个示意，她就会立刻起身，
不等话说出口。

他那声「马大，马大！」里面，
已带着将有的否决；
他告诉她，她那沉重的劳烦，
无论哪一天都是不必要的。

而他不愿马利亚因缺少
不必要的操持而受责；
那必要的一件事，正是她所做的——
坐在他的脚前。

真的，她亲爱的心里必已醒来喜乐，
做着它愿做的事，
当那位圣者站在她一边，
称她的选择为那上好的！

哦必要的一件事，哦马利亚的选择，
不要离开我们而去！
哦耶稣，愿你以这活的声音，
天天与我们交谈！

二

如今活的话语不再倾入
一只聆听的耳朵；
因为席上宾客众多，
许多人在说，许多人在听。

她以圣洁的脚步，克制而缓慢，
带着大胆而战栗的脚步，
走来，在敬拜中深深俯伏
在那神一样的头颅后面。

贵重的香膏在雪白的玉瓶里，
散出优雅的香气；
她省吃俭用攒下的一点积蓄，
在一次完全的奉献中倾尽。

她打破玉瓶，那尊贵之物！
看它的珍宝怎样倾流！
她祭司的双手膏他为王，
那由村妇马利亚生下的王。

---

约翰述说的却不一样：
他当时在场，亲眼看见
马利亚膏主的脚，
又用她的头发去擦。

或许她既膏了他的头，
随后又膏了他的脚；
而约翰最爱讲的，
恰是别人略去的那一点。

说是浪费的是犹大，
说「不然」的是耶稣；
他说她的爱预先膏了他安葬的身体：
「常有穷人和你们同在；我却不常有。」

她的双手无意间抢在了他的命定之前，
抢在那真理之王的死刑之前；
其余的妇女们都来迟了，
因为他已经离开了坟墓。

### XVI The Woman That Was a Sinner / 十六、那个有罪的女人
===Original===

His face, his words, her heart awoke;
Awoke her slumbering truth;
She judged him well; her bonds she broke,
And fled to him for ruth.

With tears she washed his weary feet;
She wiped them with her hair;
Her kisses﻿—call them not unmeet,
When they were welcome there.

What saint a richer crown could throw
At his love-royal feet!
Her tears, her lips, her hair, down go,
His reign begun to greet.

His holy manhood’s perfect worth
Owns her a woman still;
It is impossible henceforth
For her to stoop to ill.

Her to herself his words restore,
The radiance to the day;
A horror to herself no more,
Not yet a cast-away!

Her hands and kisses, ointment, tears,
Her gathered wiping hair,
Her love, her shame, her hopes, her fears,
Mingle in worship rare.

Thou, Mary, too, thy hair didst spread
To wipe the anointed feet;
Nor didst thou only bless his head
With precious spikenard sweet.

But none say thou thy tears didst pour
To wash his parched feet first;
Of tears thou couldst not have such store
As from this woman burst!

If not in love she first be read,
Her queen of sorrow greet;
Mary, do thou anoint his head,
And let her crown his feet.

Simon, her kisses will not soil;
Her tears are pure as rain;
The hair for him she did uncoil
Had been baptized in pain.

Lo, God hath pardoned her so much,
Love all her being stirs!
His love to his poor child is such
That it hath wakened hers!

But oh, rejoice, ye sisters pure,
Who scarce can know her case﻿—
There is no sin but has its cure,
Its all-consuming grace!

He did not leave her soul in hell,
’Mong shards the silver dove;
But raised her pure that she might tell
Her sisters how to love!

She gave him all your best love can!
Despised, rejected, sad﻿—
Sure, never yet had mighty man
Such homage as he had!

Jesus, by whose forgiveness sweet,
Her love grew so intense,
Earth’s sinners all come round thy feet:
Lord, make no difference!

===Chinese===

他的脸、他的话唤醒了她的心；
唤醒了她沉睡的真实；
她认得他；她挣断了自己的捆索，
逃到他那里求怜悯。

她用眼泪洗他疲惫的脚；
她用头发把它们擦干；
她的亲吻——不要说它们不当，
它们在那里是受欢迎的。

哪位圣徒能在他那爱之王的脚前
抛下更丰盛的冠冕！
她的眼泪、她的唇、她的头发都落下，
庆贺他掌权的开端。

他那圣洁人性的完全价值
承认她仍是一个女人；
从此以后，她再也不可能
向邪恶屈身。

他的话把她归还给她自己，
把光辉归还给白昼；
她不再是自己的恐惧，
却也不再是被弃的人！

她的双手和亲吻、香膏、眼泪，
她拢起的擦发的发，
她的爱、她的羞、她的盼、她的惧，
融成一场罕见的敬拜。

你，马利亚，也曾铺开头发
去擦那受膏的脚；
你也不止用珍贵的哪哒香膏
去膏祝他的头。

但没人说你曾倾洒眼泪
先洗他干渴的脚；
眼泪，你不可能有那么多，
像从这个女人身上涌出的！

若她不能首先被算在爱里，
就请向她，忧愁的王后，致意；
马利亚，你去膏他的头，
让她去冠冕他的脚。

西门，她的亲吻不会弄脏；
她的眼泪纯净如雨；
她为他解开的那头长发，
曾在痛苦里受过洗。

看哪，上帝赦免了她这么多，
爱震撼了她全部的生命！
他对这可怜孩子的爱如此深重，
竟唤醒了她的爱！

但哦，要欢喜，你们纯洁的姊妹们，
你们几乎不懂她的处境——
没有一种罪是没有药医的，
没有一种消尽万罪的恩典！

他没有把她的灵魂撇在阴间，
撇在碎片中间的银鸽；
他使她纯洁地站起，好叫她去告诉
她的姊妹们怎样去爱！

她把他献上了你们最好的爱所能献的一切！
被藐视，被弃绝，忧伤——
真的，从没有一个伟人
受过他这样的敬奉！

耶稣啊，因着你甘甜的赦免，
她的爱才烧得这样炽烈，
地上一切的罪人都来到你脚前：
主啊，请你不要分别！

## A Song in a Dream / 梦中的一支歌
===Original===

I dreamed of a song, I heard it sung;
In the ear that sleeps not its music rung.
And the tones were upheld by harmonies deep,
Where the spirit floated; yea, soared, on their sweep
With each wild unearthly word and tone,
Upward, it knew not whither bound,
In a calm delirium of mystic sound﻿—
Up, where the Genius of Thought alone
Loveth in silence to drink his fill
Of dews that from unknown clouds distil.
A woman’s voice the deep echoes awoke,
In the caverns and solitudes of my soul;
But such a voice had never broke
Through the sea of sounds that about us roll,
Choking the ear in the daylight strife.
There was sorrow and triumph, and death and life
In each chord-note of that prophet-song,
Blended in one harmonious throng:
Such a chant, ere my voice has fled from death,
Be it mine to mould of the parting breath.

===Chinese===

我梦见一支歌，我听见它被唱起；
在不眠的耳中它的乐声回荡。
音调被深沉的和声托举，
灵魂漂浮其上，是的，随它们的荡漾高飞，
随着每一个狂野、非尘世的字与音，
向上，不知要去往何处，
在一种神秘音响的静稳迷醉里——
向上，到那唯有思想之灵
独自在静默中畅饮的地方，
畅饮从未知云朵滴落的露。
一个女人的声音唤醒了深沉的回响，
在我灵魂的洞穴与孤寂里；
可这样的声音从不曾
穿透我们四周翻滚的声音之海，
那在白昼的争闹里拥塞双耳的噪声。
那支先知之歌的每一个和弦音里，
都有忧伤与凯旋，有死亡与生命，
融成一支和谐的合唱：
但愿在我的声音从死亡逃走之前，
我能用这离世的呼吸铸就这样一曲。

## Songs of the Days and Nights / 昼与夜之歌
===Original===



===Chinese===

（组诗）

### Songs of the Summer Days / 夏日白昼之歌

### Songs of the Summer Days / 
===Original===

I

A glory on the chamber wall!
A glory in the brain!
Triumphant floods of glory fall
On heath, and wold, and plain.

Earth lieth still in hopeless bliss;
She has, and seeks no more;
Forgets that days come after this,
Forgets the days before.

Each ripple waves a flickering fire
Of gladness, as it runs;
They laugh and flash, and leap and spire,
And toss ten thousand suns.

But hark! low, in the world within,
One sad aeolian tone:
“Ah! shall we ever, ever win
A summer of our own?”

II

A morn of winds and swaying trees﻿—
Earth’s jubilance rushing out!
The birds are fighting with the breeze;
The waters heave about.

White clouds are swept across the sky,
Their shadows o’er the graves;
Purpling the green, they float and fly
Athwart the sunny waves.

The long grass﻿—an earth-rooted sea﻿—
Mimics the watery strife.
To boat or horse? Wild motion we
Shall find harmonious life.

But whither? Roll and sweep and bend
Suffice for Nature’s part;
But motion to an endless end
Is needful for our heart.

III

The morn awakes like brooding dove,
With outspread wings of gray;
Her feathery clouds close in above,
And roof a sober day.

No motion in the deeps of air!
No trembling in the leaves!
A still contentment everywhere,
That neither laughs nor grieves!

A film of sheeted silver gray
Shuts in the ocean’s hue;
White-winged feluccas cleave their way
In paths of gorgeous blue.

Dream on, dream on, O dreamy day,
Thy very clouds are dreams!
Yon child is dreaming far away﻿—
He is not where he seems.

IV

The lark is up, his faith is strong,
He mounts the morning air;
Lone voice of all the creature throng,
He sings the morning prayer.

Slow clouds from north and south appear,
Black-based, with shining slope;
In sullen forms their might they rear,
And climb the vaulted cope.

A lightning flash, a thunder boom!﻿—
Nor sun nor clouds are there;
A single, all-pervading gloom
Hangs in the heavy air.

A weeping, wasting afternoon
Weighs down the aspiring corn;
Amber and red, the sunset soon
Leads back to golden morn.

===Chinese===

一

卧房的墙上有一片荣光！
头脑里有一片荣光！
凯旋的荣光洪流般倾泻
在荒原、旷野和平川上。

大地静静躺卧在无望之福里；
她已拥有，便不再寻求；
忘记这一天之后还有天日，
忘记之前曾有过的天日。

每一道涟漪都摇着一簇
欢欣的火，当它奔流；
它们欢笑又闪耀，跳跃又腾起，
抛掷着千万个太阳。

可是听！低低的，在内在的世界里，
一声忧愁的风神琴音：
「啊！我们可曾、可曾赢得
一个属于我们自己的夏天？」

二

一个风摇树摆的清晨——
大地的欢腾夺门而出！
鸟儿正与微风相斗；
水面四处荡漾。

白云被扫过长天，
它们的影子掠过坟莹；
染紫了绿野，它们飘飞，
横过阳光下的波浪。

长草——一片扎根土地的海——
模仿着水面的争斗。
乘船还是骑马？在狂放的运动里
我们将找到和谐的生命。

但往哪里去？翻滚、横扫、弯俯，
对大自然来说已尽够了；
可奔向无穷终点的运动，
才是我们的心所需要的。

三

清晨醒来，像一只抱窝的鸽子，
展开灰色的翅膀；
她羽翼般的云在上面合拢，
搭成一个素净的白昼。

空气的深 处没有一丝动静！
树叶没有一丝颤抖！
到处是一种安然的满足，
既不欢笑，也不忧愁！

一层银灰的薄幕
罩住了海洋的色；
白翼的小帆船破开航路，
在绚蓝的航道里。

梦下去，梦下去，哦梦一样的白昼，
你的云本身就是梦！
那边那个孩子正梦在远方——
他并不在他看去所在的地方。

四

云雀起来了，它的信心坚强，
它攀上清晨的天空；
它是万物合唱中孤独的声音，
唱着清晨的祷告。

云从南北两方缓缓出现，
黑色的底，明亮的坡；
它们以阴沉的形貌竖起威力，
攀登那穹隆的顶。

一道闪电，一声霹雳！——
太阳和云都不见了；
一片弥漫一切的幽暗
悬在沉闷的空气里。

一个哭泣着、消损着的下午
压弯了扬花的玉米；
琥珀与绯红，日落很快
又把金色的清晨领回。

### Songs of the Summer Nights / 夏日夜晚之歌

### Songs of the Summer Nights / 夏日夜晚之歌
===Original===

I

The dreary wind of night is out,
Homeless and wandering slow;
O’er pale seas moaning like a doubt,
It breathes, but will not blow.

It sighs from out the helpless past,
Where doleful things abide;
Gray ghosts of dead thought sail aghast
Across its ebbing tide.

O’er marshy pools it faints and flows,
All deaf and dumb and blind;
O’er moor and mountain aimless goes﻿—
The listless woesome wind!

Nay, nay!﻿—breathe on, sweet wind of night!
The sigh is all in me;
Flow, fan, and blow, with gentle might,
Until I wake and see.

II

The west is broken into bars
Of orange, gold, and gray;
Gone is the sun, fast come the stars,
And night infolds the day.

My boat glides with the gliding stream,
Following adown its breast
One flowing mirrored amber gleam,
The death-smile of the west.

The river moves; the sky is still,
No ceaseless quest it knows:
Thy bosom swells, thy fair eyes fill
At sight of its repose.

The ripples run; all patient sit
The stars above the night.
In shade and gleam the waters flit:
The heavens are changeless bright!

III

Alone I lie, buried amid
The long luxurious grass;
The bats flit round me, born and hid
In twilight’s wavering mass.

The fir-top floats, an airy isle,
High o’er the mossy ground;
Harmonious silence breathes the while
In scent instead of sound.

The flaming rose glooms swarthy red;
The borage gleams more blue;
Dim-starred with white, a flowery bed
Glimmers the rich dusk through.

Hid in the summer grass I lie,
Lost in the great blue cave;
My body gazes at the sky,
And measures out its grave.

IV

What art thou, gathering dusky cool,
In slow gradation fine?
Death’s lovely shadow, flickering full
Of eyes about to shine.

When weary Day goes down below,
Thou leanest o’er his grave,
Revolving all the vanished show
The gracious splendour gave.

Or art thou not she rather﻿—say﻿—
Dark-browed, with luminous eyes,
Of whom is born the mighty Day,
That fights and saves and dies?

For action sleeps with sleeping light;
Calm thought awakes with thee:
The soul is then a summer night,
With stars that shine and see.

===Chinese===

一

夜里那忧愁的风出了门，
无家可归，缓缓游荡；
它在惨白的海上像一声疑问般呜咽，
它呼吸，却不肯吹拂。

它从那无助的过往里叹出，
那里住着悲哀的事物；
死去思想的灰色幽灵惊惶地
驶过它退潮的水流。

它在沼泽的水潭上衰弱地流，
又聋又哑又盲；
它在荒原与群山间无目的地走——
这倦怠的、悲哀的风！

不，不！——吹吧，吹下去，夜里的甜风！
叹息全在我自己里面；
流淌吧，扇动吧，吹拂吧，带着温柔的力量，
直到我醒来看见。

二

西天碎成了一道道
橙色、金黄与灰的长条；
太阳落了，星星匆匆来到，
夜把白昼拥进怀里。

我的船随流淌的河水滑行，
顺流追随着它胸前
一道流动的、琥珀色的镜光，
那是西天临终的微笑。

河水在动；天空却静止，
它不知什么叫无尽的追寻：
你的胸怀起伏，你美丽的眼睛盈满，
只因看见了它的安息。

涟漪奔跑；星辰
安坐，忍耐，在夜之上。
波光在明暗间穿梭：
天穹是不变的明亮！

三

我独自躺着，埋在
修长而丰茂的草里；
蝙蝠在我四周飞掠，生于暮色、
藏于暮色摇曳的一团。

杉树的顶冠漂浮着，像一座轻盈的岛，
高悬在生苔的地面上空；
和谐的静默同时在呼吸，
以香气代替声音。

火红的玫瑰暗成深红；
琉璃苣显得更蓝；
缀满白星的一张花床
透过浓密的暮色微微发光。

我藏在夏天的草里躺着，
迷失在那蓝色的大洞穴；
我的身体凝望天空，
量度出它的坟墓。

四

你是什么，收拢着暗沉的凉，
在缓慢精细的层次里？
死亡可爱的影子，闪烁着
满满将要点亮的眼睛。

当疲惫的白昼落到下面，
你俯在他的坟上，
回想着那仁慈的辉煌
所给出的一切已然消逝的景象。

还是说，你其实是她——请说——
那位黑眉下有发亮眼睛的，
从她生出那强大的白昼，
那争战、拯救而又死去的白昼？

因为行动随光一同睡了；
安静的思考随你醒来：
那时灵魂就是一个夏夜，
缀着既照耀、又观看的星。

### Songs of the Autumn Days / 秋日白昼之歌
===Original===

I

We bore him through the golden land,
One early harvest morn;
The corn stood ripe on either hand﻿—
He knew all about the corn.

How shall the harvest gathered be
Without him standing by?
Without him walking on the lea,
The sky is scarce a sky.

The year’s glad work is almost done;
The land is rich in fruit;
Yellow it floats in air and sun﻿—
Earth holds it by the root.

Why should earth hold it for a day
When harvest-time is come?
Death is triumphant o’er decay,
And leads the ripened home.

II

And though the sun be not so warm,
His shining is not lost;
Both corn and hope, of heart and farm,
Lie hid from coming frost.

The sombre woods are richly sad,
Their leaves are red and gold:
Are thoughts in solemn splendour clad
Signs that we men grow old?

Strange odours haunt the doubtful brain
From fields and days gone by;
And mournful memories again
Are born, are loved, and die.

The mornings clear, the evenings cool
Foretell no wintry wars;
The day of dying leaves is full,
The night of glowing stars.

III

’Tis late before the sun will rise,
And early he will go;
Gray fringes hang from the gray skies,
And wet the ground below.

Red fruit has followed golden corn;
The leaves are few and sere;
My thoughts are old as soon as born,
And chill with coming fear.

The winds lie sick; no softest breath
Floats through the branches bare;
A silence as of coming death
Is growing in the air.

But what must fade can bear to fade﻿—
Was born to meet the ill:
Creep on, old Winter, deathly shade!
We sorrow, and are still.

IV

There is no longer any heaven
To glorify our clouds;
The rising vapours downward driven
Come home in palls and shrouds.

The sun himself is ill bested
A heavenly sign to show;
His radiance, dimmed to glowing red,
Can hardly further go.

An earthy damp, a churchyard gloom,
Pervade the moveless air;
The year is sinking to its tomb,
And death is everywhere.

But while sad thoughts together creep,
Like bees too cold to sting,
God’s children, in their beds asleep,
Are dreaming of the spring.

===Chinese===

一

我们抬着他穿过金色的土地，
在一个早收的清晨；
玉米在两旁熟立——
关于玉米，他什么都懂。

没有他站在近旁，
收获怎能完成？
没有他走在草场上，
天空几乎不成其为天空。

一年的欢快工作将近完成；
大地硕果丰盈；
金黄色泽漂浮在空气和阳光里——
大地用根把它牵住。

收获的季节既已来到，
大地何必再把它多留一天？
死亡胜过了腐朽，
领着熟透的回家。

二

虽然太阳已不那么温暖，
它的照耀并未落空；
心田与农田的庄稼和希望，
都藏起来躲避将来的霜。

暗色的树林富丽而忧伤，
叶子红红又黄黄：
披着庄严华服的思绪，
莫非是我们要老去的征象？

陌生的气味从逝去的田野
和逝去的日子缠上犹疑的头脑；
哀伤的记忆重新
生出，被爱，然后死去。

清晨晴明，傍晚凉爽，
并未预告冬日的战争；
叶子死去的那一天是圆满的，
那夜晚缀满灼灼的星。

三

太阳迟迟才肯升起，
又早早就要离去；
灰色的天垂下灰色的流苏，
润湿了下方的土地。

红艳的果实接替了金色的玉米；
叶子稀少而枯焦；
我的念头一诞生就苍老，
因将临的恐惧而发凉。

风病倒了；没有一丝最轻的呼吸
飘过光秃的枝条；
一种像死亡将至的寂静
正在空气里生长。

但注定要凋零的，就受得住凋零——
它生来就为迎向这祸殃：
爬过来吧，老冬天，死亡的阴影！
我们悲伤，却仍安静。

四

不再有一方天堂
来给我们的云加冕；
升腾的雾气被向下驱赶，
裹着寿衣和裹尸布回家。

连太阳自己也窘于
显出一个天上的记号；
他的光辉，暗成闷红，
几乎再也照不下去。

一股土腥的湿，一座墓园的阴沉，
漫满不动的空气；
这一年正沉入它的坟墓，
死亡无处不在。

但当忧伤的思绪挤作一团，
像冻得无力螫人的蜜蜂，
上帝的儿女们，在床上睡着，
正梦着春天。

### Songs of the Autumn Nights / 
===Original===

I

O night, send up the harvest moon
To walk about the fields,
And make of midnight magic noon
On lonely tarns and wealds.

In golden ranks, with golden crowns,
All in the yellow land,
Old solemn kings in rustling gowns,
The shocks moon-charmed stand.

Sky-mirror she, afloat in space,
Beholds our coming morn:
Her heavenly joy hath such a grace,
It ripens earthly corn;

Like some lone saint with upward eyes,
Lost in the deeps of prayer:
The people still their prayers and sighs,
And gazing ripen there.

II

So, like the corn moon-ripened last,
Would I, weary and gray,
On golden memories ripen fast,
And ripening pass away.

In an old night so let me die;
A slow wind out of doors;
A waning moon low in the sky;
A vapour on the moors;

A fire just dying in the gloom;
Earth haunted all with dreams;
A sound of waters in the room;
A mirror’s moony gleams;

And near me, in the sinking night,
More thoughts than move in me﻿—
Forgiving wrong, and loving right,
And waiting till I see.

III

Across the stubble glooms the wind;
High sails the lated crow;
The west with pallid green is lined;
Fog tracks the river’s flow.

My heart is cold and sad; I moan,
Yet care not for my grief;
The summer fervours all are gone;
The roses are but leaf.

Old age is coming, frosty, hoar;
The snows of time will fall;
My jubilance, dream-like, no more
Returns for any call!

O lapsing heart! thy feeble strain
Sends up the blood so spare,
That my poor withering autumn brain
Sees autumn everywhere!

IV

Lord of my life! if I am blind,
I reck not﻿—thou canst see;
I well may wait my summer mind,
When I am sure of thee!

I made no brave bright suns arise,
Veiled up no sweet gray eves;
I hung no rose-lamps, lit no eyes,
Sent out no windy leaves!

I said not “I will cast a charm
These gracious forms around;”
My heart with unwilled love grew warm;
I took but what I found!

When cold winds range my winter-night,
Be thou my summer-door;
Keep for me all my young delight,
Till I am old no more.

===Chinese===

一

哦夜啊，派收获的月亮上来，
去田野间四处走走，
在孤独的湖沼和原野上
把午夜变作魔法的正午。

一排排金黄，戴着金黄的冠冕，
在整片黄色的土地上，
穿着窸窣作响长袍的、庄严的老王们——
那一个个禾垛，被月光迷住，肃立。

她是天上的一面镜子，漂浮在太空中，
注视着我们将至的清晨：
她天上的喜乐带着这样一种恩泽，
竟催熟了地上的玉米；

像一位孤独的圣徒，眼睛向上，
迷失在祷告的深处：
人们停下了他们的祈祷和叹息，
凝望着，就在那里成熟。

二

就这样，像那被月光最后催熟的玉米，
但愿我，疲惫而灰白，
在金色的记忆上迅速成熟，
一边成熟，一边离去。

让我在这样一个古老的夜里死去；
门外一阵缓缓的风；
一轮亏月低挂在天上；
荒野上一片雾；

炉火正在幽暗中熄灭；
大地处处被梦萦绕；
屋里有流水的声响；
一面镜子里月色的微芒；

而在沉落的夜里，在我近旁，
有比在我里面活动的更多的思绪——
宽想着错，爱着善，
静静等候，直到我看见。

三

风在茬地上布下幽暗；
迟归的乌鸦高飞；
西天镶着一线苍白的绿；
雾跟踪着河的流向。

我的心又冷又愁；我呜咽，
却并不在意我的忧愁；
夏天的炽热都已过去；
玫瑰只剩下了叶。

老年正来，披着白霜；
时间的雪终将落下；
我的欢腾，像梦一样，再也
不肯应任何召唤回来！

哦衰弱的心！你微弱的搏动
送上的血这样稀薄，
我可怜的、枯萎的秋日头脑
看什么都是秋天！

四

我生命的主！我若是瞎了，
我也不在乎——你能看见；
我尽可以等候我夏日的心境，
因为我确信了你！

我没有造出勇敢明亮的太阳升起，
没有蒙起甜美灰暗的黄昏；
我没有挂起玫瑰的灯，没有点亮眼睛，
没有放出风中的叶子！

我没有说「我要在这四周
施展一道魅力」；
我的心因不由自主的爱而温暖；
我只是领受了所遇见的！

当寒风在我冬夜里游荡，
愿你做我夏天的门；
替我守着我全部年轻的欢喜，
直到我不再年老。

### Songs of the Winter Days / 冬日白昼之歌

### Songs of the Winter Days / 冬日白昼之歌
===Original===

I

The sky has turned its heart away,
The earth its sorrow found;
The daisies turn from childhood’s play,
And creep into the ground.

The earth is black and cold and hard;
Thin films of dry white ice,
Across the rugged wheel-tracks barred,
The children’s feet entice.

Dark flows the stream, as if it mourned
The winter in the land;
With idle icicles adorned,
That mill-wheel soon will stand.

But, friends, to say ’tis cold, and part,
Is to let in the cold;
We’ll make a summer of the heart,
And laugh at winter old.

II

With vague dead gleam the morning white
Comes through the window-panes;
The clouds have fallen all the night,
Without the noise of rains.

As of departing, unseen ghost,
Footprints go from the door;
The man himself must long be lost
Who left those footprints hoar!

Yet follow thou; tread down the snow;
Leave all the road behind;
Heed not the winds that steely blow,
Heed not the sky unkind;

For though the glittering air grow dark,
The snow will shine till morn;
And long ere then one dear home-spark
Will winter laugh to scorn.

III

Oh wildly wild the roaring blast
Torments the fallen snow!
The wintry storms are up at last,
And care not how they go!

In foam-like wreaths the water hoar,
Rapt whistling in the air,
Gleams through the dismal twilight frore;
A region in despair,

A spectral ocean lies outside,
Torn by a tempest dark;
Its ghostly billows, dim descried,
Leap on my stranded bark.

Death-sheeted figures, long and white,
Rave driving through the spray;
Or, bosomed in the ghastly night,
Shriek doom-cries far away.

IV

A morning clear, with frosty light
From sunbeams late and low;
They shine upon the snow so white,
And shine back from the snow.

Down tusks of ice one drop will go,
Nor fall: at sunny noon
’Twill hang a diamond﻿—fade, and grow
An opal for the moon.

And when the bright sad sun is low
Behind the mountain-dome,
A twilight wind will come and blow
Around the children’s home,

And puff and waft the powdery snow,
As feet unseen did pass;
While, waiting in its bed below,
Green lies the summer grass.

===Chinese===

一

天空把它的心转开，
大地找到了它的忧伤；
雏菊从童年的游戏里转过身，
爬回地底下。

大地又黑又冷又硬；
薄薄的干冰，
横梗在硌脚的辙印上，
逗引着孩子们的脚。

溪水流得幽暗，仿佛在哀悼
大地上的冬天；
装饰着闲置的冰锥，
那水磨的轮子不久就要停住。

可是朋友们，若只说一句「天冷」就散去，
便正好把寒冷放了进来；
我们要在心头造一个夏天，
笑看这老冬天。

二

发白的清晨带着模糊的死光
透进窗玻璃；
云整夜都在降落，
却没有雨的声息。

像离去时无形的幽灵
留下的脚印，出了门又去；
留下这些霜白脚印的人，
自己怕是早已迷失！

但你只管跟随；踏倒积雪；
把整条路留在身后；
别理会钢铁般吹刮的风，
别理会不善的天空；

因为纵使闪耀的空气转暗，
雪会一直亮到天明；
而在那之前很久，一粒亲爱的家的火星
就会把冬天笑到狼狈。

三

哦，狂吼的暴风那样疯狂地
折磨落下的雪！
冬天的风暴终于起来了，
全不管自己刮向哪里！

像泡沫一样的水柱，白色的，
被裹挟着呼啸在空中，
在阴惨的冰冻暮色里闪烁；
一片绝望的疆域，

一片幽灵的海横在外面，
被黑色的风暴撕扯；
它鬼影般的巨浪，隐约可辨，
扑向我搁浅的船。

裹着寿衣的身影，颀长而白，
嘶喊着驰过飞沫；
或者，伏在狰狞的黑夜里，
在远处尖叫着末日的呼号。

四

一个晴朗的早晨，带着霜光，
来自迟升而低斜的阳光；
它们照在那样白的雪上，
又从雪上照回来。

沿着冰的獠牙，一滴水珠下行，
却不落下：到了晴朗的正午
它会悬成一粒钻石——褪去，又长成
一轮月亮的蛋白石。

而当明亮而忧伤的太阳低垂
在山峦的穹顶后面，
一阵黄昏的风会吹来，
绕着孩子们的家打转，

吹扬起粉状的雪，
仿佛有无形的脚步经过；
而此刻，在下面它的床里等着，
青青的夏草正绿着。

### Songs of the Winter Nights / 
===Original===

I

Back shining from the pane, the fire
Seems outside in the snow:
So love set free from love’s desire
Lights grief of long ago.

The dark is thinned with snow-sheen fine,
The earth bedecked with moon;
Out on the worlds we surely shine
More radiant than in June!

In the white garden lies a heap
As brown as deep-dug mould:
A hundred partridges that keep
Each other from the cold.

My father gives them sheaves of corn,
For shelter both and food:
High hope in me was early born,
My father was so good.

II

The frost weaves ferns and sultry palms
Across my clouded pane;
Weaves melodies of ancient psalms
All through my passive brain.

Quiet ecstasy fills heart and head:
My father is in the room;
The very curtains of my bed
Are from Love’s sheltering loom!

The lovely vision melts away;
I am a child no more;
Work rises from the floor of play;
Duty is at the door.

But if I face with courage stout
The labour and the din,
Thou, Lord, wilt let my mind go out
My heart with thee stay in.

III

Up to my ear my soul doth run﻿—
Her other door is dark;
There she can see without the sun,
And there she sits to mark.

I hear the dull unheeding wind
Mumble o’er heath and wold;
My fancy leaves my brain behind,
And floats into the cold.

Like a forgotten face that lies
One of the speechless crowd,
The earth lies spent, with frozen eyes,
White-folded in her shroud.

O’er leafless woods and cornless farms,
Dead rivers, fireless thorps,
I brood, the heart still throbbing warm
In Nature’s wintered corpse.

IV

To all the world mine eyes are blind:
Their drop serene is﻿—night,
With stores of snow piled up the wind
An awful airy height.

And yet ’tis but a mote in the eye:
The simple faithful stars
Beyond are shining, careless high,
Nor heed our storms and jars.

And when o’er storm and jar I climb﻿—
Beyond life’s atmosphere,
I shall behold the lord of time
And space﻿—of world and year.

Oh vain, far quest!﻿—not thus my heart
Shall ever find its goal!
I turn me home﻿—and there thou art,
My Father, in my soul!

===Chinese===

一

炉火从窗玻璃上反射回来，
仿佛亮在外面 的雪里：
爱这样从爱的欲望里解脱出来，
照亮了许久以前的忧伤。

黑暗被细腻的雪光冲淡，
大地佩戴着月亮；
在外面 的诸世界上，我们必定照耀得
比六月里更加辉煌！

白色的花园里躺着一堆
深褐色像新翻的土：
一百只鹧鸪，彼此偎着，
互相遮挡寒冷。

我的父亲给它们一束束的玉米，
既是庇护也是食粮：
高昂的盼望早早在我心里生出，
因为我的父亲这样善良。

二

严寒在我的蒙霜窗上
织出蕨叶和闷热的棕榈；
在我安静的头脑里织出
古老诗篇的旋律。

安静的狂喜充满心和头：
我的父亲就在房里；
连我床四周的帐帘
也出自爱的遮蔽的织机！

可爱的异象消散了；
我不再是孩子；
劳作从游戏的地面上升起；
责任已在门口。

但我若以坚定的勇敢
面对劳碌与喧嚣，
主啊，你就会让我的心智出去，
让我的心留在你里面。

三

我的灵魂一路跑上我的耳朵——
她另一扇门是黑的；
在那里她不需要太阳也看得见，
在那里她坐着观看。

我听见那麻木不觉的风
在荒野和旷野上喃喃；
我的想象把头脑留在身后，
漂浮进寒冷里。

像沉默人群中的一张
被遗忘的脸那样躺着，
大地耗尽了，眼睛冻结，
白色地裹在她的裹尸布里。

在无叶的树林和无谷的农田上空，
在死去的河流、无火的村庄上空，
我沉思，这颗心仍在
大自然冬殒的尸身里温暖地跳动。

四

对整个世界，我的眼睛都瞎了：
它们的阴翳是——夜，
连同风堆起的重重积雪，
堆到可畏的、虚空的高处。

可那不过眼里的一粒微尘：
单纯而忠实的星辰
在更远处照耀，漫不经心的高远，
全不理会我们的风暴与争闹。

当我越过风暴与争闹攀缘而上——
越过生命的大气，
我将看见时间与空间的主——
世界与年岁的主。

哦徒劳的远征！——我的心
这样永远找不到它的目标！
我转身回家——而你就在那里，
我的父，在我的灵魂里！

### Songs of the Spring Days / 春日白昼之歌

### Songs of the Spring Days / 
===Original===

I

A gentle wind, of western birth
On some far summer sea,
Wakes daisies in the wintry earth,
Wakes hopes in wintry me.

The sun is low; the paths are wet,
And dance with frolic hail;
The trees﻿—their spring-time is not yet﻿—
Swing sighing in the gale.

Young gleams of sunshine peep and play;
Clouds shoulder in between;
I scarce believe one coming day
The earth will all be green.

The north wind blows, and blasts, and raves,
And flaps his snowy wing:
Back! toss thy bergs on arctic waves;
Thou canst not bar our spring.

II

Up comes the primrose, wondering;
The snowdrop droopeth by;
The holy spirit of the spring
Is working silently.

Soft-breathing breezes woo and wile
The later children out;
O’er woods and farms a sunny smile
Is flickering about.

The earth was cold, hard-hearted, dull;
To death almost she slept:
Over her, heaven grew beautiful,
And forth her beauty crept.

Showers yet must fall, and waters grow
Dark-wan with furrowing blast;
But suns will shine, and soft winds blow,
Till the year flowers at last.

III

The sky is smiling over me,
Hath smiled away the frost;
White daisies star the sky-like lea,
With buds the wood’s embossed.

Troops of wild flowers gaze at the sky
Up through the latticed boughs;
Till comes the green cloud by and by,
It is not time to house.

Yours is the day, sweet bird﻿—sing on;
The winter is forgot;
Like an ill dream ’tis over and gone:
Pain that is past, is not.

Joy that was past is yet the same:
If care the summer brings,
’Twill only be another name
For love that broods, not sings.

IV

Blow on me, wind, from west and south;
Sweet summer-spirit, blow!
Come like a kiss from dear child’s mouth,
Who knows not what I know.

The earth’s perfection dawneth soon;
Ours lingereth alway;
We have a morning, not a noon;
Spring, but no summer gay.

Rose-blotted eve, gold-branded morn
Crown soon the swift year’s life:
In us a higher hope is born,
And claims a longer strife.

Will heaven be an eternal spring
With summer at the door?
Or shall we one day tell its king
That we desire no more?

===Chinese===

一

一阵温柔的风，生于远方
某个夏日海洋的西风，
唤醒寒冬土地里的雏菊，
唤醒寒冬之中的我。

太阳很低；小径湿漉，
欢蹦的冰雹在上面跳舞；
树木——它们的春天还没到——
在狂风里摇着叹息。

年轻的阳光窥看又嬉戏；
云朵挤进来插在中间；
我几乎不敢相信，将来的某一天
大地会全然转绿。

北风吹着，咆哮着，怒吼着，
拍打着他雪白的翅膀：
回去吧！把你的冰山抛回北极的海浪；
你拦不住我们的春天。

二

报春花探上来，满心惊奇；
雪花莲在旁边垂着头；
春天神圣的灵
正在静静做工。

轻柔呼吸的微风哄劝着
迟生的孩子们出来；
在树林和农田上，一个阳光的微笑
正四处闪烁。

大地曾又冷、心又硬、又迟钝；
几乎要睡到死亡里去：
在她上面，天空渐渐美丽，
她的美也悄悄爬了出来。

阵雨还要落下，流水还要
被犁沟般的寒风吹得暗淡；
但太阳会照耀，软风会吹拂，
直到这一年终于开花。

三

天空朝我微笑着，
已把霜微笑尽了；
白雏菊点缀着天空般的草场，
树林缀满了蓓蕾。

一队队野花仰望着天空，
透过格子般的枝桠；
等到那绿色的云迟早来到，
才到归家的时候。

这一天是你的，甜美的鸟——唱下去吧；
冬天已被忘却；
它像一场噩梦，过去了，消散了：
过去的痛，已不再是痛。

过去的喜乐却仍是同一种喜乐：
若夏天带来忧虑，
那也不过是另一个名字，
叫作沉思的爱、而不歌唱的爱。

四

吹向我吧，风，从西边和南边；
甜美的夏日之灵，吹吧！
来吧，像亲爱的孩子嘴上的一个吻，
他还不知道我所知道的。

大地的完美很快就要破晓；
我们的却始终拖延；
我们有清晨，却没有正午；
有春天，却没有欢畅的夏天。

缀满玫瑰的黄昏、烙着金印的清晨，
快去加冕那疾驰之年的生命：
在我们里面，一个更高的盼望正出生，
并要求一场更长的争战。

天堂会是一个永恒的春天、
门口站着夏天吗？
还是有一天，我们要对那里的王说：
我们别无所求？

### Songs of the Spring Nights / 春日夜晚之歌

### Songs of the Spring Nights / 春日夜晚之歌
===Original===

I

The flush of green that dyed the day
Hath vanished in the moon;
Flower-scents float stronger out, and play
An unborn, coming tune.

One southern eve like this, the dew
Had cooled and left the ground;
The moon hung half-way from the blue,
No disc, but conglobed round;

Light-leaved acacias, by the door,
Bathed in the balmy air,
Clusters of blossomed moonlight bore,
And breathed a perfume rare;

Great gold-flakes from the starry sky
Fell flashing on the deep:
One scent of moist earth floating by,
Almost it made me weep.

II

Those gorgeous stars were not my own,
They made me alien go!
The mother o’er her head had thrown
A veil I did not know!

The moon-blanched fields that seaward went,
The palm-flung, dusky shades,
Bore flowering grasses, knotted, bent,
No slender, spear-like blades.

I longed to see the starry host
Afar in fainter blue;
But plenteous grass I missed the most,
With daisies glimmering through.

The common things were not the same!
I longed across the foam:
From dew-damp earth that odour came﻿—
I knew the world my home.

III

The stars are glad in gulfy space﻿—
Friendly the dark to them!
From day’s deep mine, their hiding-place,
Night wooeth every gem.

A thing for faith ’mid labour’s jar,
When up the day is furled,
Shines in the sky a light afar,
Mayhap a home-filled world.

Sometimes upon the inner sky
We catch a doubtful shine:
A mote or star? A flash in the eye
Or jewel of God’s mine?

A star to us, all glimmer and glance,
May teem with seraphim:
A fancy to our ignorance
May be a truth to Him.

IV

The night is damp and warm and still,
And soft with summer dreams;
The buds are bursting at their will,
And shy the half moon gleams.

My soul is cool, as bathed within
By dews that silent weep﻿—
Like child that has confessed his sin,
And now will go to sleep.

My body ages, form and hue;
But when the spring winds blow,
My spirit stirs and buds anew,
Younger than long ago.

Lord, make me more a child, and more,
Till Time his own end bring,
And out of every winter sore
I pass into thy spring.

===Chinese===

一

染绿了白昼的那片绿意，
已在月光里消隐；
花香更浓地飘出，弹奏着
一支尚未出生、将临的曲子。

一个像这样的南国夜晚，露水
曾凉透又离开了地面；
月亮从蓝天垂下一半，
不是圆盘，而是一团浑圆的光；

门边轻叶的金合欢，
沐浴在温软的空气里，
负载着一簇簇开花的月光，
呼出稀有的芬芳；

金色的大雪片从星空
闪烁着落向深处：
一缕湿土的气息飘过，
几乎使我落泪。

二

那些华丽的星不是我的，
它们使我成了异乡人！
母亲往她头上抛下的面纱，
我竟不认识！

那随月光泛白、向大海延展的田野，
那棕榈投下的幽暗影，
长着密结弯垂花穗的草，
不是那细长如矛的叶。

我渴望看见那群里星宿
在更淡的蓝里闪烁；
但我最怀念的，是那丰茂的草，
和闪现在草间的雏菊。

寻常的事物都不一样了！
我隔着海浪思念：
那气味从露湿的土地飘来——
我认出了这世界是我的家。

三

群星在深邃的太空里欢喜——
黑暗于它们是友好的！
从白昼的深矿，它们藏身之处，
夜把每一颗宝石引来。

在劳碌争闹中当信的一件事：
当白昼卷起收起，
天边远处亮着一盏灯，
或许是一个住满了家的世界。

有时在内心的天空上
我们瞥见一点可疑的光：
是一粒微尘还是星？是眼中的闪
还是上帝矿里的宝石？

对我们而言只是一颗星，闪烁的一瞥，
也许孕育着满世界的撒拉弗；
对我们的愚昧只是一场幻想，
对他也许是一个真理。

四

夜潮湿、温暖而安静，
柔软得像夏天的梦；
花蕾随心所欲地绽开，
半月羞怯地放光。

我的灵魂清凉，仿佛在里面
沐浴过无声哭泣的露水——
像一个孩子，刚认完了罪，
现在要去睡了。

我的身体在形貌与颜色上老去；
但当春风吹起，
我的灵魂便骚动、重新发芽，
比许久以前更年轻。

主啊，使我更像孩子，越来越像，
直到时间抵达它自己的尽头，
让我从每一场凛冽的寒冬里
出来，进入你的春天。

## The Three Horses / 三匹马
===Original===

What shall I be?﻿—I will be a knight
Walled up in armour black,
With a sword of sharpness, a hammer of might.
And a spear that will not crack﻿—
So black, so blank, no glimmer of light
Will betray my darkling track.

Saddle my coal-black steed, my men,
Fittest for sunless work;
Old Night is steaming from her den,
And her children gather and lurk;
Bad things are creeping from the fen,
And sliding down the murk.

Let him go!﻿—let him go! Let him plunge!﻿—Keep away!
He’s a foal of the third seal’s brood!
Gaunt with armour, in grim array
Of poitrel and frontlet-hood,
Let him go, a living castle, away﻿—
Right for the evil wood.

I and Ravenwing on the course,
Heavy in fighting gear﻿—
Woe to the thing that checks our force,
That meets us in career!
Giant, enchanter, devil, or worse﻿—
What cares the couched spear!

Slow through the trees zigzag I ride.
See! the goblins!﻿—to and fro!
From the skull of the dark, on either side,
See the eyes of a dragon glow!
From the thickets the silent serpents glide﻿—
I pass them, I let them go;

For somewhere in the evil night
A little one cries alone;
An aged knight, outnumbered in fight,
But for me will be stricken prone;
A lady with terror is staring white,
For her champion is overthrown.

The child in my arms, to my hauberk prest,
Like a trembling bird will cling;
I will cover him over, in iron nest,
With my shield, my one steel wing,
And bear him home to his mother’s breast,
A radiant, rescued thing.

Spur in flank, and lance in rest,
On the old knight’s foes I flash;
The caitiffs I scatter to east and west
With clang and hurtle and crash;
Leave them the law, as knaves learn it best,
In bruise, and breach, and gash.

The lady I lift on my panting steed;
On the pommel she holds my mace;
Hand on bridle I gently lead
The horse at a gentle pace;
The thickets with martel-axe I heed,
For the wood is an evil place.

What treasure is there in manly might
That hid in the bosom lies!
Who for the crying will not fight
Had better be he that cries!
A man is a knight that loves the right
And mounts for it till he dies.

Alas, ’tis a dream of ages hoar!
In the fens no dragons won;
No giants from moated castles roar;
Through the forest wide roadways run;
Of all the deeds they did of yore
Not one is left to be done!

===Chinese===

我该做什么样的人？——我要做一名骑士，
裹在乌黑的铠甲里，
佩一柄锋利的剑，一柄威力的锤，
和一支不会折断的长矛——
那样黑，那样暗，没有一丝光的闪动
会泄露我暗夜里的行踪。

备好我乌黑的骏马，我的部从，
它最配不见天日的差事；
老夜正从她的巢穴里蒸腾，
她的孩子们正聚拢、潜伏；
坏东西正从沼泽里爬出，
滑下那一片幽暗。

放它走！——放它走！让它腾跃！——都让开！
它是第三印马驹的后裔！
披挂到牙齿，列着森严的阵仗，
胸甲与面甲齐备，
放它走，一座活的城堡，直奔——
那邪恶的森林正前方。

我和「鸦翼」并辔上路，
一身沉重的战装——
凡拦阻我们冲力的东西遭殃，
凡在疾驰中撞上我们的遭殃！
巨人、妖法师、魔鬼，或更糟的——
平端的长矛何曾在意！

我缓缓地之字形穿行林间。
看！那些妖精！——来来回回！
从黑暗的头颅里，在道路两旁，
看，龙的眼睛在发光！
无声的蛇从灌木里滑出——
我经过，我放它们过去；

因为这邪恶之夜的某个地方，
有一个小家伙在独自啼哭；
一位年迈的骑士，寡不敌众，
若没有我就会倒下；
一位贵妇吓得面无人色，
因为她的护卫已被打翻。

那孩子在我怀里，贴着我的铠甲，
会像一只发抖的小鸟偎依；
我要把他掩进这铁的巢，
用我的盾，我唯一的钢翼，
然后送他回他母亲的怀抱，
一个重放光彩、获救的小东西。

马刺刺胁，长矛夹稳，
我向老骑士的仇敌闪击；
把那些恶棍打得四散东西，
一片铿锵、轰撞与迸裂；
给他们留下法律，无赖们最懂它——
写在高伤、破甲和裂口里。

我把那贵妇扶上我喘息的马；
她扶着鞍头，握着我的锤；
我一手牵缰，缓缓地引着
那马迈出从容的步子；
我挥着战斧开路，留心灌丛，
因为这林子是个邪恶的地方。

男儿的膂力里藏着怎样的珍宝，
它深藏在他胸中！
不肯为啼哭而战的人，
还不如去做那啼哭的人！
爱慕正义、为它上马直到死的，
才是一个骑士。

唉，这是太古年代的一场梦！
沼泽里再没有龙被降伏；
没有巨人从带壕的城堡里咆哮；
宽阔的大道穿林而过；
他们往昔建立的功业，
竟没有一件留下来待做！

===Original===

If I should saddle old Ravenwing
And hie me out at night,
Scared little birds away would spring
An ill-shot arrow’s flight:
The idle fancy away I fling,
Now I will dream aright!

Let a youth bridle Twilight, my dapple-gray,
With broad rein and snaffle bit;
He must bring him round at break of day
When the shadows begin to flit,
When the darkness begins to dream away,
And the owls begin to sit.

Ungraithed in plate or mail I go,
With only my sword﻿—gray-blue
Like the scythe of the dawning come to mow
The night-sprung shadows anew
From the gates of the east, that, fair and slow,
Maid Morning may walk through.

I seek no forest with darkness grim,
To the open land I ride;
Low light, from the broad horizon’s brim,
Lies wet on the flowing tide,
And mottles with shadows dun and dim
The mountain’s rugged side.

Steadily, hasteless, o’er valley and hill.
O’er the moor, along the beach,
We ride, nor slacken our pace until
Some city of men we reach;
There, in the market, my horse stands still,
And I lift my voice and preach.

Wealth and poverty, age and youth
Around me gather and throng;
I tell them of justice, of wisdom, of truth,
Of mercy, and law, and wrong;
My words are moulded by right and ruth
To a solemn-chanted song.

They bring me questions which would be scanned,
That strife may be forgot;
Swerves my balance to neither hand,
The poor I favour no jot;
If a man withstand, out sweeps my brand.
I slay him upon the spot.

But what if my eye have in it a beam
And therefore spy his mote?
Righteousness only, wisdom supreme
Can tell the sheep from the goat!
Not thus I dream a wise man’s dream,
Not thus take Wrong by the throat!

Lead Twilight home. I dare not kill;
The sword myself would scare.﻿—
When the sun looks over the eastern hill,
Bring out my snow-white mare:
One labour is left which no one will
Deny me the right to share!

Take heed, my men, from crest to heel
Snow-white have no speck;
No curb, no bit her mouth must feel,
No tightening rein her neck;
No saddle-girth drawn with buckle of steel
Shall her mighty breathing check!

Lay on her a cloth of silver sheen,
Bring me a robe of white;
Wherever we go we must be seen
By the shining of our light﻿—
A glistening splendour in forest green,
A star on the mountain-height.

===Chinese===

倘若我备好老「鸦翼」
连夜驰出门去，
惊起的小鸟只会跳开，
像一支射歪的箭：
把这无谓的空想抛掉，
这回我要正经地做梦！

叫一个青年给「暮色」套上缰，我那匹灰花马，
用宽缰和小衔铁；
他必须在破晓时把它牵来，
当影子开始逃逸，
当黑暗开始梦幻般消散，
猫头鹰开始归巢。

我不披挂板甲或锁子甲，
只带着我的剑——灰蓝色，
像黎明的大镰，来重新刈割
夜里滋生的阴影，
从东方的门外，公正而缓慢地，
好让晨之少女走过来。

我不去寻幽暗狰狞的森林，
我骑向开阔的大地；
低低的光，从辽阔地平线的边缘，
湿漉漉地躺在流动的潮上，
又用暗淡的斑驳影子
点染山峦嶙峋的侧面。

沉着地，不疾不徐，越过山谷和丘陵，
越过荒原，沿着海滩，
我们骑行，直到抵达
某座人类的城，才放缓步伐；
在那里，集市上，我的马站定，
我扬起声音传讲。

富人与穷人、老者与少年
在我四围聚拢围拢；
我向他们讲公义、讲智慧、讲真理，
讲怜悯、讲律法、讲邪恶；
我的话被正义与同情
铸成一首庄严吟诵的歌。

他们带来争端要我裁断，
好让纷争被忘却；
我的天平不向任何一边偏，
我对穷人也不偏袒分毫；
若有人顽抗，我的剑就扫出，
当场把他新杀。

可倘若我自己眼里有一根梁木，
因而才看见他的刺呢？
唯有公义、唯有至高的智慧
能分辨绵羊和山羊！
我不能这样梦想智者的梦，
不能这样扼住邪恶的咽喉！

把「暮色」牵回去。我不敢杀伐；
那剑会吓着我自己。——
等太阳望过东边的山冈，
牵出我雪白的母马：
还有一件苦工，没有人会
否认我分享的权利！

当心，我的部从，从鬃到蹄，
雪白不得有一斑点；
她的嘴不许感到勒、感到衔，
她的颈不许有收紧的缰；
不许有钢扣扣紧的鞍带
来束住她雄浑的呼吸！

给她披一袭银光闪闪的鞍布，
给我取一件白袍；
我们无论走到哪里，都要靠
我们光的照耀被人看见——
在绿色森林里是一道闪亮的华彩，
在高山之巅是一颗星。

===Original===

With jar and shudder the gates unclose;
Out in the sun she leaps!
A unit of light and power she goes
Levelling vales and steeps:
The wind around her eddies and blows,
Before and behind her sleeps.

Oh joy, oh joy to ride the world
And glad, good tidings bear!
A flag of peace on the winds unfurled
Is the mane of my shining mare:
To the sound of her hoofs, lo, the dead stars hurled
Quivering adown the air!

Oh, the sun and the wind! Oh, the life and the love!
Where the serpent swung all day
The loud dove coos to the silent dove;
Where the web-winged dragon lay
In its hole beneath, on the rock above
Merry-tongued children play.

With eyes of light the maidens look up
As they sit in the summer heat
Twining green blade with golden cup﻿—
They see, and they rise to their feet;
I call aloud, for I must not stop,
“Good tidings, my sisters sweet!”

For mine is a message of holy mirth
To city and land of corn;
Of praise for heaviness, plenty for dearth,
For darkness a shining morn:
Clap hands, ye billows; be glad, O earth,
For a child, a child is born!

Lo, even the just shall live by faith!
None argue of mine and thine!
Old Self shall die an ecstatic death
And be born a thing divine,
For God’s own being and God’s own breath
Shall be its bread and wine.

Ambition shall vanish, and Love be king,
And Pride to his darkness hie;
Yea, for very love of a living thing
A man would forget and die,
If very love were not the spring
Whence life springs endlessly!

The myrtle shall grow where grew the thorn;
Earth shall be young as heaven;
The heart with remorse or anger torn
Shall weep like a summer even;
For to us a child, a child is born,
Unto us a son is given!

Lord, with thy message I dare not ride!
I am a fool, a beast!
The little ones only from thy side
Go forth to publish thy feast!
And I, where but sons and daughters abide,
Would have walked about, a priest!

Take Snow-white back to her glimmering stall;
There let her stand and feed!﻿—
I am overweening, ambitious, small,
A creature of pride and greed!
Let me wash the hoofs, let me be the thrall,
Jesus, of thy white steed!

===Chinese===

城门带着轰响与震颤洞开；
她跃进太阳里！
她是一束光与力的单元，
踏平了山谷与陡坡：
风在她四周打着旋吹刮，
她的身前身后一片安静。

哦喜乐，骑遍这世界、
传递美好福音的喜乐！
在风里展开的一面和平之旗，
是我那闪亮母马的鬃毛：
听她蹄声，看哪，死去的星被掷下，
颤动着划过长空！

哦，这太阳和风！哦，这生命与爱！
毒蛇终日盘绕的地方，
喧闹的鸽子正向安静的鸽子咕鸣；
膜翼的龙曾躺卧的
底下洞穴，如今在那上面的岩石上，
孩子们舌头欢快地玩耍。

少女们抬起发亮的眼睛，
当她们坐在夏天的暑热里，
把绿茎和金杯编在一处——
她们看见，便站起身来；
我大声呼喊，因为我不能停留：
「好消息，我甜美的姊妹们！」

因为我带来的是神圣欢乐的信息，
给城市，给产粮的大地：
以赞美换沉重，以丰足换匮乏，
以闪亮的早晨换黑暗：
拍手吧，波涛；欢喜吧，大地，
因为一个孩子，一个孩子降生了！

看哪，就连义人也必因信得生！
没有人再争论你的我的！
老的己要死于一场出神的死，
重生为一件神圣之物，
因为上帝自己的存在、上帝自己的气息
将成为它的饼和酒。

野心必要消散，爱必要作王，
骄傲要逃回它的黑暗；
是啊，人为了对一个活物的爱
竟会忘记一切、死去，
倘若爱不是那眼泉——
生命从它无穷无尽地涌出！

桃金娘要长在荆棘长过的地方；
大地要年轻得像天堂；
被悔恨或愤怒撕裂的心
要哭得像一个夏日黄昏那样温柔；
因为给我们生了一个孩子，一个孩子，
赐给我们一个儿子！

主啊，带着你的信息我不敢骑行！
我是愚人，是畜生！
唯有小孩子从你身旁
出发去宣告你的筵席！
而我，在唯有儿女安住的地方，
竟想走来走去，做个祭司！

把「雪白」牵回她微光的马厩；
让她站在那里吃食！——
我狂妄、野心、渺小，
是一个又骄傲又贪婪的受造物！
让我来洗那些蹄子，让我做那奴仆，
耶稣，为你白色的骏马！

## The Golden Key / 金钥匙
===Original===

From off the earth the vapours curled,
Went up to meet their joy;
The boy awoke, and all the world
Was waiting for the boy!

The sky, the water, the wide earth
Was full of windy play﻿—
Shining and fair, alive with mirth,
All for his holiday!

The hill said “Climb me;” and the wood
“Come to my bosom, child;
Mine is a merry gamboling brood,
Come, and with them go wild.”

The shadows with the sunlight played,
The birds were singing loud;
The hill stood up with pines arrayed﻿—
He ran to join the crowd.

But long ere noon, dark grew the skies,
Pale grew the shrinking sun:
“How soon,” he said, “for clouds to rise
When day was but begun!”

The wind grew rough; a wilful power
It swept o’er tree and town;
The boy exulted for an hour,
Then weary sat him down.

And as he sat the rain began,
And rained till all was still:
He looked, and saw a rainbow span
The vale from hill to hill.

He dried his tears. “Ah, now,” he said,
“The storm was good, I see!
Yon pine-dressed hill, upon its head
I’ll find the golden key!”

He thrid the copse, he climbed the fence,
At last the top did scale;
But, lo, the rainbow, vanished thence,
Was shining in the vale!

“Still, here it stood! yes, here,” he said,
“Its very foot was set!
I saw this fir-tree through the red,
This through the violet!”

He searched and searched, while down the skies
Went slow the slanting sun.
At length he lifted hopeless eyes,
And day was nearly done!

Beyond the vale, above the heath,
High flamed the crimson west;
His mother’s cottage lay beneath
The sky-bird’s rosy breast.

“Oh, joy,” he cried, “not all the way
Farther from home we go!
The rain will come another day
And bring another bow!”

Long ere he reached his mother’s cot,
Still tiring more and more,
The red was all one cold gray blot,
And night lay round the door.

But when his mother stroked his head
The night was grim in vain;
And when she kissed him in his bed
The rainbow rose again.

Soon, things that are and things that seem
Did mingle merrily;
He dreamed, nor was it all a dream,
His mother had the key.

===Chinese===

水汽从地面卷起，
升上去迎接它们的欢喜；
男孩醒了，整个世界
都在等候这男孩！

天空、流水、辽阔的大地
充满了风的嬉戏——
明亮又晴美，漾满欢笑，
一切都是为了他的假日！

山丘说「来爬我」；树林说
「到我这怀里来，孩子；
我有一窝欢蹦乱跳的小家伙，
来，跟它们一起撒野。」

影与阳光嬉戏，
鸟儿高声歌唱；
山丘披着松林挺立——
他跑去加入这热闹。

可还不到中午，天就暗了，
畏缩的太阳变得惨白：
「白天才刚开始，」他说，
「云怎么就这么快升起来了！」

风变得狂暴；一股任性的威力
扫过树木和城镇；
男孩欢腾了一个时辰，
然后疲乏地坐下。

他正坐着，雨下了起来，
一直下到万物安静：
他望去，看见一道彩虹横跨
山谷，从这山到那山。

他擦干眼泪。「啊，现在，」他说，
「我看明白了，这场雨是好的！
那座披着松衣的山，在它的头顶上
我会找到那把金钥匙！」

他穿过杂树林，翻过篱笆，
终于登上了山顶；
可是看，彩虹从那里消失了，
正在山谷里发亮！

「可它方才就在这儿！是的，就在这里，」他说，
「它的脚就踏在这儿！
我隔着红光看见了这棵冷杉，
隔着紫光看见了这棵！」

他找啊找啊，同时斜挂的太阳
在天上慢慢落下。
终于他抬起绝望的眼睛，
白昼已将尽！

山谷之外，荒野之上，
猩红的西天高高地烧着；
他母亲的小屋躺在下面，
在天鸟玫色的胸脯底下。

「哦，好在，」他喊道，「并不是越走
离家越远！
雨改天还会再来，
还会带来另一道彩虹！」

还没到他母亲的小屋，
他已越来越疲惫，
那片红色早成了一团冰冷的灰斑，
夜已围拢在门前。

可当母亲抚着他的头，
狰狞的黑夜就枉然狰狞；
当她在床上亲吻他，
彩虹又升了起来。

很快，实在的事物和看似虚幻的事物
快活地混作一处；
他做梦了——却又不全是梦——
母亲手里握着那把钥匙。

## Somnium Mystici / 神秘主义者的梦
===Original===

*A Microcosm in Terza Rima*

I

Quiet I lay at last, and knew no more
Whether I breathed or not, so worn I lay
With the death-struggle. What was yet before
Neither I met, nor turned from it away;
My only conscious being was the rest
Of pain gone dead﻿—dead with the bygone day,
And long I could have lingered all but blest
In that half-slumber. But there came a sound
As of a door that opened﻿—in the west
Somewhere I thought it. As the hare the hound,
The noise did start my eyelids and they rose.
I turned my eyes and looked. Then straight I found
It was my chamber-door that did unclose,
For a tall form up to my bedside drew.
Grand was it, silent, its very walk repose;
And when I saw the countenance, I knew
That I was lying in my chamber dead;
For this my brother﻿—brothers such are few﻿—
That now to greet me bowed his kingly head,
Had, many years agone, like holy dove
Returning, from his friends and kindred sped,
And, leaving memories of mournful love,
Passed vanishing behind the unseen veil;
And though I loved him, all high words above.
Not for his loss then did I weep or wail,
Knowing that here we live but in a tent,
And, seeking home, shall find it without fail.
Feeble but eager, toward him my hands went﻿—
I too was dead, so might the dead embrace!
Taking me by the shoulders down he bent,
And lifted me. I was in sickly case,
But, growing stronger, stood up on the floor,
There turned, and once regarded my dead face
With curious eyes: its brow contentment wore,
But I had done with it, and turned away.
I saw my brother by the open door,
And followed him out into the night blue-gray.
The houses stood up hard in limpid air,
The moon hung in the heavens in half decay,
And all the world to my bare feet lay bare.

II

===Chinese===

一则三韵体的微观宇宙

一

我终于安静地躺着，再不知道
自己是否还在呼吸，我被那场
死亡的挣扎磨得这样疲惫。前方是什么，
我既不曾迎上去，也不曾躲开；
我唯一知道的只是痛已死去——
随逝去的一天一同死去的安息，
在那半睡半醒里我几乎可以幸福地
流连许久。但来了一个声响，
像一扇门打开——我想它
在西边某处。像野兔听见猎犬，
那声响惊起我的眼，眼便睁开了。
我转眼望去。随即我便发现
是我卧房的门在开启，
一个高大的身影走到我床前。
它庄严、无声，连行走都像安息；
当我看见那面容，我便知道
我正躺在我的卧房里，死了；
因为这是我的兄长——这样的兄长少有——
他此刻向我低下他王者般的头，
许多年前，他像一只圣洁的鸽子
归巢，离开亲友启程，
留下满载哀伤之爱的记忆，
隐没到那看不见的帷幕后去了；
虽然我爱他，胜过一切崇高的言语。
那时我不曾为他的离去哭泣哀号，
因为知道我们在此不过是住在帐棚，
寻求家的人，必不落空地寻见。
我虚弱而急切地朝他伸出双手——
我也是死者了，死者正好可以拥抱！
他俯身抓住我的双肩，
把我举了起来。我还病弱不堪，
但渐渐有力气，站到了地板上，
回头，带着好奇端详我那张死去的脸：
它眉宇间带着满足，
但我已和它两清，转过身去。
我看见兄长立在敞开的门边，
便跟着他走进蓝灰的夜里。
房屋在澄澈的空气中棱角分明，
月亮悬在天上，半是残缺，
整个世界向我的赤脚赤裸呈现。

===Original===

Now I had suffered in my life, as they
Must suffer, and by slow years younger grow,
From whom the false fool-self must drop away,
Compact of greed and fear, which, gathered slow,
Darkens the angel-self that, evermore,
Where no vain phantom in or out shall go,
Moveless beholds the Father﻿—stands before
The throne of revelation, waiting there,
With wings low-drooping on the sapphire-floor,
Until it find the Father’s ideal fair,
And be itself at last: not one small thorn
Shall needless any pilgrim’s garments tear;
And but to say I had suffered I would scorn
Save for the marvellous thing that next befell:
Sudden I grew aware I was new-born;
All pain had vanished in the absorbent swell
Of some exalting peace that was my own;
As the moon dwelt in heaven did calmness dwell
At home in me, essential. The earth’s moan
Lay all behind. Had I then lost my part
In human griefs, dear part with them that groan?
“ ’Tis weariness!” I said; but with a start
That set it trembling and yet brake it not,
I found the peace was love. Oh, my rich heart!
For, every time I spied a glimmering spot
Of window pane, “There, in that silent room,”
Thought I, “mayhap sleeps human heart whose lot
Is therefore dear to mine!” I cared for whom
I saw not, had not seen, and might not see!
After the love crept prone its shadow-gloom,
But instant a mightier love arose in me,
As in an ocean a single wave will swell,
And heaved the shadow to the centre: we
Had called it prayer, before on sleep I fell.
It sank, and left my sea in holy calm:
I gave each man to God, and all was well.
And in my heart stirred soft a sleeping psalm.

III

===Chinese===

我这一生受过苦，正如凡人所必受，
靠缓慢的年岁变得年轻，虚妄愚昧的己
必须从中剥落，
它由贪婪与恐惧结成，慢慢积聚，
遮暗了那天使的自己——它始终
在那没有虚幻出入的地方，
静默地仰望天父——立在
启示的宝座前等候，
翅膀低垂在蓝宝石的地面上，
直到寻见天父那美好的理想，
直到它自己终于成全：没有一根小刺
会无缘无故划破朝圣者的衣袍；
我本羞于说我曾受苦，
若不是紧接着发生了那件奇事：
我骤然觉察自己重新出生了；
一切疼痛都消失在某种高涨的
安宁的吸纳之潮里，那安宁属于我；
如同月亮居于天，宁静也居于
我里面，是本质的。大地的呻吟
全都落在了身后。难道我竟失去了
与人的哀哭的一份，与呻吟者的亲爱的一份？
「这不过是倦怠！」我说；但心猛然一惊，
颤动它却并未折断，
我发现那安宁原来是爱。哦，我富足的心！
因为每当 我瞥见窗玻璃上一点微光，「那里，那间安静的屋子里，」
我想，「也许睡着一颗人的心，它的命运
因此与我的相亲！」我顾念那些
我看不见、不曾见过、也未必能见的人！
爱后面爬行着它的阴影的阴郁，
但顷刻间一股更大的爱在我里面升起，
像大洋里单独一道浪涌起，
把那阴影掀到了中心：
在我入睡之前，我们曾把这叫作祷告。
它沉落了，留下我的海一片圣洁的平静：
我把每个人交托给上帝，一切都好了。
一首沉睡的诗篇在我心里轻轻动了动。

三

===Original===

No gentlest murmur through the city crept;
Not one lone word my brother to me had spoken;
But when beyond the city-gate we stepped
I knew the hovering silence would be broken.
A low night wind came whispering: through and through
It did baptize me with the pledge and token
Of that soft spirit-wind which blows and blew
And fans the human world since evermore.
The very grass, cool to my feet, I knew
To be love also, and with the love I bore
To hold far sympathy, silent and sweet,
As having known the secret from of yore
In the eternal heart where all things meet,
Feelings and thinkings, and where still they are bred.
Sudden he stood, and with arrested feet
I also. Like a half-sunned orb, his head
Slow turned the bright side: lo, the brother-smile
That ancient human glory on me shed
Clothed in which Jesus came forth to wile
Unto his bosom every labouring soul,
And all dividing passions to beguile
To winsome death, and then on them to roll
The blessed stone of the holy sepulchre!
“Thank God,” he said, “thou also now art whole
And sound and well! For the keen pain, and stir
Uneasy, and sore grief that came to us all,
In that we knew not how the wine and myrrh
Could ever from the vinegar and gall
Be parted, are deep sunk, yea drowned in God;
And yet the past not folded in a pall,
But breathed upon, like Aaron’s withered rod,
By a sweet light that brings the blossoms through,
Showing in dreariest paths that men have trod
Another’s foot-prints, spotted of crimson hue,
Still on before wherever theirs did wend;
Yea, through the desert leading, of thyme and rue,
The desert souls in which young lions rend
And roar﻿—the passionate who, to be blest,
Ravin as bears, and do not gain their end,
Because that, save in God, there is no rest.”

IV

===Chinese===

没有一丝最轻的低语掠过城市；
我的兄长不曾对我说过一个字；
但当我们迈出城门，
我知道那低回的寂静就要打破。
一阵低低的夜风前来低语：它
彻里彻外地为我施洗，用那应许与印记——
那柔和的灵之风，从亘古以来
就一直吹拂、扇动着人类世界。
连脚下清凉的草，我也认得
同样是爱，并且与我所怀的爱
有着遥远的共鸣，安静而甘甜，
仿佛它从起初就知晓那奥秘，
在一切相遇的永恒的心里，
感受与思想，至今仍在那里孕育。
他忽然站住，我也随之
收步。他的头像一颗半沐阳光的星，
缓缓转出明亮的一面：看哪，那兄长的微笑，
那古老的人性荣光洒在我身上，
耶稣当年正是披着它出来，
把每一个劳苦的灵魂诱向他胸怀，
把一切使人分裂的激情诱向
一种可爱的死，然后为他们滚开
那圣墓的福石！
「感谢上帝，」他说，「你如今也痊愈、
健全、安好了！因为那刺骨的痛、那不安的
烦乱、那临到我们众人的深重忧伤——
那时我们不知道酒与没药
怎能从醋与苦胆中分离出来——
如今都深深沉没，是的，淹死在上帝里；
而往昔并没有裹进寿衣，
而是被轻轻呵了一口气，像亚伦那根枯杖，
被一道甜蜜的光催开了花朵，
在人们走过的最荒凉的路途上
显出另一双足迹，带着猩红的斑点，
无论他们的脚走向哪里，它总在前面；
是啊，它引路穿过旷野，穿过百里香与芸香，
穿过年轻狮子抓撕、
咆哮的旷野之魂——那些暴烈的人，他们为了蒙福，
像熊一样抢食，却达不到目的，
因为除非在上帝里面，就不得安息。」

四

===Original===

Something my brother said to me like this,
But how unlike it also, think, I pray:
His eyes were music, and his smile a kiss;
Himself the word, his speech was but a ray
In the clear nimbus that with verity
Of absolute utterance made a home-born day
Of truth about him, lamping solemnly;
And when he paused, there came a swift repose,
Too high, too still to be called ecstasy﻿—
A purple silence, lanced through in the close
By such keen thought that, with a sudden smiling,
It grew sheen silver, hearted with burning rose.
He was a glory full of reconciling,
Of faithfulness, of love with no self-stain,
Of tenderness, and care, and brother-wiling
Back to the bosom of a speechless gain.

V

===Chinese===

我兄长对我说的话有些像这样，
却又何等不像，请你想想：
他的眼睛是音乐，他的微笑是亲吻；
他自己就是那道，他的言语不过是
环绕他的一片清辉中的一线光，
那清辉以绝对言说的真实，
在他四围造出一个家常的白昼，
是真理的，庄严地亮着；
当他停顿，就有一阵迅疾的安息来临，
太高、太静，称不上狂喜——
一片紫色的静默，在结尾处
被那样锋利的思想穿透，它带着
一抹突然的微笑，化为闪亮的银，
心里燃着玫瑰。他是一团
满含和好的荣光，满含信实，
满含没有自污的爱，
满含温柔、眷顾，和把弟兄诱回
一场无言之获的怀抱里的手笔。

五

===Original===

I cannot tell how long we joyous talked,
For from my sense old time had vanished quite,
Space dim-remaining﻿—for onward still we walked.
No sun arose to blot the pale, still night﻿—
Still as the night of some great spongy stone
That turns but once an age betwixt the light
And the huge shadow from its own bulk thrown,
And long as that to me before whose face
Visions so many slid, and veils were blown
Aside from the vague vast of Isis’ grace.
Innumerous thoughts yet throng that infinite hour,
And hopes which greater hopes unceasing chase,
For I was all responsive to his power.
I saw my friends weep, wept, and let them weep;
I saw the growth of each grief-nurtured flower;
I saw the gardener watching﻿—in their sleep
Wiping their tears with the napkin he had laid
Wrapped by itself when he climbed Hades’ steep;
What wonder then I saw nor was dismayed!
I saw the dull, degraded monsters nursed
In money-marshes, greedy men that preyed
Upon the helpless, ground the feeblest worst;
Yea all the human chaos, wild and waste,
Where he who will not leave what God hath cursed
Now fruitless wallows, now is stung and chased
By visions lovely and by longings dire.
“But who believeth, he shall not make haste,
Even passing through the water and the fire,
Or sad with memories of a better lot!
He, saved by hope, for all men will desire,
Knowing that God into a mustard-jot
May shut an aeon; give a world that lay
Wombed in its sun, a molten unorbed clot,
One moment from the red rim to spin away
Librating﻿—ages to roll on weary wheel
Ere it turn homeward, almost spent its day!
Who knows love all, time nothing, he shall feel
No anxious heart, shall lift no trembling hand;
Tender as air, but clothed in triple steel,
He for his kind, in every age and land,
Hoping will live; and, to his labour bent,
The Father’s will shall, doing, understand.”
So spake my brother as we onward went:
His words my heart received, as corn the lea,
And answered with a harvest of content.
We came at last upon a lonesome sea.

VI

===Chinese===

我说不清我们欢谈了多久，
因为旧的时间已从我的感官里消失，
空间还模糊地留着——因为我们仍在前行。
没有太阳升起来抹去这苍白、静止的夜——
静得像某块巨大的海绵般的星石之夜，
一个纪元才在光与它自身巨躯投下的
巨大阴影之间翻转一次；
在我面前滑过那么多异象、
那么多帷 幔从伊西丝恩典的浩茫里
被吹开的这段时间，于我也同样漫长。
无数思绪仍挤满那无穷的一小时，
盼望后面还有更大的盼望不断追赶，
因为我全然回应着他的力量。
我看见我的朋友们哭，我哭了，且任他们哭；
我看见每朵由哀伤滋养的花如何生长；
我看见那位园丁在看顾——当他们睡着，
他用自己那块巾子为他们拭泪，那巾子
是他登上阴间陡坡时单独包好的；
难怪我看见了也不惊惶！
我看见那些迟钝、堕落的怪物，
养育在金钱的沼泽里，贪婪的人
猎食无助者，把最弱的碾得最碎；
是啊，看见全部人类的混沌，狂野而荒芜，
凡不肯离弃上帝所咒诅之物的，
在那里徒然打滚，时而又被可爱的异象
和可怕的渴望蜇刺、驱赶。
「但那信的人必不着急，
哪怕行经水与火，
或因记念更美的往昔而忧伤！
他既因盼望得救，就必为万人祈愿，
知道上帝能把一个永世
收进一粒芥子；能给一个世界——它曾孕育
在自己的太阳里，一团熔化的、无轨的凝块——
一刻间从红的边缘旋转着甩出，
悬在平衡里——再经历亿万斯年
在疲惫的轮上滚动，才转向归途，
那时它的白昼几乎耗尽！
谁认识了爱的一切、时间于他为零，谁就不再
心里焦灼，不再发抖地举手；
他温柔如空气，却披着三重的钢，
为了他的同类，在每一个时代、每一片土地，
怀着盼望生活；他向劳碌倾身，
行着，就明白天父的旨意。」
我的兄长一路走着这样说：
我的心领受他的话，像田地领受种子，
并以一季满足的丰收作答。
我们终于来到一片寂寞的海。

六

===Original===

And onward still he went, I following
Out on the water. But the water, lo,
Like a thin sheet of glass, lay vanishing!
The starry host in glorious twofold show
Looked up, looked down. The moment I saw this,
A quivering fear thorough my heart did go:
Unstayed I walked across a twin abyss,
A hollow sphere of blue; nor floor was found
Of questing eye, only the foot met the kiss
Of the cool water lightly crisping round
The edges of the footsteps! Terror froze
My fallen eyelids. But again the sound
Of my guide’s voice on the still air arose:
“Hast thou forgotten that we walk by faith?
For keenest sight but multiplies the shows.
Lift up thine eyelids; take a valiant breath;
Terrified, dare the terror in God’s name;
Step wider; trust the invisible. Can Death
Avail no more to hearten up thy flame?”
I trembled, but I opened wide mine eyes,
And strode on the invisible sea. The same
High moment vanished all my cowardice,
And God was with me. The well-pleased stars
Threw quivering smiles across the gulfy skies,
The white aurora flashed great scimitars
From north to zenith; and again my guide
Full turned on me his face. No prison-bars
Latticed across a soul I there descried,
No weather-stains of grief; quiet age-long
Brooded upon his forehead clear and wide;
Yet from that face a pang shot, vivid and strong,
Into my heart. For, though I saw him stand
Close to me in the void as one in a throng,
Yet on the border of some nameless land
He stood afar; a still-eyed mystery
Caught him whole worlds away. Though in my hand
His hand I held, and, gazing earnestly,
Searched in his countenance, as in a mine,
For jewels of contentment, satisfy
My heart I could not. Seeming to divine
My hidden trouble, gently he stooped and kissed
My forehead, and his arms did round me twine,
And held me to his bosom. Still I missed
That ancient earthly nearness, when we shared
One bed, like birds that of no morrow wist;
Roamed our one father’s farm; or, later, fared
Along the dusty highways of the old clime.
Backward he drew, and, as if he had bared
My soul, stood reading there a little time,
While in his eyes tears gathered slow, like dew
That dims the grass at evening or at prime,
But makes the stars clear-goldener in the blue:
And on his lips a faint ethereal smile
Hovered, as hangs the mist of its own hue
Trembling about a purple flower, the while
Evening grows brown. “Brother! brother!”

===Chinese===

他仍旧向前走，我跟着
走出到水面上。可是看哪，那水
像一片薄薄的玻璃，铺展着渐隐！
繁星的队伍以双份的荣耀
仰望着，也俯望着。我一见这景象，
一阵战栗的恐惧穿过我的心：
我毫不迟延地走过一片孪生的深渊，
一只蓝色的空心球；探寻的眼
找不到底，只有脚底碰到
凉凉的水，轻轻绉 在脚印的四缘！
恐惧冻住了我垂落的眼。但又一次，
我引路人的声音在静止的空气里响起：
「难道你忘了我们本是凭信而行？
因为最敏锐的视力不过是景象的倍增。
抬起你的眼；勇敢地吸一口气；
战栗着，也要奉上帝的名敢于直面这恐惧；
跨大步；信靠那看不见的。难道死亡
再不能鼓起你的火焰了吗？」
我发着抖，还是睁大了眼睛，
在那看不见的海上大步走去。就在那
至高的时刻，我全部的怯懦消失了，
上帝与我同在。满心喜悦的星辰
把颤动的微笑抛过深渊般的天空，
白色的极光从北到天顶挥出巨大的弯刀；
我的引路人再次
把脸完全转向我。我在那脸上
看不出一道栅栏囚着灵魂，
没有忧伤的风雨痕；静穆的、历久的高远
栖息在他清朗宽阔的额头上；
然而有一阵痛楚从那脸上射出，鲜明而有力，
射进我心里。因为，虽然我见他站在
虚空里我近旁，像人群中挨着的一个人，
却又站在某片无名之地的边界上，
离得遥远；一种静眼的奥秘
把他整个儿带到若干世界之外。虽然我手里
握着他的手，虽然我恳切凝望，
在他面容里，像在矿里，
寻觅满足的宝石，我的心
却无法满足。他似乎察觉了
我隐藏的愁苦，温柔地俯身亲吻
我的额头，用双臂环绕我，
把我抱进他的胸怀。可我仍旧怀念
那古老尘世的亲近，当年我们同睡
一张床，像不知有明天的小鸟；
同游我们唯一父亲的田庄；或稍后，一起走上
古老家园尘土飞扬的大路。
他向后退开，仿佛已把我的灵魂
剥露，站在那里读了一小会儿，
他眼里慢慢聚起泪水，像黄昏
或清晨使草朦胧的露，
却使星星在蓝天里更呈纯金：
