Yes, enough; but Love divine
Turned the water into wine!

When should wine like water flow,
But when home two glad hearts go!
When, in sacred bondage bound,
Soul in soul hath freedom found!
Such the time when, holy sign,
Jesus turned the water wine.

Good is all the feasting then;
Good the merry words of men;
Good the laughter and the smiles;
Good the wine that grief beguiles;﻿—
Crowning good, the Word divine
Turning water into wine!

Friends, the Master with you dwell!
Daily work this miracle!
When fair things too common grow,
Bring again their heavenly show!
Ever at your table dine,
Turning water into wine!

So at last you shall descry
All the patterns of the sky:
Earth a heaven of short abode;
Houses temples unto God;
Water-pots, to vision fine,
Brimming full of heavenly wine.

===Chinese===

「他们没有酒了！」她说。
可他们饼是够的；
门边的石缸
也盛着解渴的满满存水：
是的，本已足够；但神圣的爱
把水变成了酒！

酒什么时候该像水一样流淌？
正是两颗欢欣的心一同回家的时候！
正是被神圣的联结系在一起、
灵魂在灵魂里寻见自由的时候！
那就是那个时刻，神圣的表记——
耶稣把水变成酒。

那时一切宴席都是好的；
人们欢快的言语是好的；
笑声和微笑是好的；
宽慰忧伤的酒是好的；——
而最好的，是那神圣的圣言
把水变成酒！

朋友们，愿主与你们同住！
愿你们天天行这奇迹！
当美好的事物变得太过寻常，
就再次带回它们天上的光华！
愿他天天与你们同席，
把水变成酒！

这样，终有一天你们会看明
天上一切的样式：
大地是一处短暂寄居的天堂；
房屋是献给上帝的殿宇；
而那些水缸，在美好的异象里，
满溢着天上的酒。

## Blind Bartimeus / 瞎眼的巴底买
===Original===

As Jesus went into Jericho town,
’Twas darkness all, from toe to crown,
About blind Bartimeus.
He said, “My eyes are more than dim,
They are no use for seeing him:
No matter﻿—he can see us!”

“Cry out, cry out, blind brother﻿—cry;
Let not salvation dear go by.﻿—
Have mercy, Son of David.”
Though they were blind, they both could hear﻿—
They heard, and cried, and he drew near;
And so the blind were saved.

O Jesus Christ, I am very blind;
Nothing comes through into my mind;
’Tis well I am not dumb:
Although I see thee not, nor hear,
I cry because thou may’st be near:
O son of Mary, come!

I hear it through the all things blind:
Is it thy voice, so gentle and kind﻿—
“Poor eyes, no more be dim”?
A hand is laid upon mine eyes;
I hear, and hearken, see, and rise;﻿—
’Tis He! I follow him!

===Chinese===

当耶稣走进耶利哥城，
从脚到头都是一片黑暗，
包裹着瞎眼的巴底买。
他说：「我的眼睛岂止是昏花，
它们根本看不见他：
没关系——他能看见我们！」

「喊吧，喊吧，瞎眼的弟兄——喊吧；
别让宝贵的救恩走过去。
大卫的子孙啊，可怜我们。」
他们虽然瞎，却都听得见——
他们听见，就呼喊，他就近前来；
瞎眼的人就这样得救了。

哦耶稣基督，我也是全然瞎的；
什么都透不进我的头脑；
幸好我不是哑巴：
虽然我看不见你，也听不见你，
我仍要呼喊，因为你可能就在近旁：
哦马利亚的儿子，来吧！

我透过一切瞎眼的事物听见了：
那是你的声音吗，这样温柔这样良善——
「可怜的眼睛，不要再昏花了」？
有一只手正按在我的眼睛上；
我听见，侧耳，看见，站起来；——
是他！我跟随他！

## Come Unto Me / 到我这里来
===Original===

Come unto me, the Master says:﻿—
But how? I am not good;
No thankful song my heart will raise,
Nor even wish it could.

I am not sorry for the past,
Nor able not to sin;
The weary strife would ever last
If once I should begin!

Hast thou no burden then to bear?
No action to repent?
Is all around so very fair?
Is thy heart quite content?

Hast thou no sickness in thy soul?
No labour to endure?
Then go in peace, for thou art whole;
Thou needest not his cure.

Ah, mock me not! I often sigh;
I have a nameless grief,
A faint sad pain﻿—but such that I
Can look for no relief.

Come, come to him who made thy heart;
Come weary and oppressed;
To come to Jesus is thy part,
His part to give thee rest.

New grief, new hope he will bestow,
Thy grief and pain to quell;
Into thy heart himself will go,
And that will make thee well.

===Chinese===

到我这里来，主说：——
可是怎么来？我并不良善；
我的心唱不出感恩的歌，
甚至连愿望都没有。

我不为过去懊悔，
也没能力不犯罪；
那疲惫的争战会永远持续，
只要我一开头！

那你难道没有重担可背？
没有可悔的行为？
你四围的一切都那样美好吗？
你的心全然知足吗？

你灵魂里难道没有病？
没有劳碌要忍受？
那你就平平安安地去吧，因为你是健全的；
你不需要他的医治。

啊，不要嘲笑我！我常常叹息；
我有一种说不出名目的忧伤，
一阵微弱的钝痛——痛得
让我不敢指望任何解脱。

来吧，到那造了你心的他那里去；
疲惫的、受压的，都来；
来到耶稣面前是你的本分，
给你安息是他的本分。

他将赐下新的忧伤、新的盼望，
来平息你的忧伤与疼痛；
他自己要进到你心里去，
那就会使你痊愈。

## Blessed Are the Poor in Spirit / 虚心的人有福了
===Original===

*For Theirs Is the Kingdom of Heaven*

Our Father, hear our longing prayer,
And help this prayer to flow,
That humble thoughts, which are thy care,
May live in us, and grow.

For lowly hearts shall understand
The peace, the calm delight
Of dwelling in thy heavenly land,
A pleasure in thy sight.

Give us humility, that so
Thy reign may come within,
And when thy children homeward go,
We too may enter in.

Hear us, our Saviour: ours thou art,
Though we are not like thee;
Give us thy spirit in our heart,
Large, lowly, trusting, free.

===Chinese===

因为天国是他们的

我们的父，垂听我们渴慕的祷告，
也帮助这祷告流涌，
让谦卑的意念——你所眷顾的——
在我们里面活着，生长。

因为唯有谦卑的心才能明白
那平安、那安宁的喜乐：
住在你天上的国土里，
在你眼前蒙悦纳。

赐我们谦卑，好让你的国度
降临在我们里面，
当你的儿女们归家的时候，
我们也能进去。

垂听我们，我们的救主：你是我们的，
虽然我们还不像你；
求你把你的灵放在我们心里，
宽宏、谦卑、信靠、自由。

## Blessed Are They That Mourn / 哀恸的人有福了
===Original===

*For They Shall Be Comforted*

Speak to our hearts, O Father! Say
What we have been to thee;
How we have wandered far away,
And hardly turned to see.

Then lifted hands will hide the face;
Then tears our grief will prove
That such hath been the Father’s grace,
And such the children’s love.

Then shall our spirits hold at once
A comfort and a pain;
For we shall know thy wandering sons
Are turning home again.

With such glad grief, such tearful joy,
Be our repentance blest;
Thy comfort then, without alloy,
Shall give us heavenly rest.

===Chinese===

因为他们必得安慰

父啊，对我们的心说话！告诉我们
我们在你眼中曾是怎样；
我们怎样漂泊到了远方，
又几乎不曾回头看一看。

那时，举起的双手会遮住脸；
那时，眼泪会证明我们的悲伤——
天父的恩典原来是这样，
儿女的爱原来是这样。

那时，我们的灵将同时怀有
一份安慰和一份痛；
因为我们将知道，你那些流荡的儿子
正在转身回家。

愿我们的悔改就这样蒙福，
怀着这样欢喜的忧伤、这样含泪的喜乐；
那时你无杂质的安慰
将赐我们天上的安息。

## Blessed Are the Meek / 温柔的人有福了
===Original===

*For They Shall Inherit the Earth*

O son of man﻿—name of thy choice,
Our brother-Lord, our life,
The story says thy noble voice
Was never heard in strife.

Loving always, asleep, awake,
Talking, or drinking wine﻿—
Even uttering woe, thy love would make
The sons of God divine.

Without a place to lay thy head,
That head yet wore earth’s crown;
At thy command diseases fled,
The winds and waves lay down.

In all things like thy brethren made,
Grant, king of kings, that we,
In humble royalty arrayed,
Possess the earth like thee.

===Chinese===

因为他们必承受地土

哦人子——你自己拣选的名，
我们的兄长之主、我们的生命，
福音书里说，你那尊贵的声音
从不曾在争闹中被听见。

无论睡着、醒着，你总是爱着，
无论谈话，还是饮酒——
即便宣说灾祸，你的爱也要使
上帝的儿女们成为神圣。

你没有地方可以枕头，
那头颅却戴着大地的冠冕；
你一吩咐，疾病就逃遁，
风和浪也都躺卧安静。

你凡事与你的弟兄相同，
万王之王啊，求你使我们，
披上谦卑的王权，
像你一样承受这大地。

## Blessed Are They That Hunger / 饥渴慕义的人有福了
===Original===

*And Thirst After Righteousness: For They Shall Be Filled*

If we were longing for the bread
That cometh down from heaven;
If for the water that he said
To thirsty souls is given;

Then boldly should we come to thee,
And plead for that we want;
For in our souls desire would be
An earnest of the grant.

But when thy sun shines from the skies,
Earth smiles back to her lord:
In upward looks our hopes arise,
Responsive to thy word.

Our souls, dry empty vessels set
Thy rain to hold and lend,
Lie open to thy heaven, O let
The righteousness descend.

===Chinese===

饥渴慕义的人有福了，因为他们必得饱足

我们若渴慕那从天上
降下来的粮；
若渴慕他所说赐给
干渴灵魂的水；

我们就必坦然来到你面前，
恳求我们所缺的；
因为在我们灵魂里的渴望，
就是那恩赐的定金。

当你的太阳从天上照耀，
大地便向她的主回以微笑：
我们的盼望在仰望中升起，
应和着你的话语。

我们的灵魂，像一只只摆着的
干涸空器皿，为盛接、倒出你的雨，
向你的天敞开，哦，愿公义
降下来。

## Blessed Are the Merciful / 怜恤人的人有福了
===Original===

*For They Shall Obtain Mercy*

It was an awful hour that gave
Thee, Lord, the strength to win
Unholy men up from the grave
Of darkness and of sin.

And is this all thou dost require
For thy forgiveness now﻿—
That we to loftier bliss aspire
By doing even as thou?

Thou risest on our darksome earth,
Radiant of human light,
That men may see, recall their birth,
And claim its lofty right;

The right to pardon and to bless,
By service high to rule;
Upheld with wealth of tenderness
From God the pitiful.

===Chinese===

因为他们必蒙怜恤

那是一个可畏的时辰，它给了你，
主啊，得胜的力量，
把不圣洁的人从那黑暗
与罪恶的坟墓里拉起来。

而你如今所要的报偿
难道仅是这赦免——
要我们盼望更高的福乐，
就是行事像你一样？

你在我们幽暗的大地上升起，
散发着属人的光，
好叫人们看见，记起自己的出生，
认领那崇高的权利；

赦免与祝福的权利，
以崇高的服事掌权的权利；
由丰盛的温柔扶持，
那温柔来自怜悯的上帝。

## Blessed Are the Pure in Heart / 清心的人有福了
===Original===

*For They Shall See God*

Father, our bosoms, dark and drear,
Are in such evil case
With hate, ambition, care, and fear.
We cannot see thy face.

Cast out our Legion; cleanse thy room.
But not to leave it bare;
Let Christ into his temple come,
And devils will not dare.

His light will cleanse the eyes to see,
Open the ears to hear;
And so the house prepared for thee,
Thy vision will draw near.

Thy glory shall free entrance win,
When thou com’st to thy place;
And full of holy eyes within
We shall behold thy face.

===Chinese===

因为他们必得见神

父啊，我们的胸怀又暗又沉，
被仇恨、野心、忧虑和恐惧
糟蹋到这般田地，
我们看不见你的脸。

赶出我们的群鬼；洁净你的殿。
但不要让它空着；
让基督进入他的圣殿，
鬼魔就不敢停留。

他的光将洁净眼睛去看，
打开耳朵去听；
这样，那为你预备的屋子，
就会迎来你的异象。

你的荣耀必将畅行无阻地进来，
当你来到你的居所；
满屋都是圣洁的眼睛，
我们必得见你的脸。

## Morning Hymn / 晨歌
===Original===

O Lord of life, thy quickening voice
Awakes my morning song!
In gladsome words I would rejoice
That I to thee belong.

I see thy light, I feel thy wind;
The world, it is thy word;
Whatever wakes my heart and mind,
Thy presence is, my Lord.

The living soul which I call me
Doth love, and long to know;
It is a thought of living thee,
Nor forth of thee can go.

Therefore I choose my highest part,
And turn my face to thee;
Therefore I stir my inmost heart
To worship fervently.

Lord, let me live and will this day﻿—
Keep rising from the dead;
Lord, make my spirit good and gay﻿—
Give me my daily bread.

Within my heart, speak, Lord, speak on,
My heart alive to keep,
Till comes the night, and, labour done,
In thee I fall asleep.

===Chinese===

哦生命的主，你苏醒的声音
唤醒了我清晨的歌！
我要以欢欣的言语庆贺
我竟属于你。

我看见你的光，我感到你的风；
这世界就是你的话语；
凡唤醒我心与头脑的，
都是你的同在，我的主。

我这称作我的活着的灵魂，
它爱着，渴慕认识；
它是你——永活的你——的一个念头，
永远走不出你之外。

所以我拣选我至高的那部分，
把脸转向你；
所以我搅动我最深处的心，
火热地敬拜。

主啊，让我今天活着、愿意——
不断从死里起来；
主啊，使我的灵良善而欢畅——
赐给我日用的饮食。

在我的心里，说吧，主，继续说，
使我的心保持活着，
直到夜来临，劳碌完毕，
我在你里面入睡。

## Evening Hymn / 晚歌
===Original===

O God, whose daylight leadeth down
Into the sunless way,
Who with restoring sleep dost crown
The labour of the day!

What I have done, Lord, make it clean
With thy forgiveness dear;
That so to-day what might have been,
To-morrow may appear.

And when my thought is all astray,
Yet think thou on in me;
That with the new-born innocent day
My soul rise fresh and free.

Nor let me wander all in vain
Through dreams that mock and flee;
But even in visions of the brain,
Go wandering toward thee.

===Chinese===

哦上帝，你把日光引下
那不见太阳的路途，
又以恢复元气的睡眠
加冕白日的辛劳！

我所做过的，主啊，愿你以
宝贵的赦免将它洁净；
好叫今天本可能成为的，
明天能够显明。

即使我的思绪全然迷乱，
也求你仍在我里面思想；
好叫我的灵魂随那新生的、
无辜的白日，清新自由地升起。

也不要让我徒然穿行在
那些嘲弄又逃遁的梦里；
而要让我即便在头脑的幻象中，
也一路游向你。

## Noontide Hymn / 正午之歌
===Original===

I love thy skies, thy sunny mists,
Thy fields, thy mountains hoar,
Thy wind that bloweth where it lists﻿—
Thy will, I love it more.

I love thy hidden truth to seek
All round, in sea, on shore;
The arts whereby like gods we speak﻿—
Thy will to me is more.

I love thy men and women, Lord,
The children round thy door;
Calm thoughts that inward strength afford﻿—
Thy will than these is more.

But when thy will my life doth hold
Thine to the very core,
The world, which that same will doth mould,
I love, then, ten times more!

===Chinese===

我爱你的天空、你阳光中的薄雾、
你的田野、你霜白的群山、
你那随意吹拂的风——
而你的旨意，我更爱。

我爱在四围寻求你隐藏的真理，
在海里，在岸上；
爱那些使我们如神明般说话的技艺——
你的旨意于我更胜这些。

我爱你的男男女女，主啊，
爱你门边四围的孩子们；
爱那带来内在力量的安静思绪——
你的旨意更胜这一切。

而当你的旨意握住我的生命，
把它连核心都变成你的，
那被同一旨意塑造的世界，
我便爱它十倍地更多！

## The Thankless Lady / 不知感恩的贵妇
===Original===

It is May, and the moon leans down at night
Over a blossomy land;
Leans from her window a lady white,
With her cheek upon her hand.

“Oh, why in the blue so misty, moon?
Why so dull in the sky?
Thou look’st like one that is ready to swoon
Because her tear-well is dry.

“Enough, enough of longing and wail!
Oh, bird, I pray thee, be glad!
Sing to me once, dear nightingale,
The old song, merry mad.

“Hold, hold with thy blossoming, colourless, cold,
Apple-tree white as woe!
Blossom yet once with the blossom of old,
Let the roses shine through the snow!”

The moon and the blossoms they gloomily gleam,
The bird will not be glad:
The dead never speak when the mournful dream,
They are too weak and sad.

Listened she listless till night grew late,
Bound by a weary spell;
Then clanked the latch of the garden-gate,
And a wondrous thing befell:

Out burst the gladness, up dawned the love.
In the song, in the waiting show;
Grew silver the moon in the sky above.
Blushed rosy the blossom below.

But the merry bird, nor the silvery moon,
Nor the blossoms that flushed the night
Had one poor thanks for the granted boon:
The lady forgot them quite!

===Chinese===

正是五月，夜里月亮俯下身来，
照着一片开花的土地；
一位白衣的贵妇从她的窗里俯身，
手托着腮。

「哦，月亮，你为何在朦胧的蓝里？
为何在天上这样暗淡？
你看上去像一个就要晕倒的人，
因为她的泪泉已经流干。

「够了，够了这渴望和哀号！
哦鸟儿，求你欢畅起来吧！
给我唱一次，亲爱的夜莺，
唱那支老歌，快乐得发狂。

「停一停吧，你这开花的、无色又清冷的、
白得像哀愁的苹果树！
再开一次从前那样的花吧，
让玫瑰从雪里透出光来！」

月亮和花木阴郁地闪着微光，
鸟儿不肯欢畅：
在哀伤的梦里，死者从不说话，
他们太虚弱、太悲伤。

她无精打采地听着，直到夜深，
被一个疲倦的魔咒缚住；
这时花园的门闩咔哒一响，
一件奇妙的事发生了：

欢欣迸发出来，爱升起来，
在歌声里，在等待的景象里；
天上的月亮变成了银色，
树下的花泛起了玫瑰红。

可是那欢快的鸟、那银色的月亮，
还有染红了夜晚的花朵，
都没有为这应允的恩赐得到
一声可怜的感谢：
那位贵妇把它们全忘光了！

## The Sea-Shell / 海贝
===Original===

“Listen, darling, and tell to me
What the murmurer says to thee,
Murmuring ’twixt a song and a moan,
Changing neither tune nor tone.”

“Yes, I hear it﻿—far and faint,
Like thin-drawn prayer of drowsy saint;
like the falling of sleep on a weary brain,
When the fevered heart is quiet again.”

“By smiling lip and fixed eye,
You are hearing more than song or sigh:
The wrinkled thing has curious ways﻿—
I want to know what words it says.”

“I hear a wind on a boatless main
Sigh like the last of a vanishing pain;
On the dreaming waters dreams the moon,
But I hear no words in their murmured tune.”

“If it does not say that I love thee well,
’Tis a senseless, ill-curved, worn-out shell.
If it is not of love, why sigh or sing?
’Tis a common, mechanical, useless thing.”

“It whispers of love﻿—’tis a prophet-shell﻿—
Of a peace that comes and all shall be well;
It speaks not a word of your love to me,
But it tells me to love you eternally.”

===Chinese===

「听着，亲爱的，告诉我
那低语者对你说些什么，
它在歌与叹息之间低鸣，
调子和腔调都不变换。」

「是的，我听见了——遥远而微弱，
像困倦圣徒拉得又细又长的祷告；
像睡意落上疲惫的头脑，
当发烫的心终于重归安静。」

「凭你微笑的唇和专注的眼睛，
你听见的不止是歌或叹息：
这皱巴巴的东西有些古怪的话——
我想知道它说的是什么。」

「我听见一片风吹过无船的大海，
叹息得像一阵正在消退的疼痛的最后余音；
月亮在梦的水面上做着梦，
但在它们低吟的调子里，我听不见字句。」

「它若不说我爱你爱得深，
那它就是一只没有知觉、弧度糟糕、用坏了的贝壳。
若不是讲爱，它何必叹息或歌唱？
那它就只是一件平庸的、机械的、无用的东西。」

「它低语着爱——它是一只有预言能力的贝壳——
说一种将要来临、万事终将安好的平安；
它一字不提你对我的爱，
却吩咐我永远地爱你。」

## Autumn Song / 秋歌
===Original===

Autumn clouds are flying, flying
O’er the waste of blue;
Summer flowers are dying, dying,
Late so lovely new.
Labouring wains are slowly rolling
Home with winter grain;
Holy bells are slowly tolling
Over buried men.

Goldener light sets noon a sleeping
Like an afternoon;
Colder airs come stealing, creeping
From the misty moon;
And the leaves, of old age dying,
Earthy hues put on;
Out on every lone wind sighing
That their day is gone.

Autumn’s sun is sinking, sinking
Down to winter low;
And our hearts are thinking, thinking
Of the sleet and snow;
For our sun is slowly sliding
Down the hill of might;
And no moon is softly gliding
Up the slope of night.

See the bare fields’ pillaged prizes
Heaped in golden glooms!
See, the earth’s outworn sunrises
Dream in cloudy tombs!
Darkling flowers but wait the blowing
Of a quickening wind;
And the man, through Death’s door going,
Leaves old Death behind.

Mourn not, then, clear tones that alter;
Let the gold turn gray;
Feet, though feeble, still may falter
Toward the better day!
Brother, let not weak faith linger
O’er a withered thing;
Mark how Autumn’s prophet finger
Burns to hues of Spring.

===Chinese===

秋云飞着，飞着，
掠过蓝色的荒原；
夏花谢着，谢着，
不久前还那样清新可爱。
载重的马车缓缓滚动，
载着过冬的谷粒回家；
神圣的钟缓缓敲着，
为下葬的人们送行。

金色的光让正午睡意沉沉，
像午后的时光；
更冷的空气悄悄潜来，
从雾蒙蒙的月亮那里；
而叶子，正在老去、凋零，
披上泥土的颜色；
向每一阵孤寂的风叹息
它们的日子已经过去。

秋天的太阳沉落，沉落，
向低低的冬天沉去；
我们的心思想着，想着
雨夹雪和积雪；
因为我们的太阳正缓缓滑下
权能的山坡；
却没有一轮月亮轻轻爬上
夜晚的斜坡。

看那光秃田野被洗劫的战利品，
堆在金色的幽暗里！
看，大地用旧了的一场场日出
在云的坟墓里做梦！
暗处的花只是在等候
一阵苏醒之风吹来；
而人，穿过死亡之门走去，
把老旧的死亡留在身后。

所以，不要为清越音调的改变而哀恸；
任金色转成灰色；
脚步虽然虚弱，仍可以蹒跚着
迈向更好的日子！
弟兄啊，不要让软弱的信心
在枯萎之物上流连；
看哪，秋天那先知的手指
正烧出春天的颜色。

## Spring Song / 春歌
===Original===

Days of old,
Ye are not dead, though gone from me;
Ye are not cold,
But like the summer-birds fled o’er some sea.
The sun brings back the swallows fast
O’er the sea;
When he cometh at the last,
The days of old come back to me.

===Chinese===

往日啊，
你们虽已离我而去，却并未死去；
你们并不冰冷，
只是像夏鸟一样飞过了某片海。
太阳正把燕子
一群群带回海上；
当他最后来临的时候，
往日就会回到我身边。

## What Makes Summer? / 是什么造成了夏天？
===Original===

Winter froze both brook and well;
Fast and fast the snowflakes fell;
Children gathered round the hearth
Made a summer of their mirth;
When a boy, so lately come
That his life was yet one sum
Of delights﻿—of aimless rambles.
Romps and dreams and games and gambols,
Thought aloud: “I wish I knew
What makes summer﻿—that I do!”
Father heard, and it did show him
How to write a little poem.

What makes summer, little one,
Do you ask? It is the sun.
Want of heat is all the harm,
Summer is but winter warm.
’Tis the sun﻿—yes, that one there,
Dim and gray, low in the air!
Now he looks at us askance,
But will lift his countenance
Higher up, and look down straighter.
Rise much earlier, set much later,
Till we sing out, “Hail, Well-comer,
Thou hast brought our own old Summer!”

When the sun thus rises early
And keeps shining all day rarely,
Up he draws the larks to meet him,
Earth’s bird-angels, wild to greet him;
Up he draws the clouds, and pours
Down again their shining showers;
Out he draws the grass and clover,
Daisies, buttercups all over;
Out he wiles all flowers to stare
At their father in the air﻿—
He all light, they how much duller,
Yet son-suns of every colour!
Then he draws their odours out,
Sends them on the winds about.
Next he draws out flying things﻿—
Out of eggs, fast-flapping wings;
Out of lumps like frozen snails,
Butterflies with splendid sails;
Draws the blossoms from the trees,
From their hives the buzzy bees,
Golden things from muddy cracks﻿—
Beetles with their burnished backs;
Laughter draws he from the river
Gleaming back to the gleam-giver;
Light he sends to every nook
That no creature be forsook;
Draws from gloom and pain and sadness,
Hope and blessing, peace and gladness,
Making man’s heart sing and shine
With his brilliancy divine:
Summer, thus it is he makes it,
And the little child he takes it.

===Chinese===

冬天冻住了小溪和水井；
雪花一片接一片落下；
孩子们围在炉边，
用自己的欢笑造了一个夏天；
这时一个男孩，来到世上还不久，
他的人生还只是一整串
欢喜——一场场漫无目的的游荡、
嬉闹、梦、游戏和欢蹦——
大声想着：「真希望我知道
是什么造成了夏天——真想知道！」
父亲听见了，这倒给他指点了
怎样写一首小诗。

是什么造成了夏天，小家伙，
你在问吗？是太阳。
缺了热才是一切的害处，
夏天不过是暖和起来的冬天。
是太阳——对，就是那边那个，
昏灰晦暗，低低挂在空中！
现在他还斜着眼看我们，
但他会抬起他的脸，
越升越高，看得越来越直，
起得越来越早，落得越来越晚，
直到我们欢呼：「万岁，受欢迎的客，
你带回了我们自己的老夏天！」

当太阳这样早早升起，
整日那样出色地照耀，
他把云雀一只只拉上来迎接他，
那些大地的鸟天使，狂喜地迎接他；
他把云拉上来，又把云
闪亮的阵雨倾泻下去；
他把草和三叶草引出来，
引出满地的雏菊和毛茛；
他诱出所有的花，让它们仰望
它们空中的父亲——
他浑身是光，它们暗淡得多，
却是各种颜色的子太阳！
然后他引出它们的香气，
差它们乘着风四处飘散。
接着他引出一切会飞的——
从蛋里引出急拍的双翅；
从冻蜗牛似的团块里
引出张着华美帆翼的蝴蝶；
从树上引出花朵，
从蜂巢引出嗡嗡的蜜蜂，
从泥缝里引出金色的小东西——
那些背部磨亮的甲虫；
他从河里引出笑声，
河又把光亮还给赐光者；
他把光送到每个角落，
好叫没有一个受造物被遗忘；
他从阴郁、疼痛和悲伤里
引出盼望与祝福、平安与欢畅，
使人心里以他神圣的辉煌
又唱又亮：
夏天，他就这样造成，
而那小孩子听懂了。

===Original===

Day’s work done, adown the west
Lingering he goes to rest;
Like a child, who, blissful yet,
Is unwilling to forget,
And, though sleepy, heels and head,
Thinks he cannot go to bed.
Even when down behind the hill
Back his bright look shineth still,
Whose keen glory with the night
Makes the lovely gray twilight﻿—
Drawing out the downy owl,
With his musical bird-howl;
Drawing out the leathery bats﻿—
Mice they are, turned airy cats﻿—
Noiseless, sly, and slippery things
Swimming through the air on wings;
Drawing out the feathery moth,
Lazy, drowsy, very loath;
Drawing children to the door
For one goodnight-frolic more;
Drawing from the glow-worms’ tails
Glimmers green in grassy dales;
Making ocean’s phosphor-flashes
Glow as if they were sun-ashes.

Then the moon comes up the hill,
Wide awake, but dreaming still,
Soft and slow, as if in fear
Lest her path should not be clear.
Like a timid lady she
Looks around her daintily,
Begs the clouds to come about her,
Tells the stars to shine without her,
Then unveils, and, bolder grown,
Climbs the steps of her blue throne:
Stately in a calm delight,
Mistress of a whole fair night,
Lonely but for stars a few,
There she sits in silence blue,
And the world before her lies
Faint, a round shade in the skies!

But what fun is all about
When the humans are shut out!
Shadowy to the moon, the earth
Is a very world of mirth!
Night is then a dream opaque
Full of creatures wide awake!
Noiseless then, on feet or wings,
Out they come, all moon-eyed things!
In and out they pop and play,
Have it all their own wild way,
Fly and frolic, scamper, glow;
Treat the moon, for all her show,
State, and opal diadem,
Like a nursemaid watching them.
And the nightingale doth snare
All the merry tumult rare,
All the music and the magic,
All the comic and the tragic,
All the wisdom and the riot
Of the midnight moonlight diet,
In a diamond hoop of song,
Which he trundles all night long.

What doth make the sun, you ask,
Able for such mighty task?
He is not a lamp hung high
Sliding up and down the sky,
He is carried in a hand:
That’s what makes him strong and grand!
From that hand comes all his power;
If it set him down one hour,
Yea, one moment set him by,
In that moment he would die,
And the winter, ice, and snow
Come on us, and never go.

Need I tell you whose the hand
Bears him high o’er sea and land?

===Chinese===

一天的工做完了，沿着西天，
他迟迟不肯去安歇；
像一个孩子，还浸在福气里，
舍不得忘掉这一切，
虽然眼皮沉重，脚也酸了，
还想着不能就这么上床。
即使他落到了山后，
他明亮的目光还从山脊反照，
它那敏锐的荣光与黑夜
调成了可爱的灰色暮色——
它引出绒毛的猫头鹰，
带着它音乐般的鸟鸣；
引出皮革翅膀的蝙蝠——
本是老鼠，却变成了空中的猫——
无声、狡黠又滑溜的小东西，
乘着翅膀在空气里游动；
引出羽衣的飞蛾，
懒洋洋、困沉沉，老大不情愿；
把孩子们引到门口，
再玩一场睡前的好闹；
引出萤火虫的尾巴，
在草谷里闪着绿光；
使海洋的磷光闪烁发亮，
仿佛那是太阳的灰烬。

然后月亮爬上山来，
完全醒着，却还在做梦，
轻柔和缓，仿佛生怕
自己的路不够清亮。
她像一位羞怯的贵妇，
娇雅地环顾四周，
求云朵到她身边来，
叫星星们在外面亮着，
然后揭开面纱，胆子渐渐大了，
登上她蓝色宝座的台阶：
端庄地沉浸在平静的喜悦里，
做整整一个良夜的女主人，
身边只有寥寥几颗星，
她坐在那里，浸在蓝色的静默里，
而世界躺在她面前，
黯淡地，像天空中一团圆圆的影！

可是，人都关在门外以后，
四下里该多热闹啊！
在月亮眼里影影绰绰的大地，
是一个十足的欢乐世界！
夜这时是一场不透光的梦，
里面挤满了醒着的生灵！
于是，踏着脚或扇着翅，
它们全出来了，所有长着月眼的东西！
它们进进出出地又蹦又玩，
由着性子撒野，
飞着、闹着、奔跑着、发着光；
它们待月亮，不管她多么气派、
多么庄严、戴着蛋白石的冠冕，
都只当她是照看孩子的保姆。
而夜莺用歌声
捕捉那珍罕的欢腾，
捕捉那全部的音乐和魔法，
全部的滑稽和悲怆，
全部的智慧和放纵——
那午夜的月光盛宴——
装进一个钻石的歌环，
整个夜晚滚动着它。

你问，是什么使太阳
能担这样的大工？
他并不是一盏挂得高高的灯，
在天上滑上滑下，
他是被托在一只手里的：
这才使他强壮而威严！
他的一切能力都来自那只手；
那只手若把他放下一个时辰，
是啊，哪怕放下一瞬间，
在那一瞬间他就会熄灭，
而冬天、坚冰和大雪
就会压到我们头上，再也不走。

还需要我告诉你，那只手
是谁的吗？——他把太阳高举在海洋与陆地之上。

## The Mistletoe / 槲寄生
===Original===

Kiss me: there now, little Neddy,
Do you see her staring steady?
There again you had a chance of her!
Didn’t you catch the pretty glance of her?
See her nest! On any planet
Never was a sweeter than it!
Never nest was such as this is:
’Tis the nest of all the kisses,
With the mother kiss-bird sitting
All through Christmas, never flitting,
Kisses, kisses, kisses hatching,
Sweetest birdies, for the catching!
Oh, the precious little brood
Always in a loving mood!﻿—
There’s one under Mamy’s hood!

There, that’s one I caught this minute,
Musical as any linnet!
Where it is, your big eyes question,
With of doubt a wee suggestion?
There it is﻿—upon mouth merry!
There it is﻿—upon cheek cherry!
There’s another on chin-chinnie!
Now it’s off, and lights on Minnie!
There’s another on nose-nosey!
There’s another on lip-rosy!
And the kissy-bird is hatching
Hundreds more for only catching.

Why the mistletoe she chooses,
And the Christmas-tree refuses?
There’s a puzzle for your mother?
I’ll present you with another!
Tell me why, you question-asker,
Cruel, heartless mother-tasker﻿—
Why, of all the trees before her,
Gathered round, or spreading o’er her,
Jenny Wren should choose the apple
For her nursery and chapel!
Or Jack Daw build in the steeple
High above the praying people!
Tell me why the limping plover
O’er moist meadow likes to hover;
Why the partridge with such trouble
Builds her nest where soon the stubble
Will betray her hop-thumb-cheepers
To the eyes of all the reapers!﻿—
Tell me, Charley; tell me, Janey;
Answer all, or answer any,
And I’ll tell you, with much pleasure,
Why this little bird of treasure
Nestles only in the mistletoe,
Never, never goes the thistle to.

Not an answer? Tell without it?
Yes﻿—all that I know about it:﻿—
Mistletoe, then, cannot flourish,
Cannot find the food to nourish
But on other plant when planted﻿—
And for kissing two are wanted.
That is why the kissy-birdie
Looks about for oak-tree sturdy
And the plant that grows upon it
Like a wax-flower on a bonnet.

===Chinese===

亲我一下：好了，小内迪，
你看见她定定地盯着吗？
你又错过了一次机会！
你难道没接住她那漂亮的一瞥？
看她的巢！在任何星球上
都没有比这更甜的巢！
从来没有哪个巢是这样：
这是一切亲吻的巢，
那只亲吻的母鸟坐在里面，
整个圣诞节都不飞走，
孵着亲吻，亲吻，亲吻，
最甜美的小鸟，等着人捉！
哦这窝珍贵的小雏鸟，
永远一副亲热的模样！——
妈妈头巾下面就藏了一只！

喏，这是我这一分钟捉住的一只，
唱得跟任何红雀一样好听！
「它在哪儿呢？」你的大眼睛问着，
带一点点怀疑的小提示？
它在这儿——落在快活的嘴上！
它在这儿——落在樱桃般的脸颊上！
又一只落在小下巴上！
看，它飞走，落到了明妮身上！
又一只落在鼻鼻上！
又一只落在玫瑰般的唇上！
那亲吻鸟还在孵着
数以百计的，只等人来捉。

为什么她偏偏选中槲寄生，
却不要圣诞树？
这道题给你妈妈？
我再送你们一道！
告诉我为什么，你这爱提问的小家伙，
残忍的、狠心的折磨妈妈的小家伙——
为什么在她面前所有的树里，
聚拢的也好、荫覆的也好，
鹪鹩珍妮偏偏选中苹果树
做她的育儿室和小教堂！
或者寒鸦杰克偏要在尖塔里筑巢，
高高在祷告的人们头顶上！
告诉我为什么跛足的千鸟
爱在湿草地上盘旋；
为什么山鹑费那么大劲
把巢筑在很快就会只剩麦茬的地方，
把她的唧唧跳跳的雏鸟们
暴露在所有割麦人的眼里！——
告诉我，查利；告诉我，简妮；
全都答，或答一道也行，
我就满怀欢喜地告诉你们，
为什么这只小小的宝鸟
只在槲寄生里安家，
永远、永远不去蓟草那儿。

一个答案都没有？不答也告诉你们？
好——把我所知道的都告诉你们：——
槲寄生这东西，不能独自茂盛，
找不到养分的食粮，
除非种在别的植物上——
而亲吻，也必须两个人才成。
这就是为什么亲吻小鸟
要四处寻找结实的橡树，
寻找那长在树上的槲寄生，
像女帽上的一朵蜡花。

===Original===

But, my blessed little mannie,
All the birdies are not cannie
That the kissy-birdie hatches!
Some are worthless little patches,
Which indeed if they don’t smutch you,
’Tis they’re dead before they touch you!
While for kisses vain and greedy,
Kisses flattering, kisses needy,
They are birds that never waddled
Out of eggs that only addled!
Some there are leave spots behind them,
On your cheek for years you’d find them:
Little ones, I do beseech you,
Never let such birdies reach you.

It depends what net you venture
What the sort of bird will enter!
I will tell you in a minute
What net takes kiss﻿—lark or linnet﻿—
Any bird indeed worth hatching
And just therefore worth the catching:
The one net that never misses
Catching at least some true kisses,
Is the heart that, loving truly,
Always loves the old love newly;
But to spread out would undo it﻿—
Let the birdies fly into it.

===Chinese===

可是，我受福的小家伙们，
亲吻鸟孵出的
并非个个都是好鸟！
有些是无用的小破团，
它们若没把你弄脏，
那是因为还没碰到你，就已经死了！
至于那些虚荣又贪求的吻、
谄媚的吻、乞讨的吻，
它们是从来不曾从蛋里
摇摇摆摆走出来的鸟——那些蛋只是坏蛋！
有些鸟会在你身后留下斑点，
在你脸颊上多少年都找得到：
小家伙们，我恳求你们，
千万别让那样的鸟碰到你们。

你张什么样的网去冒险，
就会飞进什么样的鸟！
我立刻就告诉你们
什么网捉得住吻——红雀也好云雀也好——
确实值得孵、
也因此值得捉的任何鸟：
那张从不落空、
至少能捉到几分真吻的网，
就是一颗真正爱着的心，
对旧爱永远保持新爱；
但把它摊开就会坏事——
让小鸟们自己飞进去。

## Wild Flowers / 野花
===Original===

Content Primroses,
With hearts at rest in your thick leaves’ soft care,
Peeping as from his mother’s lap the child
Who courts shy shelter from his own open air!﻿—
Hanging Harebell,
Whose blue heaven to no wanderer ever closes,
Though thou still lookest earthward from thy domed cell!﻿—
Fluttering-wild
Anemone, so well
Named of the Wind, to whom thou, fettered-free,
Yieldest thee, helpless﻿—wilfully,
With “Take me or leave me,”
“Sweet Wind, I am thine own Anemone!﻿—”
Thirsty Arum, ever dreaming
Of lakes in wildernesses gleaming!﻿—
Fire-winged Pimpernel,
Communing with some hidden well,
And secrets with the sun-god holding,
At fixed hour folding and unfolding!﻿—
How is it with you, children all,
When human children on you fall,
Gather you in eager haste,
Spoil your plenty with their waste﻿—
Fill and fill their dropping hands?
Feel you hurtfully disgraced
By their injurious demands?
Do you know them from afar,
Shuddering at their merry hum,
Growing faint as near they come?
Blind and deaf they think you are﻿—
Is it only ye are dumb?
You alive at least, I think,
Trembling almost on the brink
Of our lonely consciousness:
If it be so,
Take this comfort for your woe,
For the breaking of your rest,
For the tearing in your breast,
For the blotting of the sun,
For the death too soon begun,
For all else beyond redress﻿—
Or what seemeth so to be﻿—
That the children’s wonder-springs
Bubble high at sight of you,
Lovely, lowly, common things:
In you more than you they see!
Take this too﻿—that, walking out,
Looking fearlessly about,
Ye rebuke our manhood’s doubt,
And our childhood’s faith renew;
So that we, with old age nigh,
Seeing you alive and well
Out of winter’s crucible,
Hearing you, from graveyard crept,
Tell us that ye only slept﻿—
Think we die not, though we die.

===Chinese===

知足的报春花，
心安在你们厚叶的柔护里，
像孩子从母亲膝上探头，
在自己敞开的天地里还羞求荫蔽！——
悬垂的风铃草，
你们的蓝色天堂从不向任何流浪者关闭，
虽然你始终从穹顶的小室向下凝望大地！——
翻飞野性的
银莲花，这名字
取得多好，以风为名，你被缚却自由地，
把自己交给它，无助——又任性，
说着「要我不要我随你」，
「甜蜜的风，我是你的银莲花！——」
干渴的斑龙芋，永远梦想着
荒野里闪烁的湖泊！——
火翅的繁缕，
与某口隐秘的井交通，
与太阳神互守着秘密，
在固定的钟点开合！——
孩子们，当人类的孩子们
扑到你们身上，
急不可待地把你们采摘，
用他们的浪费糟蹋你们的丰盈——
装满他们捧不完的双手，
那时你们是怎样的心情？
你们可觉得受了伤害的羞辱，
被他们强横的索取？
你们可远远就认出他们，
在他们欢快的嗡嚷里发抖，
他们越走近你们越虚弱？
他们以为你们又盲又聋——
难道你们只是不会说话？
我想，你们至少是活的，
颤抖在我们孤独意识的
边缘：
倘若真是这样，
就请收下这份安慰，为了你们的忧伤，
为了你们安息的被打破，
为了你们胸膛的被撕裂，
为了太阳的被遮灭，
为了过早开始的死亡，
为了一切无法补救的——
或看似无法补救的——
那就是：孩子们惊奇的泉源
一看见你们就高高涌起，
你们这些可爱、卑微、寻常的东西：
他们在你们里面看见的，比你们更多！
再收下这一份——你们一走出来，
无所畏惧地四下张望，
就斥责了我们成年的疑惑，
更新了我们童年的信心；
于是我们，纵然老境已近，
看见你们从冬天的坩埚里
活生生、好端端地出来，
听见你们从墓园里爬起来
告诉我们：你们只是睡着了——
便想：我们虽然死了，却并未死去。

===Original===

Thus ye die not, though ye die﻿—
Only yield your being up,
Like a nectar-holding cup:
Deaf, ye give to them that hear,
With a greatness lovely-dear;
Blind, ye give to them that see﻿—
Poor, but bounteous royally.
Lowly servants to the higher,
Burning upwards in the fire
Of Nature’s endless sacrifice,
In great Life’s ascent ye rise,
Leave the lowly earth behind,
Pass into the human mind,
Pass with it up into God,
Whence ye came though through the clod﻿—
Pass, and find yourselves at home
Where but life can go and come;
Where all life is in its nest,
At loving one with holy Best;﻿—
Who knows?﻿—with shadowy, dawning sense
Of a past, age-long somnolence!

===Chinese===

你们就这样虽死而不死——
只是交出你们的存在，
像一只盛满琼浆的杯：
聋的，你们给那些听得见的，
带着一种可亲的伟大；
盲的，你们给那些看得见的——
贫穷，却王室般慷慨。
作为更高者的卑微仆役，
在自然无尽献祭的火里
向上燃烧，
在伟大生命的攀升中你们升起，
把卑微的土地留在身后，
进入人的头脑，
再随它一同升入上帝，
你们本从他而来，虽曾途经泥土——
过去，便发现你们到了家，
在唯有生命能来能去的地方；
在那里一切生命都在它的巢里，
与神圣的至善亲爱为一；——
谁知道呢？——也许还带着一丝昏昧初醒的感觉，
记起一场亘古漫长的沉睡！

## Professor Noctutus / 诺克图图斯教授
===Original===

Nobody knows the world but me.
The rest go to bed; I sit up and see.
I’m a better observer than any of you all,
For I never look out till the twilight fall,
And never then without green glasses,
And that is how my wisdom passes.

I never think, for that is not fit:
I observe. I have seen the white moon sit
On her nest, the sea, like a fluffy owl,
Hatching the boats and the long-legged fowl!
When the oysters gape﻿—you may make a note﻿—
She drops a pearl into every throat.

I can see the wind: can you do that?
I see the dreams he has in his hat,
I see him shaking them out as he goes,
I see them rush in at man’s snoring nose.
Ten thousand things you could not think,
I can write down plain with pen and ink!

You know that I know; therefore pull off your hat,
Whether round and tall, or square and flat:
You cannot do better than trust in me;
You may shut your eyes in fact﻿—I see!
Lifelong I will lead you, and then, like the owl,
I will bury you nicely with my spade and showl.

===Chinese===

除了我，没人认识这世界。
别人都上床睡觉；我坐着守夜观看。
我比你们所有人都更会观察，
因为我从不趁天亮往外看，非要等暮色降临，
而且看的时候必定戴上墨绿的眼镜，
我的智慧就是这样炼成的。

我从不思考，因为思考不合适：
我只观察。我看见过白月亮
蹲在她的巢——大海——上，像一只绒毛的猫头鹰，
孵着小船和长腿的水鸟！
当牡蛎张开嘴——你可以记下一笔——
她就往每只喉咙里投下一颗珍珠。

我能看见风：你们能吗？
我看见他帽子里的那些梦，
我看见他一路走一路把梦抖出来，
我看见梦涌进人打鼾的鼻孔。
一万件你们想都想不到的事，
我能用纸笔白纸黑字写下来！

你们知道我知道；所以快脱帽致敬吧，
不管是圆高帽，还是方扁帽：
你们最好干脆信靠我；
事实上你们可以闭上眼睛——我看得见！
我会领你们一辈子，最后，像猫头鹰那样，
用我的铲子和铁锹把你们体面地埋掉。

## Bird-Songs / 鸟之歌
===Original===

I will sing a song,
Said the owl.
You sing a song, sing-song
Ugly fowl!
What will you sing about,
Night in and day out?

All about the night,
When the gray
With her cloak smothers bright,
Hard, sharp day.
Oh, the moon! the cool dew!
And the shadows!﻿—tu-whoo!

I will sing a song,
Said the nightingale.
Sing a song, long, long,
Little Neverfail!
What will you sing about,
Day in or day out?

All about the light
Gone away,
Down, away, and out of sight:
Wake up, day!
For the master is not dead,
Only gone to bed.

I will sing a song,
Said the lark.
Sing, sing, Throat-strong,
Little Kill-the-dark!
What will you sing about,
Day in and night out?

I can only call!
I can’t think!
Let me up, that’s all!
I see a chink!
I’ve been thirsting all night
For the glorious light!

===Chinese===

我要唱一支歌，
猫头鹰说。
你唱吧，唱吧，唱个不停，
丑陋的鸟！
你要唱什么呢，
整日整夜地唱？

我要唱那黑夜，
唱那灰色
用她的斗篷闷熄明亮、
坚硬尖利的白昼。
哦月亮！哦清凉的露！
还有那些影子！——吐—呼！

我要唱一支歌，
夜莺说。
唱吧，唱吧，长长的，
小「从不失败」！
你要唱什么呢，
日日夜夜地唱？

我要唱那光，
它去了远方，
向下、向远方，看不见了：
醒来吧，白昼！
因为主人没有死，
只是上床睡了。

我要唱一支歌，
云雀说。
唱吧，唱吧，大嗓门，
小「杀死黑暗」！
你要唱什么呢，
整日整夜地唱？

我只会叫！
我不会想！
让我上去，就这一件事！
我看见了一道裂缝！
我渴了一整夜，
渴慕那荣耀的光！

## The Unseen Model / 看不见的模特
===Original===

Forth to his study the sculptor goes
In a mood of lofty mirth:
“Now shall the tongues of my carping foes
Confess what my art is worth!
In my brain last night the vision arose,
To-morrow shall see its birth!”

He stood like a god; with creating hand
He struck the formless clay:
“Psyche, arise,” he said, “and stand;
In beauty confront the day.
I have sought nor found thee in any land;
I call thee: arise; obey!”

The sun was low in the eastern skies
When spoke the confident youth;
Sweet Psyche, all day, his hands and eyes
Wiled from the clay uncouth,
Nor ceased when the shadows came up like spies
That dog the steps of Truth.

He said, “I will do my will in spite
Of the rising dark; for, see,
She grows to my hand! The mar-work night
Shall hurry and hide and flee
From the glow of my lamp and the making might
That passeth out of me!”

In the flickering lamplight the figure swayed,
In the shadows did melt and swim:
With tool and thumb he modelled and made,
Nor knew that feature and limb
Half-obeying, half-disobeyed,
And mocking eluded him.

At the dawning Psyche of his brain
Joyous he wrought all night:
The oil went low, and he trimmed in vain,
The lamp would not burn bright;
But he still wrought on: through the high roof-pane
He saw the first faint light!

The dark retreated; the morning spread;
His creatures their shapes resume;
The plaster stares dumb-white and dead;
A faint blue liquid bloom
Lies on each marble bosom and head;
To his Psyche clings the gloom.

Backward he stepped to see the clay:
His visage grew white and sear;
No beauty ideal confronted the day,
No Psyche from upper sphere,
But a once loved shape that in darkness lay,
Buried a lonesome year!

From maidenhood’s wilderness fair and wild
A girl to his charm had hied:
He had blown out the lamp of the trusting child,
And in the darkness she died;
Now from the clay she sadly smiled,
And the sculptor stood staring-eyed.

He had summoned Psyche﻿—and Psyche crept
From a half-forgotten tomb;
She brought her sad smile, that still she kept,
Her eyes she left in the gloom!
High grace had found him, for now he wept,
And love was his endless doom!

Night-long he pined, all day did rue;
He haunted her form with sighs:
As oft as his clay to a lady grew
The carvers, with dim surmise,
Would whisper, “The same shape come to woo,
With its blindly beseeching eyes!”

===Chinese===

雕塑家走进他的画室，
怀着一种高昂的欢欣：
「这下，我那些爱挑剔的仇人的舌头
该承认我艺术的价值了！
昨夜异象在我脑中升起，
明天就将看到它诞生！」

他站着，像一位神；用创造的手
拍击无形的黏土：
「普赛克，起来，」他说，「站住；
以美迎接白昼。
我在哪一国都寻你不获；
我召唤你：起来；服从！」

太阳还低低挂在东天，
这自信的青年说着话；
甜美的普赛克，他一整天用手和眼
从粗粝的黏土里诱导，
直到影子像密探一样爬上来，
也不停手——那密探总跟踪真理的脚步。

他说：「任黑夜升起，我也要行我的旨意，
因为你看，
她正在我手中成形！败事的黑夜
只配仓皇躲藏、逃遁，
躲开我灯的光，和我身上
涌出的创造的伟力！」

在摇曳的灯光里，那形体晃动，
在暗影里消融、游动：
他用刀具和拇指捏塑修造，
却不知道五官和肢体
一半服从，一半违逆，
嘲弄着他，从他手里溜走。

为着他心中的那个黎明的普赛克，
他欢欣地劳作了一整夜：
油快尽了，怎么挑灯芯也没用，
灯就是亮不起来；
但他仍在做：透过高高的天窗，
他看见了第一缕微光！

黑暗退去；清晨铺展；
他的造物们恢复了形状；
那石膏呆白地瞪着，死气沉沉；
一层淡蓝的水光浮在
每个大理石的胸脯和头上；
幽暗缠着他的普赛克。

他退后一步看那黏土：
他的脸色变得惨白干枯；
迎着白昼的并非理想的美，
不是来自上界的普赛克，
而是一个曾经深爱的形貌，曾在黑暗里
孤独地埋了一年！

从少女时代那美丽而荒芜的旷野，
一个女孩曾应他的魅力而来：
他吹灭了那孩子信靠的灯，
她在黑暗中死去；
此刻她从黏土里哀伤地微笑，
雕塑家站在那里，眼睛发直。

他召唤的是普赛克——爬出来的普赛克
却来自一座半被遗忘的坟；
她带来了她至今保留的哀伤微笑，
眼睛却留在了幽暗里！
高天的恩典找到了他，因为此刻他哭了，
而爱成了他无尽的定命！

他整夜伤怀，整日悔恨；
他的叹息缠着那个形貌：
此后每当他手里的黏土
长成一位女子的身形，
雕刻匠们便会暗自猜疑，低语：
「又是那个形貌来求他了，
带着那双盲目恳求的眼睛！」

## Legend of the Corrievrechan / 科里弗雷坎漩涡传奇
===Original===

Prince Breacan of Denmark was lord of the strand
And lord of the billowy sea;
Lord of the sea and lord of the land,
He might have let maidens be!

A maiden he met with locks of gold,
Straying beside the sea:
Maidens listened in days of old,
And repented grievously.

Wiser he left her in evil wiles,
Went sailing over the sea;
Came to the lord of the Western Isles:
Give me thy daughter, said he.

The lord of the Isles he laughed, and said:
Only a king of the sea
May think the Maid of the Isles to wed,
And such, men call not thee!

Hold thine own three nights and days
In yon whirlpool of the sea,
Or turn thy prow and go thy ways
And let the isle-maiden be.

Prince Breacan he turned his dragon prow
To Denmark over the sea:
Wise women, he said, now tell me how
In yon whirlpool to anchor me.

Make a cable of hemp and a cable of wool
And a cable of maidens’ hair,
And hie thee back to the roaring pool
And anchor in safety there.

The smiths of Greydule, on the eve of Yule,
Will forge three anchors rare;
The hemp thou shalt pull, thou shalt shear the wool,
And the maidens will bring their hair.

Of the hair that is brown thou shalt twist one strand,
Of the hair that is raven another;
Of the golden hair thou shalt twine a band
To bind the one to the other!

The smiths of Greydule, on the eve of Yule,
They forged three anchors rare;
The hemp he did pull, and he shore the wool,
And the maidens brought their hair.

He twisted the brown hair for one strand,
The raven hair for another;
He twined the golden hair in a band
To bind the one to the other.

He took the cables of hemp and wool.
He took the cable of hair,
He hied him back to the roaring pool,
He cast the three anchors there.

The whirlpool roared, and the day went by,
And night came down on the sea;
But or ever the morning broke the sky
The hemp was broken in three.

The night it came down, the whirlpool it ran,
The wind it fiercely blew;
And or ever the second morning began
The wool it parted in two.

The storm it roared all day the third,
The whirlpool wallowed about,
The night came down like a wild black bird,
But the cable of hair held out.

Round and round with a giddy swing
Went the sea-king through the dark;
Round went the rope in the swivel-ring,
Round reeled the straining bark.

===Chinese===

丹麦的布列坎王子是海滩的主人，
也是波涛大海的主人；
既是海的主人又是陆的主人，
他本该放过那些少女！

他遇见一位金发的少女，
在海边信步游荡：
古时的少女总肯听人说话，
事后却深深懊悔。

他心生恶计，把她撇下，
扬帆渡海而去；
来见西群岛的领主：
把你的女儿给我，他说。

群岛的领主哈哈大笑，说：
唯有海中的君王
才配迎娶群岛的少女，
而你可算不上这样的人！

你且在那边的海中漩涡里
坚守三天三夜，
否则就掉转船头走你的路，
随那海岛少女去吧。

布列坎王子把他龙首的船头
掉向来时的大海：
女智者们，他说，现在告诉我
怎样在那漩涡里下锚。

用麻搓一条缆，用毛搓一条缆，
再用少女的头发搓一条，
快回到那咆哮的漩涡，
在那里安全下锚。

灰丘的铁匠们在圣诞前夜
会锻出三枚稀世的锚；
麻你自己种，毛你自己剪，
少女们自会把头发带来。

棕色的头发你要搓成一股，
乌黑的头发再搓一股；
金色的头发你要编成一条带，
把两股束在一处！

灰丘的铁匠们在圣诞前夜
锻出了三枚稀世的锚；
麻他种了，毛他剪了，
少女们也送来了头发。

他用棕发搓成一股，
用黑发搓成另一股；
他把金发编成一条带，
把两股束在一处。

他带上麻缆和毛缆，
带上那条发缆，
快快回到咆哮的漩涡，
在那里抛下三枚锚。

漩涡咆哮，白昼过去，
夜幕落向大海；
可不等清晨划破天空，
麻缆已断成三截。

第二夜降临，漩涡奔旋，
狂风猛烈地刮；
不等第二个早晨开始，
毛缆断成了两段。

第三天风暴终日咆哮，
漩涡翻滚倾侧，
夜像一只狂野的黑鸟压下来，
可那发缆撑住了。

一圈又一圈，晕眩地回旋，
海中之王在黑暗里打转；
绳在转环里跟着转，
绷紧的船身跟着打转。

===Original===

Prince Breacan he stood on his dragon prow,
A lantern in his hand:
Blest be the maidens of Denmark now,
By them shall Denmark stand!

He watched the rope through the tempest black
A lantern in his hold:
Out, out, alack! one strand will crack!
It is the strand of gold!

The third morn clear and calm came out:
No anchored ship was there!
The golden strand in the cable stout
Was not all of maidens’ hair.

===Chinese===

布列坎王子站在龙首的船头，
手里提着一盏灯：
愿丹麦的少女们如今蒙福，
丹麦要靠她们站立！

他透过漆黑的风暴盯着那绳，
一盏灯提在手中：
不好了，不好了，哎呀！一股要断！
断的是那股金发！

第三个清晨晴朗而平静地来到：
那里已没有抛锚的船！
那条结实的缆绳里的金股，
并不全是少女的头发。

## The Dead Hand / 死人的手
===Original===

The witch lady walked along the strand,
Heard a roaring of the sea,
On the edge of a pool saw a dead man’s hand,
Good thing for a witch lady!

Lightly she stepped across the rocks,
Came where the dead man lay:
Now pretty maid with your merry mocks,
Now I shall have my way!

On a finger shone a sapphire blue
In the heart of six rubies red:
Come back to me, my promise true,
Come back, my ring, she said.

She took the dead hand in the live,
And at the ring drew she;
The dead hand closed its fingers five,
And it held the witch lady.

She swore the storm was not her deed,
Dark spells she backward spoke;
If the dead man heard he took no heed,
But held like a cloven oak.

Deathly cold, crept up the tide,
Sure of her, made no haste;
Crept up to her knees, crept up each side,
Crept up to her wicked waist.

Over the blue sea sailed the bride
In her love’s own sailing ship,
And the witch she saw them across the tide
As it rose to her lying lip.

Oh, the heart of the dead and the hand of the dead
Are strong hasps they to hold!
Fled the true dove with the kite’s new love,
And left the false kite with the old.

===Chinese===

女巫沿着海滩行走，
听见大海咆哮，
在一泓池水边看见一只死人的手，
对女巫可是件好东西！

她轻盈地踏过礁石，
来到死人躺卧的地方：
爱嘲笑的漂亮姑娘啊，这回
我可要如愿以偿了！

一根手指上闪着一枚蓝宝石，
嵌在六颗红宝石的中央：
回到我这儿来，我信实的许诺，
回来吧，我的戒指，她说。

她用活手握住那只死手，
去撸那枚戒指；
死手的五指却一把攥紧，
把女巫牢牢攥住。

她赌咒说那场风暴不是她搞的，
又倒着念起黑咒语；
死人若听见也毫不理会，
只是像一棵裂不开的橡树那样攥着。

死一样的冷，潮水悄悄爬上来，
笃定了她，并不着急；
爬上她的膝，从两侧爬上来，
爬上她作恶的腰身。

蓝海上驶过了那位新娘，
乘着她爱人自己的帆船，
女巫隔着涨起的潮水望着他们，
潮水漫到了她说谎的唇边。

哦，死人的心和死人的手，
是最牢固的门闩！
真鸽子带着鸢的新爱飞走了，
把假鸢留给了旧爱。

## To Lady Noel Byron / 致诺埃尔·拜伦夫人
===Original===

Men sought, ambition’s thirst to slake,
The lost elixir old
Whose magic touch should instant make
The meaner metals gold.

A nobler alchymy is thine
Which love from pain doth press:
Gold in thy hand becomes divine,
Grows truth and tenderness.

===Chinese===

人们为解野心的渴，
苦苦寻索古老的灵药，
它魔法的一点，
能把贱金属变成黄金。

你却掌握着更高贵的炼金术，
从痛苦里榨出爱来：
黄金在你手中化为神圣，
长成真实与温柔。

## To Garibaldi, with a Book / 随书赠加里波第
===Original===

When at Philippi, he who would have freed
Great Rome from tyrants, for the season brief
That lay ’twixt him and battle, sought relief
From painful thoughts, he in a book did read,
That so the death of Portia might not breed
Unmanful thoughts, and cloud his mind with grief:
Brother of Brutus, of high hearts the chief,
When thou at length receiv’st thy heavenly meed,
And I have found my hoping not in vain,
Tell me my book has wiled away one pang
That out of some lone sacred memory sprang,
Or wrought an hour’s forgetfulness of pain,
And I shall rise, my heart brimful of gain,
And thank my God amid the golden clang.

===Chinese===

当年在腓立比，那位立志把伟大罗马
从暴君手中解放的人，在通往战役的
短暂间歇里，为了从痛苦的思绪中
得一点纾解，便捧读一本书，
免得波西亚的死唤起
非丈夫气概的念头，使他的心蒙上悲伤：
布鲁图斯的弟兄啊，高尚心灵的领袖，
当你终于领受你天上的赏赐，
而我也发现我的盼望没有落空，
请告诉我，我的书曾引开过一阵剧痛——
那痛从某个孤独神圣的记忆里涌出——
或曾换来一小时的忘痛，
我必将起来，心里盛满收获，
在金色的铿锵中感谢我的上帝。

## To the Same / 致同一位
===Original===

Dead, why defend thee, who in life
For thy worst foe hadst died;
Who, thy own name a word of strife,
Didst silent stand aside?

Grand in forgiveness, what to thee
The big world’s puny prate!
Or thy great heart hath ceased to be
Or loveth still its mate!

===Chinese===

死去的人啊，何必再为你辩护呢——
你在世时，连你最坏的仇人
你肯为他而死；
当你的名字成为争斗的词，
你只是静静站在一旁？

你在赦免中那样崇高，这大世界
琐碎的聒噪与你何干！
要么你那颗伟大的心已不复存在，
要么它仍在爱着它的同伴！

## The Holy Midnight / 神圣的午夜
===Original===

Ah, holy midnight of the soul,
When stars alone are high;
When winds are resting at their goal,
And sea-waves only sigh!

Ambition faints from out the will;
Asleep sad longing lies;
All hope of good, all fear of ill,
All need of action dies;

Because God is, and claims the life
He kindled in thy brain;
And thou in him, rapt far from strife,
Diest and liv’st again.

===Chinese===

啊，灵魂的神圣午夜，
只有星辰高悬；
风已停在它们的归宿，
只有海波还在叹息！

野心从意志里退去、昏沉；
伤心的渴望睡着；
对善的一切盼望、对恶的一切恐惧、
一切行动的必要，都死了；

因为上帝存在，并索回
他在你头脑里点燃的生命；
而你在他里面，远远超脱了争斗，
死去，又再活过来。

## Hard Times / 艰难时世
===Original===

I am weary, and very lonely,
And can but think﻿—think.
If there were some water only
That a spirit might drink﻿—drink,
And arise,
With light in the eyes
And a crown of hope on the brow,
To walk abroad in the strength of gladness,
Not sit in the house, benumbed with sadness﻿—
As now!

But, Lord, thy child will be sad﻿—
As sad as it pleases thee;
Will sit, not seeking to be glad,
Till thou bid sadness flee,
And, drawing near,
With thy good cheer
Awake thy life in me.

===Chinese===

我疲倦，而且非常孤独，
只能想——想。
倘若有一处水泉，
让灵可以喝——喝，
然后起来，
眼里带着光，
额头戴着盼望的冠冕，
凭着欢喜的力量到外面行走，
而不是坐在屋里，被悲伤冻僵——
像现在这样！

可是主啊，你的孩子甘愿忧伤——
忧伤到你喜悦的程度；
愿意坐着，不刻意求乐，
直到你吩咐忧伤逃去，
并且临近，
带着你的好意，
在你里面唤醒我的生命。

## Summer Song / 夏歌
===Original===

Murmuring, ’twixt a murmur and moan,
Many a tune in a single tone,
For every ear with a secret true﻿—
The sea-shell wants to whisper to you.”

“Yes﻿—I hear it﻿—far and faint,
Like thin-drawn prayer of drowsy saint;
Like the muffled sounds of a summer rain;
Like the wash of dreams in a weary brain.”

“By smiling lip and fixed eye,
You are hearing a song within the sigh:
The murmurer has many a lovely phrase﻿—
Tell me, darling, the words it says.”

“I hear a wind on a boatless main
Sigh like the last of a vanishing pain;
On the dreaming waters dreams the moon﻿—
But I hear no words in the doubtful tune.”

“If it tell thee not that I love thee well,
’Tis a senseless, wrinkled, ill-curved shell:
If it be not of love, why sigh or sing?
’Tis a common, mechanical, stupid thing!”

“It murmurs, it whispers, with prophet voice
Of a peace that comes, of a sealed choice;
It says not a word of your love to me,
But it tells me I love you eternally.”

===Chinese===

低吟着，在低吟与叹息之间，
一个音调里藏着许多曲子，
为每只耳朵藏一句真言——
这海贝想对你低语。」

「是的——我听见了——遥远而微弱，
像困倦圣徒拉得又细又长的祷告；
像一场夏日细雨那被蒙住的声音；
像梦在疲惫头脑里轻轻的淘洗。」

「凭你微笑的唇和专注的眼睛，
你在叹息里听出了一支歌：
这低语者有许多可爱的乐句——
告诉我，亲爱的，它说的是什么。」

「我听见一片风吹过无船的大海，
叹息得像一阵正在消退的疼痛的最后余音；
月亮在梦的水面上做着梦——
可在这可疑的调子里，我听不出字句。」

「它若不告诉你我爱你爱得深，
它就是一只没知觉、皱巴巴、弧度糟糕的贝壳：
若不是讲爱，它何必叹息或歌唱？
那它就只是一件平庸、机械、愚蠢的东西！」

「它低吟着，它低语着，用先知的声音
说一种将要来临的平安、一个封好的拣选；
它一字不提你对我的爱，
却告诉我：我永远地爱你。」

## Picture Songs / 画中歌
===Original===

I

A pale green sky is gleaming;
The steely stars are few;
The moorland pond is steaming
A mist of gray and blue.

Along the pathway lonely
My horse is walking slow;
Three living creatures only,
He, I, and a home-bound crow!

The moon is hardly shaping
Her circle in the fog;
A dumb stream is escaping
Its prison in the bog.

But in my heart are ringing
Tones of a lofty song;
A voice that I know, is singing,
And my heart all night must long.

II

Over a shining land﻿—
Once such a land I knew﻿—
Over its sea, by a soft wind fanned,
The sky is all white and blue.

The waves are kissing the shores,
Murmuring love and for ever;
A boat gleams green, and its timeful oars
Flash out of the level river.

Oh to be there with thee
And the sun, on wet sands, my love!
With the shining river, the sparkling sea,
And the radiant sky above!

III

The autumn winds are sighing
Over land and sea;
The autumn woods are dying
Over hill and lea;
And my heart is sighing, dying,
Maiden, for thee.

The autumn clouds are flying
Homeless over me;
The nestless birds are crying
In the naked tree;
And my heart is flying, crying,
Maiden, to thee.

The autumn sea is crawling
Up the chilly shore;
The thin-voiced firs are calling
Ghostily evermore:
Maiden, maiden! I am falling
Dead at thy door.

IV

The waters are rising and flowing
Over the weedy stone﻿—
Over it, over it going:
It is never gone.

Waves upon waves of weeping
Went over the ancient pain;
Glad waves go over it leaping﻿—
Still it rises again!

===Chinese===

一

一片淡绿的天在闪光；
钢色的星寥寥无几；
荒原的池塘蒸腾着
一缕灰蓝的雾。

沿着那条寂寞的小路，
我的马缓缓走着；
只有三个活物，
它，我，和一只归巢的乌鸦！

月亮在雾里
勉强圈出她的圆；
一条哑默的溪流正
逃出泥沼的囚笼。

但在我心里回响着
一支崇高的歌的音调；
一个我认得的声音在歌唱，
我的心必须整夜渴慕。

二

在一片闪亮的土地上——
我曾认识这样一片土地——
在它的海上，软风轻扇，
天空全是白色与蔚蓝。

波涛亲吻着海岸，
低语着爱、低语着永远；
一叶小船泛着绿光，它应时的桨
从平镜的河面闪闪出水。

哦，多想与你在那里，
和太阳，在湿润的沙滩上，我的爱人！
有闪亮的河流、粼粼的大海，
还有头顶那明光熠熠的天空！

三

秋风叹息着
掠过陆地和海洋；
秋天的树林凋零着
漫过山丘和草场；
而我的心也在叹息、凋零，
姑娘啊，为了你。

秋云飞着，
无家可归，从我头顶掠过；
无巢的鸟儿啼着，
在光秃的树上；
而我的心也在飞着、啼着，
姑娘啊，向你飞去。

秋天的海爬行着
爬上清冷的海岸；
细嗓的杉树呼喊着，
鬼气森森，永不停歇：
姑娘啊，姑娘！我正倒下，
死在你的门前。

四

水涨起来，流过去，
漫过那生苔的石头——
一遍遍漫过它，流过它：
它却从不曾被带走。

哀哭的浪，一浪接一浪，
漫过那古老的疼痛；
欢欣的浪跳跃着漫过它——
它仍旧一次次立起！

## A Dream Song / 一支梦之歌
===Original===

I dreamed of a song﻿—I heard it sung;
In the ear of my soul its strange notes rung.
What were its words I could not tell,
Only the voice I heard right well,
For its tones unearthly my spirit bound
In a calm delirium of mystic sound﻿—
Held me floating, alone and high,
Placeless and silent, drinking my fill
Of dews that from cloudless skies distil
On desert places that thirst and sigh.
’Twas a woman’s voice, deep calling to deep,
Rousing old echoes that all day sleep
In cavern and solitude, each apart,
Here and there in the waiting heart;﻿—
A voice with a wild melodious cry
Reaching and longing afar and high.
Sorrowful triumph, and hopeful strife,
Gainful death, and new-born life,
Thrilled in each note of the prophet-song.
In my heart it said: O Lord, how long
Shall we groan and travail and faint and pray,
Ere thy lovely kingdom bring the day!

1842.

===Chinese===

我梦见一支歌——我听见它被唱起；
它奇异的音符在我灵魂的耳中回响。
它唱的什么词我听不清，
只把那声音听得真真切切，
因为它非尘世的音调把我的灵缚进
一种神秘音响的静稳迷醉里——
托着我漂浮，孤零零地高高漂浮，
没有方位，没有声息，畅饮着
从无云的天空滴落到
那些又渴又叹的荒漠之地的露。
那是一个女人的声音，深渊呼唤着深渊，
唤醒古老的回声——它们整日沉睡
在洞穴与孤寂里，各自分开，
东一处西一处，睡在等候的心中；——
一个声音，带着一声狂野而悦耳的呼号，
伸展着、渴慕着，向远方、向高处。
忧伤的凯旋，怀望的争斗，
有收获的死，新生的生命，
在先知之歌的每个音符里颤动。
它在我心里说：哦主啊，还要多久
我们才不再呻吟、劬劳、昏厥、祷告，
你可爱的国度才迎来那日！

一八四二年。

## A Manchester Poem / 一首曼彻斯特的诗
===Original===

’Tis a poor drizzly morning, dark and sad.
The cloud has fallen, and filled with fold on fold
The chimneyed city; and the smoke is caught,
And spreads diluted in the cloud, and sinks,
A black precipitate, on miry streets.
And faces gray glide through the darkened fog.

Slave engines utter again their ugly growl,
And soon the iron bands and blocks of stone
That prison them to their task, will strain and quiver
Until the city tremble. The clamour of bells,
Importunate, keeps calling pale-faced forms
To gather and feed those Samsons’ groaning strength
With labour; and among the many come
A man and woman﻿—the woman with her gown
Drawn over her head, the man with bended neck
Submissive to the rain. Amid the jar,
And clash, and shudder of the awful force,
They enter and part﻿—each to a different task,
But each a soul of knowledge to brute force,
Working a will through the organized whole
Of cranks and belts and levers, pinions and screws
Wherewith small man has eked his body out,
And made himself a mighty, weary giant.
In labour close they pass the murky day,
’Mid floating dust of swift-revolving wheels,
And filmy spoil of quick contorted threads,
Which weave a sultry chaos all about;
Until, at length, old darkness, swelling slow
Up from the caves of night to make an end,
Chokes in its tide the clanking of the looms,
The monster-engines, and the flying gear.
’Tis Earth that draws her curtains, and calls home
Her little ones, and sets her down to nurse
Her tired children﻿—like a mother-ghost
With her neglected darlings in the dark.
So out they walk, with sense of glad release,
And home﻿—to a dreary place! Unfinished walls,
Earth-heaps, and broken bricks, and muddy pools
Lie round it like a rampart against the spring,
The summer, and all sieges of the year.

===Chinese===

这是一个凄冷的毛毛雨的早晨，昏暗而愁惨。
云塌了下来，一层又一层地
填满这座烟囱林立的城市；烟被兜住，
在云里散成稀薄的一片，又沉淀
成黑色的沉积，落在泥泞的街上。
灰色的面孔在变暗的雾里滑动。

奴隶般的机器重新发出丑陋的咆哮，
很快，那囚禁它们服劳役的
铁箍和石块就要绷紧、颤抖，
直到全城震颤。钟声急切地
催着一张张苍白的身影前来，
聚集起来，用劳作喂养
那些参孙呻吟的力气；在许多人中间
走来一个男人和一个女人——女人把外裙
拉起来罩在头上，男人缩着脖子
顺从地淋着雨。在巨力的
震响、碰撞与战栗之中，
他们进门，分开——各自去往不同的活计，
但每一个都是蛮力面前的一个有知的灵魂，
借曲轴、皮带、杠杆、齿轮和螺杆
组成的整体施行一个意志，
人以此扩出自己的身躯，
把自己变成一个强大的、疲惫的巨人。
他们在劳作中挨过晦暗的一天，
四围是飞旋轮子扬起的浮尘，
和疾速扭卷的纱线拉出的蛛网般的废絮，
织成一片闷热的混沌；
直到最后，老黑暗从夜的洞穴
缓缓涨起，要给这一切收场，
用它的潮水哽住织机的铿锵、
那些怪物般的机器和飞转的齿轮。
这是大地拉上她的帐幔，唤她的
小家伙们回家，坐下来哺乳
她疲倦的儿女——像一位幽灵母亲，
在黑暗中守着她被忽略的宝贝。
于是他们走出来，怀着解脱的欢喜，
回家——回到一个凄凉的地方！残墙、
土堆、碎砖和泥泞的水洼
围在四周，像一道对抗春天、
对抗夏天、对抗一年所有围攻的壁垒。

===Original===

But, Lo, the dark has opened an eye of fire!
The room reveals a temple, witnessed by signs
Seen in the ancient place! Lo, here is light,
Yea, burning fire, with darkness on its skirts;
Pure water, ready to baptize; and bread;
And in the twilight edges of the light,
A book; and, for the cunning-woven veil,
Their faces﻿—hiding God’s own holiest place!
Even their bed figures the would-be grave
Where One arose triumphant, slept no more!
So at their altar-table they sit down
To eat their Eucharist; for, to the heart
That reads the live will in the dead command,
He is the bread, yea, all of every meal.
But as, in weary rest, they silent sit,
They gradually grow aware of light
That overcomes their lamp, and, through the blind,
Casts from the window-frame two shadow-glooms
That make a cross of darkness on the white.
The woman rises, eagerly looks out:
Lo, some fair wind has mown the earth-sprung fog,
And, far aloft, the white exultant moon,
From her blue window, curtained all with white,
Looks greeting them﻿—God’s creatures they and she!
Smiling she turns; he understands the smile:
To-morrow will be fair﻿—as holy, fair!
And lying down, in sleep they die till morn,
While through their night throb low aurora-gleams
Of resurrection and the coming dawn.
They wake: ’tis Sunday. Still the moon is there,
But thin and ghostly﻿—clothed upon with light,
As if, while they were sleeping, she had died.
They dress themselves, like priests, in clean attire,
And, through their lowly door, enter God’s room.
The sun is up, the emblem on his shield.
One side the street, the windows all are moons
To light the other side that lies in shade.
See, down the sun-side, an old woman come
In a red cloak that makes the whole street glad!
A long-belated autumn-flower she seems,
Dazed by the rushing of the new-born life
Up hidden stairs to see the calling sun,
But in her cloak and smile they know the spring,
And haste to meet her through slow dissolving streets
Widening to larger glimmers of growing green.
Oh, far away the streets repel the spring!
Yet every stone in the dull pavement shares
The life that thrills anew the outworn earth,
A right Bethesda angel﻿—for all, not some!

===Chinese===

可是看哪，黑暗睁开了一只火的眼睛！
这房间显出一座殿宇，有古代圣所
得见过的表记为证！看，这里有光，
是啊，燃烧的火，边缘镶着黑暗；
有清水，可以施洗；有饼；
在光的微明的边界上，
有一本书；而那巧织的帷幔，
则是他们自己的脸——遮着上帝至圣的所在！
连他们的床也预示着那座心愿中的坟墓，
曾有一位从那里得胜复活，不再睡去！
于是他们在祭坛般的桌旁坐下，
吃他们的圣餐；因为对那颗
能在死的诫命里读出活的旨意的心，
他就是那饼，是啊，每一餐的全部。
但当他们疲惫地歇息、默默坐着，
渐渐察觉一道盖过灯火的光，透过百叶，
把窗框的两道影投在白墙上，
组成一个黑暗的十字。
女人站起来，急切地向外望：
看哪，一阵好风割倒了地上生起的雾，
高天之上，那白色的、得胜的月亮，
从她蓝色的窗里，垂着白色的帐，
向他们致意——她和他们同是上帝的造物！
她微笑着转身；他懂得那微笑：
明天会是晴天——像圣日一样，晴好！
他们躺下，在睡眠里死去直到清晨，
而整夜有复活与将至的黎明
那极光的微芒在他们夜里低低搏动。
他们醒来：是礼拜天。月亮还在，
却已稀薄如幽灵——披着光，
仿佛趁他们睡着，她死过了一遭。
他们像祭司一样穿上洁净的衣裳，
穿过他们低矮的门，走进上帝的房间。
太阳升起来了，盾牌上带着他的徽记。
街道的一侧，窗玻璃全成了月亮，
照亮躺在阴影里的另一侧。
看，顺着向阳的一边，走来一位老妇人，
披一件红斗篷，喜坏了整条街！
她像一朵迟开太久的秋花，
被涌上新生命的热流弄得目眩——
那生命正爬上隐蔽的楼梯去望召唤的太阳，
而在她的斗篷和微笑里，他们认出了春天，
急忙穿过缓缓消融的街道去迎她，
街道渐渐开阔，泛出越来越大的新绿微光。
哦，遥远的街道还在排斥春天！
但沉闷路面上每一块石头，都分享着
再次震彻这疲惫大地的生命，
是一位真正的毕士大天使——为一切人，不只一些人！

===Original===

A street unfinished leads them forth at length
Where green fields bask, and hedgerow trees, apart,
Stand waiting in the air as for some good,
And the sky is broad and blue﻿—and there is all!
No peaceful river meditates along
The weary flat to the less level sea!
No forest brown, on pillared stems, its boughs
Meeting in gothic arches, bears aloft
A groined vault, fretted with tremulous leaves!
No mountains lift their snows, and send their brooks
Down babbling with the news of silent things!
But love itself is commonest of all,
And loveliest of all, in all the worlds!
And he that hath not forest, brook, or hill,
Must learn to read aright what commoner books
Unfold before him. If ocean solitudes﻿—
Then darkness dashed with glory, infinite shades,
And misty minglings of the sea and sky.
If only fields﻿—the humble man of heart
Will revel in the grass beneath his foot,
And from the lea lift his glad eye to heaven,
God’s palette, where his careless painter-hand
Sweeps comet-clouds that net the gazing soul;
Streaks endless stairs, and blots half-sculptured blocks;
Curves filmy pallors; heaps huge mountain-crags;
Nor touches where it leaves not beauty’s mark.
To them the sun and air are feast enough,
As through field-paths and lanes they slowly walk;
But sometimes, on the far horizon dim
A veil is lifted, and they spy the hills,
Cloudlike and faint, yet sharp against the sky;
Then wakes an unknown want, which asks and looks
As for some thing forgot﻿—loved long ago,
But on the hither verge of childhood dropt:
’Tis but home-sickness roused in the soul by Spring!
Fresh birth and eager growth, reviving life,
Which is because it would be, fill the world;
The very light is new-born with the grass;
The stones themselves are warm; the brown earth swells,
Filled, sponge-like, with dark beams, which nestle close
And brood unseen and shy, and potent warm
In every little corner, nest, and crack
Where buried lurks a blind and sleepy seed
Waiting the touch of the finger of the sun.
The mossy stems and boughs, where yet no life
Oozes exuberant in brown and green,
Are clad in golden splendours, crossed and lined
With shuttle-shadows weaving lovely change.
Through the tree-tops the west wind rushing goes,
Calling and rousing the dull sap within:
The fine jar down the stem sinks tremulous,
From airy root thrilling to earthy branch.

===Chinese===

一条未修完的街终于把他们引出城外，
那里绿色的田野沐着阳光，篱畔的树木
各自伫立，在空气里像在等候什么好事，
天空辽阔湛蓝——而这便是一切！
没有安宁的河流沿着疲惫的平川
冥想着流向更低平的海！
没有棕色的森林，在柱式的树干上
把枝桠聚成哥特的尖拱，高擎
一道肋拱的穹窿，颤动的叶作它的花格！
没有群山举起积雪、派出溪流
潺潺地把静物的消息捎下山来！
但爱本身，在一切世界里，
都是最寻常、也是最可爱的！
而没有森林、溪流和山冈的人，
就必须学会好好读那些更平常的书，
它们在他面前展开。若是海洋的幽寂——
那就是掺着荣耀的黑暗，无限的层次，
海与天蒙蒙的交融。
若只有田野——心灵谦卑的人
也会痴迷于脚下的草，
从草场抬起欢喜的眼望天，
那是上帝的调色盘，他随手挥洒的画笔
扫出网住凝望之魂的彗星云；
勾出无尽的阶梯，点出半雕的巨石；
弯出膜蒙的苍白；堆出巍峨的岩峰；
凡是笔触所到，无不留下美的印记。
对他们来说，阳光和空气已是足够的盛宴，
当他们沿着田间小径和巷子缓缓步行；
但有时，在远处朦胧的地平线上，
一道帷幔掀起，他们窥见了群山，
云一般缥缈，却在天幕上轮廓分明；
于是醒了一种无名的渴望，它张望、它询问，
像在找一件被遗忘的东西——很久以前爱过的，
却在童年的门槛上失落了：
那不过是春天在灵魂里唤醒的乡愁！
新鲜的诞生和急切的生长，复苏的生命，
因为「愿在」而「正在」的存在，充满世界；
连光也随青草一同新生；
石头自己也暖了；褐色的大地鼓胀，
像海绵一样吸满暗色的光线，它们偎依着，
不见而羞怯地伏着，温热而有力量，
在每一个小小的角落、缝隙和巢穴，
那里潜伏着一粒又盲又倦的种子，
等候太阳手指的触摸。
生苔的树干和枝条，虽然还没有
生命从里面渗涌出棕与绿，
却已披上金色的华彩，梭子般的影子
在上面穿来穿去，织出可爱的变幻。
西风穿过树梢疾掠而去，
呼唤并唤醒树里沉闷的树液：
那细微的震颤顺着树干沉落，
从空中的根直颤到入土的枝。

===Original===

And though as yet no buddy baby dots
Sparkle the darkness of the hedgerow twigs,
The smoke-dried bark appears to spread and swell
In the soft nurture of the warm light-bath.
The sun had left behind him the keystone
Of his low arch half-way when they turned home,
Filled with pure air, and light, and operant spring:
Back, like the bees, they went to their dark house
To store their innocent spoil in honeyed thought.

But on their way, crossing a field, they chanced
Upon a spot where once had been a home,
And roots of walls still peered out, grown with moss.
’Twas a dead cottage, mouldered quite, where yet
Lay the old shadow of a vanished care;
The little garden’s blunt, half-blotted map
Was yet discernible by thinner grass
Upon the walks. There, in the midst of dry
Bushes, dead flowers, rampant, uncomely weeds,
A single snowdrop drooped its snowy drop,
The lonely remnant of a family
That in the garden dwelt about the home﻿—
Reviving with the spring when home was gone:
They see; its spiritual counterpart
Wakes up and blossoms white in their meek souls﻿—
A longing, patient, waiting hopefulness,
The snowdrop of the heart; a heavenly child,
That, pale with the earthly cold, hangs its fair head
As it had nought to say ’gainst any world;
While they in whom it dwells, nor knows itself,
Inherit in their meekness all the worlds.

I love thee, flower, as a slow lingerer
Upon the verge of my humanity.
Lo, on thine inner leaves and in thy heart
The loveliest green, acknowledging the grass﻿—
White-minded memory of lowly friends!
But almost more I love thee for the earth
Which clings to thy transfigured radiancy,
Uplifted with thee from thine abandoned grave;
Say rather the soiling of thy garments pure
Upon thy road into the light and air,
The heaven of thy new birth. Some gentle rain
Will one day wash thee white, and send the earth
Back to the earth; but, sweet friend, while it clings,
I love the cognizance of our family.

===Chinese===

虽然篱枝的黑暗里还没有蓓蕾的
小点点在闪烁，被烟熏干的树皮
却仿佛在温暖光浴的柔养里
舒展、鼓胀。
他们转身回家时，太阳已把他低拱的
拱顶石落到了半途；
他们装满了纯净的空气、光和
运行的春天：像蜜蜂一样，他们回到
自己幽暗的家，把清白的斩获
酿成蜜一般的思想。

但归途中，穿过一片田地，他们偶然
撞见一个地方，那里曾有过一个家，
墙根还探出土来，覆满了苔。
那是一间死去的村舍，早已朽尽，
却还躺着一种消失了的操劳的旧影；
小花园那张模糊了一半的钝地图，
还能凭步道上较稀的草辨认出来。
就在那里，在干枯的灌木、死花
和疯长而丑陋的野草中间，
一株雪花莲垂着它雪白的小钟，
是一个家族孤独的遗孤——
那个家族曾在这个家四围的园中居住——
家没了，它却随春天一同复活：
他们看见了；它属灵的对应物
便在他们温静的灵魂里醒来，开出白花——
一种渴慕的、忍耐的、等候的盼望，
心的雪花莲；一个天上的孩子，
被尘世的寒冷冻得苍白，垂着美丽的头，
仿佛对任何世界都无可指摘；
而怀着它的这些人，它自己却不自知，
在温静里承受了所有的世界。

我爱你，花，爱你这流连在我
人性边缘上的迟缓的旅人。
看哪，在你内层的叶瓣和你的心里，
有最可爱的绿，向青草致意——
那是对卑微朋友的一颗白色心肠的记忆！
但我几乎更爱你，为了那点泥土，
它粘在你变形的辉光上，
随你一起从你废弃的坟里被举起；
或者不如说，那是你纯净的衣袍
在通往光与空气的路上、在你新生
的天国里沾上的尘污。
某场温柔的雨终有一天会把你洗白，
把泥土送还给泥土；可是甜美的朋友啊，趁它还粘着，
我爱这我们同族的印记。

===Original===

With careful hands uprooting it, they bore
The little plant a willing captive home﻿—
Fearless of dark abode, because secure
In its own tale of light. As once of old
The angel of the annunciation shone,
Bearing all heaven into a common house,
It brings in with it field and sky and air.
A pot of mould its one poor tie to earth,
Its heaven an ell of blue ’twixt chimney-tops,
Its world the priests of that small temple-room,
It takes its prophet-place with fire and book,
Type of primeval spring, whose mighty arc
Hath not yet drawn the summer up the sky.
At night, when the dark shadow of the cross
Will enter, clothed in moonlight, still and wan
Like a pale mourner at its foot the flower
Will, drooping, wait the dawn. Then the dark bird
Which holds breast-caged the secret of the sun,
And therefore hangs himself a prisoner caged,
Will break into its song﻿—Lo, God is light!

Weary and hopeful, to their sleep they go;
And all night long the snowdrop glimmers white
Thinning the dark, unknowing it, and unseen.

---

Out of my verse I woke, and saw my room,
My precious books, the cherub-forms above,
And rose, and walked abroad, and sought the woods;
And roving odours met me on my way.
I entered Nature’s church, a shimmering vault
Of boughs, and clouded leaves﻿—filmy and pale
Betwixt me and the sun, while at my feet
Their shadows, dark and seeming solid, lay
Like tombstones o’er the vanished flowers of Spring.
The place was silent, save for the broken song
Of some Memnonian, glory-stricken bird
That burst into a carol and was still;
It was not lonely: golden beetles crept,
Green goblins, in the roots; and squirrel things
Ran, wild as cherubs, through the tracery;
And here and yonder a flaky butterfly
Was doubting in the air, scarlet and blue.
But ’twixt my heart and summer’s perfect grace,
Drove a dividing wedge, and far away
It seemed, like voice heard loud yet far away
By one who, waking half, soon sleeps outright:﻿—
Where was the snowdrop? where the flower of hope?
In me the spring was throbbing; round me lay
Resting fulfilled, the odour-breathing summer!
My heart heaved swelling like a prisoned bud,
And summer crushed it with its weight of light!

===Chinese===

他们用细致的双手把它连根挖起，
把这小小的植株当作甘愿的俘虏带回家——
它不怕幽暗的居所，因为它自己
藏着光的故事，足够安稳。正如当年
传报喜讯的天使发光，
把整个天堂带进一座平常的屋宇，
它也把田野、天空和空气一并带来。
一盆泥土是它与大地的唯一可怜的维系，
它的一爿天空是烟囱之间的一线蓝，
它的世界是那间小小殿宇的祭司们，
它带着火与书就位于它的先知之位，
是太初春天的表记，那春天的大弧
还没有把夏天拉上天空。
夜里，当十字架的暗影进来，
披着月光，静默而苍白，
像一个哀悼者立在它的脚前，那花
将垂着头等候黎明。于是那只黑色的鸟——
它胸中锁着太阳的秘密，
所以把自己囚在笼里——
将放声唱起来：看哪，上帝就是光！

他们带着疲惫与盼望，去睡了；
整夜雪花莲闪着白，
不知不觉地稀释着黑暗，也无人看见。

---

我从我的诗里醒来，看见我的房间、
我珍贵的书、上方那些小天使的形影，
便起身出门，走向树林；
游荡的香气在路上迎接我。
我走进大自然的教堂，一座微光闪烁的
枝桠的穹窿，和蒙着云翳的叶——
在我与太阳之间如膜如纱，
而我的脚边躺着它们浓黑而似乎坚实的影，
像春天的消逝之花上面的墓碑。
这地方寂静，只有一只荣耀击中的
门农式的鸟断续的歌，
迸出一串欢啭，又归于沉静；
它并不孤独：金色的甲虫在根间爬行，
像绿色的小精怪；松鼠一样的小东西
狂野如小天使，在枝格间窜跳；
这里那里，一只蝶翅斑斓的蝴蝶
在半空中绯红与蓝地犹疑。
但在我的心与夏天完全的恩典之间，
楔进了一道劈分，它显得那样遥远，
像一个人半醒时听见的声音，响亮却很远，
转眼又沉沉睡去：——
雪花莲在哪里？盼望之花在哪里？
我里面，春天在搏动；我四周，
躺着安息而圆满的、吐着香气的夏天！
我的心像一枚囚禁的花蕾那样鼓胀，
夏天用它光的重压把它压疼！

===Original===

Winter is full of stings and sharp reproofs,
Healthsome, not hurtful, but yet hurting sore;
Summer is too complete for growing hearts﻿—
Too idle its noons, its morns too triumphing,
Too full of slumberous dreams its dusky eves;
Autumn is full of ripeness and the grave;
We need a broken season, where the cloud
Is ruffled into glory, and the dark
Falls rainful o’er the sunset; need a world
Whose shadows ever point away from it;
A scheme of cones abrupt, and flattened spheres,
And circles cut, and perfect laws the while
That marvellous imperfection ever points
To higher perfectness than heart can think;
Therefore to us, a flower of harassed Spring,
Crocus, or primrose, or anemone,
Is lovely as was never rosiest rose;
A heath-bell on a waste, lonely and dry,
Says more than lily, stately in breathing white;
A window through a vaulted roof of rain
Lets in a light that comes from farther away,
And, sinking deeper, spreads a finer joy
Than cloudless noon-tide splendorous o’er the world:
Man seeks a better home than Paradise;
Therefore high hope is more than deepest joy,
A disappointment better than a feast,
And the first daisy on a wind-swept lea
Dearer than Eden-groves with rivers four.

===Chinese===

冬天满是芒刺和尖刻的责备，
有益健康，并不伤害，却疼得厉害；
夏天对成长中的心来说太完整了——
它的正午太闲适，它的清晨太凯旋，
它昏暗的黄昏太多催眠的梦；
秋天满是成熟和坟墓；
我们需要一个残缺的季节，那里的云
被揉皱成荣耀，那里的黑暗
携着雨落在日落上；需要一个
影子永远指向自身之外的世界；
需要一个骤然的锥体、压扁的球、
被裁切的圆的图式，却始终有完全的法则，
那奇妙的残缺永远指向
比心所能想的更高的完全；
因此对我们来说，一朵饱经风霜的春花，
番红花、报春花或银莲花，
比最艳的玫瑰更可爱，从来如此；
荒原上一朵孤干的石楠花，
比端庄吐白的百合说得更多；
一场雨的拱顶上的一扇小窗，
漏进来的光来自更远的地方，
沉得更深，铺开比无云的正午
辉煌普照更细致的欢喜：
人寻求一个比乐园更好的家；
所以崇高的盼望胜过最深的喜乐，
一场失望胜过一场盛宴，
而风吹草场上的第一朵雏菊，
比四条大河环绕的伊甸林更珍贵。

## Riddles / 谜语
===Original===

I

I have only one foot, but thousands of toes;
My one foot stands well, but never goes;
I’ve a good many arms, if you count them all,
But hundreds of fingers, large and small;
From the ends of my fingers my beauty grows;
I breathe with my hair, and I drink with my toes;
I grow bigger and bigger about the waist
Although I am always very tight laced;
None e’er saw me eat﻿—I’ve no mouth to bite!
Yet I eat all day, and digest all night.
In the summer, with song I shake and quiver,
But in winter I fast and groan and shiver.

II

There is a plough that hath no share,
Only a coulter that parteth fair;
But the ridges they rise
To a terrible size
Or ever the coulter comes near to tear:
The horses and ridges fierce battle make;
The horses are safe, but the plough may break.

Seed cast in its furrows, or green or sear,
Will lift to the sun neither blade nor ear:
Down it drops plumb
Where no spring-times come,
Nor needeth it any harrowing gear;
Wheat nor poppy nor blade has been found
Able to grow on the naked ground.

For My Grandchild

III

Who is it that sleeps like a top all night,
And wakes in the morning so fresh and bright
That he breaks his bed as he gets up,
And leaves it smashed like a china cup?

IV

I’ve a very long nose, but what of that?
It is not too long to lie on a mat!

I have very big jaws, but never get fat:
I don’t go to church, and I’m not a church rat!

I’ve a mouth in my middle my food goes in at,
Just like a skate’s﻿—that’s a fish that’s a flat.

In summer I’m seldom able to breathe,
But when winter his blades in ice doth sheathe

I swell my one lung, I look big and I puff,
And I sometimes hiss.﻿—There, that’s enough!

===Chinese===

一

我只有一只脚，却有成千的脚趾；
我的独脚站得稳稳，却从不走动；
要说手臂嘛，我也有不少，
可手指却有成百，有大也有小；
我的美从指尖上生长出来；
我用头发呼吸，用脚趾喝水；
我的腰身越长越粗，
虽然我总是勒得紧紧的；
没人见我吃东西——我没有嘴咬东西！
可我整天吃，整夜消化。
夏天，我随着歌声摇曳颤动，
冬天，我却斋戒、呻吟、发抖。

二

有一张犁，没有犁铧，
只有一把犁刀，分垄分得公正；
可那些垄越隆越高，
高得吓人，
不等犁刀近前来破开；
马和垄展开恶战；
马安然无恙，犁却可能折断。

播进它沟里的种子，无论青绿还是枯干，
都长不出向太阳的叶，也长不出穗：
它笔直地坠落
到一个没有春天的地方，
也不需要任何耙地的农具；
小麦、罂粟还是草叶，从来没有一样
能在那光秃的地面上生长。

给我的孙儿

三

是谁整夜睡得像只陀螺，
早晨醒来又那样精神、那样明亮，
一起身就把床给压垮，
把它摔得像一只瓷杯那样粉碎？

四

我的鼻子很长，可那又怎样？
再长也不妨碍我趴在垫子上！

我的嘴巴很大，可从来不发胖：
我不上教堂，也不是教堂的老鼠！

我肚子正中有一张嘴，食物就从那儿进，
就像鳐鱼那样——那是一种扁扁的鱼。

夏天我几乎喘不上气，
可一到冬天，把它的刀刃插进冰里，
我就鼓起我唯一的肺，装得大大的，喷着气，
有时还要嘶嘶作响。——好了，就这些！

## Baby / 宝宝
===Original===

Where did you come from, baby dear?
Out of the everywhere into here.

Where did you get those eyes so blue?
Out of the sky as I came through.

What makes the light in them sparkle and spin?
Some of the starry twinkles left in.

Where did you get that little tear?
I found it waiting when I got here.

What makes your forehead so smooth and high?
A soft hand stroked it as I went by.

What makes your cheek like a warm white rose?
I saw something better than any one knows.

Whence that three-cornered smile of bliss?
Three angels gave me at once a kiss.

Where did you get this pearly ear?
God spoke, and it came out to hear.

Where did you get those arms and hands?
Love made itself into bonds and bands.

Feet, whence did you come, you darling things?
From the same box as the cherubs’ wings.

How did they all just come to be you?
God thought about me, and so I grew.

But how did you come to us, you dear?
God thought about you, and so I am here.

===Chinese===

你是从哪里来的，亲爱的宝宝？
从「处处」来到「这里」。

你那双眼睛怎么这样蓝？
我来的时候一路从天空里捡的。

眼睛里的光为什么又闪又转？
留了些星星的眨眼在里面。

你那颗小小的泪珠是哪来的？
我到这里时它已经等在那儿了。

你的额头怎么这样光洁高阔？
一只柔软的手在我经过时抚过它。

你的脸颊怎么像一朵温热的白玫瑰？
我看见了比谁知道的都更好的东西。

那个三角形的幸福微笑从哪儿来？
三位天使同时给了我一个吻。

这只珍珠般的小耳朵是哪来的？
上帝说话，它就出来听。

这双胳膊和小手是哪来的？
爱把自己变成了链环和纽带。

小脚呀，你们从哪儿来，可爱的小东西？
和天使的翅膀用的是同一只匣子。

这一切怎么恰好就成了你？
上帝想着我，我就长大了。

可你是怎么来到我们这里的，小亲亲？
上帝想着你，我就到这里来了。

## Up and Down / 上与下
===Original===

The sun is gone down
And the moon’s in the sky
But the sun will come up
And the moon be laid by.

The flower is asleep.
But it is not dead,
When the morning shines
It will lift its head.

When winter comes
It will die! No, no,
It will only hide
From the frost and snow.

Sure is the summer,
Sure is the sun;
The night and the winter
Away they run.

===Chinese===

太阳落了山，
月亮升上天；
可太阳还会升上来，
月亮就得靠一边。

花儿睡着了，
可它没有死；
等晨光一亮，
它就抬起头。

冬天来了
它会死！不，不，
它只是躲起来，
避开霜和雪。

夏天笃定要来，
太阳笃定回来；
黑夜呀冬天呀，
撒腿跑开。

## Up in the Tree / 在树上
===Original===

What would you see, if I took you up
My little aerie-stair?
You would see the sky like a clear blue cup
Turned upside down in the air.

What would you do, up my aerie-stair
In my little nest on the tree?
With cry upon cry you would ripple the air
To get at what you would see.

And what would you reach in the top of the tree
To still your grasping grief?
Not a star would you clutch of all you would see,
You would gather just one green leaf.

But when you had lost your greedy grief,
Content to see from afar,
Your hand it would hold a withering leaf,
But your heart a shining star.

===Chinese===

若我带你登上
我的小鹰巢梯，你会看见什么？
你会看见天空像一只澄蓝的杯子
倒扣在空气之中。

在我的鹰巢梯上，树上的小巢里，
你会做些什么？
你会一声连一声地啼叫，搅动空气，
只想去够你望见的一切。

在树的顶梢，你要伸手去够什么，
来平息你攫取的悲伤？
你望见的星星一颗也抓不住，
你只拾得到一片绿叶。

可等你放下了贪求的悲伤，
安心于远远观望，
你手中握着的会是一片枯萎的叶，
你心中却有一颗闪亮的星。

## A Baby-Sermon / 婴儿的布道
===Original===

The lightning and thunder
They go and they come:
But the stars and the stillness
Are always at home.

===Chinese===

闪电和雷鸣
来了又去：
而星星与静谧
永远在家里。

## Little Bo-Peep / 小波比
===Original===

Little Bo-Peep, she has lost her sheep,
And will not know where to find them;
They are over the height and out of sight,
Trailing their tails behind them!

Little Bo-Peep woke out of her sleep,
Jump’d up and set out to find them:
“The silly things! they’ve got no wings,
And they’ve left their trails behind them!

“They’ve taken their tails, but they’ve left their trails,
And so I shall follow and find them!”
For wherever a tail had dragged a trail
The grass lay bent behind them.

She washed in the brook, and caught up her crook.
And after her sheep did run
Along the trail that went up the dale
Across the grass in the sun.

She ran with a will, and she came to a hill
That went up steep like a spire;
On its very top the sun seemed to stop,
And burned like a flame of fire.

But now she went slow, for the hill did go
Up steeper as she went higher;
When she reached its crown, the sun was down,
Leaving a trail of fire.

And her sheep were gone, and hope she had none.
For now was no trail behind them.
Yes, there they were! long-tailed and fair!
But to see was not to find them!

Golden in hue, and rosy and blue,
And white as blossom of pears,
Her sheep they did run in the trail of the sun,
As she had been running in theirs!

After the sun like clouds they did run,
But she knew they were her sheep:
She sat down to cry and look up at the sky,
But she cried herself to sleep.

And as she slept the dew down wept,
And the wind did blow from the sky;
And doings strange brought a lovely change:
She woke with a different cry!

Nibble, nibble, crop, without a stop!
A hundred little lambs
Did pluck and eat the grass so sweet
That grew in the trail of their dams!

She gave one look, she caught up her crook,
Wiped away the sleep that did blind her;
And nibble-nibble-crop, without a stop
The lambs came nibbling behind her.

Home, home she came, both tired and lame,
With three times as large a stock;
In a month or more, they’ll be sheep as before,
A lovely, long-wooled flock!

But what will she say, if, one fine day,
When they’ve got their bushiest tails,
Their grown-up game should be just the same,
And again she must follow mere trails?

Never weep, Bo-Peep, though you lose your sheep,
Tears will turn rainbow-laughter!
In the trail of the sun if the mothers did run,
The lambs are sure to run after;

===Chinese===

小波比（Little Bo-Peep）丢了她的羊，
不知道上哪儿去找它们；
它们翻过高岗、出了視野，
把尾巴拖在身后呢！

小波比从睡梦里醒来，
跳起身就去找羊：
“傻东西！你们又没长翅膀，
倒把踪迹留在了地上！

“尾巴你们带走了，踪迹却留下，
我顺着找准能追上！”
因为尾巴拖过的地方，
青草都朝着后方弯躺。

她在溪里洗了把脸，抄起牧杖，
沿着踪迹追赶羊群，
小道弯弯爬上山谷，
穿过太阳底下的草菌。

她一股劲儿地跑，跑到一座山前，
山体陡得像塔尖一般；
太阳仿佛就停在山顶尖上，
烧得像一团火焰。

可这会儿她慢了下来，因为那山
越往上爬越是陡峭；
等她登上山顶，太阳已落了山，
只留下一道火的踪道。

她的羊不见了，希望也没了——
地上再没留下踪迹。
燋，那不足它们！长尾多好看！
可望得见偏偏追不及！

金色的、玫瑰色的、蓝莹莹的，
还有梨花一样白，
她的羊正沿着太阳的踪迹奔跑——
正像她方才追它们的踪迹来！

它们像云朵追着太阳跑，
可她认得那是自家的羊；
她坐下来哭，仰望着天空，
哭着哭着睡着了。

她睡着时露珠往下落泪，
风从天上阵阵吹来；
奇妙的事情带来美妙的变化：
她醒来时喊出的声儿都不一样啦！

咩咩嚼、咩咩啃，一口也不停！
一百只小羊羔
正在大吃特吃那么甜的草——
长在羊妈妈踪迹旁的嫩草！

她望了一眼，抄起牧杖，
擦掉迷眼的睡意；
咩咩啃啊嚼啊一口不停，
小羊羔边啃边跟在她身后。

回了家、回了家，又累又瘸，
羊群多了两倍还不止；
再过个把月，它们都会长回大羊，
一身长毛、可爱的一群！

可要是有一天，天气正晴好，
它们的尾巴长得最蓬最茂，
却又玩起长大了的老把戏，
害她只好再顺着踪迹去找——她说什么才好？

别哭啦，波比，羊丢了也不怕，
眼泪会变成彩虹般的笑！
既然羊妈妈追着太阳跑，
羊羔准会跟在后头追上；

===Original===

But a day is coming when little feet drumming
Will wake you up to find them﻿—
All the old sheep﻿—how your heart will leap!﻿—
With their big little lambs behind them!

===Chinese===

可总有一天，小蹄子咚咚敲响，
会把你唤醒去迎接——
老羊全回来了——你的心要跳多高！——
身后还跟着长大了的小羊羔！

## Little Boy Blue / 小蓝孩儿
===Original===

Little Boy Blue lost his way in a wood﻿—
Sing apples and cherries, roses and honey:
He said, “I would not go back if I could,
It’s all so jolly and funny!”

He sang, “This wood is all my own﻿—
Apples and cherries, roses and honey!
Here I will sit, a king on my throne,
All so jolly and funny!”

A little snake crept out of a tree﻿—
Apples and cherries, roses and honey:
“Lie down at my feet, little snake,” said he﻿—
All so jolly and funny!

A little bird sang in the tree overhead﻿—
“Apples and cherries, roses and honey:”
“Come and sing your song on my finger,” he said,
All so jolly and funny.

Up coiled the snake; the bird came down,
And sang him the song of Birdie Brown.

But little Boy Blue found it tiresome to sit
Though it was on a throne: he would walk a bit!

He took up his horn, and he blew a blast:
“Snake, you go first, and, birdie, come last.”

Waves of green snake o’er the yellow leaves went;
The snake led the way, and he knew what he meant:

But by Boy Blue’s head, with flutter and dart,
Flew Birdie Brown, her song in her heart.

Boy Blue came where apples grew fair and sweet:
“Tree, drop me an apple down at my feet.”

He came where cherries hung plump and red:
“Come to my mouth, sweet kisses,” he said.

And the boughs bow down, and the apples they dapple
The grass, too many for him to grapple;

And the cheeriest cherries, with never a miss,
Fall to his mouth, each a full-grown kiss.

He met a little brook singing a song:
“Little brook,” he said, “you are going wrong,

“You must follow me, follow me, follow, I say,
Do as I tell you, and come this way.”

And the song-singing, sing-songing forest brook
Leapt from its bed and after him took;

And the dead leaves rustled, yellow and wan,
As over their beds the water ran.

He called every bird that sat on a bough;
He called every creature with poop and prow﻿—

I mean, with two ends, that is, nose and tail:
With legs or without, they followed full sail;

Squirrels that carried their tails like a sack,
Each his own on his little brown humpy back;

Snails that drew their own caravans,
Poking out their own eyes on the point of a lance,

And houseless slugs, white, black, and red﻿—
Snails too lazy to build a shed;

And butterflies, flutterbys, weasels, and larks,
And owls, and shrew-mice, and harkydarks,

Cockchafers, henchafers, cockioli-birds,
Cockroaches, henroaches, cuckoos in herds;

===Chinese===

小蓝孩儿（Little Boy Blue）在树林里迷了路——
唱吧，苹果樱桃，玫瑰蜂蜜：
他说：“就算能回去我也不回去，
这儿一切都欢天喜地！”

他唱道：“这树林全归我所有——
苹果樱桃，玫瑰蜂蜜！
我要坐在这儿，像国王坐上宝座，
一切都欢天喜地！”

一条小蛇从树里爬了出来——
苹果樱桃，玫瑰蜂蜜：
“躺在我脚边吧，小蛇，”他说——
一切都欢天喜地！

一只小鸟在头顶的枝上歌唱——
“苹果樱桃，玫瑰蜂蜜：”
“来，落在我手指上唱你的歌，”他说，
一切都欢天喜地。

蛇盘了起来；鸟儿落了下来，
给他唱起布朗小鸟（Birdie Brown）的歌。

可小蓝孩儿觉得坐着腻了，
哪怕是坐在宝座上：他想走一走！

他拿起号角，吹了一声响：
“蛇，你打头，小鸟，你殿后。”

绿蛇一浪一浪，掠过黄叶前行；
蛇在前头引路，它明白主人的心意：

而在小蓝孩儿的头旁，扑闪着飞掠，
是布朗小鸟，歌儿藏在心窝。

小蓝孩儿走到苹果长得又美又甜的地方：
“苹果树，掉一个苹果到我脚边吧。”

他走到樱桃饱满鲜红的地方：
“到我这嘴里来吧，甜蜜的吻，”他说。

树枝弯弯下垂，苹果点点洒洒
落满草地，多得他抱也抱不下；

最喜人的樱桃，一颗不落空，
落进他的嘴，每颗都是长成的一吻。

他遇见一条小溪正唱着歌：
“小溪，”他说，“你走错了路，

“你得跟着我，跟着我，跟着我，我说，
照我吩咐的，往这边来。”

那条唱着歌儿、哼着调儿的林中小溪
从溪床上跳起，跟在他身后奔去；

枯叶簌簌作响，又黄又暗淡，
流水漫过了它们的床。

他把枝上的每一只鸟儿都唤齐；
他把每个带“船尾船头”的生灵都唤起——

我是说，长着两头的，就是鼻子和尾巴：
有腿的没腿的，全都满帆跟随；

松鼠把尾巴当麻袋一样背着，
各自驮在棕色的小驼背上；

蜗牛赶着自家的大篷车，
把眼睛顶在枪矛尖上探出张望，

还有无家可归的蛞蝓，白的黑的红的——
是懒得不肯盖房子的蜗牛；

还有蝴蝶、飞飞蝶，黄鼠狼和云雀，
还有猫头鹰、鼩鼱，还有听呀雀，

金龟子、母金龟，叽里咕噜鸟，
公蟑螂、母蟑螂，成群结队的布谷鸟；

===Original===

The dappled fawns fawning, the fallow-deer following;
The swallows and flies, flying and swallowing﻿—

All went flitting, and sailing, and flowing
After the merry boy running and blowing.

The spider forgot, and followed him spinning,
And lost all his thread from end to beginning;

The gay wasp forgot his rings and his waist﻿—
He never had made such undignified haste!

The dragon-flies melted to mist with their hurrying;
The mole forsook his harrowing and burrowing;

The bees went buzzing, not busy but beesy,
And the midges in columns, upright and easy.

But Little Boy Blue was not content,
Calling for followers still as he went,

Blowing his horn, and beating his drum,
And crying aloud, “Come all of you, come!”

He said to the shadows, “Come after me;”
And the shadows began to flicker and flee,

And away through the wood went flattering and fluttering,
Shaking and quivering, quavering and muttering.

He said to the wind, “Come, follow; come, follow
With whistle and pipe, with rustle and hollo;”

And the wind wound round at his desire,
As if Boy had been the gold cock on the spire;

And the cock itself flew down from the church
And left the farmers all in the lurch.

Everything, everything, all and sum,
They run and they fly, they creep and they come;

The very trees they tugged at their roots,
Only their feet were too fast in their boots﻿—

After him leaning and straining and bending,
As on through their boles the army kept wending,

Till out of the wood Boy burst on a lea,
Shouting and calling, “Come after me,”

And then they rose with a leafy hiss
And stood as if nothing had been amiss.

Little Boy Blue sat down on a stone,
And the creatures came round him every one.

He said to the clouds, “I want you there!”
And down they sank through the thin blue air.

He said to the sunset far in the west,
“Come here; I want you; ’tis my behest!”

And the sunset came and stood up on the wold,
And burned and glowed in purple and gold.

Then Little Boy Blue began to ponder:
“What’s to be done with them all, I wonder!”

He thought a while, then he said, quite low,
“What to do with you all, I am sure I don’t know!”

The clouds clodded down till dismal it grew;
The snake sneaked close; round Birdie Brown flew;

The brook, like a cobra, rose on its tail,
And the wind sank down with a what-will-you wail,

===Chinese===

花斑小鹿谄媚地讨好，黇鹿成行相随；
燕子和苍蝇，边飞边吞——

全都翅儿翩翩、悠悠荡荡、涟涟涪涪
追着那又跑又吹号的快活孩子。

蜘蛛忘了形，边吐丝边跟来，
把丝从头到尾吐了个精光；

花俏的黄蜂忘了它的环纹和细腰——
它可从没这么失过体面地赶过急！

蜻蜓匆忙得化成了一片薄雾；
鼹鼠丢下了它的耙掘和打洞；

蜜蜂嗡嗡赶路，不是忙着，而是“蜂”着，
蠓虫排成纵队，笔挺又从容。

可小蓝孩儿还不满足，
一路走还一路招兵买马，

吹着号，打着鼓，
大声喊：“你们全都来，来！”

他对影子说：“跟我来；”
影子便开始摇曳奔逃，

穿过树林一路阿谀又扑闪，
哆嗦、颤动、结巴、咕哝。

他对风说：“来，跟上来；跟上来，
带着口哨和笛声，带着沙沙和呼喊；”

风便顺着他的心意盘旋，
仿佛小蓝孩儿就是塔尖上的金公鸡；

那只金公鸡自己也从教堂飞下，
把庄稼人全都撂在原地抓瞎。

一切的一切，全部和总和，
跑的飞的，爬的蠕的，全都来了；

连树木都拼命拽着自己的根，
只是它们的脚在靴子里拴得太牢——

朝他倾着、绷着、弯着，
队伍穿过它们的树干继续前行，

直到小蓝孩儿冲出树林来到草地，
喊着叫着：“跟我来，”

于是它们伴着叶片的嘶声直起身，
站在那儿仿佛什么事也没发生过。

小蓝孩儿在一块石头上坐下，
生灵们一个个围了上来。

他对云说：“我要你们到这儿来！”
云便穿过稀薄的蓝天沉了下来。

他对远在西边的落日说：
“过来；我要你；这是我的命令！”

落日就来了，立在荒原之上，
燃着、耀着，紫一片金一片。

小蓝孩儿开始琢磨：
“这么一大群可拿它们怎么办！”

他想了一会儿，然后低声说：
“拿你们怎么办，我是真不知道！”

云阴沉沉地压下来，天色越来越晦暗；
蛇悄悄贴过来；布朗小鸟绕着圈飞；

小溪像条眼镜蛇，用尾巴立起身，
风瘫了下来，发出一声“你要怎样啊”的哀鸣，

===Original===

And all the creatures sat and stared;
The mole opened the eyes that he hadn’t, and glared;

And for rats and bats, and the world and his wife
Little Boy Blue was afraid of his life.

Then Birdie Brown began to sing,
And what he sang was the very thing:

“Little Boy Blue, you have brought us all hither:
Pray, are we to sit and grow old together?”

“Go away; go away,” said Little Boy Blue;
“I’m sure I don’t want you! get away﻿—do.”

“No, no; no, no; no, yes, and no, no,”
