I said, and I grew warmer
Though the brooks were frozen.

Spring sits on her nest,
Daisies and white clover;
And my heart at rest
Lies in the spring’s young nest:
My love she loves me best,
And the frost is over!
Spring sits on her nest,
Daisies and white clover!

===Chinese===

*我很冷*

我很冷，
在夏天的天气里；
太阳照出他全部的金，
可我很冷——
唉，我们老了，
爱与和我一起！
哦，我真冷，
在夏天的天气里！

忽然我暖和起来，
虽然小河都冻了：
「真的，轻蔑伤过她！」
我说，我就暖和起来；
「更好的男人，那迷人的
至少认识一打！」
我说，我就更暖和起来，
虽然小河都冻了。

春天坐在她的巢上，
雏菊和白三叶草；
而我安宁的心
躺在春天年轻的巢里：
我的爱她最爱我，
霜已经过去了！
春天坐在她的巢上，
雏菊和白三叶草！

### An Improvisation / 即兴

### An Improvisation / 
===Original===

The stars cleave the sky.
Yet for us they rest,
And their race-course high
Is a shining nest!

The hours hurry on.
But where is thy flight,
Soft pavilion
Of motionless night?

Earth gives up her trees
To the holy air;
They live in the breeze;
They are saints at prayer!

Summer night, come from God,
On your beauty, I see,
A still wave has flowed
Of eternity!

===Chinese===

星辰剖开天空。
可为我们它们安歇，
它们高处的赛道
是一个闪光的巢！

时辰匆匆向前。
可你的飞翔在哪里，
柔软的帷帐，
不动的夜？

大地交出她的树，
给圣洁的空气；
它们活在上风里；
它们是祷告的圣徒！

夏夜，从神而来的，
在你的美上，我看见，
流过了一道
安静的永恒之波！

### Equity / 公道

### Equity / 
===Original===

No bird can sing in tune but that the Lord
Sits throned in equity above the heaven,
And holds the righteous balance always even;
No heart can true response to love afford
Wherein from one to eight not every chord
Is yet attuned by the spirits seven:
For tuneful no bird sings but that the Lord
Is throned in equity above high heaven.

Oh heart, by wrong unfilial scathed and scored,
And from thy humble throne with mazedness driven,
Take courage: when thy wrongs thou hast forgiven,
Thy rights in love thy God will see restored:
No bird could sing in tune but that the Lord
Sits throned in equity above the heaven.

===Chinese===

没有一只鸟能唱得合调，若不是主
坐在公义的宝座上，在高天之上，
永远持定那正直的天平；
没有一颗心能真回应爱，
若在它里面，从一到八，不是每一条弦
都已被那七灵调准：
因为没有一只鸟能唱得合调，若不是主
坐在公义的宝座上，在高天之上。

哦心啊，被不孝的错行灼伤划破，
又从你卑微的宝座上被迷乱驱赶，
要刚强：当你已饶恕了你的冤屈，
你的神必在爱里看顾你的权利得恢复：
没有一只鸟能唱得合调，若不是主
坐在公义的宝座上，在高天之上。

### The Consoler / 安慰者

### The Consoler / 
===Original===

*On an Engraving of Scheffer’s Christus Consolator*

I

What human form is this? what form divine?
And who are these that gaze upon his face
Mild, beautiful, and full of heavenly grace,
With whose reflected light the gazers shine?
Saviour, who does not know it to be thine?
Who does not long to fill a gazer’s place?
And yet there is no time, there is no space
To keep away thy servants from thy shrine!
Here if we kneel, and watch with faithful eyes,
Thou art not too far for faithful eyes to see,
Thou art not too far to turn and look on me,
To speak to me, and to receive my sighs.
Therefore for ever I forget the skies,
And find an everlasting Sun in thee.

II

Oh let us never leave that happy throng!
From that low attitude of love not cease!
In all the world there is no other peace,
In all the world no other shield from wrong.
But chiefly, Saviour, for thy feet we long﻿—
For no vain quiet, for no pride’s increase﻿—
But that, being weak, and Thou divinely strong,
Us from our hateful selves thou mayst release.
We wander from thy fold’s free holy air,
Forget thy looks, and take our fill of sin!
But if thou keep us evermore within,
We never surely can forget thee there﻿—
Breathing thy breath, thy white robe given to wear,
And loving thee for all thou diedst to win!

III

To speak of him in language of our own,
Is not for us too daringly to try;
But, Saviour, we can read thy history
Upon the faces round thy humble throne;
And as the flower among the grass makes known
What summer suns have warmed it from the sky,
As every human smile and human sigh
Is witness that we do not live alone,
So in that company﻿—in those sweet tears,
The first-born of a rugged melted heart,
In those gaunt chains for ever torn apart,
And in the words that weeping mother hears,
We read the story of two thousand years,
And know thee somewhat, Saviour, as thou art.

===Chinese===

*观谢弗尔版画「安慰者基督」*

I

这是怎样的人形？怎样的神性之形？
这些凝望他脸的人又是谁——
那脸温和、美好、满有属天的恩，
凝望的人都被它反照的光照亮？
救主啊，谁不认识那是你的脸？
谁不渴慕占一个凝望者的位置？
然而没有时间、没有空间
能把你的仆人隔在你的圣所外！
我们若在这里跪下，以忠信的眼守望，
你就不至于远到忠信的眼看不见，
你不至于远到不能转身看我，
不能对我说话，不能收下我的叹息。
所以我永远忘记诸天，
而在你里面找到一轮永在的太阳。

II

哦，愿我们永不离开那快乐的群体！
不从那爱的低姿态中止息！
全世界再没有别的平安，
全世界再没有别的抵挡错行的盾。
但首要的，救主啊，我们渴慕你的脚——
不为虚妄的安静，不为骄傲的加增——
而是因为，我们软弱，而你神圣地刚强，
愿你把我们从我们可憎的自己释放。
我们从你羊圈自由圣洁的空气里游荡，
忘记你的面容，放纵地吃罪！
但你若永远保守我们在里面，
我们在那里就绝不会忘记你——
呼吸你的呼吸，得穿你的白袍，
并且爱你，为你赢得的一切而爱！

III

用我们自己的言语谈论他，
不是我们可以大胆尝试的；
可是，救主啊，我们能读你的历史，
在你卑微宝座四围的众脸上；
正如花在草丛中透露
怎样的夏日从天上暖过它，
正如每一个人的微笑和叹息
都见证我们不是独自活着，
照样，在那群人中——在那些甜美的泪里，
在一颗粗硬被熔之心的头生子里，
在那些被永远扯断的嶙峋锁链里，
在那哭泣的母亲听见的话语里，
我们读出两千年的故事，
并且多少认识你，救主，照你的所是。

### To —﻿—﻿— / 致———

### To —﻿—﻿— / 
===Original===

I cannot write old verses here,
Dead things a thousand years away,
When all the life of the young year
Is in the summer day.

The roses make the world so sweet,
The bees, the birds have such a tune,
There’s such a light and such a heat
And such a joy this June,

One must expand one’s heart with praise,
And make the memory secure
Of sunshine and the woodland days
And summer twilights pure.

Oh listen rather! Nature’s song
Comes from the waters, beating tides,
Green-margined rivers, and the throng
Of streams on mountain-sides.

So fair those water-spirits are,
Such happy strength their music fills,
Our joy shall be to wander far
And find them on the hills.

===Chinese===

我在这里写不出古老的诗行，
那些死了一千年的东西，
当新年全部的生命
都在这夏日的白昼里。

玫瑰把世界弄得这样甜，
蜜蜂、鸟儿有这样一支曲，
这个六月有这样的光、这样的热，
这样的欢喜，

人必须敞开心来赞美，
并且把记忆牢牢守定——
守定阳光和林中的日子，
和夏天纯净的黄昏。

哦，不如去听！自然的歌
来自众水，来自拍岸的潮，
来自绿岸的河流，和那
山坡上一群群的溪。

那些水灵那样美好，
它们的音乐满有欢喜的力量，
我们的喜乐将是远远漫游，
在群山之上把它们寻见。

### To a Sister / 致一位姐妹

### To a Sister / 
===Original===

A fresh young voice that sings to me
So often many a simple thing,
Should surely not unanswered be
By all that I can sing.

Dear voice, be happy every way
A thousand changing tones among,
From little child’s unfinished lay
To angel’s perfect song.

In dewy woods﻿—fair, soft, and green
Like morning woods are childhood’s bower﻿—
Be like the voice of brook unseen
Among the stones and flowers;

A joyful voice though born so low,
And making all its neighbours glad;
Sweet, hidden, constant in its flow
Even when the winds are sad.

So, strengthen in a peaceful home,
And daily deeper meanings bear;
And when life’s wildernesses come
Be brave and faithful there.

Try all the glorious magic range,
Worship, forgive, console, rejoice,
Until the last and sweetest change﻿—
So live and grow, dear voice.

===Chinese===

一个清新的年轻声音，常向我
唱着许多简单的事物，
理当不至没有回应，
用我所能唱的一切。

亲爱的声音，愿你在千百种
变化的音调中样样快乐，
从小孩子未完的歌谣，
到天使完全的歌唱。

在带露的树林里——美好、柔软、青绿，
像清晨的树林是童年的凉亭——
愿你像看不见的溪流的嗓音，
在石头和花中间；

一个喜乐的嗓音，虽然生得这样低，
却叫它一切的邻舍不得不快乐；
甜美、隐藏、涌流不止，
即使风在悲伤。

就这样，在平安的家中长壮，
天天结出更深的意义；
当人生的旷野来到，
在那里要勇敢、要忠信。

去尝试那全部荣耀的魔法音域，
敬拜、饶恕、安慰、欢欣，
直到那最后、最甜的改变——
就这样活着长大，亲爱的声音。

### Contrition / 悔罪

### Contrition / 
===Original===

Out of the gulf into the glory,
Father, my soul cries out to be lifted.
Dark is the woof of my dismal story,
Thorough thy sun-warp stormily drifted!﻿—
Out of the gulf into the glory,
Lift me, and save my story.

I have done many things merely shameful;
I am a man ashamed, my father!
My life is ashamed and broken and blameful﻿—
The broken and blameful, oh, cleanse and gather!
Heartily shame me, Lord, of the shameful!
To my judge I flee with my blameful.

Saviour, at peace in thy perfect purity,
Think what it is, not to be pure!
Strong in thy love’s essential security,
Think upon those who are never secure.
Full fill my soul with the light of thy purity:
Fold me in love’s security.

O Father, O Brother, my heart is sore aching!
Help it to ache as much as is needful;
Is it you cleansing me, mending, remaking,
Dear potter-hands, so tender and heedful?
Sick of my past, of my own self aching﻿—
Hurt on, dear hands, with your making.

Proud of the form thou hadst given thy vessel,
Proud of myself, I forgot my donor;
Down in the dust I began to nestle,
Poured thee no wine, and drank deep of dishonour!
Lord, thou hast broken, thou mendest thy vessel!
In the dust of thy glory I nestle.

===Chinese===

出离深渊，进入荣耀，
父啊，我的魂呼求被举起。
我阴郁故事的纬线何等黑，
在你的日头经线上被风暴吹积！——
出离深渊，进入荣耀，
举起我，救救我的故事。

我做过许多单单可耻的事；
我是一个羞愧的人，我的父！
我的生命又羞愧、又破碎、又担罪——
那破碎担罪的，哦，求你洗净收聚！
主啊，叫我为可耻的由衷羞愧！
我带着我的罪逃向我的审判者。

救主啊，安息在你完全的纯净里，
想一想不纯净是什么滋味！
靠你爱之本质的安稳刚强，
想一想那些永不安稳的人。
用你纯净的光充满我的魂：
把我裹进爱的安稳。

哦父，哦兄，我的心疼痛得很！
帮它痛到所需要的程度；
是你在洁净我、修补我、重造我吗，
亲爱的陶匠之手，这样温柔细心？
我厌透了我的过去，为我自己的疼——
继续造吧，亲爱的手，继续你们的制作。

我曾为你器皿的形自负，
为自己骄傲，忘了我的赐予者；
我在尘土里开始安卧，
不给你斟酒，却深饮了羞辱！
主啊，你打碎了你破碎的器皿，又修补它！
我在你荣耀的尘土里安卧。

### The Shortest and Sweetest of Songs / 最短最甜的歌

### The Shortest and Sweetest of Songs / 
===Original===

Come
Home.

===Chinese===

回
家。

## Russell Gurney / 拉塞尔·格尼
===Original===

In that high country whither thou art gone,
Right noble friend, thou walkest with thy peers,
The gathered great of many a hundred years!
Few are left like thee﻿—few, I say, not none,
Else were thy England soon a Babylon,
A land of outcry, mockery, and tears!
Higher than law, a refuge from its fears,
Wast thou, in whom embodied Justice shone.
The smile that gracious broke on thy grand face
Was like the sunrise of a morn serene
Among the mountains, making sweet their awe.
Thou both the gentle and the strong didst draw;
Thee childhood loved, and on thy breast would lean,
As, whence thou cam’st, it knew the lofty place.

===Chinese===

在你所去的那高天之乡，
真正高贵的朋友，你与同侪同行，
那是数百年间萃聚的群英！
如你者所剩无几——无几，我说，并非无人，
否则你的英格兰不久将沦为巴比伦，
沦为叫嚣、讥嘲与眼泪之地！
你高于律法，是律法之恐惧的避难所，
公义在你身上化身为光。
那和蔼的笑容绽放在你庄严的脸上，
宛若一个静谧清晨的日出
照进群山之间，令它们的敬畏变甜。
你既吸引柔弱者，也吸引刚强者；
孩童们爱你，愿倚在你胸前，
仿佛知道你来自那高天之乡。

## To One Threatened with Blindness / 致濒临失明者
===Original===

I

Lawrence, what though the world be growing dark,
And twilight cool thy potent day enclose!
The sun, beneath the round earth sunk, still glows
All the night through, sleepless and young and stark.
Oh, be thy spirit faithful as the lark,
More daring: in the midnight of thy woes,
Dart through them, higher than earth’s shadow goes,
Into the Light of which thou art a spark!
Be willing to be blind﻿—that, in thy night,
The Lord may bring his Father to thy door,
And enter in, and feast thy soul with light.
Then shall thou dream of darksome ways no more,
Forget the gloom that round thy windows lies,
And shine, God’s house, all radiant in our eyes.

II

Say thou, his will be done who is the good!
His will be borne who knoweth how to bear!
Who also in the night had need of prayer,
Both when awoke divinely longing mood,
And when the power of darkness him withstood.
For what is coming take no jot of care:
Behind, before, around thee as the air,
He o’er thee like thy mother’s heart will brood.
And when thou hast wearied thy wings of prayer,
Then fold them, and drop gently to thy nest,
Which is thy faith; and make thy people blest
With what thou bring’st from that ethereal height,
Which whoso looks on thee will straightway share:
He needs no eyes who is a shining light!

===Chinese===

I

劳伦斯啊，纵然世界正渐转昏暗，
纵然清凉的暮色围拢你炽烈的白昼！
太阳沉入圆球般的大地之下，依然灼燃，
彻夜不息，无眠、年轻而凛然。
哦，愿你的心灵如云雀般忠贞，
更加无畏：在你忧患的午夜之中，
一冲而穿，飞得比大地的阴影更高，
升入那光——你本是它的一点火花！
甘愿失明吧——好叫你的黑夜里，
主（Lord）引他的父来到你门前，
进屋坐席，以光华盛宴你的灵魂。
从此你不会再梦见幽暗的路径，
忘却伏在你窗畔的沉沉晦暗，
放光吧，神的殿宇，在我们眼中辉煌灼灼。

II

你要说：愿那至善者的旨意成就！
他的旨意，懂得承受的人必能承受！
他也曾在黑夜中需要祷告，
无论是神圣的渴慕将他唤醒之时，
还是黑暗的权势与他对抗之际。
对将临的事不要有一丝挂虑：
他在你身后、身前、四围，如空气弥漫，
像母亲的心，将你温存覆庇。
当你祷告的双翼已然飞倦，
就收拢它们，轻轻落回你的巢——
那巢便是你的信心；再让你的人民
因你从那缥缈高处带回的而蒙福，
凡仰望你的人，必立时同得恩眷：
自己既是一道光辉，何须再要眼睛！

## To Aubrey de Vere / 致奥布里·德·维尔
===Original===

Ray of the Dawn of Truth, Aubrey de Vere,
Forgive my play fantastic with thy name,
Distilling its true essence by the flame
Which Love ’neath Fancy’s limbeck lighteth clear.
I know not what thy semblance, what thy cheer;
If, as thy spirit, hale thy bodily frame,
Or furthering by failure each high aim;
If green thy leaf, or, like mine, growing sear;
But this I think, that thou wilt, by and by﻿—
Two journeys stoutly, therefore safely trod﻿—
We laying down the staff, and He the rod﻿—
So look on me I shall not need to cry﻿—
“We must be brothers, Aubrey, thou and I:
We mean the same thing﻿—will the will of God!”

===Chinese===

真理黎明的一束光，奥布里·德·维尔，
饶恕我拿你的名字作的奇想戏笔，
借爱的火焰——它在幻想的曲颈甑下
燃得澄明——蒸取其中的真髓。
我不知你的容貌，不知你的神采；
不知你的身躯是否如灵魂般康健，
还是以一次次失败推进着崇高的志愿；
不知你的叶子是否青翠，还是像我的一样渐凋；
但我想，终有一日——
两段旅程都已坚忍走完，因而稳当——
我们放下行杖，他放下惩戒之杖——
你这样望我一眼，我便无需呼喊——
「奥布里，你我必是兄弟：
我们怀着同一个心意——愿上帝的旨意成全！」

## General Gordon / 戈登将军
===Original===

I

Victorious through failure! faithful Lord,
Who for twelve angel legions wouldst not pray
From thine own country of eternal day,
To shield thee from the lanterned traitor horde,
Making thy one rash servant sheathe his sword!﻿—
Our long retarded legions, on their way,
Toiling through sands, and shouldering Nile’s down-sway,
To reach thy soldier, keeping at thy word,
Thou sawest foiled﻿—but glorifiedst him,
Over ten cities giving him thy rule!
We will not mourn a star that grew not dim,
A soldier-child of God gone home from school!
A dregless cup, with life brimmed, he did quaff,
And quaffs it now with Christ’s imperial staff!

II

Another to the witnesses’ roll-call
Hath answered, “Here I am!” and so stepped out﻿—
With willingness crowned everywhere about,
Not the head only, but the body all,
In one great nimbus of obedient fall,
His heart’s blood dashing in the face of doubt﻿—
Love’s last victorious stand amid the rout!
—Silence is left, and the untasted gall.
No chariot with ramping steeds of fire
The Father sent to fetch his man-child home;
His brother only called, “My Gordon, come!”
And like a dove to heaven he did aspire,
His one wing Death, his other, Heart’s-desire.
—Farewell a while! we climb where thou hast clomb!

===Chinese===

I

借失败而得胜！忠信的主（Lord）啊，
当年你不肯从永恒白昼的故乡
求遣十二营天使前来护卫，
救你脱离那手执灯火的叛党之众，
喝令你那鲁莽的仆人收剑入鞘！——
你看见我们那久久被耽搁的军团，
一路在沙海中跋涉、逆着尼罗河的奔流，
前去接应你那谨守你话语的兵士——
他们受挫了——你却使他得了荣耀，
把十座城的权柄交给他执掌！
我们决不为这样一颗从未黯淡的星辰哀恸，
不为神的一个军中孩子放学归家哀恸！
他一饮而尽那盛满生命、毫无渣滓的杯，
如今又在基督的君王杖旁畅饮此杯！

II

又一位在殉道者的点名册上
应声答道：「我在这里！」随即出列——
甘愿为冠冕环戴他周身，
不只是头颅，而是整个身躯，
汇成顺服倾倒的一圈大光轮，
他心里的血溅在疑惑的脸上——
这是爱在溃败之中最后一次得胜的坚守！
——留下的是寂静，和那未曾尝的苦胆。
父没有差来火车与腾跃的火马，
接他的成年之子回家；
只有他的兄弟呼唤：「我的戈登，来吧！」
他便如鸽子一般升向高天，
一翼是死，另一翼是心中的渴慕。
——暂别了！我们正攀向你登临过的高处！

## Written for One in Sore Pain / 写给剧痛中的某人
===Original===

Shepherd, on before thy sheep,
Hear thy lamb that bleats behind!
Scarce the track I stumbling keep!
Through my thin fleece blows the wind!

Turn and see me, Son of Man!
Turn and lift thy Father’s child;
Scarce I walk where once I ran:
Carry me﻿—the wind is wild!

Thou art strong﻿—thy strength wilt share;
My poor weight thou wilt not feel;
Weakness made thee strong to bear,
Suffering made thee strong to heal!

I were still a wandering sheep
But for thee, O Shepherd-man!
Following now, I faint, I weep,
Yet I follow as I can!

Shepherd, if I fall and lie
Moaning in the frosty wind,
Yet, I know, I shall not die﻿—
Thou wilt miss me﻿—and wilt find!

===Chinese===

牧人啊，你在羊群前面行，
听背后你小羊的哀鸣！
我跌跌撞撞，勉强跟住路径！
寒风吹透我单薄的绒毛！

回身看我吧，人子！
回身扶起你父的孩子；
从前我奔跑，如今举步维艰：
抱我走吧——风这样狂！

你强壮——愿将力量分我；
我这点轻负重你毫不觉；
软弱曾使你坚忍能背负，
受苦曾使你刚强能医治！

若不是你，哦牧人，
我仍是迷途的羔羊！
如今跟随，我昏沉，我哭泣，
却仍尽力跟随！

牧人啊，我若跌倒，
卧在霜风里呻吟，
但我知道，我不会死——
你会惦念我——并寻回我！

## Christmas, 1873 / 圣诞，1873
===Original===

Christmas-Days are still in store:﻿—
Will they change﻿—steal faded hither?
Or come fresh as heretofore,
Summering all our winter weather?

Surely they will keep their bloom
All the countless pacing ages:
In the country whence they come
Children only are the sages!

Hither, every hour and year,
Children come to cure our oldness﻿—
Oft, alas, to gather sear
Unbelief, and earthy boldness!

Men they grow and women cold,
Selfish, passionate, and plaining!
Ever faster they grow old:﻿—
On the world, ah, eld is gaining!

Child, whose childhood ne’er departs!
Jesus, with the perfect father!
Drive the age from parents’ hearts;
To thy heart the children gather.

Send thy birth into our souls,
With its grand and tender story.
Hark! the gracious thunder rolls!﻿—
News to men! to God old glory!

===Chinese===

圣诞节仍在前方存驻：——
它们会变吗——会褪色地飘来？
还是一如往昔那样新鲜，
让我们整个寒冬如沐夏暖？

无疑它们会保持芬芳
历经无数缓缓行进的世代：
在它们所自的国度，
唯有孩童才是智者！

每个时辰、每个年头，
都有孩子来医治我们的老朽——
唉，却往往染上枯萎的
不信与尘俗的狂傲！

他们长成冷淡的男男女女，
自私、暴躁、满口怨尤！
他们老得越来越快：——
苍老啊，正在侵占这世界！

孩童啊，你的童年永不离去！
耶稣，同着完全的天父！
把衰朽从父母心中驱走；
叫孩子们都聚到你心头。

差遣你的降生进入我们灵魂，
带着那壮丽而温柔的故事。
听啊！恩慈的雷声滚动！——
向世人报佳音！向上帝归旧荣！

## Christmas, 1884 / 圣诞，一八八四
===Original===

Though in my heart no Christmas glee,
Though my song-bird be dumb,
Jesus, it is enough for me
That thou art come.

What though the loved be scattered far,
Few at the board appear,
In thee, O Lord, they gathered are,
And thou art here.

And if our hearts be low with lack,
They are not therefore numb;
Not always will thy day come back﻿—
Thyself will come!

===Chinese===

纵然我心中没有圣诞的欢悦，
纵然我的鸣禽喑哑无声，
耶稣，为我已足——
因你已降临。

所爱的人纵然四散远方，
席间只坐着寥寥几人，
主（Lord）啊，他们都在你里面团聚，
而你就在这里。

我们的心纵因匮乏而低沉，
却并未因此麻木；
你的节期不会永远归来——
你自己必再临！

## A Song for Christmas / 圣诞之歌
===Original===

Hark, in the steeple the dull bell swinging
Over the furrows ill ploughed by Death!
Hark the bird-babble, the loud lark singing!
Hark, from the sky, what the prophet saith!

Hark, in the pines, the free Wind, complaining﻿—
Moaning, and murmuring, “Life is bare!”
Hark, in the organ, the caught Wind, outstraining,
Jubilant rise in a soaring prayer!

Toll for the burying, sexton tolling!
Sing for the second birth, angel Lark!
Moan, ye poor Pines, with the Past condoling!
Burst out, brave Organ, and kill the Dark!

II

Sit on the ground, and immure thy sorrow;
I will give freedom to mine in song!
Haunt thou the tomb, and deny the morrow;
I will go watch in the dawning long!

For I shall see them, and know their faces﻿—
Tenderer, sweeter, and shining more;
Clasp the old self in the new embraces;
Gaze through their eyes’ wide open door.

Loved ones, I come to you: see my sadness;
I am ashamed﻿—but you pardon wrong!
Smile the old smile, and my soul’s new gladness
Straight will arise in sorrow and song!

===Chinese===

听哪，尖塔里晦暗的钟摆动，
在死亡犁乱的垄沟上空！
听哪鸟儿的喧鸣，云雀的高歌！
听哪，天上先知的诉说！

听哪，松林里自由的风在抱怨——
呜咽着，低语着：「生活赤贫！」
听哪，风琴里被擒的风奋力挣动，
欢腾地升作腾空的祷告！

为埋葬鸣钟，司事正敲！
为重生歌唱，天使的云雀！
呻吟吧，可怜的松树，与往昔同悲！
迸发吧，勇敢的风琴，杀死黑暗！

II

你坐在地上，把悲伤幽禁；
我要用歌声释放我的！
你去萦绕坟莹，否认明天；
我要去守候漫长的黎明！

因为我将看见他们，认得他们的脸——
更温柔、更甜美、更明亮；
在新拥抱里紧拥旧日的自己；
从他们眼窗敞开的门凝望。

亲爱的人，我向你们走来：看我的忧伤；
我羞愧——但你们宽恕过错！
露出旧日的微笑，我灵魂的新喜乐
立时会在忧伤与歌声中升起！

## To My Aging Friends / 致我渐老的朋友们
===Original===

It is no winter night comes down
Upon our hearts, dear friends of old;
But a May evening, softly brown,
Whose wind is rather cold.

We are not, like yon sad-eyed West,
Phantoms that brood o’er Time’s dust-hoard,
We are like yon Moon﻿—in mourning drest,
But gazing on her lord.

Come nearer to the hearth, sweet friends,
Draw nigher, closer, hand and chair;
Ours is a love that never ends,
For God is dearest there!

We will not talk about the past,
We will not ponder ancient pain;
Those are but deep foundations cast
For peaks of soaring gain!

We, waiting Dead, will warm our bones
At our poor smouldering earthly fire;
And talk of wide-eyed living ones
Who have what we desire.

O Living, ye know what is death﻿—
We, by and by, shall know it too!
Humble, with bated, hoping breath,
We are coming fast to you!

===Chinese===

降临我们心头的并不是冬夜，
亲爱的老朋友们；
而是一个五月的黄昏，柔和的褐金色，
只是风略微清冷。

我们并不像那边哀愁眼色的西天，
是守着时间尘埃宝藏出神的幻影；
我们像那轮月亮——身披丧服，
却凝望着她的夫君。

来更靠近炉火吧，亲爱的朋友们，
再近些，手挨着手，椅挨着椅；
我们的爱永无尽头，
因为在炉边，上帝最为亲爱！

我们不谈过往，
不细数旧日的伤痛；
那些不过是深深奠下的根基，
为的是高耸入云的峰峦！

我们这些等候着的死者，且来烘暖筋骨，
守着尘世这炉焖燃的微火；
谈谈那些睁大眼睛的活人，
他们拥有我们所渴想的。

哦，活人们啊，你们知道死是什么——
我们，不久之后，也终将知晓！
谦卑地屏住满怀希望的呼吸，
我们正快快地向你们赶来！

## Christmas Song of the Old Children / 老孩子们的圣诞歌
===Original===

Well for youth to seek the strong,
Beautiful, and brave!
We, the old, who walk along
Gently to the grave,
Only pay our court to thee,
Child of all Eternity!

We are old who once were young,
And we grow more old;
Songs we are that have been sung,
Tales that have been told;
Yellow leaves, wind-blown to thee,
Childhood of Eternity!

If we come too sudden near,
Lo, Earth’s infant cries,
For our faces wan and drear
Have such withered eyes!
Thou, Heaven’s child, turn’st not away
From the wrinkled ones who pray!

Smile upon us with thy mouth
And thine eyes of grace;
On our cold north breathe thy south.
Thaw the frozen face:
Childhood all from thee doth flow﻿—
Melt to song our age’s snow.

Gray-haired children come in crowds,
Thee, their Hope, to greet:
Is it swaddling clothes or shrouds
Hampering so our feet?
Eldest child, the shadows gloom:
Take the aged children home.

We have had enough of play,
And the wood grows drear;
Many who at break of day
Companied us here﻿—
They have vanished out of sight,
Gone and met the coming light!

Fair is this out-world of thine,
But its nights are cold;
And the sun that makes it fine
Makes us soon so old!
Long its shadows grow and dim﻿—
Father, take us back with him!

1891.

===Chinese===

年轻人去追寻强壮、
美丽与勇敢，多好！
我们这些老人，正温顺地
一路走向坟墓，
只向你献上敬意，
永恒之全体的小孩！

我们曾是年轻人，如今老了，
而且越来越老；
我们是已被唱过的歌，
是已被讲过的故事；
是被风吹向你的黄叶，
永恒的童年！

若我们骤然靠近，
看哪，地上的婴孩会啼哭，
因为我们苍白凄惶的脸上
有这样枯萎的眼睛！
你，天父的孩子，却不转脸
离开那些满带皱纹祈祷的人！

用你的嘴和你恩惠的眼
向我们微笑；
向我们寒冷的北地吹你的南风。
融化这冻僵的脸：
童年全都从你涌流——
把我们老年的雪融成歌。

白发的孩子们成群而来，
向你、他们的盼望致意：
裹住我们脚步的
是襁褓还是寿衣？
长子啊，阴影渐浓：
带这些老去的孩子们回家。

我们已经玩够了，
树林变得凄清；
许多在破晓时分
与我们同来这里的人——
他们已从眼前消失，
去迎见那将临的光！

你造的外面世界虽美，
它的夜晚却冷；
使它明媚的太阳
使我们这么快变老！
它的影子越拉越长越暗——
父啊，带我们与他同归！

1891.

## Christmas Meditation / 圣诞默想
===Original===

He who by a mother’s love
Made the wandering world his own,
Every year comes from above,
Comes the parted to atone,
Binding Earth to the Father’s throne.

Nay, thou comest every day!
No, thou never didst depart!
Never hour hast been away!
Always with us, Lord, thou art,
Binding, binding heart to heart!

===Chinese===

他借着一位母亲的爱，
将流离的世界收归己有，
年年从高天降临，
使隔绝的得与神和好，
将大地系于父的宝座。

不，你天天都来！
不，你从未离去！
没有一个时辰离开过！
主（Lord）啊，你总与我们同在，
系连着，系连着心与心！

## The Old Castle / 古堡
===Original===

The brother knew well the castle old,
Every closet, each outlook fair,
Every turret and bartizan bold,
Every chamber, garnished or bare.
The brother was out in the heavenly air;
Little ones lost the starry way,
Wandered down the dungeon stair.
The brother missed them, and on the clay
Of the dungeon-floor he found them all.
Up they jumped when they heard him call!
He led the little ones into the day﻿—
Out and up to the sunshine gay,
Up to the father’s own door-sill﻿—
In at the father’s own room door,
There to be merry and work and play,
There to come and go at their will,
Good boys and girls to be lost no more!

===Chinese===

哥哥熟悉那座古堡，
每个小室，每处眺望的风景，
每座角楼与凸出的挑台，
每间屋子，或华饰或空敞。
哥哥出外，正身处属天的清气里；
小小孩童们迷了星光的路，
一路误下了地牢的阶梯。
哥哥不见了他们，在牢底
泥地上把他们全都寻见。
他们听见他呼唤，一跃而起！
他领着小小孩童们走进白昼——
走出、升上欢畅的日光，
升到父亲自家的门槛——
跨进父亲自家的房门，
在那里欢欣、做工、游戏，
在那里随心来去自如，
好男孩好女孩，从此不再走失！

## Christmas Prayer / 圣诞祷告
===Original===

Cold my heart, and poor, and low,
Like thy stable in the rock;
Do not let it orphan go,
It is of thy parent stock!
Come thou in, and it will grow
High and wide, a fane divine;
Like the ruby it will glow,
Like the diamond shine!

===Chinese===

我的心冷，贫寒，低矮，
像你岩洞里的马厩；
别让它孤零零地离去，
它是出于你的血脉！
你进来，它就会长得
高广，成为神圣的殿宇；
它会像红宝石般发亮，
像钻石般闪耀！

## Song of the Innocents / 诸圣婴孩之歌
===Original===

Merry, merry we well may be,
For Jesus Christ is come down to see:
Long before, at the top of the stair,
He set our angels a waiting there,
Waiting hither and thither to fly,
Tending the children of the sky,
Lest they dash little feet against big stones,
And tumble down and break little bones;
For the path is rough, and we must not roam;
We have learned to walk, and must follow him home!

===Chinese===

欢欣，欢欣，我们尽可以快乐，
因为耶稣基督已经下来看望我们：
早先，在阶梯的顶端，
他就派定我们的天使在那里等候，
随时准备飞东飞西，
看顾这些属天的孩子，
免得他们小脚撞上大石头，
跌一跤摔断小小的骨头；
因为路径崎岖，我们不可乱跑；
我们已学会走路，必得跟随他回家！

## Christmas Day and Every Day / 圣诞日与每一日
===Original===

Star high,
Baby low:
’Twixt the two
Wise men go;
Find the baby,
Grasp the star﻿—
Heirs of all things
Near and far!

===Chinese===

星在高天，
婴孩在低处：
智者在这两者间
上下求索；
寻见婴孩，
握住星辰——
便是近处远处
万物的主嗣！

## Rondel / 回旋诗
===Original===

I follow, tottering, in the funeral train
That bears my body to the welcoming grave.
As those I mourn not, that entomb the brave,
But smile as those that lay aside the vain;

To me it is a thing of poor disdain,
A clod I would not give a sigh to save!
I follow, careless, in the funeral train,
My outworn raiment to the cleansing grave.

I follow to the grave with growing pain﻿—
Then sudden cry: Let Earth take what she gave!
And turn in gladness from the yawning cave﻿—
Glad even for those whose tears yet flow amain:
They also follow, in their funeral train,
Outworn necessities to the welcoming grave!

===Chinese===

我蹒跚地跟在送葬的队伍里，
它载着我的身体去往迎候的坟墓。
我不像安葬勇士的人们那样哀恸，
而是像放下虚荣的人那样微笑；

对我，它是一件不足恋的东西，
一块土坷垃，我不愿叹一口气去挽留！
我淡然地跟在送葬的队伍里，
把穿旧的外袍送去洁净的坟墓。

我走向坟墓，忧伤渐渐上涌——
随即忽然呼喊：让大地收回她的馈赠！
便欣喜地转身，离开张口的墓穴——
甚至为那些还在泪如泉涌的人欢喜：
他们也跟着各自的送葬队伍，
把穿旧了的必需品送进迎候的坟墓！

## A Prayer / 祷告
===Original===

*When I Look Back Upon My Life Nigh Spent*

When I look back upon my life nigh spent,
Nigh spent, although the stream as yet flows on,
I more of follies than of sins repent,
Less for offence than Love’s shortcomings moan.
With self, O Father, leave me not alone﻿—
Leave not with the beguiler the beguiled;
Besmirched and ragged, Lord, take back thine own:
A fool I bring thee to be made a child.

===Chinese===

*当我回望这将近耗尽的一生*

当我回望这将近耗尽的一生——
溪流虽仍在流淌，它已近耗尽，
我悔恨的，愚行多于罪愆，
哀叹爱的亏缺，多于过犯。
父啊，别把我独自留给自我——
别把受骗的留给行骗的；
污损褴褛的，主（Lord）啊，收回你自己的：
我带一个愚人来，求你使他成为孩童。

## Home from the Wars / 战罢归家
===Original===

A tattered soldier, gone the glow and gloss,
With wounds half healed, and sorely trembling knee,
Homeward I come, to claim no victory-cross:
I only faced the foe, and did not flee.

===Chinese===

一个衣衫褴褛的士兵，光华与光润都已褪尽，
带着半愈的伤口和颤抖不止的膝盖，
我归家来，不图什么胜利的十字勋章：
我只是面对了仇敌，没有逃跑。

## God; Not Gift / 是上帝，而非恩赐
===Original===

Gray clouds my heaven have covered o’er;
My sea ebbs fast, no more to flow;
Ghastly and dry, my desert shore
Parched, bare, unsightly things doth show.

’Tis thou, Lord, cloudest up my sky;
Stillest the heart-throb of my sea;
Tellest the sad wind not to sigh,
Yea, life itself to wait for thee!

Lord, here I am, empty enough!
My music but a soundless moan!
Blind hope, of all my household stuff,
Leaves me, blind hope, not quite alone!

Shall hope too go, that I may trust
Purely in thee, and spite of all?
Then turn my very heart to dust﻿—
On thee, on thee, I yet will call.

List! list! his wind among the pines
Hark! hark! that rushing is his sea’s!
O Father, these are but thy signs!﻿—
For thee I hunger, not for these!

Not joy itself, though pure and high﻿—
No gift will do instead of thee!
Let but my spirit know thee nigh,
And all the world may sleep for me!

===Chinese===

灰云把我的一片天遮满；
我的海急退，不再涨潮；
凄惨干涸，我荒漠的岸上
露出焦渴、赤裸、丑陋的东西。

是你，主啊，使我的天昏暗；
使我海的搏动归于止息；
吩咐忧伤的风不要叹息，
甚至叫生命本身等候你！

主啊，我在这里，够空了！
我的音乐只是无声的呻吟！
盲目的盼望——我家仅存的家当——
留下我，盲目的盼望，不至于全然孤单！

连盼望也要离去吗，好叫我
纯然信你，不顾一切？
那就把我这颗心化为尘土——
我仍要呼求你，呼求你。

听啊！听啊！他的风穿过松林；
看哪！看哪！那奔腾是他的海！
父啊，这些不过是你的记号！——
我饥渴的是你，不是这些！

连喜乐本身，纵然纯净高远——
没有任何恩赐能代替你！
只要我的灵知道你临近，
整个世界都可以为我安睡！

## To Any Friend / 致任何朋友
===Original===

If I did seem to you no more
Than to myself I seem,
Not thus you would fling wide the door,
And on the beggar beam!

You would not don your radiant best,
Or dole me more than half!
Poor palmer I, no angel guest;
A shaking reed my staff!

At home, no rich fruit, hanging low,
Have I for Love to pull;
Only unripe things that must grow
Till Autumn’s maund be full!

But I forsake my niggard leas,
My orchard, too late hoar,
And wander over lands and seas
To find the Father’s door.

When I have reached the ancestral farm,
Have clomb the steepy hill,
And round me rests the Father’s arm,
Then think me what you will.

===Chinese===

倘若我在你眼中
不过如我在自己眼中那般，
你就不会这样敞开大门，
对这乞丐满目含情！

你不会穿上你最光鲜的衣裳，
也不会分我多于一半的茶点！
我只是可怜的朝圣客，不是天使贵宾；
一根颤抖的芦苇是我手杖！

在家里，没有低垂的丰美果实
可供爱来采摘；
只有尚未成熟、必须生长
直到秋篮满盈的青果！

但我撇下我那吝啬的草地，
撇下我迟霜的果园，
漂泊过陆地与海洋
去寻找天父的家门。

等我到了那祖传的田庄，
爬上那陡峭的山坡，
父的臂膀环抱我安歇，
那时你随怎么想我都行。

## Winter Song / 冬日之歌
===Original===

They were parted then at last?
Was it duty, or force, or fate?
Or did a worldly blast
Blow-to the meeting-gate?

An old, short story is this!
A glance, a trembling, a sigh,
A gaze in the eyes, a kiss﻿—
Why will it not go by!

===Chinese===

他们终究还是被拆散了？
是责任，是强力，还是命运？
还是一阵世俗的狂风，
把相会之门砰然吹闭？

这是一个古老而短小的故事！
一瞥，一阵颤栗，一声叹息，
一次眼底的凝望，一个吻——
它为什么就是不肯过去！

## At My Window After Sunset / 日落后在我窗前
===Original===

Heaven and the sea attend the dying day,
And in their sadness overflow and blend﻿—
Faint gold, and windy blue, and green and gray:
Far out amid them my pale soul I send.

For, as they mingle, so mix life and death;
An hour draws near when my day too will die;
Already I forecast unheaving breath,
Eviction on the moorland of yon sky.

Coldly and sadly lone, unhoused, alone,
Twixt wind-broke wave and heaven’s uncaring space!
At board and hearth from this time forth unknown!
Refuge no more in wife or daughter’s face!

Cold, cold and sad, lone as that desert sea!
Sad, lonely, as that hopeless, patient sky!
Forward I cannot go, nor backward flee!
I am not dead; I live, and cannot die!

Where are ye, loved ones, hither come before?
Did you fare thus when first ye came this way?
Somewhere there must be yet another door!﻿—
A door in somewhere from this dreary gray!

Come walking over watery hill and glen,
Or stoop your faces through yon cloud perplext;
Come, any one of dearest, sacred ten,
And bring me patient hoping for the next.

Maker of heaven and earth, father of me,
My words are but a weak, fantastic moan!
Were I a land-leaf drifting on the sea,
Thou still wert with me; I were not alone!

I am in thee, O father, lord of sky,
And lord of waves, and lord of human souls!
In thee all precious ones to me more nigh
Than if they rushing came in radiant shoals!

I shall not be alone although I die,
And loved ones should delay their coming long;
Though I saw round me nought but sea and sky,
Bare sea and sky would wake a holy song.

They are thy garments; thou art near within,
Father of fathers, friend-creating friend!
Thou art for ever, therefore I begin;
Thou lov’st, therefore my love shall never end!

Let loose thy giving, father, on thy child;
I pray thee, father, give me everything;
Give me the joy that makes the children wild;
Give throat and heart an old new song to sing.

Ye are my joy, great father, perfect Christ,
And humble men of heart, oh, everywhere!
With all the true I keep a hoping tryst;
Eternal love is my eternal prayer.

1890.

===Chinese===

天空与大海送别垂死的日子，
在共有的忧伤里漫溢交融——
淡金、风吹的蓝、绿与灰：
我把苍白的灵魂送往它们的远处。

因为正如它们交融，生与死也相混；
我的日子也将死去，那时辰已近；
我已预感到不再起伏的呼吸，
预感被逐到那边天空的荒原。

寒冷凄凉的孤独，无家，无伴，
在被风折断的浪与上苍冷漠的虚空之间！
从此在餐桌与炉边成了一个陌生人！
妻子的脸、女儿的脸不再是避难所！

冷，又冷又凄凉，孤零如那荒凉的海！
忧伤，孤独，如那无望而坚忍的天空！
我向前去不得，向后逃不得！
我没有死；我活着，又死不了！

你们在哪里，先我而来的亲爱的人？
你们初走这条路时，也是这般光景吗？
某处必定还有另一扇门！——
某处有一扇门，通出这凄清的灰暗！

来吧，走过水漫的山峦与幽谷，
或者从那困惑的云端俯下你们的脸；
来吧，最亲爱、最神圣的十人中任何一个，
带给我耐心，好等待下一位。

造天地的主，我的父，
我的话不过是软弱离奇的呻吟！
我纵然是一片漂在海上的陆地叶子，
你仍与我同在；我并不孤单！

我在你里面，父啊，天空之主，
波浪之主，人类灵魂之主！
在你里面，我一切珍爱的人都离我更近，
胜过他们成群结队、光辉灿烂地奔赴而来！

虽然我死，我也不会孤单，
纵然亲爱的人迟迟不来；
纵然我四顾只看见海与天，
赤裸的海与天也会唤醒一支圣歌。

它们是你的衣裳；你就在近处里面，
万父之父，创造朋友的朋友！
你永在，所以我要重新开始；
你爱，所以我的爱永不止息！

父啊，把你的给予释放在你孩子身上；
我求你，父啊，把一切都给我；
给我那使孩子们欢腾的喜乐；
给喉咙和心一首古老而新颖的歌。

你们是我的喜乐，伟大的父，完全的基督，
还有心里谦卑的人，哦，在各处！
我与一切真实者守着盼望之约；
永恒的爱是我永恒的祷告。

1890.

## A Father to a Mother / 父亲对母亲说
===Original===

When God’s own child came down to earth,
High heaven was very glad;
The angels sang for holy mirth;
Not God himself was sad!

Shall we, when ours goes homeward, fret?
Come, Hope, and wait on Sorrow!
The little one will not forget;
It’s only till to-morrow!

===Chinese===

当上帝亲生的孩子降世，
高天欢喜异常；
天使们为圣洁的欢愉歌唱；
连上帝自己也不悲伤！

我们的孩子归天家时，我们还要忧愁吗？
来吧，盼望，来服事忧伤！
那小家伙不会忘记；
那不过是等到明天！

## The Temple of God / 上帝的殿
===Original===

In the desert by the bush,
Moses to his heart said “Hush.”

David on his bed did pray;
God all night went not away.

From his heap of ashes foul
Job to God did lift his soul,

God came down to see him there,
And to answer all his prayer.

On a dark hill, in the wind,
Jesus did his father find,

But while he on earth did fare,
Every spot was place of prayer;

And where man is any day,
God can not be far away.

But the place he loveth best,
Place where he himself can rest,

Where alone he prayer doth seek,
Is the spirit of the meek.

To the humble God doth come;
In his heart he makes his home.

===Chinese===

旷野里，在焚棘旁，
摩西对自己的心说：「安静。」

大卫在床上祷告；
上帝整夜未曾离开。

约伯从污秽的灰堆
向上帝举起灵魂，

上帝下来到那里看他，
应允他全部的祷告。

在一座暗山上，在风中，
耶稣寻见了他的父，

但他在世上行走的时候，
每一处都是祷告之地；

人无论哪天在哪里，
上帝都不会离得太远。

但他最喜爱的居所，
他自己能安歇的地方，

他唯独寻求祷告之处，
是温柔人的心灵。

上帝来到谦卑者那里；
在他心里安家。

## Going to Sleep / 入睡
===Original===

Little one, you must not fret
That I take your clothes away;
Better sleep you so will get,
And at morning wake more gay﻿—
Saith the children’s mother.

You I must unclothe again,
For you need a better dress;
Too much worn are body and brain;
You need everlastingness﻿—
Saith the heavenly father.

I went down death’s lonely stair;
Laid my garments in the tomb;
Dressed again one morning fair;
Hastened up, and hied me home﻿—
Saith the elder brother.

Then I will not be afraid
Any ill can come to me;
When ’tis time to go to bed,
I will rise and go with thee﻿—
Saith the little brother.

===Chinese===

小宝贝，你不必烦恼，
我拿走你的衣裳；
这样你会睡得更好，
早晨醒来更欢畅——
孩子的母亲说。

我必须再为你脱一次衣，
因为你需要更好的衣裳；
身体和头脑都已磨损太多；
你需要的是永恒——
天上的父亲说。

我走下死亡孤寂的楼梯；
把我的衣服留在坟墓里；
一个晴朗的早晨重新穿好；
急忙起身，赶回家去——
长兄说。

那么我就不再害怕
会有什么灾祸临到我；
到了该上床的时候，
我就起身跟你走——
小弟弟说。

## To-Morrow / 明天
===Original===

My to-morrow is but a flitting
Fancy of the brain;
God’s to-morrow an angel sitting,
Ready for joy or pain.

My to-morrow has no soul,
Dead as yesterdays;
God’s﻿—a brimming silver bowl
Of life that gleams and plays.

My to-morrow, I mock you away!
Shadowless nothing, thou!
God’s to-morrow, come, dear day,
For God is in thee now.

===Chinese===

我的明天不过是脑中
飞掠的一缕幻想；
上帝的明天是一位端坐的天使，
预备好迎接喜乐或忧伤。

我的明天没有灵魂，
同昨天一样死寂；
上帝的明天是一只盈满的银碗，
盛着闪烁跃动的生命。

我的明天，我嘲笑着把你赶走！
你这无影的虚空！
上帝的明天，来吧，亲爱的一天，
因为上帝如今就在你里面。

## Foolish Children / 愚昧的孩子们
===Original===

Waking in the night to pray,
Sleeping when the answer comes,
Foolish are we even at play﻿—
Tearfully we beat our drums!
Cast the good dry bread away,
Weep, and gather up the crumbs!

“Evermore,” while shines the day,
“Lord,” we cry, “thy will be done!”
Soon as evening groweth gray,
Thy fair will we fain would shun!
“Take, oh, take thy hand away!
See the horrid dark begun!”

“Thou hast conquered Death,” we say,
“Christ, whom Hades could not keep!”
Then, “Ah, see the pallid clay!
Death it is,” we cry, “not sleep!
Grave, take all. Shut out the Day.
Sit we on the ground and weep!”

Gathering potsherds all the day,
Truant children, Lord, we roam;
Fret, and longer want to play,
When at cool thy voice doth come!﻿—
Elder Brother, lead the way;
Make us good as we go home.

===Chinese===

夜里醒来祷告，
应答来到时却睡着了，
连玩耍时我们也愚昧——
我们含泪敲着鼓！
把好好的干面包丢掉，
哭着去拾碎渣！

白日放光时，我们「永远」
呼喊：「主啊，愿你的旨意成就！」
天色一转灰暗，
我们便想躲开你美善的旨意！
「拿开，哦，拿开你的手！
看那可怕的黑暗开始了！」

「你已经战胜死亡，」我们说，
「基督，阴间关不住你！」
转眼却喊：「啊，看那苍白的泥土！
这是死，」我们哭道，「不是睡！
坟墓啊，把一切都拿去吧。关掉白昼。
我们坐在地上哭吧！」

整日捡拾破陶片，
逃学的孩子，主啊，我们游荡；
你清凉时分的呼声来到，
我们还烦躁，还想多玩！——
长兄啊，为我们领路；
在回家的路上把我们变好。

## Love Is Home / 爱就是家
===Original===

Love is the part, and love is the whole;
Love is the robe, and love is the pall;
Ruler of heart and brain and soul,
Love is the lord and the slave of all!
I thank thee, Love, that thou lov’st me;
I thank thee more that I love thee.

Love is the rain, and love is the air,
Love is the earth that holdeth fast;
Love is the root that is buried there,
Love is the open flower at last!
I thank thee, Love all round about,
That the eyes of my love are looking out.

Love is the sun, and love is the sea;
Love is the tide that comes and goes;
Flowing and flowing it comes to me;
Ebbing and ebbing to thee it flows!
Oh my sun, and my wind, and tide!
My sea, and my shore, and all beside!

Light, oh light that art by showing;
Wind, oh wind that liv’st by motion;
Thought, oh thought that art by knowing;
Will, that art born in self-devotion!
Love is you, though not all of you know it;
Ye are not love, yet ye always show it!

Faithful creator, heart-longed-for father,
Home of our heart-infolded brother,
Home to thee all thy glories gather﻿—
All are thy love, and there is no other!
O Love-at-rest, we loves that roam﻿—
Home unto thee, we are coming home!

===Chinese===

爱是部分，爱也是全部；
爱是华服，爱也是殓衣；
统管心、脑与灵魂的
爱，是万有的主宰，也是万有的奴仆！
爱你，我感谢你，因你爱我；
更感谢你，因我爱你。

爱是雨，爱是空气，
爱是紧紧把握的大地；
爱是埋在土里的根，
爱是终于绽放的花！
感谢你，四围环绕的爱，
因我爱的那双眼正向外凝望。

爱是太阳，爱是海洋；
爱是来来去去的潮汐；
它涨了又涨，涌向我；
退了又退，流向你！
哦，我的太阳，我的风，我的潮！
我的海，我的岸，和我身畔的一切！

光啊，以照耀而存在的光；
风啊，以流动而活着的风；
思想啊，以认知而成立的思想；
意志啊，生于自我奉献的意志！
爱就是你们，虽然你们并非全都知晓；
你们不是爱，却总把爱显明！

信实的创造者，心灵渴慕的父亲，
我们心中怀抱的弟兄的家园，
家园啊，你一切的荣耀都归聚于此——
一切都出于你的爱，此外别无其他！
哦，安息的爱，我们这些漂泊的爱——
归向你，归向你，我们正在回家！

## Faith / 信心
===Original===

Earth, if aught should check thy race,
Rushing through unfended space,
Headlong, stayless, thou wilt fall
Into yonder glowing ball!”

“Beggar of the universe,
Faithless as an empty purse!
Sent abroad to cool and tame,
Think’st I fear my native flame?”

“If thou never on thy track
Turn thee round and hie thee back,
Thou wilt wander evermore,
Outcast, cold﻿—a comet hoar!”

“While I sweep my ring along
In an air of joyous song,
Thou art drifting, heart awry,
From the sun of liberty!”

===Chinese===

「地球啊，若有什么拦住你的奔行，
当你冲过无遮蔽的太空，
你会头也不回、无可挽回地
坠入那边燃烧的火球！」

「宇宙的乞丐，
像空钱袋一样无信！
我被派到外面来冷却驯服，
你以为我怕我本源的火焰？」

「你若从不在自己的轨道上
转身归回，
你将永远流浪，
被弃、冰冷——一颗灰白的彗星！」

「当我在欢歌的气息里
扫过我的环轨，
你却心志歪斜地漂离，
离开那自由的太阳！」

## Waiting / 等候
===Original===

*I Waited for the Master*

I waited for the Master
In the darkness dumb;
Light came fast and faster﻿—
My light did not come!

I waited all the daylight,
All through noon’s hot flame:
In the evening’s gray light,
Lo, the Master came!

===Chinese===

*我等候夫子（the Master）*

我在喑哑的黑暗里
等候夫子；
光来得越来越快——
我的光却迟迟不来！

我等候了一整个白昼，
穿过正午灼热的火焰：
在暮色灰蒙的光里，
看哪，夫子来了！

## Our Ship / 我们的船
===Original===

Had I a great ship coming home,
With big plunge o’er the sea,
What bright things, hid from star and foam,
Lay in her heart for thee!

The stormy billows heave and dip,
The wild winds veer and play;
But, regnant all, God’s stately ship
Is steering home this way!

===Chinese===

若我有一艘巨轮归航，
一路劈波越海而来，
多少明亮的珍宝，避于星与浪沫之外，
安放在她心中给你！

风暴的巨浪起伏翻涌，
狂风转向嬉戏；
但统御一切的，是上帝庄严的船，
正朝这边驶向家乡！

## My Heart Thy Lark / 我心，你的云雀
===Original===

Why dost thou want to sing
When thou hast no song, my heart?
If there be in thee a hidden spring,
Wherefore will no word start?

On its way thou hearest no song,
Yet flutters thy unborn joy!
The years of thy life are growing long﻿—
Art still the heart of a boy?﻿—

Father, I am thy child!
My heart is in thy hand!
Let it hear some echo, with gladness wild,
Of a song in thy high land.

It will answer﻿—but how, my God,
Thou knowest; I cannot say:
It will spring, I know, thy lark, from thy sod﻿—
Thy lark to meet thy day!

===Chinese===

你既没有歌，我的心啊，
为什么还想要歌唱？
若你里面藏着一眼泉，
为什么涌不出一句言辞？

一路上你听不见歌声，
你未生的喜乐却扇动翅膀！
你的生命之年渐渐长了——
你还是一颗少年的心吗？——

父啊，我是你的孩子！
我的心握在你手中！
愿它听见某个回声，怀着狂喜，
来自你高天国度的歌。

它会应答——但如何应答，我的神，
你知道；我说不出：
它必跃起，我知道，作你的云雀，从你的草地——
你的云雀，去迎接你的白日！

## Two in One / 二而一
===Original===

Were thou and I the white pinions
On some eager, heaven-born dove,
Swift would we mount to the old dominions,
To our rest of old, my love!

Were thou and I trembling strands
In music’s enchanted line,
We would wait and wait for magic hands
To untwist the magic twine.

Were we two sky-tints, thou and I,
Thou the golden, I the red;
We would quiver and glow and darken and die,
And love until we were dead!

Nearer than wings of one dove,
Than tones or colours in chord,
We are one﻿—and safe, and for ever, my love,
Two thoughts in the heart of one Lord.

===Chinese===

倘若你我是那白色的羽翼，
长在某只急切、天生的鸽子上，
我们会迅疾飞升到那古老的疆土，
回到我们旧日的安息，我的爱人！

倘若你我是颤抖的琴弦，
拧在音乐施了魔法的线上，
我们会一直等待，等待神奇的手
来解开这魔法的缠结。

倘若我们是两片天色，你和我，
你是金色，我是红色；
我们会颤动、发光、转暗、消逝，
爱到我们死去！

比一只鸽子的双翼更近，
比和弦中的音与色更亲，
我们已合而为一——安稳，直到永远，我的爱人，
是一位主心里的两个意念。

## Bedtime / 就寝时光
===Original===

Come, children, put away your toys;
Roll up that kite’s long line;
The day is done for girls and boys﻿—
Look, it is almost nine!
Come, weary foot, and sleepy head,
Get up, and come along to bed.”

The children, loath, must yet obey;
Up the long stair they creep;
Lie down, and something sing or say
Until they fall asleep,
To steal through caverns of the night
Into the morning’s golden light.

We, elder ones, sit up more late,
And tasks unfinished ply,
But, gently busy, watch and wait﻿—
Dear sister, you and I,
To hear the Father, with soft tread,
Coming to carry us to bed.

===Chinese===

来吧，孩子们，把玩具收好；
把那只风筝的长线卷起；
女孩男孩们，一天结束了——
看，快到九点啦！
来吧，疲倦的小脚，昏睡的小脑袋，
起身，跟着上床去。

孩子们虽不情愿，还是得听从；
他们爬上长长的楼梯；
躺下来，唱点什么或说点什么，
直到沉沉睡去，
悄悄穿过黑夜的洞穴，
潜入清晨金色的光里。

我们这些年长的，坐得更晚，
手中还做着未完的事，
却温柔地忙碌着，守望等候——
亲爱的姐妹，你和我，
要听见父踏着轻柔的脚步，
前来抱我们上床。

## A Prayer / 祷告
===Original===

*Thou Who Mad’st the Mighty Clock*

Thou who mad’st the mighty clock
Of the great world go;
Mad’st its pendulum swing and rock,
Ceaseless to and fro;
Thou whose will doth push and draw
Every orb in heaven,
Help me move by higher law
In my spirit graven.

Like a planet let me swing﻿—
With intention strong;
In my orbit rushing sing
Jubilant along;
Help me answer in my course
To my seasons due;
Lord of every stayless force,
Make my Willing true.

===Chinese===

*你造了这巨大的钟*

你使这大世界
这座巨钟走动；
你使它的钟摆摇摆晃荡，
不息地来回往复；
你以意志推动牵引
天上的每个星体，
求你助我按更高的律法运行，
它铭刻在我灵里。

让我像一颗行星运转——
怀着坚定的意向；
在我的轨道上疾驰，一路
欢腾地放声歌唱；
助我在行程中
应合我当令的季节；
每个不止息之力量的主啊，
使我的愿欲成真。

## A Song Prayer / 歌之祷告
===Original===

Lord Jesus,
Oh, ease us
Of Self that oppresses,
Annoys and distresses
Body and brain
With dull pain!

Thou never,
Since ever,
Save one moment only,
Wast left, or wast lonely:
We are alone,
And make moan.

Far parted,
Dull-hearted,
We wander, sleep-walking,
Mere shadows, dim-stalking:
Orphans we roam,
Far from home.

Oh new man,
Sole human,
God’s son, and our brother,
Give each to the other﻿—
No one left out
In cold doubt!

High Father,
Oh gather
Thy sons and thy daughters,
Through fires and through waters,
Home to the nest
Of thy breast!

There under
The wonder
Of great wings of healing,
Of love and revealing,
Teach us anew
To sing true.

===Chinese===

主（Lord）耶稣啊，
求你宽解我们，
除去那压制的「自我」，
它烦扰、磨折
身体与头脑，
以钝钝的疼痛！

你从未——
自永远以来——
除了一霎那时，
被撇下，或孤寂：
而我们孤单，
徒自悲叹。

远离暌隔，
心神钝滞，
我们游荡，如梦游一般，
只是暗影，昏昏潜行：
我们如孤儿漂泊，
远离家园。

哦新人，
独一真人，
神的儿子，我们的弟兄，
把我们彼此相赐——
别让一人被撇下，
在冰冷的疑惑里！

高天的父啊，
求你招聚
你的儿子和女儿，
经过火、经过水，
归回你
胸怀的巢！

在那里，在
医治的大翼、
爱与启示的
奇妙荫下，
重新教导我们
唱真实的歌。

## Reciprocity / 互爱
===Original===

Her mother, Elfie older grown,
One evening, for adieu,
Said, “You’ll not mind being left alone,
For God takes care of you!”

In child-way her heart’s eye did see
The correlation’s node:
“Yes,” she said, “God takes care o’ me,
An’ I take care o’ God.”

The child and woman were the same,
She changed not, only grew;
’Twixt God and her no shadow came:
The true is always true!

As daughter, sister, promised wife,
Her heart with love did brim:
Now, sure, it brims as full of life,
Hid fourteen years in him!

1892.

===Chinese===

埃尔菲长大了些，一天晚上，
她的母亲道晚安告别时说：
「你一个人留下不会介意吧，
因为有上帝看顾你！」

她的心眼以孩子的方式
看见了那关联的结点：
「是的，」她说，「上帝看顾我，
我也看顾上帝。」

孩子和女人是同一个人，
她没有变，只是长大；
上帝与她之间没有阴影来临：
真的永远是真的！

作女儿、作姊妹、作订了婚的妻子，
她的心满溢着爱：
如今，它必定仍满溢着生命，
已在他里面藏了十四年！

1892.

## What the Lord Saith / 主所说的话
===Original===

Trust my father, saith the eldest-born;
I did trust him ere the earth began;
Not to know him is to be forlorn;
Not to love him is﻿—not to be man.

He that knows him loves him altogether;
With my father I am so content
That through all this dreary human weather
I am working, waiting, confident.

He is with me; I am not alone;
Life is bliss, because I am his child;
Down in Hades will I lay the stone
Whence shall rise to Heaven his city piled.

Hearken, brothers, pray you, to my story!
Hear me, sister; hearken, child, to me:
Our one father is a perfect glory;
He is light, and there is none but he.

Come then with me; I will lead the way;
All of you, sore-hearted, heavy-shod,
Come to father, yours and mine, I pray;
Little ones, I pray you, come to God!

===Chinese===

信靠我的父，长子说；
大地开始之前我就信靠他；
不认识他就是孤苦无依；
不爱他——就不算为人。

认识他的人必全然爱他；
我与我的父如此相契，
以致穿过这一切凄凉的人间风雨，
我仍做工、等候、满怀信心。

他与我同在；我并不孤单；
生命是福乐，因为我是他的孩子；
我要在阴间安放那基石，
他的城将从那里升起，高筑到天。

听啊，兄弟们，请听我的故事！
听我说，姊妹；孩子，听我说：
我们独一的父是完全的荣耀；
他是光，除他别无其他。

那就跟我来吧；我为你领路；
你们所有心伤、步履沉重的人，
来吧，到你的、也是我的父这里来，我恳求；
小孩子们啊，我求你们，归向上帝！

## How Shall He Sing Who Hath No Song / 没有歌的人怎能歌唱
===Original===

How shall he sing who hath no song?
He laugh who hath no mirth?
Will cannot wake the sleeping song!
Yea, Love itself in vain may long
To sing with them that have a song,
Or, mirthless, laugh with Mirth!
He who would sing but hath no song
Must speak the right, denounce the wrong,
Must humbly front the indignant throng,
Must yield his back to Satire’s thong,
Nor shield his face from liar’s prong,
Must say and do and be the truth,
And fearless wait for what ensueth,
Wait, wait, with patience sweet and strong,
Until God’s glory fill the earth;
Then shall he sing who had no song,
He laugh who had no mirth!

Yea, if in land of stony dearth
Like barren rock thou sit,
Round which the phantom-waters flit
Of heart- and brain-mirage
That can no thirst assuage,
Yet be thou still, and wait, wait long;
A right sea comes to drown the wrong;
God’s glory comes to fill the earth,
And thou, no more a scathed rock,
Shalt start alive with gladsome shock,
Shalt a hand-clapping billow be,
And shout with the eternal sea!

To righteousness and love belong
The dance, the jubilance, the song,
When the great Right hath quelled the wrong,
And Truth hath stilled the lying tongue!
Then men must sing because of song,
And laugh because of mirth!
And this shall be their anthem strong﻿—
Hallow! the glad God fills the earth,
And Love sits down by every hearth!

===Chinese===

没有歌的人怎能歌唱？
没有欢乐的人怎能欢笑？
意志唤不醒沉睡的歌！
是的，连爱本身也只能徒然渴望
与有歌的人一同歌唱，
或者，无欢地随欢乐而笑！
想歌唱却没有歌的人，
必须言说正理，指斥错谬，
必须谦卑地面对恼怒的众人，
必须把脊背交给讥讽的鞭笞，
不以手遮脸躲避说谎者的尖刺，
必须言真理、行真理、成为真理，
无畏地等候随之而来的一切，
等候，等候，怀着甘甜而刚强的忍耐，
直到上帝的荣耀充满全地；
那时，没有歌的人必歌唱，
没有欢乐的人必欢笑！

是的，你若坐在石头般贫瘠之地，
像一块荒岩，
心与脑的海市蜃楼
幻化出虚渺的水影，
在你四周流连，
却解不了丝毫干渴——
你仍要安静，等候，久久等候；
正义之海终将淹没邪恶；
上帝的荣耀必来充满全地，
而你，不再是那焦痕累累的岩石，
必在欢欣的震撼中苏醒过来，
化作一浪拍手的波涛，
与永恒的大海一同呼喊！

舞蹈、欢腾、歌声，
本属于公义与爱，
当大公义制服了邪恶，
真理使说谎的舌安静！
那时人必因有歌而不得不唱，
因有欢乐而不得不笑！
这将是他们刚强的颂歌——
圣哉！喜乐的上帝充满全地，
爱坐在每一个炉边！

## This World / 这个世界
===Original===

Thy world is made to fit thine own,
A nursery for thy children small,
The playground-footstool of thy throne,
Thy solemn school-room, Father of all!
When day is done, in twilight’s gloom,
We pass into thy presence-room.

Because from selfishness and wrath,
Our cold and hot extremes of ill,
We grope and stagger on the path﻿—
Thou tell’st us from thy holy hill,
With icy storms and sunshine rude,
That we are all unripe in good.

Because of snaky things that creep
Through our soul’s sea, dim-undulant,
Thou fill’st the mystery of thy deep
With faces heartless, grim, and gaunt;
That we may know how ugly seem
The things our spirit-oceans teem.

Because of half-way things that hold
Good names, and have a poisonous breath﻿—
Prudence that is but trust in gold,
And faith that is but fear of death﻿—
Amongst thy flowers, the lovely brood,
Thou sendest some that are not good.

Thou stay’st thy hand from finishing things
To make thy child love the complete;
Full many a flower comes up thy springs
Unshamed in imperfection sweet;
That through good all, and good in part,
Thy work be perfect in the heart.

Because, in careless confidence,
So oft we leave the narrow way,
Its borders thorny hedges fence,
Beyond them marshy deeps affray;
But farther on, the heavenly road
Lies through the gardens of our God.

Because thy sheep so often will
Forsake the meadow cool and damp
To climb the stony, grassless hill,
Or wallow in the slimy swamp,
Thy sicknesses, where’er they roam,
Go after them to bring them home.

One day, all fear, all ugliness,
All pain, all discord, dumb or loud,
All selfishness, and all distress,
Will melt like low-spread morning cloud,
And heart and brain be free from thrall,
Because thou, God, art all in all!

===Chinese===

你的世界是照你自己造的，
是你幼小儿女的育儿室，
是你宝座前的游戏脚凳，
是你庄重的课堂，万有之父！
一日事毕，在暮色昏暗里，
我们走进你的觐见室。

因为出于自私与暴怒，
我们一冷一热的两种极端之恶，
我们在路上摸索踉跄——
你从你的圣山告诉我们，
用冰冷的风暴与粗犷的骄阳：
我们在良善上都未成熟。

因为有大蛇般的东西游动
穿过我们灵魂之海，幽暗起伏，
你便以无情、狰狞、枯瘦的面孔
充满你深渊的奥秘；
好叫我们知道，我们灵之海洋
滋生的东西看来何等丑陋。

因为有半途的东西顶着
好名声，却吐着毒气——
那不过是对黄金之信靠的「谨慎」，
那不过是对死亡之恐惧的「信心」——
在你的花朵、那可爱的族群中间，
你也差来一些不好的。

你克制着手，不把万物做完，
好叫你的孩子爱慕完全；
你的春天里有许许多多花
带着甜美的不完善、坦然绽放；
好叫借着全部的善、与部分的善，
你的工作在心中得以完全。

因为我们漫不经心、自恃放胆，
常常离开那窄路，
它的边界围起荆棘的篱笆，
篱外是骇人的泥沼深潭；
但再往前去，那天上的路
正穿过我们上帝的花园。

因为你的羊群常常
撇下清凉湿润的草场，
去爬那多石无草的山丘，
或在黏滑的泥沼里打滚，
你的疾病便随处追着他们，
要把他们带回家中。

终有一天，一切恐惧，一切丑陋，
一切疼痛，一切或哑或响的不和，
一切自私，一切愁苦，
都会像低垂的晨云一样消融，
心和头脑都脱离奴役，
因为上帝啊，你是万有中的万有！

## Saint Peter / 圣彼得
===Original===

O Peter, wherefore didst thou doubt?
Indeed the spray flew fast about,
But he was there whose walking foot
Could make the wandering hills take root;
And he had said, “Come down to me,”
Else hadst thou not set foot on sea!
Christ did not call thee to thy grave!
Was it the boat that made thee brave?

“Easy for thee who wast not there
To think thou more than I couldst dare!
It hardly fits thee though to mock
Scared as thou wast that railway shock!
Who saidst this morn, ‘Wife, we must go﻿—
The plague will soon be here, I know!’
Who, when thy child slept﻿—not to death﻿—
Saidst, ‘Life is now not worth a breath!’ ”

Saint Peter, thou rebukest well!
It needs no tempest me to quell,
Not even a spent lash of its spray!
Things far too little to affray
Will wake the doubt that’s worst of all﻿—
Is there a God to hear me call?
But if he be, I never think
That he will hear and let me sink!

Lord of my little faith, my Lord,
Help me to fear nor fire nor sword;
Let not the cross itself appall
Which bore thee, Life and Lord of all;
Let reeling brain nor fainting heart
Wipe out the soreness that thou art;
Dwell farther in than doubt can go,
And make I hope become I know.

“Come to my side,” some stormy way,
My feet, atoning to thy will,
Shall, heaved and tossed, walk toward thee still;
No heart of lead shall sink me where
Prudence lies crowned with cold despair,
But I shall reach and clasp thy hand,
And on the sea forget the land!

===Chinese===

哦，彼得（Peter）啊，你为什么疑惑？
浪花固然四处疾飞，
但他就在那里，他行走的脚
能让游移的山岭扎根；
而且他说过：「下来到我这里来，」
否则你根本不会踏上海面！
基督不是叫你去赴坟墓！
难道是那条船给了你胆量？

「你不在场，自然容易
以为你比我更敢作敢为！
可你实在不该嘲笑我——
那回坐火车受了惊，你不也吓坏了！
今天早上是谁说的：『妻子，我们得走——
我知道瘟疫很快就要来了！』
孩子睡着时——并不是死了——
是谁说：『现在这条命连一口气都不值！』」

圣彼得啊，你责备得好！
压垮我用不着一场风暴，
甚至不用它衰竭的一鞭浪花！
远比这微不足道的小事
就会唤醒那最坏的疑惑——
到底有没有一位神听我呼求？
但若他存在，我绝不认为
他会听见却任我沉没！

我小小信心之主，我的主（Lord）啊，
帮助我既不惧火也不惧剑；
连那十字架也不叫我心惊——
它曾承载你，生命与万有之主；
别让眩晕的头脑或昏厥的心，
把你所受的酸痛抹去；
愿你住得比疑惑所能到达的更深，
把「我希望」变成「我知道」。

「到我这边来」——无论哪条风暴之路，
我的双脚，归顺你的旨意，
必在颠簸摇撼中依然向你走去；
没有铅沉的心能把我坠入
那谨慎盘踞、戴着冰冷绝望冠冕的深处，
我必要伸手抓住你的手，
在海面上忘掉陆地！

## Zacchaeus / 撒该
===Original===

To whom the heavy burden clings,
It yet may serve him like a staff;
One day the cross will break in wings,
The sinner laugh a holy laugh.

The dwarfed Zacchaeus climbed a tree,
His humble stature set him high;
The Lord the little man did see
Who sought the great man passing by.

Up to the tree he came, and stopped:
“To-day,” he said, “with thee I bide.”
A spirit-shaken fruit he dropped,
Ripe for the Master, at his side.

Sure never host with gladder look
A welcome guest home with him bore!
Then rose the Satan of rebuke
And loudly spake beside the door:

“This is no place for holy feet;
Sinners should house and eat alone!
This man sits in the stranger’s seat
And grinds the faces of his own!”

Outspoke the man, in Truth’s own might:
“Lord, half my goods I give the poor;
If one I’ve taken more than right
With four I make atonement sure!”

“Salvation here is entered in;
This man indeed is Abraham’s son!”
Said he who came the lost to win﻿—
And saved the lost whom he had won.

===Chinese===

重担缠身的人，
它或许仍能像手杖一样扶助他；
终有一天，十字架会破茧成翼，
罪人会发出圣洁的欢笑。

矮小的撒该爬上一棵树，
他卑微的身材把他举高；
主看见了那个小人——
他正寻觅那位路过的伟人。

他走到树前，停住脚步：
「今天，」他说，「我住在你家。」
一颗被灵摇动的果子落下来，
熟透了，正落在主人身旁。

从来没有任何一位主人
带着更欢喜的神色迎客还家！
这时，那责难的撒但
在门旁高声说道：

「这不是圣洁之足该踏的地方；
罪人应当独自吃住！
这人坐在陌生人的位上，
压榨自己同胞的脸面！」

那人凭真理的大能开口：
「主啊，我把一半家财给穷人；
我若讹诈了谁，就还他四倍，
作为确实的赔付！」

「救恩今天临到了这家；
这人真是亚伯拉罕的子孙！」
那来寻找迷失者的一位说——
并拯救了他所寻回的迷羊。

## After Thomas Kemp / 仿托马斯·阿·肯皮斯
===Original===

I

Who follows Jesus shall not walk
In darksome road with danger rife;
But in his heart the Truth will talk,
And on his way will shine the Life.

So, on the story we must pore
Of him who lives for us, and died,
That we may see him walk before,
And know the Father in the guide.

II

In words of truth Christ all excels,
Leaves all his holy ones behind;
And he in whom his spirit dwells
Their hidden manna sure shall find.

Gather wouldst thou the perfect grains,
And Jesus fully understand?
Thou must obey him with huge pains,
And to God’s will be as Christ’s hand.

III

What profits it to reason high
And in hard questions court dispute,
When thou dost lack humility,
Displeasing God at very root!

Profoundest words man ever spake
Not once of blame washed any clear;
A simple life alone could make
Nathanael to his master dear.

IV

The eye with seeing is not filled,
The ear with hearing not at rest;
Desire with having is not stilled;
With human praise no heart is blest.

Vanity, then, of vanities
All things for which men grasp and grope!
The precious things in heavenly eyes
Are love, and truth, and trust, and hope.

V

Better the clown who God doth love
Than he that high can go
And name each little star above
But sees not God below!

What if all things on earth I knew,
Yea, love were all my creed,
It serveth nothing with the True;
He goes by heart and deed.

VI

If thou dost think thy knowledge good,
Thy intellect not slow,
Bethink thee of the multitude
Of things thou dost not know.

Why look on any from on high
Because thou knowest more?
Thou need’st but look abroad, to spy
Ten thousand thee before.

Wouldst thou in knowledge true advance
And gather learning’s fruit,
In love confess thy ignorance,
And thy Self-love confute.

VII

This is the highest learning,
The hardest and the best﻿—
From self to keep still turning,
And honour all the rest.

If one should break the letter,
Yea, spirit of command,
Think not that thou art better,
Thou may’st not always stand!

We all are weak﻿—but weaker
Hold no one than thou art;
Then, as thou growest meeker,
Higher will go thy heart.

VIII

Sense and judgment oft indeed
Spy but little and mislead,
Ground us on a shelf!

Happy he whom Truth doth teach,
Not by forms of passing speech,
But her very self!

===Chinese===

I

跟从耶稣的人不会行走
在危机四伏的幽暗路上；
真理会在他心中说话，
生命会在他路上发光。

所以，我们必须细读
那位为我们死而活着者的故事，
好看见他行在前头，
并在引路者身上认识父。

II

在真实的言语上，基督超越众人，
把所有圣徒远远留在身后；
而那有他圣灵内住的人，
必寻见那隐藏的吗哪。

你想收取完美的谷粒，
想完全明白耶稣吗？
你必须竭尽全力顺服他，
作神旨意中基督的手。

III

高谈阔论有什么益处，
在难题上好争辩，
当你缺少谦卑，
从根本上不讨神的喜悦！

人说过的最深奥的话语，
也从未洗去谁的罪责；
唯有纯朴的生命
才能使拿但业被主人所爱。

IV

眼看，看不饱；
耳听，听不足；
欲望得了拥有也不止息；
人心得着人的称赞也不得福。

虚空啊，虚空的虚空——
人所攫取、摸索的一切！
在天眼看来宝贵的，
是爱、真理、信靠与盼望。

V

神所爱的乡野相人，胜过
那能登上高天
叫出每颗小星名字、
却看不见脚下之神的人！

纵然我知晓世上万事，
是的，连爱也成了我全部的信条，
在那真实者面前也毫无用处；
他看重的是心与行为。

VI

你若以为自己的知识不错，
头脑不算迟钝，
就想想那千千万万
你不知道的事吧。

为什么因知道得多，
就居高临下看人？
你只需放眼四望，就会看见
一万个走在你前面的人。

你想在真知识上长进，
收取学问的果实吗？
就要在爱中承认自己的无知，
驳倒你的自爱。

VII

这是最高的学问，
最艰难也最好——
不停地转离自我，
并敬重所有其他人。

若有人违犯了字句，
甚至诫命的精意，
别以为自己更好，
你也未必总能站立！

我们都软弱——但没有谁
比你更软弱；
这样，当你愈发谦和，
你的心也会升得愈高。

VIII

感官与判断，实在常常
只窥见一点，还引人入歧途，
把我们搁浅在暗礁上！

那人真有福——真理亲自教导他，
不是借着转瞬即逝的言辞形式，
而是借着真理自己！

===Original===

Why of hidden things dispute,
Mind unwise, howe’er astute,
Making that thy task
Where the Judge will, at the last,
When disputing all is past,
Not a question ask?

Folly great it is to brood
Over neither bad nor good,
Eyes and ears unheedful!
Ears and eyes, ah, open wide
For what may be heard or spied
Of the one thing needful!

===Chinese===

为什么为隐秘的事争辩，
不明智的心啊，无论多么精明，
竟把这当作你的职事——
而在最后，当一切争辩过去，
那审判者根本
不会问一句这样的事？

对那无所谓坏也无所谓好之事
苦苦思虑，眼耳却疏忽大意，
这是大大的愚昧！
耳朵和眼睛啊，要大大张开，
去听、去看那
唯一不可少的事！

## To Gordon, Leaving Khartoum / 致离开喀土穆的戈登
===Original===

The silence of traitorous feet!
The silence of close-pent rage!
The roar, and the sudden heart-beat!
And the shot through the true heart going,
The truest heart of the age!
And the Nile serenely flowing!

Carnage and curses and cries!
He utters never a word;
Still as a child he lies;
The wind of the desert is blowing
Across the dead man of the Lord;
And the Nile is softly flowing.

But the song is stilled in heaven
To welcome one more king:
For the truth he hath witnessed and striven,
And let the world go crowing,
And Mammon’s church-bell go ring,
And the Nile blood-red go flowing!

Man who hated the sword
Yet wielded the sword and axe﻿—
Farewell, O arm of the Lord,
The Lord’s own harvest mowing﻿—
With a wind in the smoking flax
Where our foul rivers are flowing!

In war thou didst cherish peace,
Thou slewest for love of life:
Hail, hail thy stormy release
Go home and await thy sowing,
The patient flower of thy strife,
Thy bread on the Nile cast flowing.

Not thy earth to our earth alone,
Thy spirit is left with us!
Thy body is victory’s throne,
And our hearts around it are glowing:
Would that we others died thus
Where the Thames and the Clyde are flowing!

===Chinese===

背叛者的脚步，静默！
紧闭的怒火，静默！
吼声，与骤然的心跳！
子弹正穿过那颗真诚的心，
这个时代最真诚的心！
尼罗河平静地流淌！

杀戮、咒诅与哭喊！
他一言不发；
他躺着，静得像个孩子；
沙漠的风正吹过
主之死者的身躯；
尼罗河轻柔地流淌。

但天上的歌声也静了片刻，
迎接又一位君王来临：
为了他见证并力争的真理，
且任凭世界去自鸣得意，
任凭玛门的教堂钟鸣响，
任凭尼罗河流淌成血红！

憎恶刀剑的人
却挥起了刀剑与斧钺——
别了，主的手臂，
主亲自收割他的庄稼——
把风吹进将残的灯火，
在我们污浊的河流之上！

战乱中你珍爱和平，
你杀戮是因热爱生命：
欢呼吧，欢呼你风暴般的解脱，
回家去等候你的播种，
你抗争那忍耐的花朵，
你撒在尼罗河上的饼。

不只你的尘土归于我们的尘土，
你的灵仍留驻我们中间！
你的身体是胜利的宝座，
我们的心在它周围灼灼发光：
但愿我们其余人也能这样死去，
在泰晤士河与克莱德河流淌的地方！

## Song of the Saints and Angels / 圣徒与天使之歌
===Original===

*January 26, 1885*

Gordon, the self-refusing,
Gordon, the lover of God,
Gordon, the good part choosing,
Welcome along the road!

Thou knowest the man, O Father!
To do thy will he ran;
Men’s praises he did not gather:
There is scarce such another man!

Thy black sheep’s faithful shepherd
Who knew not how to flee,
Is torn by the desert leopard,
And comes wounded home to thee!

Home he is coming the faster
That the way he could not miss:
In thy arms, oh take him, Master,
And heal him with a kiss!

Then give him a thousand cities
To rule till their evils cease,
And their wailing minor ditties
Die in a psalm of peace.

===Chinese===

*一八八五年一月二十六日*

戈登，那舍己的，
戈登，那爱神的，
戈登，那选了上好福分的，
欢迎你走在这归途上！

父啊，你认识这人！
他奔走，只为行你的旨意；
他不去收取人的称赞：
这样的人几乎再无第二个！

你黑羊的忠心牧人，
他不知何为逃跑，
被荒漠的豹撕碎了，
带着伤归回你这里！

他正加速归家，
因为这条路他不会走岔：
主啊，伸出你的双臂接纳他，
用一个亲吻医治他！

然后给他一千座城，
让他治理，直到诸恶止息，
直到他们哀哭的小调
消逝在一篇平安的诗篇里。

## Failure / 失败
===Original===

Farewell, O Arm of the Lord!
Man who hated the sword,
Yet struck and spared not the thing abhorred!
Farewell, O word of the Word!
Man who knew no failure
But the failure of the Lord!

===Chinese===

别了，主的手臂！
那憎恶刀剑的人，
却挥击不饶那可憎之物！
别了，圣道中的话语！
不知道失败的人——
只知主的失败！

## To E. G., Dedicating a Book / 致 E. G.，题献一册书
===Original===

A broken tale of endless things,
Take, lady: thou art not of those
Who in what vale a fountain springs
Would have its journey close.

Countless beginnings, fair first parts,
Leap to the light, and shining flow;
All broken things, or toys or hearts,
Are mended where they go.

Then down thy stream, with hope-filled sail,
Float faithful fearless on, loved friend;
’Tis God that has begun the tale
And does not mean to end.

===Chinese===

一个未完的故事，讲的是无尽的事，
请收下，女士：你不是那种人——
无论泉水从哪个山谷涌出，
便要它的旅程在那里终止。

无数的开端，美好的开篇，
跃入光中，闪亮地流淌；
一切破碎之物，无论是玩具还是心，
都在流淌的途中得着修补。

那么，扬起满帆的希望，顺流而下，
忠实地、无畏地漂浮前行，亲爱的朋友；
这故事是上帝起了头的，
他并不打算将它终结。

## To G. M. T. / 致 G. M. T.
===Original===

The sun is sinking in the west,
Long grow the shadows dim;
Have patience, sister, to be blest,
Wait patiently for Him.

Thou knowest love, much love hast had,
Great things of love mayst tell,
Ought’st never to be very sad
For thou too hast lov’d well.

His house thou know’st, who on the brink
Of death loved more than thou,
Loved more than thy great heart can think,
And just as then loves now﻿—

In that great house is one who waits
For thy slow-coming foot;
Glad is he with his angel-mates
Yet often listens mute,

For he of all men loves thee best:
He haunts the heavenly clock;
Ah, he has long been up and drest
To open to thy knock!

Fear not, doubt not because of those
On whom earth’s keen winds blow;
God’s love shames all our pitying woes,
Be ready thou to go.

Forsaken dream not hearts which here
Bask in no sunny shine;
Each shall one coming day be dear
To love as good as thine.

===Chinese===

太阳正沉入西方，
暗影渐长渐朦胧；
姊妹啊，要有耐性等候福分，
耐心等候他。

你懂得爱，也曾得到许多爱，
能讲述爱的大事，
你本不该过分忧伤，
因为你也爱得深。

你认得那家的主人，他在死亡
边缘时爱你胜过你，
爱得超过你大心所能想，
如今爱正如当初——

在那大宅里有一个人
等候你迟迟的脚步；
他与天使同伴欢欣，
却常常默然侧耳，

因为众人中他爱你最深：
他守着天上的时钟；
啊，他早已起身穿戴整齐，
要来应你的叩门！

不要怕，不要疑，别为那些
被地上寒风吹打的人挂心；
上帝的爱使我们一切的哀怜蒙羞，
你只管预备动身。

别以为在此世晒不到
和煦阳光的心已被离弃；
终有一日，每一颗心都会
被如你之善的爱所珍视。

## In Memoriam Lady Caroline Charteris / 悼卡罗琳·查特里斯夫人
===Original===

The mountain-stream may humbly boast
For her the loud waves call;
The hamlet feeds the nation’s host,
The home-farm feeds the hall;

And unto earth heaven’s Lord doth lend
The right, of high import,
The gladsome privilege to send
New courtiers to Love’s court.

Not strange to thee, O lady dear,
Life in that palace fair,
For thou while waiting with us here
Didst just as they do there!

Thy heart still open to receive,
Open thy hand to give,
God had thee graced with more than leave
In heavenly state to live!

And though thou art gone up so high
Thou art not gone so far
But that thy love to us comes nigh,
As starlight from a star.

And ours must reach where’er thou art,
In far or near abode,
For God is of all love the heart,
And we are all in God.

===Chinese===

山间的小溪尽可以谦卑地夸口，
响亮的大浪为她呼号；
小村落供养着民族的大军，
家宅的田庄供养着华堂；

天上的主（Lord）将一项权利借给大地——
意义何等重大，
又是何等喜乐的特权——
差遣新的朝臣前往爱的宫廷。

那华美宫殿里的生活，
亲爱的夫人，于你并不陌生，
因为你在这里与我们一同等候时，
所行的正与那里的人一样！

你的心总敞开着领受，
你的手敞开着施与，
上帝给你的恩典，不止是准许你
活在属天的光景里！

虽然你升得那样高，
却并未走得太远——
你的爱仍临近我们，
如星光来自一颗星。

我们的爱也必达到你所在之处，
无论居所远或近，
因为上帝是一切爱的心脏，
而我们都在上帝里面。

## A Mammon-Marriage / 玛门的婚礼
===Original===

The croak of a raven hoar!
A dog’s howl, kennel-tied!
Loud shuts the carriage-door:
The two are away on their ghastly ride
To Death’s salt shore!

Where are the love and the grace?
The bridegroom is thirsty and cold!
The bride’s skull sharpens her face!
But the coachman is driving, jubilant, bold,
The devil’s pace.

The horses shivered and shook
Waiting gaunt and haggard
With sorry and evil look;
But swift as a drunken wind they staggered
’Longst Lethe brook.

Long since, they ran no more;
Heavily pulling they died
On the sand of the hopeless shore
Where never swelled or sank a tide,
And the salt burns sore.

Flat their skeletons lie,
White shadows on shining sand;
The crusted reins go high
To the crumbling coachman’s bony hand
On his knees awry.

Side by side, jarring no more,
Day and night side by side,
Each by a doorless door,
Motionless sit the bridegroom and bride
On the Dead-Sea-shore.

===Chinese===

一只灰老乌鸦的嘶叫！
一条拴在窝里的狗在嚎！
车厢门砰然关响：
两人踏上了阴森的行程，
奔向死亡的盐滩！

爱与恩典在哪里？
新郎又渴又冷！
新娘的头骨磨尖了她的脸！
而车夫驾着车，欢腾而大胆，
用着魔鬼的步速。

马匹曾颤抖摇晃，
枯瘦憔悴地等候，
神情凄苦而凶恶；
可它们像醉风一样歪斜疾驰，
沿着忘川之流。

早已，它们再不能奔跑；
它们拉着车，沉重地
死在绝望之岸的沙上——
那里从无潮汐涨落，
盐灼得生疼。

它们的骸骨平躺，
是闪亮白沙上的白影；
僵结的缰绳高高
牵向车夫正朽坏的骨手，
他双膝歪跪。

新郎新娘并肩而坐，不再争吵，
日夜并肩，
各自守着一扇无门的门，
一动不动，坐在
死海的岸边。

## A Song in the Night / 夜里的歌
===Original===

*A Brown Bird Sang on a Blossomy Tree*

A brown bird sang on a blossomy tree,
Sang in the moonshine, merrily,
Three little songs, one, two, and three,
A song for his wife, for himself, and me.

He sang for his wife, sang low, sang high,
Filling the moonlight that filled the sky;
“Thee, thee, I love thee, heart alive!
Thee, thee, thee, and thy round eggs five!”

He sang to himself, “What shall I do
With this life that thrills me through and through!
Glad is so glad that it turns to ache!
Out with it, song, or my heart will break!”

He sang to me, “Man, do not fear
Though the moon goes down and the dark is near;
Listen my song and rest thine eyes;
Let the moon go down that the sun may rise!”

I folded me up in the heart of his tune,
And fell asleep with the sinking moon;
I woke with the day’s first golden gleam,
And, lo, I had dreamed a precious dream!

===Chinese===

*一只褐鸟在繁花树上歌唱*

一只褐鸟在繁花的树上歌唱，
在月光里欢快地唱，
唱了三支小歌，一支、两支、三支，
一首给他的妻子，一首给他自己，一首给我。

他为妻子唱，低低地唱，高高地唱，
歌声灌满那灌满天空的月光；
「你呀，你呀，我爱你，活蹦的心肝！
你呀，你呀，还有你圆圆的五颗蛋！」

他对自己唱：「这贯通我、令我战栗的生命，
叫我拿它怎么办！
欢喜得太欢喜，竟变成了酸痛！
唱出来吧，歌啊，不然我的心要裂开！」

他对着我唱：「人啊，不要怕，
纵使月亮落下，黑暗临近；
听我的歌，合上你的眼睛歇息；
让月亮落下去吧，好叫太阳升起来！」

我把自己裹进他曲调的中心，
伴着西沉的月亮睡去；
白昼第一道金光里我醒来，
看哪，我做了一个珍贵的梦！

## Love’s History / 爱的历史
===Original===

Love, the baby,
Crept abroad to pluck a flower:
One said, Yes, sir; one said, Maybe;
One said, Wait the hour.

Love, the boy,
Joined the youngsters at their play:
But they gave him little joy,
And he went away.

Love, the youth,
Roamed the country, quiver-laden;
From him fled away in sooth
Many a man and maiden!

Love, the man,
Sought a service all about;
But they called him feeble, one
They could do without.

Love, the aged,
Walking, bowed, the shadeless miles,
Read a volume many-paged,
Full of tears and smiles.

Love, the weary,
Tottered down the shelving road:
At its foot, lo, Night, the starry,
Meeting him from God!

“Love, the holy,”
Sang a music in her dome,
Sang it softly, sang it slowly,
“Love is coming home!”

===Chinese===

爱，是婴孩，
爬到外面去摘一朵花：
有人说，好的，先生；有人说，也许吧；
有人说，再等等吧。

爱，是少年，
加入孩子们的游戏：
但他们没给他多少快乐，
他便走开了。

爱，是青年，
背着箭囊游荡乡野；
确实有许多男人和少女
见了他就逃开！

爱，是壮年，
四处谋求一份差事；
他们却说他软弱，
是个可有可无的人。

爱，是老者，
弓着身走过无荫的长路，
读着一本厚厚的书卷，
满是眼泪与微笑。

爱，是倦者，
蹒跚走下倾斜的路：
看哪，在路脚，繁星之夜
正从上帝那里迎他！

「爱，这圣者，」
一个乐音在她的穹顶吟唱，
轻轻地唱，缓缓地唱：
「爱正在回家！」

## The Lark and the Wind / 云雀与风
===Original===

In the air why such a ringing?
On the earth why such a droning?

In the air the lark is singing;
On the earth the wind is moaning.

“I am blest, in sunlight swinging!”
“Sad am I: the world lies groaning!”

In the sky the lark kept singing;
On the earth the wind kept moaning.

===Chinese===

空中为何这般鸣响？
地上为何这般低回？

空中，云雀在歌唱；
地上，风在呜咽。

「我有福了，在阳光里荡漾！」
「我悲伤：世界正躺着呻吟！」

天上，云雀不住地歌唱；
地上，风不住地呜咽。

## A Dead House / 死屋
===Original===

When the clock hath ceased to tick
Soul-like in the gloomy hall;
When the latch no more doth click
Tongue-like in the red peach-wall;
When no more come sounds of play,
Mice nor children romping roam,
Then looks down the eye of day
On a dead house, not a home!

But when, like an old sun’s ghost,
Haunts her vault the spectral moon;
When earth’s margins all are lost,
Melting shapes nigh merged in swoon,
Then a sound﻿—hark! there again!﻿—
No, ’tis not a nibbling mouse!
’Tis a ghost, unseen of men,
Walking through the bare-floored house!

And with lightning on the stair
To that silent upper room,
With the thunder-shaken air
Sudden gleaming into gloom,
With a frost-wind whistling round,
From the raging northern coasts,
Then, mid sieging light and sound,
All the house is live with ghosts!

Brother, is thy soul a cell
Empty save of glittering motes,
Where no live loves live and dwell,
Only notions, things, and thoughts?
Then thou wilt, when comes a Breath
Tempest-shaking ridge and post,
Find thyself alone with Death
In a house where walks no ghost.

===Chinese===

当时钟不再滴答，
不再像灵魂守着阴暗的厅堂；
当门闩不再咔嗒，
不再像舌头贴着红桃木墙；
当再没有嬉戏的声响，
老鼠和孩子都不再奔跑嬉闹，
白昼的眼睛便俯望
一座死屋，而非家园！

但当月亮，像旧日的幽魂，
萦绕着她的穹苍出没；
当大地的边缘全都隐没，
万物融化、近乎昏迷，
一声响动——听！又来了！——
不，那不是啃咬的老鼠！
是一个人眼看不见的幽魂，
走过光地板的屋子！

当闪电落在楼梯上，
通向那寂静的顶楼，
当雷声震颤的空气
骤然照亮又归于幽暗，
当寒风呼啸盘旋，
来自咆哮的北方海岸，
于是，在围攻般的光与声里，
整座屋子活满了幽魂！

弟兄啊，你的灵魂可是一间小室，
空空荡荡只余闪烁的浮尘，
没有鲜活的爱栖居，
只有观念、物件与思绪？
那么当一阵气息临到，
暴风摇撼梁柱，
你将发现自己与死亡独处，
在一座没有幽魂行走的屋中。

## Master and Boy / 主人与男孩
===Original===

“Who is this little one lying,”
Said Time, “at my garden-gate,
Moaning and sobbing and crying,
Out in the cold so late?”

“They lurked until we came near,
Master and I,” the child said,
“Then caught me, with ‘Welcome, New-year!
Happy Year! Golden-head!’

“See Christmas-day, my Master,
On the meadow a mile away!
Father Time, make me run faster!
I’m the Shadow of Christmas-day!”

“Run, my child; still he’s in sight!
Only look well to his track;
Little Shadow, run like the light,
He misses you at his back!”

Old Time sat down in the sun
On a grave-stone﻿—his legs were numb:
“When the boy to his master has run,”
He said, “Heaven’s New Year is come!”

===Chinese===

「这小孩是谁，躺在
我的花园门口，」
时间说，「呜咽、抽泣、哭喊，
这么晚了还在寒冷里？」

「他们埋伏着，等我们走近——
我和主人，」孩子说，
「然后就抓住了我，喊着：『欢迎，新年！
快乐年！金发娃！』

「看哪，圣诞日，我的主人，
就在一英里外的草地上！
时间老父，让我跑得更快些！
我是圣诞日的影子！」

「跑吧，我的孩子；他还望得见！
只要紧紧盯住他的踪迹；
小影子，跑得像光一样快，
他正回头找你呢，就在他背后！」

老时间坐在阳光里，
坐在一块墓石上——他的腿都麻了：
「等这孩子跑到他主人身边，」
他说，「天上的新年就到了！」

## The Clock of the Universe / 宇宙之钟
===Original===

A clock aeonian, steady and tall,
With its back to creation’s flaming wall,
Stands at the foot of a dim, wide stair.
Swing, swang, its pendulum goes,
Swing﻿—swang﻿—here﻿—there!
Its tick and its tack like the sledge-hammer blows
Of Tubal Cain, the mighty man!
But they strike on the anvil of never an ear,
On the heart of man and woman they fall,
With an echo of blessing, an echo of ban;
For each tick is a hope, each tack is a fear,
Each tick is a Where, each tack a Not here,
Each tick is a kiss, each tack is a blow,
Each tick says “Why,” each tack “I don’t know.”
Swing, swang, the pendulum!
Tick and tack, and go and come,
With a haunting, far-off, dreamy hum,
With a tick, tack, loud and dumb,
Swings the pendulum.

Two hands, together joined in prayer,
With a roll and a volley of spheric thunder;
Two hands, in hope spread half asunder,
An empty gulf of longing embrace;
Two hands, wide apart as they can fare
In a fear still coasting not touching Despair,
But turning again, ever round to prayer:
Two hands, human hands, pass with awful motion
From isle to isle of the sapphire ocean.

The silent, surfaceless ocean-face
Is filled with a brooding, hearkening grace;
The stars dream in, and sink fainting out,
And the sun and the moon go walking about,
Walking about in it, solemn and slow,
Solemn and slow, at a thinking pace,
Walking about in it to and fro,
Walking, walking about.

With open beak and half-open wing
Ever with eagerness quivering,
On the peak of the clock
Stands a cock:
Tip-toe stands the cock to crow﻿—
Golden cock with silver call
Clear as trumpet tearing the sky!
No one yet has heard him cry,
Nor ever will till the hour supreme
When Self on itself shall turn with a scream,
What time the hands are joined on high
In a hoping, despairing, speechless sigh,
The perfect groan-prayer of the universe
When the darkness clings and will not disperse
Though the time is come, told ages ago,
For the great white rose of the world to blow:
—Tick, tack, to the waiting cock,
Tick, tack, goes the aeon-clock!

===Chinese===

一座永世的钟，沉稳而高挺，
背靠着创造之火焰的墙垣，
立在一段昏暗宽阶的脚下。
摆起，摆回，它的钟摆摇荡，
摆——荡——这里——那里！
它的滴与嗒像大锤的击打，
出自土八该隐，那大能之人！
却敲在没有耳朵的砧上，
落在男人与女人的心间，
带回祝福的回响、咒诅的回响；
每一声滴是盼望，每一声嗒是恐惧，
每一声滴问「在哪里」，每一声嗒答「不在这里」，
每一声滴是亲吻，每一声嗒是打击，
每一声滴说「为什么」，每一声嗒说「我不知道」。
摆起，摆回，那钟摆！
滴与嗒，去与来，
带着萦绕、遥远、如梦的嗡鸣，
带着滴、嗒，响亮又喑哑，
钟摆摇荡。

两根指针，合拢一同祷告，
伴着一阵滚球般的雷鸣；
两根指针，因盼望半张，
空留一道渴念拥抱的鸿沟；
两根指针，张到不能再开，
在恐惧中贴岸而行，不触绝望，
却又转回，永远转回祷告：
两根指针，人的手，以可畏的动作
从这座岛到那座岛，越过蓝宝石的海洋。

寂静的、无面的海洋之面
盈满一种孵育的、倾听的恩典；
星辰梦入其中，又晕出沉没，
太阳与月亮在其间行走，
行走其间，庄重而缓慢，
庄重而缓慢，以沉思的步速，
在其间来来回回，
行走，行走不停。

张着喙，半张着翅，
永远因热望而颤动，
在钟的顶巅
立着一只雄鸡：
雄鸡踮起脚尖将要啼鸣——
金鸡，银色的啼声，
清亮如撕裂天空的号角！
还没有人听它啼过，
也永不会听见，直到那至高的时辰，
当「自我」尖叫着转而反噬自身，
正当指针在高处合拢，
发出盼望而绝望、无言的叹息，
宇宙那完全的呻吟之祷——
当黑暗紧附不离，不肯消散，
尽管时刻已到，远古已宣告，
世界这朵大白玫瑰当要绽放：
——滴，嗒，向着等待的雄鸡，
滴，嗒，永世之钟在走！

===Original===

A polar bear, golden and gray,
Crawls and crawls around the top.
Black and black as an Ethiop
The great sea-serpent lies coiled beneath,
Living, living, but does not breathe.
For the crawling bear is so far away
That he cannot hear, by night or day,
The bourdon big of his deep bear-bass
Roaring atop of the silent face,
Else would he move, and none knows then
What would befall the sons of men!

Eat up old Time, O raging Bear;
Take Bald-head, and the children spare!
Lie still, O Serpent, nor let one breath
Stir thy pool and stay Time’s death!
Steady, Hands! for the noon is nigh:
See the silvery ghost of the Dawning shy
Low on the floor of the level sky!
Warn for the strike, O blessed Clock;
Gather thy clarion breath, gold Cock;
Push on the month-figures, pale, weary-faced Moon;
Tick, awful Pendulum, tick amain;
And soon, oh, soon,
Lord of life, and Father of boon,
Give us our own in our arms again!

Then the great old clock to pieces will fall
Sans groaning of axle or whirring of wheel.
And away like a mist of the morning steal,
To stand no more in creation’s hall;
Its mighty weights will fall down plumb
Into the regions where all is dumb;
No more will its hands, in horror or prayer,
Be lifted or spread at the foot of the stair
That springs aloft to the Father’s room;
Its tick and its tack, When?﻿—Not now,
Will cease, and its muffled groan below;
Its sapphire face will dissolve away
In the dawn of the perfect, love-potent day;
The serpent and bear will be seen no more,
Growling atop, or prone on the floor;
And up the stair will run as they please
The children to clasp the Father’s knees.

O God, our father, Allhearts’ All,
Open the doors of thy clockless hall!

===Chinese===

一只北极熊，金色夹着灰白，
在钟顶上一圈一圈地爬。
黑而又黑，如埃塞俄比亚人，
大海蛇盘卧在下面，
活着，活着，却不呼吸。
因为爬行的熊离得那么远，
无论昼夜，它都听不见
它那深沉熊腔的巨大低音
在寂静的钟面上轰鸣，
否则它便会动，那时无人知晓
人类的儿女会遭遇什么！

吞掉老时间吧，咆哮的熊；
吃掉那秃头的，饶过孩子们！
躺着别动，蛇啊，别让一口气
搅动你的水渊，阻了时间的死！
稳住，指针！正午已近：
看那羞怯黎明的银色幽影
低低贴在平坦天空的地板上！
报时待击吧，蒙福的钟；
聚起你号角般的气息，金鸡；
推动月份的字码吧，苍白倦容的月亮；
滴答，可畏的钟摆，疾速滴答；
不久，哦，不久，
生命之主，恩赐之父，
把我们亲爱的人还给我们，回到我们怀中！

那时这座巨大的老钟将散成碎片，
没有车轴的呻吟，没有车轮的飞转。
它将像晨雾一样悄悄溜走，
不再立在创造的大厅；
它沉重的钟锤将笔直坠下，
坠入万籁俱寂的地界；
它的指针不再在惊恐或祷告中
在那直通父之居所的阶梯脚下
举起或张开；
它的滴与嗒，「何时？」——「还不」，
将止息，连同下面那闷哑的呻吟；
它蓝宝石的钟面将消融
在完全的、爱能沛然的黎明；
蛇与熊将不再出现，
不再在顶上咆哮，或俯卧在地；
孩子们将随意跑上阶梯，
去搂住父亲的膝。

上帝啊，我们的父，万众之心的一切，
打开你无钟之殿的门吧！

## The Thorn in the Flesh / 肉中之刺
===Original===

Within my heart a worm had long been hid.
I knew it not when I went down and chid
Because some servants of my inner house
Had not, I found, of late been doing well,
But then I spied the horror hideous
Dwelling defiant in the inmost cell﻿—
No, not the inmost, for there God did dwell!
But the small monster, softly burrowing,
Near by God’s chamber had made itself a den,
And lay in it and grew, the noisome thing!
Aghast I prayed﻿—’twas time I did pray then!
But as I prayed it seemed the loathsome shape
Grew livelier, and did so gnaw and scrape
That I grew faint. Whereon to me he said﻿—
Some one, that is, who held my swimming head,
“Lo, I am with thee: let him do his worst;
The creature is, but not his work, accurst;
Thou hating him, he is as a thing dead.”
Then I lay still, nor thought, only endured.
At last I said, “Lo, now I am inured
A burgess of Pain’s town!” The pain grew worse.
Then I cried out as if my heart would break.
But he, whom, in the fretting, sickening ache,
I had forgotten, spoke: “The law of the universe
Is this,” he said: “Weakness shall be the nurse
Of strength. The help I had will serve thee too.”
So I took courage and did bear anew.
At last, through bones and flesh and shrinking skin,
Lo, the thing ate his way, and light came in,
And the thing died. I knew then what it meant,
And, turning, saw the Lord on whom I leant.

===Chinese===

我心中长久藏着一条虫。
我下去责备时并不知晓——
只因我发现，内室里的几个仆役
近来行事不善；
那时我才瞥见那可憎的恐怖，
公然盘踞在最里面的密室——
不，不是最里面，因为神住在那里！
但那小小的怪物，悄悄掘进，
在神的居室旁给自己挖了个窝，
躺在里面渐渐长大，那可厌的东西！
我惊骇地祷告——那时确实该祷告了！
但我祷告时，那可憎的形骸
似乎更活跃了，又是啃又是刮，
刮得我发晕。于是他对我说——
就是那位扶住我晕眩之头的：
「看哪，我与你同在：任它使出最狠的手段；
受咒诅的是那受造之物，而非它的作为；
你恨它，它就如死物一般。」
我便安然躺下，不思想，只是忍受。
最后我说：「看哪，如今我已惯于
作疼痛之城的市民了！」疼痛却愈发剧烈。
于是我喊了出来，心都要碎了。
但他——在那磨人的、令人作呕的酸痛中
被我忘掉的那位——开口说：「宇宙的律
就是如此，」他说：「软弱要作刚强
的乳母。我从前所得的帮助，也必帮助你。」
我便鼓起勇气，重新忍受。
最后，穿过骨头、血肉与蜷缩的皮肤，
看哪，那东西一路蛀透，光进来了，
那东西死了。那时我才明白它的意思，
一转身，看见了我所倚靠的主（Lord）。

## Lycabas / 吕卡巴斯
===Original===

A name of the Year. Some say the word means “a march of wolves,” which wolves, running in single file, are the Months of the Year. Others say the word means “the path of the light.”

O ye months of the year,
Are ye a march of wolves?
Lycabas! Lycabas! twelve to growl and slay?
Men hearken at night, and lie in fear,
Some men hearken all day!

Lycabas, verily thou art a gallop of wolves,
Gaunt gray wolves, gray months of the year, hunting in twelves,
Running and howling, head to tail,
In a single file, over the snow,
A long low gliding of silent horror and fear!
On and on, ghastly and drear,
Not a head turning, not a foot swerving, ye go,
Twelve making only a one-wolf track!
Onward ye howl, and behind we wail;
Wail behind your narrow and slack
Wallowing line, and moan and weep,
As ye draw it on, straight and deep,
Thorough the night so swart!
Behind you a desert, and eyes a-weary,
A long, bare highway, stony and dreary,
A hungry soul, and a wolf-cub wrapt,
A live wolf-cub, sharp-toothed, steel-chapt,
In the garment next the heart!

Lycabas!
One of them hurt me sore!
Two of them hurt and tore!
Three of them made me bleed!
The fourth did a terrible deed,
Rent me the worst of the four!
Rent me, and shook me, and tore,
And ran away with a growl!
Lycabas, if I feared you a jot,
You, and your devils running in twelves,
Black-mouthed, hell-throated, straight-going wolves,
I would run like a wolf, I too, and howl!
I live, and I fear you not.

But shall I not hate you, low-galloping wolves
Hunting in ceaseless twelves?
Ye have hunted away my lambs!
Ye ran at them open-mouthed,
And your mouths were gleamy-toothed,
And their whiteness with red foam frothed,
And your throats were a purple-black gulf:
My lambs they fled, and they came not back!
Lovely white lambs they were, alack!
They fled afar and they left a track
Which at night, when the lone sky clears,
Glistens with Nature’s tears!
Many a shepherd scarce thinks of a lamb
But he hears behind it the growl of a wolf,
And behind that the wail of its dam!

They ran, nor cried, but fled
From day’s sweet pasture, from night’s soft bed:
Ah me, the look in their eyes!
For behind them rushed the swallowing gulf,
The maw of the growl-throated wolf,
And they fled as the thing that speeds or dies:
They looked not behind,
But fled as over the grass the wind.

===Chinese===

「年」的一个名字。有人说这个词意为「一群狼的行进」——这些狼排成单行奔跑，便是一年的十二个月。也有人说这个词意为「光的行径」。

哦，一年的岁月啊，
你们是一队行进的狼吗？
吕卡巴斯！吕卡巴斯！十二只咆哮杀戮的狼？
人们夜里听着，恐惧地躺着，
有些人整天都在听！

吕卡巴斯，你实在是一阵狼的奔驰，
瘦骨嶙峋的灰狼，一年的灰色月份，十二只一队地猎逐，
奔跑着、嚎叫着，首尾相衔，
排成一列纵队，掠过雪原，
一道长长的、低伏的滑行，无声的恐怖与惊惧！
一路向前，凄厉而阴惨，
头也不回，脚步不偏，你们奔驰，
十二只只留下一只狼的足迹！
你们在前头嚎，我们在后面哀哭；
在你那窄而松垮、
深一脚浅一脚的行列后面哀哭、呜咽、流泪，
当你把这行迹拉得又直又深，
穿过如此漆黑的夜！
你身后是一片荒漠，和疲倦的眼睛，
一条漫长、光秃的大道，多石而荒凉，
一个饥饿的灵魂，还有一只裹着的狼崽，
一只活的狼崽，利齿、铁颚，
裹在贴心最近的那层衣裳里！

吕卡巴斯！
它们之一把我重重伤害！
它们之二把我撕咬摧折！
它们之三使我血淌！
第四只行了可怕的一举，
四只之中把我撕得最狠！
撕了我，摇撼我，撕碎我，
一声低吼便跑开了！
吕卡巴斯，我若怕你一分——
怕你和你的十二只一队的魔鬼，
黑口、地狱喉咙、一路直冲的狼——
我也会像狼一样奔跑、嚎叫！
我活着，我不怕你们。

可难道我不该恨你们吗，低伏奔驰的狼群，
无休止地十二只一队地猎逐？
你们把我羔羊都猎逐散了！
你们张着嘴向它们扑去，
你们的嘴里白齿森森，
那森森的白齿上翻着红沫，
你们的喉咙是紫黑的深渊：
我的羔羊逃散了，再没有回来！
它们本是可爱的白羔羊，唉！
它们逃向远方，留下一道痕迹，
夜里，当孤寂的天空放晴，
那痕迹闪着大自然的泪光！
多少牧人刚想起一只羔羊，
便听见它背后狼的低吼，
还有低吼背后母亲的哀鸣！

它们奔跑，不喊叫，只是逃，
逃离白日甜美的草场，逃离夜晚柔软的卧榻：
唉，它们眼中的神情啊！
因为背后是吞噬的深渊在追赶，
是咆哮喉咙的狼之巨口，
它们逃得像那不速死就必飞奔的东西：
它们头也不回，
像风掠过草叶一样逃走了。

===Original===

Oh my lambs, I would drop away
Into a night that never saw day
That so in your dear hearts you might say,
“All is well for ever and aye!”
Yet it was well to hurry away,
To hurry from me, your shepherd gray:
I had no sword to bite and slay,
And the wolfy Months were on your track!
It was well to start from work and play,
It was well to hurry from me away﻿—
But why not once look back?

The wolves came panting down the lea﻿—
What was left you but somewhere flee!
Ye saw the Shepherd that never grows old,
Ye saw the great Shepherd, and him ye knew,
And the wolves never once came near to you;
For he saw you coming, threw down his crook,
Ran, and his arms about you threw;
He gathered you into his garment’s fold,
He kneeled, he gathered, he lifted you,
And his bosom and arms were full of you.
He has taken you home to his stronghold:
Out of the castle of Love ye look;
The castle of Love is now your home,
From the garden of Love you will never roam,
And the wolves no more shall flutter you.

Lycabas! Lycabas!
For all your hunting and howling and cries,
Your yelling of “woe!” and “alas!”
For all your thin tongues and your fiery eyes,
Your questing thorough the windy grass,
Your gurgling gnar, and your horrent hair,
And your white teeth that will not spare﻿—
Wolves, I fear you never a jot,
Though you come at me with your mouths red-hot,
Eyes of fury, and teeth that foam:
Ye can do nothing but drive me home!
Wolves, wolves, you will lie one day﻿—
Ye are lying even now, this very day,
Wolves in twelves, gaunt and gray,
At the feet of the Shepherd that leads the dams,
At the feet of the Shepherd that carries the lambs!

===Chinese===

哦我的羔羊，我宁愿消逝，
坠入一个从未见过白昼的夜，
好叫你们亲爱的心里能说：
「一切永远都好！」
可是，匆匆离去也是好的，
从我这灰发牧人身边匆匆离去也是好的：
我没有剑可以刺击杀敌，
而狼一样的月份正追着你们的踪迹！
撇下工作与游戏也是好的，
从我身边匆匆离去也是好的——
可为什么一次也不回头看看？

狼群喘着气奔下草场——
你们除了逃走还能怎样！
你们看见了那位永不衰老的牧人，
你们看见了大牧者，并且认出了他，
狼群一次也没有靠近你们；
因为他望见你们跑来，丢下杖，
奔过来，用双臂环抱你们；
他把你们拢进衣褶里，
他跪下，拢聚你们，抱起你们，
他的胸怀和臂膀满满都是你们。
